meta.title: iOS parity catch-up — 2026-08
meta.purpose: Machine-readable work-list for bringing btheis15/mlr-app-ios to FULL feature parity with the web app, and beyond it where native can do better. Companion prose (the warnings, the Swift, the incident history) lives in docs/ios-parity-2026-08.md and the per-area files under docs/ios-parity-2026-08/.
meta.ios_last_sync: 2026-07-22 — the July round covered web PRs #316-#362, migrations 0114-0128
meta.product_direction: iOS is the FLAGSHIP, not a companion. Parity is the floor. A feature iOS already has is due a DEPTH AUDIT, not a tick — the web version has usually grown since.
meta.conventions: each web lib/*.ts seam maps to a Swift Services/*Service.swift; new RPCs use the Encodable param-struct + .rpc()/.from() idiom. ios_targets paths in the per-area docs are PROPOSED where the July doc didn't already name them — the iOS repo was not checked out when this was generated.
caveats: The web app is light-mode only by hard rule; iOS supports dark. Every surface here needs a dark treatment with NO web reference to copy.
Sections marked fact_checked:false did not get their verification pass — confirm identifiers before building.
Effort/priority values are the drafting agents' estimates, not measured.

how_to_use.start_with: media-token (see docs/ios-parity-2026-08.md §0) — the first true blocker

true_blockers.why: Every photo in the Feed 403s under MEDIA_AUTH=on. This is why enforcement is currently held at `report`.
Same root cause for chat bubbles — an unsigned read is rejected regardless of surface.
An unverified member currently gets a member layout full of empty lists with no explanation. They are locked out and cannot tell why.
Without a registered token the device receives nothing — every other notification feature is inert.
A shared iPad leaks the previous member's cached content to the next. Security, not polish.

how_to_use.priority_field_warning: features[].priority is the drafting agent's estimate and reads 'blocking' as 'foundational' — it marked 24 items blocking, including screens iOS already has. Use how_to_use.true_blockers for what actually blocks.
how_to_use.then: work workstreams in listed order; each per-area doc holds the build detail
how_to_use.definition_of_done: the acceptance line in the per-area doc, verified on a device
how_to_use.build_check: open 'MLR App.xcodeproj', resolve SPM, Build (Cmd-B). Watch for new Swift files missing target membership. Verify light AND dark on every new surface.

skip_web_only.reason: These web PRs exist to fight the browser. iOS does not inherit any of it — a real slice of the web app's complexity is browser tax you simply won't pay.

features.name: The list of shared albums
features.whatItDoes: Shows every shared photo/video album as a grid of cover tiles with how many items are in it and who made it, so you can tap into one.
gotchas: One embedded select per fetch: drop_boxes.select("id, title, emoji, created_by, archived_at, created_at, drop_box_media(id, storage_path, thumbnail_url, media_type, status, uploaded_by, created_at, captured_at)").order("created_at", ascending: false)
Archived boxes ARE returned by RLS (policy drop_boxes_read returns them too) — the web filters archivedAt != nil client-side. Do the same.
⚠️ storage_path is a misleading name: it is the FULL public mini URL (https://mlr-media.duckdns.org/f/dropbox/<box>/<ym>/<uuid>.jpg), not a relative path.

Nested media rows come back already RLS-filtered: someone else's held item is simply ABSENT from the array, so your item count is 'visible to me', not the true count. That is intended — the web's count is exactly items.count.
⚠️ An empty album list almost always means 'this account isn't approved yet', not 'no albums' — build the pending-approval state instead of rendering 'No albums yet'.

⚠️ Timestamp decoding will bite you. PostgREST returns timestamptz like 2026-08-09T14:22:03.481291+00:00 and Postgres trims trailing zeros, so the fractional part varies in length (sometimes absent). JSONDecoder .iso8601 REJECTS fractional seconds; a fixed ISO8601DateFormatter with .withFractionalSeconds rejects the ones without. Use a custom .custom strategy that tries both, or decode the four timestamptz columns (drop_boxes.created_at, drop_boxes.archived_at, drop_box_media.created_at, drop_box_media.captured_at) as String and parse lazily. The web compares raw ISO strings lexicographically (safe — all UTC from the same server), so keeping them as Strings matches web behavior byte-for-byte.
Tile copy: "{count} items · by {createdByName}", "Empty · by {createdByName}" for a zero-item album, and singularize ("1 item").
media_type is text with CHECK in ('image','video') — make it an enum but decode defensively. status is text CHECK in ('visible','pending','hidden') default 'visible'.

drop_boxes has exactly one FK from drop_box_media so this embed is unambiguous — but if a second FK is ever added, name it (drop_box_media!fk_name(...)) or PostgREST silently returns [] with HTTP 300 / PGRST201.
Index available: drop_box_media_box_idx (box_id, created_at desc). Both tables are in the supabase_realtime publication.
⚠️ There are NO write policies on either table. Any direct .from("drop_boxes").insert/.update/.delete from the client fails — every write is a SECURITY DEFINER RPC.

features.name: Opening a shared album link
features.whatItDoes: Tapping a link to a specific album (from Home, a call-out, or a Family Fest button) opens that album straight away instead of dumping you on the list.
gotchas: One screen, two states, switched by a query param — NOT a nested route: /drop is the album list, /drop?box=<uuid> is one open album. The shareable link is literally /drop?box=<uuid>.
On iOS: one NavigationStack with AlbumsListView → AlbumDetailView(boxId:), and map the universal link / deep link …/drop?box=<uuid> to pushing the detail view directly.
⚠️ The fest CTAs (FamilyFestSpotlight, FestStatus) and Home call-outs already emit that URL shape, so honoring it is NOT optional if you want those buttons to work.
Keep box ids lowercase everywhere — the mini's safeSeg() lowercases ?room to [a-z0-9_-] (max 40 chars), so an uppercase UUID still works but the on-disk folder won't match what you searched for.
Degrade gracefully to "This album isn't available." when the row is missing — that's the documented behavior and the web's exact copy, not an error state.
features.nativeOpportunity: Universal links / deep links can push AlbumDetailView directly, with no intermediate list render.

features.name: "Waiting for an admin to verify you"
features.whatItDoes: A brand-new member who hasn't been verified by an admin yet is told they're waiting for approval, instead of being shown an empty album screen that looks broken.
gotchas: ⚠️ An empty album list almost always means 'this account isn't approved yet', not 'no albums'.

is_approved_member() (migration 0181) is `profiles.approved is true OR is_admin is true`; new signups default to approved = false — EXCEPT the ones migration 0182 auto-approves, whose email was already on committee_roster/family_roster (the same email key that auto-links a roster slot), so some brand-new accounts land approved on first sign-in.
Migration 0183 swapped 29 read policies onto the predicate.
You can always read your OWN profiles row (policy `profiles: member read` = is_approved_member() OR id = auth.uid()), so gate the state on profiles.approved == false for the current user.
The media server returns the same signal as HTTP 403 with {"pendingApproval": true} on /media-token, /upload and /dropbox-zip — treat that JSON flag as the canonical 'unapproved' marker.
There is NO third state to handle: the mini's isApprovedMemberByToken() returns "couldn't determine" as ALLOW (pre-migration column, transient error), so you either get served or you get the 403.
Map 401/403 on /upload to 'sign-in expired OR pendingApproval' in the error copy; /upload sits behind requireUser AND requireApprovedMember.
drop_box_media read policy also allows an approved member to see their own non-visible rows: status = 'visible' OR uploaded_by = auth.uid() OR caller is_admin.

features.name: Browsing one album
features.whatItDoes: Opens an album into a scrollable grid of small photo/video previews, with a header saying how many items there are and who created it.
gotchas: Detail read is the same embedded select as the list plus .eq("id", boxId).maybeSingle().
3-col thumb grid → full-screen swipe carousel.
Header copy: "{count} items · created by {createdByName}"; empty album → "Empty — be the first to add something · created by …".
⚠️ thumbnail_url may be null (pre-0173 rows, or generation failed) — ALWAYS fall back to the full-res storage_path, never render nothing.

⚠️ A video grid tile NEEDS an explicit ▶ badge. With a generated poster frame it's indistinguishable from a photo; without one it's a black box. (The mini's poster frames are seeked ~10% in, capped at 3s — grabbing frame 0 produced a whole album of black tiles because real phone video opens on a black or half-exposed frame.)
Render the status != 'visible' badge ("Held for review") — you WILL see held rows, because RLS shows you your own.
captured_at_source is deliberately NOT selected by the web reader — nothing in the UI reads it; select it only if you want to show provenance.
Item count is 'visible to me' (RLS filters others' held items out of the nested array), not the true count.
Every /f thumbnail and full-res URL needs the signed ?t= media token appended.

features.name: Full-screen swipe through an album
features.whatItDoes: Tapping a photo opens it full screen and you swipe left/right through the whole album without closing and reopening, seeing who uploaded each one.
gotchas: Carousel chrome: an `n / total` counter with "by {uploadedByName}" underneath it; per-item Save, Remove and (admin) Approve actions live here.
The web's carousel windows to ±1 slide so a 2,000-item album keeps ≤3 media elements alive — still avoid eagerly loading full-res for offscreen pages.

⚠️ A video's URL can be repointed a few minutes later: a cross-extension transcode (.mov → .mp4) keeps the original playable until the mini has PATCHed every *_media row's storage_path to the new URL (swapMediaStoragePath), then deletes it. Do NOT treat storage_path as a stable identity key or cache it in a way that survives the swap — key your local cache on drop_box_media.id.
hlsUrl is null unless the mini runs HLS_ENABLED=on (default off) and is advertised by convention before the background ladder exists — always fall back to url.
Load the full-res file only on tap-through; the grid renders thumbnail_url.
Every media URL needs the signed ?t= token; it survives Range requests, which is why video seeking works.
features.nativeOpportunity: LazyHStack + .scrollTargetBehavior(.paging) gives you the ±1 windowing and paging physics for free, replacing the web's hand-rolled scroll-snap carousel.
features.v1Cut: View + per-file Save only — omit the admin Approve action and (if you're deferring select mode) Remove.

features.name: Dumping photos and videos into an album
features.whatItDoes: Pick a batch of photos and videos from your phone and they upload straight into the album, full quality, with progress and a retry if one fails.
rpcs: add_drop_box_media(p_box uuid, p_url text, p_type text, p_thumbnail_url text = null, p_captured_at timestamptz = null, p_captured_at_source text = null, p_credit_user_id uuid = null) → uuid
gotchas: Request shape: POST {MEDIA_URL}/upload?category=dropbox&room={boxId}, Authorization: Bearer <supabase access_token>, multipart/form-data with the field name exactly "file", plus optional capturedAt (ISO8601) and capturedAtSource ("exif"|"file").

MEDIA_URL is https://mlr-media.duckdns.org (the PRODUCTION_MEDIA_URL constant in lib/media.ts) — ⚠️ NEXT_PUBLIC_MEDIA_URL is still set to the retired Tailscale host in Vercel and is deliberately ignored in code; don't take the env var as truth.

The box id rides in ?room, sanitized server-side by safeSeg() to lowercase [a-z0-9_-], max 40 chars. A lowercase UUID survives intact; ⚠️ an uppercase UUID is lowercased — keep ids lowercase everywhere so you can find things on disk. Files land under dropbox/<box-id>/<YYYY-MM>/.

⚠️ Do NOT re-encode or compress the photo on the client. prepareImageForUpload() in lib/media.ts is now literally `return file` — an intentionally-kept no-op with a warning comment. It used to downscale to 1920px and re-encode at JPEG q0.82 through a <canvas>, which destroyed the full-resolution original before it ever left the phone AND stripped every byte of EXIF (the root cause of the whole captured_at saga 0174/0175/0176 exist to undo). On iOS: hand URLSession the file bytes from PHPickerResult.itemProvider.loadFileRepresentation / PHAssetResourceManager, NOT UIImage.jpegData(compressionQuality:). HEIC is fine — the mini converts it with sharp and keeps your original beside it.

⚠️ Never construct the stored URL — always use the returned `url`. A HEIC upload's served URL comes back as .jpg (the mini builds the display copy inline via makeDisplayCopy before responding, and keeps the upload as <uuid>_orig.heic). Deriving the URL from the filename you sent produces a 404.

Raw /upload response: { url, thumbnailUrl|null, hlsUrl|null, capturedAt|null, capturedAtSource|null, name, originalName, type, path }. ⚠️ UploadResult in lib/media.ts models only SIX of those (url, thumbnailUrl, capturedAt, capturedAtSource, type, path) — hlsUrl/name/originalName are on the wire but dropped by the web's parse.

Then attach with add_drop_box_media passing the values the SERVER returned (p_url: url, p_type: "image"|"video", p_thumbnail_url: thumbnailUrl, p_captured_at: capturedAt, p_captured_at_source: capturedAtSource) — let the mini's own read win over any client-side guess.

⚠️ Do NOT port lib/dropBoxes.ts's five-deep PGRST202 retry ladder (7-arg → 6 → 5 → 4 → 3). Every one of 0173/0174/0175/0180 explicitly drops the narrower overload it replaces, so exactly ONE signature exists; prod has 0180 applied — call the 7-param version. A real PGRST202 means the schema cache is stale or the migration was rolled back: surface it, don't paper over it, because the silent degrade drops the credit/captured-at data.

Swift call shapes: the uuid-returning RPCs come back as a BARE JSON string ("3f1c…") — decode as String then UUID(uuidString:), not as an object. Build params as [String: AnyJSON] (supabase-swift), not a Codable struct with optionals: a MISSING key changes PostgREST overload resolution, a `null` value does not.

add_drop_box_media rejects with "That folder is not available." when the box doesn't exist OR archived_at is not null (you cannot add to an archived album), "Unsupported media type." for anything but image/video, and "Sign in required." with no session.

⚠️ /upload is deliberately NOT rate-limited (globalLimiter skips /health and /upload) because a fest dump is hundreds of photos from one phone. Everything else on the mini — /f reads, /media-token, /dropbox-zip — shares a 600 requests / 15 min per-IP floor, and a whole family behind one lake WiFi IP collapses to one key, so don't hammer /f with speculative prefetches.
Concurrency: the web uploads 3 at a time (LIMIT = 3) so a big batch overlaps without stampeding the mini's ffmpeg/moderation. Copy that number.

Timeouts: server-side UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS defaults to 4 HOURS and MAX_MB is 50 GB, but ⚠️ neither means a huge upload succeeds — bandwidth and the tunnel's body cap bind first. Set a generous URLSessionConfiguration.timeoutIntervalForRequest/ForResource and use a BACKGROUND session so a backgrounded app doesn't kill a large video mid-transfer. A client abort is handled server-side (partial file unlinked on socket close), so retrying is safe.

Status codes → copy (the web's uploadErrorMessage): 507 = server out of storage ("tell an admin"), 413 = file too big, 415 = the magic-byte sniff says it isn't a photo or video at all ("Only photos and videos can be uploaded." — Tier 0; only category=chat allows non-media), 429 = upload limit (kept defensively), 401/403 = sign-in expired OR pendingApproval, network abort = "interrupted — check your connection".

Retry: keep the picked file around so a failed item can be re-sent in place without re-picking (the web's Pending struct holds the raw File; on iOS hold the temp file URL and don't delete it until the row lands).
CORS is irrelevant — native URLSession sends no Origin, so the mini's ALLOWED_ORIGINS allowlist doesn't apply. Don't chase a CORS ghost.

The web's optimistic tile matches the real DB row BY URL and therefore carries an explicit 12-second timeout fallback so a tile can't spin forever when the URL changed underneath it. Build the equivalent, or just rely on realtime + refetch.

The web picker is a plain always-mounted <input> triggered by a plain button, never from inside a popup, because an installed iOS PWA silently dropped the file otherwise — irrelevant to PHPickerViewController, but don't 'fix' the web if you touch it.
⚠️ There is NO notification or push of any kind for drop boxes — not a new album, not a new item, not a held item. Don't promise the family one; adding it is genuinely new backend work.
New uploads land status='visible' essentially always today (the mini's moderation is fire-and-forget and nothing holds retroactively) — see the moderation entries.
features.nativeOpportunity: A background URLSession keeps a multi-hundred-MB video upload alive when the app is backgrounded, which the web PWA cannot do; PHPicker file representations hand over the untouched original bytes (EXIF intact) with no canvas re-encode; and native sends no Origin so CORS never applies.
features.v1Cut: Ship picker + 3-at-a-time queue + per-tile progress + per-item retry + the error-copy map. Safe to omit: sending capturedAt/capturedAtSource at all (let the mini read the stored bytes — the simplest correct v1), p_credit_user_id (pass nil), and the URL-matched optimistic-tile plumbing with its 12s fallback (rely on realtime + refetch instead).

features.name: Photos keep the date they were actually taken
features.whatItDoes: Each photo or video carries its real shot date where possible, so an album can be ordered by when things happened rather than when someone got around to uploading.
rpcs: add_drop_box_media(p_box uuid, p_url text, p_type text, p_thumbnail_url text = null, p_captured_at timestamptz = null, p_captured_at_source text = null, p_credit_user_id uuid = null) → uuid
gotchas: captured_at is timestamptz NULL (0174); captured_at_source is text NULL (0175) with CHECK in ('exif','video','file','post').
Videos: send NOTHING. The mini reads the container's creation_time via ffprobe during /upload and returns capturedAt with source 'video'.

Photos: you can send nothing and let the mini read the stored bytes (hand-rolled JPEG/TIFF IFD reader plus a sharp/libvips fallback that opens HEIC/WebP/AVIF/TIFF, deliberately reading the _orig upload, not the display copy). That is the simplest correct v1.

⚠️ The mini only trusts 'exif' from a client — any other claimed source is downgraded to 'file' (capturedAtSource = claimed === "exif" ? "exif" : "file"), and /upload then RE-READS the stored bytes whenever the client's claim is only 'file', letting real metadata win. So if you use PHAsset.creationDate (usually better than a file mtime), send it as "file", NOT "exif". Claiming "exif" makes the server skip its own read and locks your value in against all future upgrades — the single easiest way to permanently poison album ordering.

⚠️ p_captured_at_source is validated with a SILENT fallback to 'exif': if p_captured_at is non-null and the source string isn't one of the four valid values, the row is stamped 'exif'. A typo or your own vocabulary ("photokit", "asset") permanently marks a weak guess as authoritative real metadata, and the mini's backfill sweep will then NEVER upgrade it (the sweep only moves a row UP the ranking). Always send exactly "exif", "video", "file" or "post", or send nothing. With p_captured_at null, the source is forced to null.

Provenance ranking, best first: 'exif'/'video' (real metadata read from the file) > 'file' (the picked file's mtime) > 'post' (the source post's own timestamp, an explicitly-marked proxy). The ranking is a convention in the sweep + comments; the DB only CHECKs membership in the four values.

⚠️ Keep the web's mtime heuristic guard (capturedAtForFile): reject a timestamp that is missing, pre-1995, in the future, or WITHIN 60 SECONDS OF NOW — a picker that hands over a freshly-stamped temp copy is giving you upload time in disguise, and PHPickerViewController file representations do exactly that.

⚠️ The 0174/0175 lesson: 0174 read captured_at client-side at upload time and in practice did almost nothing, because the dominant path into the Family Fest album is referencing an existing Feed post's photo, where there is no File on the client at all. All 48 items had captured_at = null and 41 had been bulk-added inside the SAME SECOND, so near-duplicates scattered — and because the sort falls back to upload time the failure was INVISIBLE. 0175 added the server-side sweep plus a SQL backfill joining drop_box_media.storage_path to post_media/posts taking min(coalesce(occurred_at, created_at)) where exactly one post owns the file, which spread those 41 photos back across 6 real days. Takeaway: an enrichment that only runs at upload time covers none of the content already there — if you add any derived field, plan the backfill in the same breath.
features.nativeOpportunity: PHAsset.creationDate is available on iOS and is usually far better than a file mtime — but it must be sent as source "file", never "exif".

features.name: Sort by when taken vs when uploaded
features.whatItDoes: Lets you flip an album between newest-uploaded-first and newest-taken-first, just on your own phone.
gotchas: Sorting is ENTIRELY client-side over the already-fetched items, and is a per-viewer, per-device viewing preference that is never written to the DB — switching it cannot reorder the album for anybody else.
Two orders (DropBoxSort): "uploaded" = newest created_at first; "captured" = newest (captured_at ?? created_at) first (never hides an item for lacking metadata).

⚠️ CLAUDE.md's Drop Box section says the grid sorts by capture date by default. It does NOT — the code default is "uploaded" (DROP_BOX_SORT_DEFAULT). The doc comment explains why: capture order made a freshly-uploaded photo scatter into the middle of the album by its shot date, which read as the app glitching or losing photos. Trust the code.
Persist the toggle in UserDefaults (the web uses localStorage key mlr.dropbox.sort — device-local, deliberately not synced, so you don't need to match the key).
If you keep the timestamps as raw ISO Strings, sorting is a plain string compare and you match web behavior byte-for-byte (they're all UTC from the same server).

features.name: Photos actually load (signed media links)
features.whatItDoes: Every photo and video request carries a short-lived signed token, so albums render instead of showing rows of broken tiles once the server starts enforcing it.
gotchas: Not drop-box-specific, but it is the #1 way an album renders as 40 broken tiles. If your Posts feed already does this, reuse it verbatim.

⚠️⚠️ Enforcement is currently MEDIA_AUTH=report, NOT on. media-auth.js has three modes (off/report/on); the mini was briefly `on` (verified on web: 220/220 signed requests) and then deliberately backed off to `report` because the native app can't sign yet. Consequence 1: unsigned /f reads today still return 200/206 and merely log a WOULD-BLOCK line, so your album will render BEFORE you implement any of this — "photos load" is NOT evidence the token works. Verify with grep WOULD-BLOCK …/media-server/logs/server.log after actually scrolling an album and scrubbing a video. Consequence 2: it goes back to `on` as soon as iOS signs, at which point every unsigned URL 403s.
GET {MEDIA_URL}/media-token with Authorization: Bearer <supabase jwt> → { token, expiresAt, ttlHours }. Behind requireUser AND the approval gate (403 + pendingApproval for an unapproved member).

Append it to EVERY media URL: …/f/…jpg?t=. It's a query param on purpose: /AVPlayer can't send headers, and a cookie would be third-party (Safari/iOS blocks those). It survives Range requests, which is why video seeking works.

The token is an HMAC over a rounded 24h window, so it is IDENTICAL for every member in that window — deliberate, so URLs are cache-stable. verifyToken also accepts the previous window, so a link works 24–48h.
⚠️ Cache it and refresh a FULL MINUTE before expiresAt so no URL can expire mid-flight (lib/mediaToken.ts does exactly that).

⚠️ Outage 1: /media-token once sent Cache-Control: private, max-age=600 with a stable ETag, so revalidation returned 304, res.ok was false, the client concluded "no token", and EVERY photo in the app 403'd (104 consecutive unsigned requests on one album, observed live). Never treat a 304 as failure — fall back to your cached token.

⚠️ Outage 2: the signing check was url.startsWith(MEDIA_URL) and MEDIA_URL had gone stale against a retired Tailscale host while all ~1,700 stored URLs were on duckdns — so every URL silently rendered unsigned, indistinguishable from "no token yet". Match by HOST against a known set (MEDIA_HOSTS), not by prefix, and include the retired host brians-mac-mini.tail49943c.ts.net in that set because stored rows may still carry it.
Don't append ?t= to non-mini URLs (Supabase avatars, data:, local file URLs) and don't append it twice (check for an existing t=).
Clear the token on sign-out (clearMediaToken()) so a shared device leaves nothing usable behind.

features.name: Who made the album and who added each photo
features.whatItDoes: Shows the name of the person who created an album, and — in the full-screen view — who uploaded the photo you're looking at.
gotchas: Resolve display names with ONE bulk call per fetch: collect every distinct created_by + uploaded_by, then profiles.select("id, display_name, avatar_url").in("id", ids). Do NOT fetch a name per row.
Fall back to the literal string "Member" when display_name is blank/absent.

Copy: list tile "{count} items · by {createdByName}" ("Empty · by {createdByName}" for zero items, count singularized as "1 item"); detail header "{count} items · created by {createdByName}" (empty → "Empty — be the first to add something · created by …"); carousel "by {uploadedByName}" under the n / total counter.
profiles is readable via policy `profiles: member read` = is_approved_member() OR id = auth.uid(), so an unverified member can read only their own row.
Realtime payloads do NOT carry the resolved uploader name — another reason to refetch the whole box rather than applying row deltas.

features.name: Save one photo or video to your phone
features.whatItDoes: Saves the original, full-quality file — the one the family actually shot — to your camera roll or out through the share sheet.
gotchas: Per file: append dl=1 to the already-token-signed URL — …/f/dropbox/<box>/<ym>/<uuid>.jpg?t=<token>&dl=1.

The mini responds with Content-Disposition: attachment AND, crucially, serves the PRESERVED ORIGINAL, not the playback rendition: a video's URL points at a bitrate-capped .mp4 built for streaming while the untouched shot file sits beside it as <uuid>_orig.<ext>. ?dl=1 hands back _orig when it exists (findOriginal() searches BOTH storage volumes — originals are deliberately kept on the external drive) and falls through to the rendition when there isn't one. The download filename is derived from the original's extension with the internal _orig marker stripped.

⚠️ The dl=1 handler sits AFTER requireMediaToken on /f, so the ?t= token is still MANDATORY. The web writes t first, then dl (order doesn't matter functionally; it just keeps its 'already signed?' check predictable).

iOS: Content-Disposition does nothing for you. Use a download task, write to a temp URL, then either PHPhotoLibrary.shared().performChanges to add to the camera roll (needs NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription) or hand it to a share sheet.

Parse the filename out of the Content-Disposition response header, or fall back to the URL's last path component — ⚠️ note the served extension may differ from what the row's URL says (_orig is a .mov behind an .mp4).
/f shares the mini's 600 requests / 15 min per-IP limiter (only /upload and /health are exempt), and a whole family behind one lake WiFi IP collapses to one key.
features.nativeOpportunity: Native can write straight into the camera roll via PHPhotoLibrary.performChanges or hand the file to a system share sheet — the web can only trigger a browser download.

features.name: Remove a photo from an album
features.whatItDoes: Lets the person who added a photo (or the album's creator, or an admin) take it back out of the album.
gotchas: Allowed for the item's uploader, the box creator, or an admin — granted execute to authenticated; it raises without auth.uid() or without an uploader/creator/admin match, so handle the throw.
void-returning RPC: empty body — call .execute() and don't try to decode.

⚠️ Files on disk are NOT deleted by the RPC. The mini's orphan-sweep.js reconciles every 6h and quarantines what no row references, purging 7 days later — but it SKIPS any file whose mtime is inside a 48h grace window (ORPHAN_GRACE_HOURS, because the client inserts its media row AFTER /upload returns), so a file deleted the day it was uploaded lingers ~48h before it's even quarantined.

⚠️ Never assume a URL 404s just because its row is gone, and don't add an iOS delete path that assumes files are gone immediately. (Historical: before that sweep existed, one hard-deleted drop box left 438 photos / ~558 MB stranded on disk forever.)
There are NO write policies on drop_box_media — a direct .delete() from the client fails; this RPC is the only path.

features.name: "Held for review" badge
features.whatItDoes: Marks a photo that the automatic content check flagged, so the person who uploaded it can see it's waiting on an admin instead of thinking it vanished.
gotchas: Render the status != 'visible' badge ("Held for review") — you WILL see held rows, because RLS shows you your own (status = 'visible' OR uploaded_by = auth.uid() OR is_admin).
Never let a member change their own item's status — there is no RPC for it; set_drop_box_media_status is admin-only.

Design intent (0171): the BEFORE INSERT trigger hold_drop_box_media_on_flagged reads the mini's media_moderation verdict keyed by the public URL and sets the NEW ROW'S OWN status = 'pending' (the item IS the content — there's no parent post to hold), logging to content_moderation_events with entity_type = 'drop_box_media'. Fail-open: no verdict row ⇒ stays visible.

⚠️ In practice today new uploads land 'visible' essentially always: /upload no longer records the verdict before responding (a perf pass made every category optimistic/fire-and-forget), so the BEFORE INSERT trigger normally finds nothing. The only way an album item is born 'pending' today is if a media_moderation row for that exact storage_path already existed — e.g. the same file was uploaded and flagged via a post first.
drop_box_media is NOT wired into the /admin Content review queue (moderation_queue()/set_content_status() never learned the entity type), so the carousel is the only place to un-hold.

features.name: Admin can release a held photo
features.whatItDoes: An admin looking at a held photo can approve it so everyone else can see it again.
rpcs: set_drop_box_media_status(p_media uuid, p_status text) — p_status in ('visible','pending','hidden') → void
gotchas: Show the Approve action in the carousel only when isAdmin && item.status != "visible".
set_drop_box_media_status raises "Admins only." — check isAdmin before showing the button, but STILL handle the throw.
It is the only place to un-hold: drop_box_media is not wired into the /admin Content review queue (moderation_queue()/set_content_status() never learned the entity type).
void-returning RPC: empty body, call .execute() and don't decode.
features.v1Cut: Omit entirely from v1 — the web can un-hold, and a held item is still visible to its own uploader.

features.name: Flagged photos are never held after the fact (backend gap)
features.whatItDoes: Today a photo the content checker flags a few seconds after upload stays visible to the whole family, because nothing goes back and holds it.
gotchas: ⚠️ This is the ONE place a backend change may be wanted for this area — and it is explicitly NOT iOS work.
⚠️ Do not write it as part of the iOS work, and do not ship it silently — raise it with Brian. Whether drop boxes SHOULD be retroactively held is a product decision he already has an opinion about.

The shape would be a ~15-line addition of a fifth `with held as (...)` block to hold_content_on_media_verdict(), updating drop_box_media set status = 'pending' where status = 'visible' and storage_path = NEW.storage_path.

⚠️ This repo's rule: a function must be recreated from its CURRENT LIVE definition (pg_policies/pg_proc), never from an older migration's copy — the 0160 lesson. hold_content_on_media_verdict is defined only in 0128_chat_moderation.sql (three blocks) and 0162_post_comment_media.sql (which adds the post_comments fourth); drop_box_media appears in neither, and it currently updates only posts, post_comments, committee_messages and house_messages.
CLAUDE.md states that a flagged verdict retroactively holds a drop-box item via "the same media_moderation trigger, 0128/0171" — that claim is WRONG.

Net effect today: a drop-box upload is fail-open and final, which happens to match the documented intent ("a shared family album should never strand photos behind an unreachable checker") but for the wrong reason, and it now also lets through definitively-flagged content the design says should be held.
DB changes here are handed over as SQL for Brian to run, not applied by tooling.

features.name: Albums fill in live
features.whatItDoes: New photos and new albums appear on their own while you're looking at the screen, without a pull-to-refresh, so a family fest dump fills in as it lands.
gotchas: Subscribe to postgres_changes event: "*" on BOTH public.drop_boxes and public.drop_box_media, debounce ~250ms, and REFETCH THE WHOLE BOX — that's what the web does (useDropBox additionally filters both subscriptions to this box's id).
⚠️ Do NOT try to apply row deltas: the payload doesn't carry the resolved uploader name, and RLS/status filtering plus your sort would have to be re-derived anyway.
Both tables are in the supabase_realtime publication already — no migration needed.
Realtime + refetch is also the cheap substitute for the web's URL-matched optimistic upload tiles and their 12-second timeout fallback.

features.name: The Family Fest 2026 album shortcut
features.whatItDoes: Home and the Family Fest screens can drop you straight into the official fest album with one tap.
gotchas: FEST_ALBUM_BOX_ID = "0000fe57-2026-4000-8000-000000000001" and FEST_ALBUM_HREF = "/drop?box=0000fe57-2026-4000-8000-000000000001" (lib/data.ts). 0000fe57 = "fest", 2026 = the year. Hardcode the same constant in Swift so Home / fest-hub CTAs can deep-link straight in without a lookup.

The row is seeded by 0172_callout_drop_box_and_fest_album.sql as insert into drop_boxes (id, title, emoji, created_by) values ('0000fe57-…', 'Family Fest 2026: Ye Olde Family Feste', '🏰', coalesce(<oldest admin>, <oldest profile>)) on conflict (id) do nothing — owned to an admin because created_by is NOT NULL and a seed row has no personal author. Any admin can manage it anyway (canManage = isAdmin || created_by == me).
⚠️ Degrade gracefully to "This album isn't available." if the row is missing — that's the documented behavior and the web's exact copy, not an error state.
The wrap-phase "upload your photos" CTAs now point HERE, not at the Feed: "post your photos" means the shared downloadable album.
⚠️ The box id is a compile-time constant in the public web bundle, which is exactly why /dropbox-zip had to be tightened to approved members — don't treat knowing the id as authorization.

features.name: Start a new album
features.whatItDoes: Any member can make a new named album (with an emoji) for people to dump photos into.
rpcs: create_drop_box(p_title text, p_emoji text = null) → uuid
gotchas: Any signed-in member may create. Granted execute to authenticated.
⚠️ There are NO write policies on drop_boxes — a direct .insert() fails. Don't waste an hour on "why does my insert 403".
Returns a BARE JSON string uuid ("3f1c…") — decode as String then UUID(uuidString:), not as an object.
title is text NOT NULL (non-optional String in Swift); emoji is text NULL (String?); created_by defaults to auth.uid() and is NOT NULL.

Build the params dictionary as [String: AnyJSON] so nil encodes as JSON null with the key still present — a MISSING key changes PostgREST overload resolution, a null value does not. Get param names wrong and you get PGRST202 at runtime, not a compile error.

⚠️ Only add_drop_box_media carries revoke all … from public, anon (0173, carried through 0180) — the other six RPCs were granted in 0171 with no revoke and no migration revokes function execute from PUBLIC anywhere, so they technically keep Postgres's default PUBLIC grant. Nothing leaks (each raises without auth.uid() or a creator/admin match) — just don't repeat "anon is revoked" as if the SQL said it.
features.v1Cut: Creation can stay web-only for v1 — iOS uploads into albums that already exist, including the fixed fest album.

features.name: Rename an album or change its emoji
features.whatItDoes: The person who made an album (or an admin) can fix its name or swap its emoji.
rpcs: update_drop_box(p_box uuid, p_title text = null, p_emoji text = null) → void
gotchas: Allowed for the box creator OR an admin; raises otherwise, so handle the throw.

⚠️ p_title = null means "LEAVE THE TITLE ALONE" (coalesce(nullif(btrim(...),''), title)) — an empty/whitespace string also means leave it alone. So in Swift you cannot express "clear the title" (it's NOT NULL — correct).
⚠️ p_emoji = null means "leave the emoji alone"; p_emoji = "" CLEARS it. You must distinguish nil from "" when sending the emoji.
Send the params explicitly every time like the web does: {p_box, p_title: title ?? null, p_emoji: emoji ?? null}. A missing key changes overload resolution; a null value does not.
void-returning: empty body — call .execute() and don't decode.
No write policies on the table — this RPC is the only path.
features.v1Cut: Album management can stay web-only for v1.

features.name: Archive an album
features.whatItDoes: Tucks a finished album out of the live list without deleting anything in it.
gotchas: Creator or admin only; handle the throw.
archived_at is timestamptz NULL — non-nil means archived. RLS still RETURNS archived boxes, so the list must filter archivedAt != nil client-side like the web.

⚠️ You cannot add media to an archived album: add_drop_box_media rejects with "That folder is not available." when the box doesn't exist OR archived_at is not null. Hide/disable the upload affordance on an archived box, and still map that error message.
void-returning: empty body, call .execute().
features.v1Cut: Album management can stay web-only for v1.

features.name: Delete an album
features.whatItDoes: Removes an album and all the photo entries in it for good.
gotchas: Creator or admin only; handle the throw. void-returning — empty body, call .execute().
drop_box_media.box_id is ON DELETE CASCADE, so deleting a box deletes its media rows.

⚠️ Files on disk are NOT deleted by the RPC. The mini's orphan-sweep.js reconciles every 6h and quarantines what no row references, purging 7 days later — but it SKIPS any file whose mtime is inside a 48h grace window (ORPHAN_GRACE_HOURS, because the client inserts its media row after /upload returns), so a file deleted the day it was uploaded lingers ~48h before it's even quarantined.

⚠️ Historical: before that sweep existed, one hard-deleted drop box left 438 photos / ~558 MB stranded on disk forever. Don't add an iOS delete path that assumes files are gone immediately, and never assume a URL 404s just because its row is gone.
features.v1Cut: Album management can stay web-only for v1.

features.name: Select mode (pick several photos at once)
features.whatItDoes: A Select button turns the grid into checkboxes so you can act on a handful of photos at once instead of one at a time.
gotchas: The web's shape: a "Select" pill → checkable grid + a Download(N) / All / Cancel toolbar.
It exists to drive the zip download and batch delete — there's no other consumer, so shipping it without those is pointless.
Each selected item needs its ROOT-RELATIVE path for the zip POST (see the zip entry) — that's mediaRelPath() in DropBoxes.tsx, the substring after /f/ with the query stripped.
features.v1Cut: Omit Select mode entirely from v1 — the web can do the photo-book export.

features.name: Download a whole album (or a selection) as one zip
features.whatItDoes: Grabs every original file in an album — or just the ones you picked — as a single zip, for photo books and backups.
gotchas: Both routes stream straight from the system zip binary — nothing is buffered.

⚠️ Both routes now require an APPROVED member, not just a valid login (isApprovedMemberByToken). This was a real hole: the box id is a compile-time constant in the public web bundle (FEST_ALBUM_BOX_ID), so a stranger with a throwaway account could have streamed back the entire family album in one request. Unapproved → 403 {"error": "An admin needs to approve your account before you can download photos.", "pendingApproval": true}.

⚠️ Both routes accept Authorization: Bearer <jwt> as well as the query/body token (bearerToken(req) is the fallback in both handlers). The query/body form exists only because a browser <a download> or form submit can't set headers. FROM iOS, USE THE HEADER and don't put the JWT in a URL — it keeps a bearer token out of logs. Verified in media-server/server.js's app.get("/dropbox-zip") / app.post("/dropbox-zip").

⚠️ Each `path` field is the item's path relative to the media ROOT — everything after /f/, e.g. posts/2026-07/<uuid>.jpg. ROOT-relative, NOT box-relative, precisely so an album can include files stored elsewhere in the tree: a Feed photo referenced into an album physically lives under posts/, not dropbox/<box>/. For a freshly uploaded item the /upload response's `path` field is already exactly this string; for anything else take the substring after /f/ and strip the query (mediaRelPath() in DropBoxes.tsx). The server normalizes and rejects traversal, silently skipping any entry it can't resolve, and returns 400 "No files selected." if nothing resolved.

⚠️ Both modes zip the ORIGINALS, not the renditions — the explicit-path branch swaps each resolved entry for its _orig file when one exists (findOriginal(resolved) || resolved), exactly like ?dl=1. So a zip can be MUCH larger than the sum of the files the rows' URLs point at; size your progress/disk expectations off the originals.

The GET (no path list) mode enumerates dropbox/<box>/ on both volumes and unions them, grouping by stem so it zips neither the _thumb.jpg previews nor both copies of a video (original wins), and skips HLS fragments. It MISSES items referenced from elsewhere in the tree — which is why the web always sends the explicit path list, even for "Download all". Do the same: POST with every item's path, for both "All" and "Selection". That mode also has its own empty answer: 404 "Nothing to download yet.", not the 400 above.

⚠️ The POST body is parsed with express.urlencoded({ limit: "512kb" }). Each path is ~45–60 bytes, so a few thousand items fit, but a truly enormous album will 413 — chunk into multiple zips above ~5,000 items.

⚠️ The zip is streamed from zip's stdout so there is NO Content-Length — you cannot show a percentage. Use indeterminate progress and a background URLSession download task; these can be hundreds of MB. (The web can't even detect "started" and just holds a busy state for 2.5s.)
⚠️ The web's mechanism (hidden form → hidden iframe, so the browser saves natively without navigating away and without URL-length limits) does NOT transfer and should not be imitated.
/dropbox-zip shares the mini's 600 requests / 15 min per-IP limiter.
features.nativeOpportunity: Native gets a plain POST + streamed background download to disk — strictly better than the web's hidden-form/iframe hack — and can send the JWT as an Authorization header instead of putting it in the URL.
features.v1Cut: Omit /dropbox-zip entirely from v1 — the web can do the photo-book export, and a phone is a poor place to receive a 3 GB zip anyway.

features.name: Remove several photos at once
features.whatItDoes: With photos selected, removes all of them from the album in one go.
gotchas: There is no bulk RPC — it's remove_drop_box_media(p_media) per item, each gated to the item's uploader, the box creator, or an admin, so a mixed selection can partially fail. Handle per-item throws.
Requires Select mode to exist first.
Files are not deleted from disk by the RPC; orphan-sweep.js quarantines unreferenced files every 6h (purge 7 days later) and skips anything whose mtime is inside the 48h ORPHAN_GRACE_HOURS window.
features.v1Cut: Omit from v1 along with Select mode.

features.name: Crediting a photo to the person who took it
features.whatItDoes: When an admin files someone else's old Feed post into an album, the photo is still credited to the member who posted it, not to the admin who filed it.
rpcs: add_drop_box_media(p_box uuid, p_url text, p_type text, p_thumbnail_url text = null, p_captured_at timestamptz = null, p_captured_at_source text = null, p_credit_user_id uuid = null) → uuid
gotchas: ⚠️ The credit rule that surprised everyone: when a Feed post's photo is referenced into an album from the post editor's "also add to an album" checkbox, credit goes to the POST'S AUTHOR, not to whoever clicked the checkbox. The common case is an admin retroactively filing a member's old post into an album — it's still that member's photo.

p_credit_user_id is honored ONLY when the caller is an admin, the target is a real profiles row, and the id differs from the caller's own; a non-admin's value is silently ignored, so nobody can attribute an upload to someone else.

The web passes post.authorId from EditPostPanel (both for newly-added and already-posted kept media) and deliberately passes NOTHING from the composer's own alsoAlbum flow, because there the poster IS the caller.
For a v1 iOS album screen you will pass p_credit_user_id: nil everywhere — that's correct. Only wire it if you also build "add this post's photos to an album" from a post you may not own.

⚠️ The "fix only covers what happens next" lesson: 0180 corrected credit only for NEW adds. The live Family Fest album already had 41 rows mis-credited to whichever admin had clicked the checkbox before the feature existed, repaired with a one-off `update drop_box_media set uploaded_by = <post's author_id> …` joined on storage_path back to post_media/posts (after verifying no storage_path mapped to more than one distinct author). No migration — a data correction. Check for this shape whenever a new derived-from-a-post field ships.
features.v1Cut: Omit — with it, the post-composer "also add to an album" picker.

features.name: A Home call-out that opens an album
features.whatItDoes: An admin's Home card can carry a button that drops everyone straight into a specific album.
gotchas: home_callouts.drop_box_id is uuid NULL → drop_boxes(id) ON DELETE SET NULL (migration 0172) and lets an admin call-out deep-link into an album.
Low priority for v1 — but if you already render call-outs on iOS, honor this column (verify in the iOS repo whether home_callouts is rendered at all).
The target URL shape is the standard /drop?box=<uuid> deep link, so it reuses the same routing work.
Degrade to "This album isn't available." if the referenced row is gone.
features.v1Cut: Omit home_callouts.drop_box_id from v1.

features.name: The sign-up card with its list of slots
features.whatItDoes: Shows a Family Fest event's sign-up list — the times you can take, or a single "who's coming" bucket — with how many spots are left on each.
gotchas: `signup_enabled boolean not null default false` gates the whole card — don't render anything when it's false.
Mirror the web's guard: if the resolved slot list is EMPTY, render nothing at all (an interval event with no times configured yet).

Normalize all three modes into ONE SlotView list before rendering: `{ key: String, slotId: UUID?, slotStart: String?, label: String, capacity: Int? }` — it's the single thing that keeps the UI and the RPCs agreeing. key = "headcount" | slot uuid | "HH:MM".

⚠️ `capacity == 0` means "immediately full", and that is a real state users hit: `signup_capacity` defaults to NULL and in interval/slots mode NULL coalesces to 0, so an event where the organizer enabled sign-ups but never typed a per-slot number renders every slot as full. Show it as full (matching web) rather than inventing an unlimited fallback. Only headcount mode treats NULL as uncapped.
RLS read on `fest_schedule_items` is public — anyone, signed in or not, reads every row (`for select using (true)`, migration 0053). An empty result really means no data.
`fest_schedule_slots` read is public too (`using (true)`); `fest_schedule_signups` read is filtered by the 0167 policy — a short signup list is NOT a short slot, it's RLS filtering (see hide-names).

Almost everything is optional: capacity, day, end_time, label, slot_start, slot_id, user_id, added_by, team_id, team_name, signup_capacity, signup_slot_minutes, signup_start_time, signup_end_time, signup_team_size, signup_instructions. The only non-null-by-contract fields on a signup row are id, schedule_item_id, name, fields, created_at. Use Int?/String?/UUID? — don't force-unwrap.
Use `.convertFromSnakeCase` (or explicit CodingKeys) — every column is snake_case, and so are the keys INSIDE the p_team_members jsonb (`for_user`, not `p_for_user`).
`signup_fields` decodes to [SignupField]; treat missing/[] as "no custom columns". `fields` on a signup decodes to [String: String]; a missing key renders as "—"; decode nil → [:].
`tournament_enabled` (0147) is a separate feature, not covered here. `source_activity_id` is provenance from the 0141 activity merge.
Don't persist signup rows to disk: on a hide-names event the cached copy is exactly the spoiler you're supposed to be suppressing.
If you also support activities, keep TWO column lists — `team_id`/`team_name` don't exist there and asking for a nonexistent column fails the whole request.

features.name: Evenly spaced time slots computed from the event's window
features.whatItDoes: For an event like "12:00 to 16:00, 60 minutes each", it works out the slots (12:00, 13:00, 14:00, 15:00) instead of anyone having to list them.
rpcs: fest_schedule_slot_starts() — NOT client-callable, revoked from anon/authenticated
gotchas: ⚠️ This mirrors the Postgres function `fest_schedule_slot_starts()` exactly and MUST NOT DRIFT, because `sign_up_for_schedule_slot` validates `p_slot` against the SQL version and raises 'That time slot isn't available' on a mismatch.
Loop condition is `while t <= end - mins` — note the `<=`, and the last slot must END by `signup_end_time`.
Requires signupEnabled && signupSlotMinutes > 0 && both signupStartTime and signupEndTime present; otherwise return [] and the card renders nothing.
`signup_start_time`/`signup_end_time` are "HH:MM" text — parse the two integers (`p[0]*60 + p[1]`), no Date involved anywhere.
capacity = `event.signupCapacity ?? 0` (0 = immediately full — a real state, don't fake an unlimited fallback).
Matching rule for signups: `signup.slotId == nil && signup.slotStart == slotStart`.
Interval slots hang off the event's own `day`. An activity interval slot has no calendar day at all, so it never gets a reminder.
`fest_schedule_slot_starts(...)` and `fest_activity_slot_starts(...)` are revoked from anon/authenticated — not callable from a client, don't try.

features.name: Hand-picked slots with their own day and time
features.whatItDoes: Supports events whose slots are an arbitrary list — "Mon 10:50am, Wed 1:48pm" — each with its own day, time, label and number of spots.
gotchas: Only used when `signup_mode = 'slots'`. Columns: id, schedule_item_id (FK on delete cascade), day text (ISO "YYYY-MM-DD"; NULL ⇒ fall back to the event's own day), start_time text not null ("HH:MM"), end_time text (optional), label text (optional override for the auto "day · time" label), capacity int (NULL ⇒ fall back to the event's signup_capacity), position int not null default 0, created_at, source_activity_slot_id.
Order by `day` (nulls first) then `start_time` — that's exactly what the web query does. `position` exists but is NOT used for ordering.
capacity = `slot.capacity ?? (event.signupCapacity ?? 0)`.

⚠️ The web keeps `slotStart = slot.startTime` on these views (it is NOT nil) and nils it at the RPC boundary instead — every call site sends `slotStart: view.slotId != nil ? nil : view.slotStart`. Do the same: `p_slot` and `p_slot_id` must NEVER both be non-null.
Matching rule: `signup.slotId == slot.id`.

⚠️ Writes are three separate RLS policies, all gated to `_can_manage_item_signups(schedule_item_id)` — a plain table write from the client, no RPC. Two failure shapes: an INSERT you're not allowed raises Postgres 42501 ("new row violates row-level security policy"), while an UPDATE/DELETE you're not allowed is SILENT (row filtered out, zero rows change). Either way it means "you're not the organizer/lead/crew" — check the affected-row count, don't just check for an error.
`day` is plain text here (not a date column) — keep it as String, see the date-labels entry.

features.name: Just a headcount — "who's coming", no times
features.whatItDoes: For events with no time slots at all: a running count of everyone who's coming, optionally capped.
rpcs: sign_up_for_schedule_slot(p_item uuid, p_slot text default null, p_for_user uuid default null, p_name text default null, p_slot_id uuid default null, p_fields jsonb default '{}', p_team_members jsonb default null, p_team_name text default null) returns uuid
gotchas: Exactly ONE SlotView: `slotId = nil`, `slotStart = nil`, `label = ""` (the card's own "Sign up" heading covers it), `capacity = signupCapacity` — which MAY BE NIL ⇒ uncapped, never "full". Headcount is the only mode where NULL capacity means no cap.
Matching rule: `slotId == nil && slotStart == nil`.
Signing up sends NEITHER p_slot nor p_slot_id ⇒ the headcount bucket; the RPC raises 'This event needs a time slot' if the event isn't actually in headcount mode.
Headcount is schedule-events ONLY (0143) — the activity check constraint allows only ('interval','slots'), so an activity can never receive "headcount".

⚠️ Dedup for headcount mode has NO unique index backing it (the 0135 index keys on slot_start, and NULLs are distinct in Postgres) — only the RPC's explicit check. Don't infer "already signed up" from a constraint violation; read the raised message.
No time dimension at all — don't render a time label for this bucket.
The manual notify button reads "🔔 Notify everyone" instead of "🔔 Notify this slot" in this mode.

features.name: The organizer's note above the slots
features.whatItDoes: Shows the free-text instructions the organizer wrote ("bring your own apron") right above the list of slots.
gotchas: `signup_instructions text` — nullable free text shown above the slots. Render nothing when it's nil/empty.

features.name: Slot days and times labeled correctly
features.whatItDoes: Makes sure a slot that's Friday at 9:00 AM says Friday at 9:00 AM everywhere — not the day before.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ INCIDENT, verbatim: every sign-up slot was LABELED A DAY EARLY across the whole fest UI — the reminders were right, the labels were wrong (fixed by migration 0168 + a one-line lib/format.ts fix). Members reported "our slot was yesterday but the reminder came this morning". The cron was never at fault. The bug was `formatDate()` doing a bare `new Date(input)`: a "YYYY-MM-DD" string parses as UTC MIDNIGHT, which renders as the PREVIOUS day in any negative-offset zone (Central). A slot stored 2026-07-31 09:00 displayed as "Thu, Jul 30 · 9:00 AM" everywhere — including the Planner's own day dropdown, so every surface agreed with itself and nothing revealed the truth until the reminder fired off the real stored date, server-side.

⚠️ And the stored DATA was shifted too, needing a separate one-off correction (no migration): the day dropdown's <option> LABEL came from formatDate while its VALUE was the true ISO day, so picking the option that read "Thu, Jul 30" persisted 2026-07-31. The label was self-consistent (weekday AND date both named Thursday the 30th), so no screen could reveal it. Corrected with `update fest_schedule_slots set day = (day::date - 1)::text where day is not null` — 10 rows hand-corrected. TAKEAWAY: a display bug in a PICKER silently corrupts the data it writes; when fixing a date-formatting bug always check whether the bad label was also feeding a form.

⚠️ The Swift equivalents are WORSE: `JSONDecoder` with `.dateDecodingStrategy = .iso8601` THROWS on "2026-07-31" (it wants a full date-time). A Date-typed `day` property doesn't mislabel — it FAILS THE WHOLE DECODE, taking the event down. KEEP `day` AS `String` in your Codable models — both `fest_schedule_items.day` (a `date` column PostgREST serializes as "2026-07-31") and `fest_schedule_slots.day` (plain text).

⚠️ `ISO8601DateFormatter()` defaults to `timeZone = GMT`. With `formatOptions = [.withFullDate]` it happily parses "2026-07-31" → UTC midnight; render that Date with any DateFormatter in `.current` and a Central device prints "Thu, Jul 30" — the exact JS bug, reproduced.

FIX: parse and format in the SAME time zone, in ONE helper — never inline `Date(...)` at a call site. Use a FestDay enum: DateFormatter with calendar .gregorian, locale en_US_POSIX, timeZone TimeZone(identifier: "America/Chicago"), dateFormat "yyyy-MM-dd" for parsing, and a formatter pinned to the SAME zone with setLocalizedDateFormatFromTemplate("EEE, MMM d") for the label. (The web's own fix parses at device-local midnight — same-zone-in/same-zone-out is what actually matters; pinning to Central additionally makes labels match the server's reminder wording for a member travelling out of zone.)

⚠️ `start_time` / `end_time` / `slot_start` are wall-clock "HH:MM" strings with NO date and NO zone. Do NOT build a Date to display them — parse the two integers and format 12-hour ("09:00" → "9:00 AM") the way `formatTime()` does. Constructing a Date from them is how a second off-by-one gets in.

If you ever compute a slot's absolute instant (to sort, or to show "starts in…"), build it from DateComponents with `timeZone = America/Chicago` so you match `run_signup_reminders()`'s `at time zone 'America/Chicago'` exactly. Don't use the device zone.

If you build ANY day picker, derive the option's label from the SAME helper that produces the value you write, and write the raw ISO string — not a re-formatted round-trip of the label. That's the corruption path above.
Anytime rows park a MEANINGLESS date in `day` — ignore it and render "Anytime all week".

VERIFY ON DEVICE BEFORE SHIPPING: whether `fest_schedule_items.day` comes back as "2026-07-31" (a date column) versus "2026-07-31T00:00:00" from your client library's serializer — the helper above handles the bare form; a full timestamp needs the other branch. It's one print statement, and it's the difference between correct labels and the incident above.

features.name: Take a slot for yourself
features.whatItDoes: Lets a signed-in member tap a slot and put their own name in it.
rpcs: sign_up_for_schedule_slot(p_item uuid, p_slot text default null, p_for_user uuid default null, p_name text default null, p_slot_id uuid default null, p_fields jsonb default '{}', p_team_members jsonb default null, p_team_name text default null) returns uuid — the FIRST inserted row's id
gotchas: ⚠️ Supabase RPC args are keyed BY NAME; a wrong key is a runtime failure, not a compile error.
`p_for_user` and `p_name` both null/empty ⇒ the row is for the CALLER. That's the self-join path.
Exactly one of `p_slot` / `p_slot_id` / neither. Neither ⇒ headcount bucket (raises 'This event needs a time slot' if the event isn't in headcount mode). Send `p_slot` ONLY when slotId == nil.
⚠️ Send `null`, NOT `[]`, for `p_team_members` on an individual sign-up — the check is `is not null and jsonb_array_length(...) > 0`, so [] also works, but null is what the web sends.

Server-enforced, all raising user-facing strings: one linked member per slot → 'Already signed up'; capacity → 'Not enough spots left' (checked once for the whole team, atomically); every entry in `signup_fields` must be non-empty → 'Please fill in "<label>"'.
All these RPCs are SECURITY DEFINER, revoked from `anon`, granted to `authenticated` — a guest gets a permission error, so prompt sign-in BEFORE calling.
The `mine` check that hides the "+ Join this slot" affordance keys on `userId` ONLY (not addedBy, not canManage).
Refetch after the call rather than mutating a local array — capacity is contested.

features.name: Sign someone else up (a member, or a name with no account)
features.whatItDoes: Lets any signed-in member fill a slot for someone else — picking a family member from the app, or just typing a name for a relative who isn't on it.
rpcs: sign_up_for_schedule_slot(p_item uuid, p_slot text default null, p_for_user uuid default null, p_name text default null, p_slot_id uuid default null, p_fields jsonb default '{}', p_team_members jsonb default null, p_team_name text default null) returns uuid
gotchas: ANY signed-in member may add anyone, and several people — migration 0136 deliberately DROPPED the organizer gate. Don't gate this on canManage.

`p_for_user` links a member and their `display_name` is snapshotted server-side into `name`. `p_name` is a typed-in, account-less name (`user_id` null). `name text not null` — always present either way.
`user_id` is an FK → profiles with `on delete SET NULL`, so the name snapshot survives a deleted account.
`added_by` records who created the row and it matters three ways: removal rights, own-entry passthrough on a hide-names event, and who receives the reminder (`coalesce(user_id, added_by)`).
One linked member per slot → 'Already signed up'. A typed name has no such dedup.
The member picker is over `profiles`.

⚠️ "Is this mine?" is the plain session uid — no preview indirection. `IdentityProvider` exposes an `effectiveUserId` (admins can preview-as a member) but this feature's component deliberately uses plain `userId`, so a plain session uid is correct on iOS too.

features.name: Extra questions the organizer requires on each person
features.whatItDoes: When the organizer asked for extra info — like "Character" for a play — each person's sign-up collects and shows it.
gotchas: `signup_fields jsonb not null default '[]'` — an ORDERED array of `[{ "id": "...", "label": "..." }, …]`. Decode to [SignupField]; treat missing/[] as "no custom columns" and skip the extra form inputs.

Per-person values live in `fest_schedule_signups.fields jsonb not null default '{}'` keyed by FIELD ID: `{ "<field id>": "<value>" }`. Decode to [String: String], nil → [:]; a missing key renders as "—".
The RPC enforces every defined field is non-empty and raises 'Please fill in "<label>"' (e.g. 'Please fill in "Character"') — surface it verbatim.
In a team sign-up each member object inside `p_team_members` carries its OWN `"fields"` object.
Field ids and labels are separate — never key values off the label.

features.name: Signing up as a pair or team
features.whatItDoes: For events run in fixed-size teams (baggo doubles), one sign-up collects everyone on the team at once and keeps them together.
rpcs: sign_up_for_schedule_slot(p_item uuid, p_slot text default null, p_for_user uuid default null, p_name text default null, p_slot_id uuid default null, p_fields jsonb default '{}', p_team_members jsonb default null, p_team_name text default null) returns uuid
gotchas: `signup_team_size int` — null/1 = individual; e.g. 2 = sign up in pairs. It applies in ANY mode, not just headcount.

⚠️ `p_team_members` is a jsonb ARRAY OF OBJECTS whose keys are snake_case and are NOT the p_ params: `[{ "for_user": "<uuid|null>", "name": "<string|null>", "fields": { "<id>": "<value>" } }, …]`. Getting these keys wrong is a runtime failure, not a compile error.

When non-empty the function generates ONE `team_id` and inserts every member sharing it, plus `p_team_name` (trimmed, nulled if blank). When null/empty you get the original single-row path from p_for_user/p_name/p_fields.
Send `null`, not `[]`, for an individual sign-up (the check is `is not null and jsonb_array_length(...) > 0`).
Capacity math is a plain people-count — a team of 2 consumes 2 seats — and the single capacity check covers the whole team ATOMICALLY, raising 'Not enough spots left'.
Group signups by `team_id` for display (a "🤝 {team name}" sub-heading over its members); `team_name` is optional.

⚠️ Teams are schedule-events ONLY — the activity RPC has no team params and PostgREST answers `PGRST202 function not found`, which reads like a missing migration. The web guards this by only spreading the team params when `kind === "schedule"`.
The roster sheet gets a "Team" column only when signupTeamSize > 1.
features.v1Cut: Omit teams entirely — render "sign up on the web" when `signup_team_size > 1` rather than silently signing up one person into a team slot. Also omit the team grouping display and the roster sheet's Team column.

features.name: Taking a name back off a slot
features.whatItDoes: Lets you remove a sign-up you made — your own, or one you entered for someone else — and lets the organizer remove any of them.
gotchas: Raises 'You can only remove a sign-up you added' unless you are the row's `user_id`, its `added_by`, or a manager. Surface the message verbatim.

The remove-affordance rule is `s.userId == uid || s.addedBy == uid || canManage`. Keep the comparison sites in ONE place — the comparison appears three times with DIFFERENT rules: the row ✕ (all three), the manager self-hiding filter (`userId` OR `addedBy`, no canManage), and the `mine` check that hides "+ Join this slot" (`userId` only).
`fest_schedule_signups` has NO insert/update/delete policy at all — every write goes through the SECURITY DEFINER RPCs.
Refetch after removal rather than mutating a local array.
Guests get a permission error (revoked from anon) — prompt sign-in first.

features.name: Surprise sign-ups: accurate count, hidden names
features.whatItDoes: For events where the lineup is a surprise (a variety show), everyone sees how many people are signed up but not who — including the organizer, until they choose to peek.
rpcs: fest_schedule_signup_counts(p_item uuid) returns table(slot_start text, slot_id uuid, cnt bigint)
gotchas: ⚠️ RLS read (0167 — read carefully): a row comes back if `user_id = auth.uid()` OR `added_by = auth.uid()` OR the parent event has `signup_hide_names = false` OR you can manage the event's sign-ups. So on a hidden event a plain member's `select` returns ONLY THEIR OWN ROWS — `signups.count` is NOT the headcount, and a short list is not a short slot.

Get the real count from `fest_schedule_signup_counts(p_item:)` — a SECURITY DEFINER RPC that counts every row regardless of RLS. It returns one row per (slot_start, slot_id) group; aggregate into the same key space as SlotView.key: `key = slot_id?.uuidString ?? slot_start ?? "headcount"`, summing cnt.
Only fetch it when names are hidden AND the viewer can't manage (that's the web's `namesHidden` condition).
⚠️ It's granted to `authenticated` only, so a signed-out viewer of a hidden event gets NO count — the web falls back to 0 there; match that rather than showing an error.

⚠️ The organizer defaults to hiding it FROM THEMSELVES too. RLS lets a manager's fetch through in full, but the UI must not render those names until the manager taps a deliberate "👀 Show participants" (which flips to "🙈 Hide again"). The reveal is PER-MOUNT ONLY, never persisted — navigating away and back starts hidden again, on purpose.
The "📋 View all" roster sheet is governed by the same flag and the same button.

YOUR OWN ENTRY ALWAYS RENDERS, hidden or not — for a manager that means client-side filtering their otherwise-full fetch down to groups where some member has `user_id == uid` OR `added_by == uid` (so a typed-in name the manager personally entered for someone without an account also shows), with a "+N more hidden…" note for the rest. Seeing what YOU entered was never the spoiler.
Don't persist signup rows to disk — on a hide-names event the cached copy is exactly the spoiler you're suppressing.
Hide-names is schedule-events ONLY — not mirrored to fest_activities.
A hidden card shows a "🙈 who's signed up is a surprise" style hint in place of the roster.
features.v1Cut: If `signup_hide_names` is true, render only the counts-RPC total and NO names at all — that's correct behavior, just less featureful. Omit the manager reveal toggle and the own-entry passthrough filtering.

features.name: "View all" — the organizer's full roster table
features.whatItDoes: Gives the person running the event one scannable table of every slot, everyone in it, and their answers to the extra questions.
gotchas: Button is "📋 View all", shown to canManage viewers — every slot × person × custom column as one scannable table.
A "Team" column appears only when `signupTeamSize > 1`.
The roster sheet has NO per-row permission check at all; it's gated wholesale by `canManage && !managerHiding`.
On a `signup_hide_names` event it stays hidden until the manager taps "👀 Show participants" (same button that governs inline names).
Custom-column values come from each row's `fields` jsonb keyed by field id; a missing key renders as "—".

features.name: "Notify this slot" — nudge everyone signed up, right now
features.whatItDoes: Lets the person running an event send everyone in a slot an immediate reminder, with an optional email as well.
rpcs: send_signup_slot_reminder_now(p_kind text, p_item uuid, p_slot_id uuid, p_slot_start text, p_minutes int default null, p_email boolean default false) returns int
gotchas: Button is "🔔 Notify this slot" (or "🔔 Notify everyone" in headcount mode), shown to canManage viewers and ONLY once at least one person is signed up for that slot.

Call shape: `p_kind: "schedule"`, `p_item: item.id`, `p_slot_id: view.slotId`, `p_slot_start: view.slotId != nil ? nil : view.slotStart` (mutually exclusive), `p_minutes: nil`, `p_email: emailToo`. Returns Int, shown as "✓ Sent to N people".

⚠️ DO NOT build a lead-time picker. It used to offer chips ("starts in 30 minutes") whose label became the notification body VERBATIM, with zero connection to the slot's stored time — so a coordinator clicking the wrong chip or the wrong slot's button told members a lead time a full day off, undetectable from the message. 0165/0168 made the RPC resolve and state the slot's real day+time via the shared `_format_slot_when(timestamptz)`. There is nothing left to pick: one "Send reminder" button.
⚠️ Passing a non-null `p_minutes` only reintroduces the wrong wording as a fallback (it's used only when no real instant resolves) AND changes the email dedup key. Always send nil.

⚠️ The returned int counts one per signed-up ROW that has someone to notify (`coalesce(user_id, added_by)`), NOT per distinct human — a coordinator who wrote in three account-less guests is the recipient of three of those sends, so N can exceed the number of people. The web still labels it "people"; don't treat N as a distinct-person count.

The email half is QUEUED, not sent inline — the RPC inserts into `fest_reminder_emails` and the mac mini's `alert-mailer.js` claims it. Nothing for iOS beyond passing `p_email`. The checkbox reads "Also email anyone signed up with an account".
`fest_reminder_emails` and `fest_signup_reminders_sent` both have RLS enabled with ZERO policies — deliberately unreadable and unwritable from any client. iOS never touches them.
This send doesn't touch the automatic-reminder dedup ledger, so it can't collide with the cron.

features.name: Tapping a slot reminder opens that event
features.whatItDoes: The automatic "your slot starts soon" push already reaches phones — tapping it needs to land on that event's sign-up card.
gotchas: Automatic reminders (0140 + 0168, pg_cron, every minute) are NOTHING FOR IOS TO BUILD — the organizer picks lead times in `signup_reminder_minutes` and the cron fires a `signup_reminder` notification per (signup, lead-time), deduped via `fest_signup_reminders_sent`.
⚠️ The only iOS work: `signup_reminder`'s deep link is `/family-fest/schedule/<item id>` — make sure your notification router handles that path (or maps it to the native screen).

`signup_reminder` is a normal, DEFAULT-ON notification and push category (0159), already in both mini senders' pushable sets (`push-sender.js` and `apns-sender.js`) — it reaches iOS through the existing APNs relay with NO new wiring.
Recipient is `coalesce(user_id, added_by)` — a coordinator who wrote in a guest gets the nudge, worded "{guest}'s … slot starts …".
Only fires for slots with a real day+time; an activity interval slot has no calendar day and is skipped.

The body states the resolved instant: "…starts in 30 minutes — Fri, Jul 31 at 9:00 AM." It resolves the instant as `(day || ' ' || start_time)::timestamp at time zone 'America/Chicago'` — match that zone if you ever compute the same thing client-side.
`run_signup_reminders()` and `signup_reminder_email_recipients(...)` are revoked from anon/authenticated — don't try to call them.
features.nativeOpportunity: The push already relays to iOS via the existing APNs sender with zero backend or sender changes — only the deep-link route needs handling, so this is the cheapest win in the area.

features.name: Knowing who counts as "the organizer"
features.whatItDoes: Decides who sees the organizer-only buttons — the fest committee, plus the event's own lead and crew.
rpcs: _can_manage_item_signups(p_item_id uuid) — granted to authenticated but the web never calls it
_can_manage_activity_item_signups(p_activity_id uuid) — granted to authenticated but the web never calls it
gotchas: Compute it client-side exactly the way the web does: `canManage = canEditFest || (uid != nil && (event.leadUserId == uid || (event.crewUserIds ?? []).contains(uid!)))` — reading `fest_schedule_items.lead_user_id uuid` and `crew_user_ids uuid[] not null default '{}'`.
`canEditFest` comes from the RPC `can_edit_fest()` (no params, returns boolean) — it's `profiles.is_admin` OR a `committee_roster` row with `committee_slug = 'family-fest'` linked to you.
Cache it — the web keys a persisted cache on the uid (`canEditFest.<uid>`) so the Edit affordances don't flicker in.
⚠️ `can_edit_fest()` is revoked from anon, so a signed-out call comes back as a PERMISSION ERROR, not `false` — treat any error as false, which is what the web's wrapper does.
This is UI-ONLY. Every server-side check re-runs the same predicate, so a wrong client answer grants nothing.
`_can_manage_item_signups(p_item_id uuid)` / `_can_manage_activity_item_signups(p_activity_id uuid)` ARE granted to authenticated, but the web never calls them — don't add a round-trip.

features.name: Guests can look, but get asked to sign in to sign up
features.whatItDoes: Someone browsing without an account still sees the sign-up card, and gets a friendly sign-in prompt the moment they try to take a slot.
gotchas: Reads (section 2 of the spec) are PUBLIC, so a guest can still SEE the card — render it.
⚠️ Every RPC in this feature is SECURITY DEFINER, `revoke`d from `anon`, and `grant execute … to authenticated` — a guest gets a PERMISSION ERROR, so prompt sign-in BEFORE calling any of them.
'Sign in required' is one of the user-facing strings the sign-up RPC itself can raise — surface it verbatim if it slips through.
`can_edit_fest()` errors (not returns false) for a signed-out caller — treat any error as false.
`fest_schedule_signup_counts` is authenticated-only, so a signed-out viewer of a hide-names event gets no count — fall back to 0, don't show an error.

features.name: Plain-English errors shown as-is
features.whatItDoes: When a sign-up can't go through, the member reads the real reason ("Not enough spots left") instead of "Something went wrong".
rpcs: sign_up_for_activity_slot(p_item uuid, p_slot text, p_for_user uuid, p_name text, p_slot_id uuid, p_fields jsonb)
gotchas: RPC errors ARE the user-facing prose. Surface `PostgrestError.message` directly in an inline error row — do not map to a generic "Something went wrong".

The SCHEDULE RPCs raise: 'Not enough spots left' (capacity), 'Already signed up' (duplicate linked member), 'Please fill in "Character"', 'That time slot isn't available', 'This event needs a time slot', 'This event isn't taking sign-ups', 'You can only remove a sign-up you added', 'Sign in required'.

⚠️ The ACTIVITY RPCs word two of them differently — 'That time slot is full' and 'Already signed up for that slot' (0138 predates 0143's rewording and was never updated) — so NEVER branch on the message text; just display it.
A wrong RPC arg key is a runtime failure, not a compile error, and surfaces as an error here — don't swallow it.
A disallowed slot UPDATE/DELETE is SILENT (zero rows changed, no error) — check affected-row counts there instead of relying on an error message.

features.name: Spot counts stay honest after every action
features.whatItDoes: Refreshes the slot list right after anyone signs up or backs out, so nobody is shown an open spot that's already gone.
gotchas: No `localStorage`/SWR-cache idiom transfers. The web wraps most reads in a stale-while-revalidate cache, but `ScheduleSignupSlots` deliberately does NOT: it fetches on mount and RE-FETCHES AFTER EVERY MUTATION (`reload()`), because capacity is contested and a stale count shows a full slot as open. Do the same — refetch after sign-up/remove rather than mutating a local array.
Don't persist signup rows to disk: on a hide-names event the cached copy is exactly the spoiler you're supposed to be suppressing.

Realtime is AVAILABLE BUT UNUSED — `fest_schedule_signups`, `fest_schedule_slots`, `fest_activity_signups`, `fest_activity_slots` are all in the `supabase_realtime` publication, so you CAN subscribe, but the web doesn't and refetch-on-action is simpler and sufficient. Skip it in v1.

features.name: "📝 Sign up" button on a Home call-out
features.whatItDoes: A Home call-out card can carry a Sign up button that drops you straight onto that event's sign-up card.
gotchas: `home_callouts.signup_item_id text` (0137) — a `fest_schedule_items` id stored as TEXT, not an FK.

⚠️ A non-null id is NOT enough on its own: the picker was later widened past 0137's signup-only list (a callout can link any fest item just to borrow its photo/details), so the web resolves the linked item's `signup_enabled` and only shows the button when it's true (`showSignup = signupItemId && signupEnabled` in `CalloutCard`). Match that or you'll render a Sign up button onto a card with no sign-up.
Only relevant if iOS renders Home callouts at all.
The deep link target is the same path the reminder push uses — reuse one router entry.

features.name: "Anytime all week" reads the rows the family actually edits
