features.whatItDoes: Moves the Anytime section (scavenger hunt, merch table) onto the same events the family edits on the web, so it stops showing stale copies.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ iOS IS CURRENTLY READING THE RETIRED TABLE. Migration 0141 converted every `fest_activities` row into an ANYTIME `fest_schedule_items` row (carrying its sign-up config, slots and signups; provenance in `source_activity_id` / `source_activity_slot_id` / `source_activity_signup_id`) and the web stopped rendering and creating activities.

Precisely: `fetchFestContent` still SELECTS the `fest_activities` rows, and `fetchActivityDrafts` / `updateActivityDetails` / the Planner's `ActivityEditor`+`ActivitySheet` still exist in source — but nothing mounts them, so it's unreachable dead code and no web surface shows that data.

The table and rows were left in place ONLY because the native app still reads them for its "Anytime" section. ⚠️ The two have been FREE TO DRIFT ever since — a web edit to a converted event does not touch the untouched activity row.
Build sign-ups against `fest_schedule_items` ONLY. You then get all three modes, teams, and hide-names for free, and you're reading the rows the family actually edits.

Move the iOS "Anytime" section onto `fest_schedule_items` where `anytime = true` (migration 0139 — a BOOLEAN FLAG, deliberately not a nullable `day`, so `day` stays NOT NULL and every date formatter stays safe). Anytime rows park a MEANINGLESS date in `day` — ignore it and render "Anytime all week".
This is a CLIENT change, not a migration — the rows are already there.
If you ship activity-backed sign-ups instead, you inherit a dead-end: no headcount, no teams, no hide-names, and a roster nobody on web can see.
features.v1Cut: Ship the read-side switch only: point the Anytime section at `fest_schedule_items where anytime = true` and render "Anytime all week". Leave the old `fest_activities` code paths in place (unused) rather than deleting them in the same pass, and don't attempt to reconcile drifted rows.

features.name: Sign-ups on the older "activity" rows (only if you must)
features.whatItDoes: Makes sign-ups also work against the retired activities data, for any screen still backed by it.
rpcs: sign_up_for_activity_slot(p_item uuid, p_slot text, p_for_user uuid, p_name text, p_slot_id uuid, p_fields jsonb) returns uuid
gotchas: ⚠️ Schedule events and activities are PARALLEL, ISOLATED implementations — nothing is shared: separate config columns, separate child tables (`fest_activity_slots.activity_id`, `fest_activity_signups.activity_id`), separate RPCs, separate manage predicates.

The activity sign-up RPC has 6 params and NO team support. ⚠️ Do NOT send `p_team_members`/`p_team_name` — that overload does not exist and PostgREST answers `PGRST202 function not found`, which reads like a missing migration. The web guards this by only spreading the team params when `kind === "schedule"`.
No headcount mode (the check constraint allows only ('interval','slots')), no teams (the columns don't exist), no hide-names, no counts RPC.
Two error strings are worded differently: 'That time slot is full' (capacity) and 'Already signed up for that slot' (duplicate) — never branch on message text, just display it.
The web deliberately selects a NARROWER column list for activities (`team_id`/`team_name` don't exist) — asking for a nonexistent column fails the whole request, so keep two column lists.
Activities have no day of their own, so interval-mode slots there are time-only and get NO automatic reminders.

The web abstracts the pair with a single `kind: "schedule" | "activity"` plus a lookup table of names (`SOURCES` in lib/scheduleSignups.ts) — do the same in Swift (an enum with computed table/RPC names) rather than two copies of the UI.
Recommended path is to NOT ship this — see the anytime/fest_schedule_items entry.

features.name: Setting up a sign-up (the organizer's configuration)
features.whatItDoes: Lets the person running an event turn sign-ups on and choose how they work — slots or headcount, spots per slot, times, instructions, extra questions, reminder lead times, team size, and whether names are hidden.
gotchas: Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for a first pass — leave it on web; organizers already use the Planner there.

The columns it edits: `signup_enabled`, `signup_capacity`, `signup_slot_minutes`, `signup_start_time`, `signup_end_time`, `signup_mode` (check in ('interval','slots','headcount')), `signup_instructions`, `signup_fields`, `signup_reminder_minutes int[]` (e.g. {1440,60,15}), `signup_reminder_email`, `signup_team_size`, `signup_hide_names`.
⚠️ `signup_capacity` left blank means capacity 0 in interval/slots mode — immediately full. If you ever build this, make that consequence visible in the editor.

⚠️ If you build ANY day picker here, derive the option's label from the SAME helper that produces the value you write, and write the raw ISO string — a display bug in a picker silently corrupts the data it writes (the 10-row day-shift incident).
Do NOT add a manual-notify lead-time picker (see the manual notify entry) — that affordance was deliberately removed.
Headcount mode and team size are schedule-only; activities keep exactly the interval/slots choice.
features.v1Cut: Ship nothing here in v1 — leave all configuration on web. If a slice is unavoidable, edit only `signup_capacity` and `signup_instructions` on an existing event, and never expose a day picker or a mode switch.

features.name: Adding, editing and deleting individual slots
features.whatItDoes: Lets the organizer add a slot, change how many people fit in one, or delete it.
gotchas: Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for a first pass — leave it on web.

⚠️⚠️ Deleting and re-adding a slot CASCADE-DELETES everyone already signed up for it (`schedule_item_id` FK on delete cascade) — exactly the kind of footgun you don't want to ship on day one. The web's answer is `updateScheduleSlotCapacity`'s edit-in-place instead.
Writes are plain table inserts/updates/deletes (NO RPC), governed by three separate RLS policies all gated to `_can_manage_item_signups(schedule_item_id)`.

⚠️ Two failure shapes: a disallowed INSERT RAISES Postgres 42501; a disallowed UPDATE/DELETE is SILENT (row filtered out, zero rows change). Check the affected-row count, don't just check for an error.

`day` is nullable text ("YYYY-MM-DD"); NULL ⇒ the event's own day. `capacity` nullable ⇒ the event's `signup_capacity`. `label` optional overrides the auto "day · time" label. `position int not null default 0` exists but isn't used for ordering.
⚠️ Any day picker must write the raw ISO string derived from the same helper that renders its label — the picker-corrupts-data incident.
features.v1Cut: Leave slot CRUD on web entirely. If anything ships, allow editing an existing slot's capacity in place (the `updateScheduleSlotCapacity` equivalent) and never expose add or delete.

features.name: Tournament section shows up on an activity
features.whatItDoes: When someone turns on tournaments for an activity, a Tournament area appears on that activity's page — and nowhere else.
gotchas: `tournament_enabled` is a column on `fest_schedule_items` (migration 0147) and on `private_activities` (0150) — it does NOT exist on `fest_activities`. The iOS "Anytime" section reads `fest_activities`, which can never host a tournament. Tournaments only ever hang off `fest_schedule_items`.

If the iOS schedule model doesn't currently select `fest_schedule_items.tournament_enabled`, add it (`boolean not null default false`, public-read like the rest of that table) — and only render the tournament section when it's true, so the section never appears on non-tournament activities.

Only mount on a real DB row. Family Fest has in-code seed schedule events whose ids are slugs (`"ye-olde-family-faire"`), not uuids. Web guards with a uuid regex before mounting anything, because `.eq("schedule_item_id", "ye-olde-...")` is a type error against a uuid column. Guard the same way (`UUID(uuidString:) != nil`).

A fest activity can hold MORE THAN ONE tournament. Only private activities are capped (migration 0151's partial unique index `tournaments_one_per_activity`, plus an idempotent `create_activity_tournament`). There is NO equivalent guard on `schedule_item_id` — repeated `create_tournament` taps on a fest activity really do stack duplicate rows. Fetch a list and render a card per row, like web does; do not `.single()`.
Fetch is `.eq("schedule_item_id", id)` or `.eq("private_activity_id", id)` accordingly, ordered by `created_at` ascending.
Guests (no session) get nothing; web renders a "Sign in to see the bracket and scores" card in place of the section.

features.name: Bracket data loads and reads in the right order
features.whatItDoes: The players, teams, games and bracket all load for a tournament and show up in the order a person expects.
gotchas: These four tables have SELECT policies ONLY — there is no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE policy on any of them. A direct `INSERT` from Swift fails with `42501`; a direct `UPDATE`/`DELETE` matches zero rows and returns SUCCESS WITH AN EMPTY ARRAY — the worst possible failure mode. Never write to these tables from the client; all writes go through `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs.

⚠️⚠️ THE ONE QUERY YOU MUST GET RIGHT: `tournaments` has TWO foreign-key relationships to `tournament_entrants` — the child FK (`tournament_entrants.tournament_id`) and `tournaments_winner_fk` (`tournaments.winner_entrant_id → tournament_entrants.id`). PostgREST can't pick one, so an unqualified embed returns HTTP 300 / `PGRST201` "more than one relationship found" and the ENTIRE fetch fails with no obvious cause. The child FK must be named: `*,tournament_entrants!tournament_entrants_tournament_id_fkey(*),tournament_matches(*),tournament_participants(*)`. If a Swift decode comes back empty for a tournament you know exists, check the HTTP status for 300 before anything else.
Recommended for iOS: FOUR SEPARATE FLAT QUERIES filtered by `tournament_id`, assembled locally — equally correct and it sidesteps the embed ambiguity entirely.

Ordering the server does NOT do for you (mirror web's `assemble()` exactly or the bracket looks scrambled): entrants sort by `seed` ascending with NULLS LAST, then `position`; matches sort by `round`, then `position`; an entrant's members are the participants with that `entrant_id` sorted by `position`; the pool is participants with `entrant_id == nil` sorted by `position`.

`round` ALWAYS starts at 1 — there is no round 0. The 0144 schema comment says "0 = play-in" but that convention is never used: both `generate_bracket` and `_tournament_build_bracket` loop `for r in 1 .. v_r`, and a play-in game is a ROUND-1 row with `is_play_in = true`. Do not build a "Round 0 = play-in" pager stage.
`tournament_matches.status` `in_progress` is in the CHECK constraint but NO RPC ever sets it — decode it, never expect it.
`reminder_minutes` is NOT NULL with a `{}` default, so decode as `[Int]` — but still coerce `nil → []` (`decodeIfPresent(...) ?? []`) like the web seam does, to survive a pre-0148 row.
`ready_notified` is server bookkeeping — never render it.

`tournament_participants.entrant_id` null = this person is in the PRE-TEAM POOL (not yet on a bracket unit). `user_id` null = an account-less typed-in name (the linked-or-typed idiom, migration 0143); `on delete set null` on `user_id` means the name snapshot survives if that member deletes their account.

`tournament_entrants.withdrawn_at` is read-only in practice: generators and standings exclude a non-null value, but NO RPC anywhere writes it and there is no UPDATE policy — from a client it is permanently null. Decode it and honour it in your filters (mirror the server), but do not build a "withdraw" button.

Timestamp decoding: `scheduled_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `withdrawn_at` come back from PostgREST as `2026-08-10T15:04:05.123456+00:00`. Swift's `.iso8601` strategy CHOKES on 6-digit fractional seconds. Reuse the app's existing custom date decoding strategy; do not add a second one. (Keeping them as `String?` and formatting on demand, like web, is also valid.)

Web's `useTournament(host)` SWR/localStorage cache does not port. In Swift use whatever cache the app already has, and KEEP THE UID IN THE KEY — a shared cache key once leaked one member's private data to the next user on this codebase.
No backend change is needed for anything in this area: migrations 0144–0154 are applied in production and the web feature is live.
Nothing about canvas/EXIF/image handling is relevant — there is no media in this feature at all.

features.name: Watch the bracket, one round at a time
features.whatItDoes: Anyone can flip through the bracket round by round and see who plays who, who won, and the score.
gotchas: The bracket pages ONE ROUND AT A TIME, driven by a segmented control, so a round fits a phone with no horizontal scrolling. Default the pager to the earliest round that still has an undecided match with both slots filled; else the last round.

Round labels: `Final` / `SF` / `QF` computed as `maxRound - round`, else `R{n}` — and `R{n}` ONLY, always, when nothing has a `nextMatchId`. Round-robin and pool games have no progression pointers, so "Final / SF / QF" labels are WRONG there; web decides with `matches.allSatisfy { $0.nextMatchId == nil }` → fall back to `"Round n · Game m"`.

A match card is two stacked rows (slot 1, divider, slot 2) plus a footer strip. Slot label: entrant name, else `"Bye"` if the match is complete, else `"TBD"`. Winner row gets a tint + bold. Footer shows a `Play-in` or `Ready` chip, the scheduled time if any, and "Tap to score" for managers.
A BYE IS NOT A GAME: `(slot1 == nil) != (slot2 == nil) && status == .complete`. Dim it and make it non-tappable.
Tappable to score only when: not rearranging, viewer is a manager, both slots filled OR already complete, and it isn't a bye.
Key play-in labelling off `is_play_in`, never off a round number.
For pools, filter by `stage` per tab — a card list mixing pool games and knockout games is meaningless.

features.name: "Now" summary for spectators
features.whatItDoes: A simple screen showing which games are up right now and the last few results, for family members who will never open the bracket grid.
gotchas: The `ready` matches, plus the last four completed ones as "X beat Y, 21–13". Most family members will never open the bracket grid — the doc calls this "cheap and high-value".
`in_progress` is never set by any RPC, so "what's happening now" must be derived from `status == 'ready'`, not from an in-progress state.
Scores are optional everywhere, so a completed match may have a winner and no score — don't render "X beat Y, –".

features.name: Champion banner
features.whatItDoes: When a tournament is finished, everyone sees who won.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ `tournaments.winner_entrant_id` CAN GO STALE — do not trust it as your champion. `_tournament_advance` clears the final match's result during a cascade but never touches the `tournaments` row; only `clear_match_result` called directly on the final resets `status`/`winner_entrant_id`. So: record the final → tournament is `complete` with a champion → then change a semifinal → the final is correctly cleared and re-opened, but the tournament still reads `status='complete'` with the OLD champion. The web has this bug too.

A second route to the same stale state: `generate_bracket_from_pools` sets `status='live'` WITHOUT `winner_entrant_id = null` (unlike `generate_bracket`/`generate_round_robin`/`generate_pools`, which all null it), so regenerating a pools knockout leaves the previous champion in place.

In Swift, DERIVE the champion from the final match: the `stage='bracket'` match with `next_match_id == nil`, `status == "complete"`, and a non-nil `winner_entrant_id`. Only fall back to the column for round-robin/pools where there is no single final in the same sense.
Do NOT fix the server-side defect as part of the iOS port — work around it client-side and raise it separately so web and iOS get the fix together (§15 gap #1).

features.name: The bracket updates live while you watch
features.whatItDoes: Scores and matchups appear on your phone the moment someone else enters them, without pulling to refresh.
gotchas: All four tables have `replica identity full` and are in the `supabase_realtime` publication.
Web opens a single channel per host and subscribes to `postgres_changes` on all four tables UNFILTERED, debounced 250 ms, then refetches the whole tournament.
REFETCH-AND-REASSEMBLE rather than patching rows — the cascade means one RPC can change a dozen rows at once and you'll never reconstruct that from individual change events.
This alone makes the phone a live scoreboard during fest week, which is most of the value.
features.nativeOpportunity: In Swift you can do better than web: filter the three child tables with `tournament_id=eq.<id>` instead of subscribing unfiltered.

features.name: Tapping a tournament notification opens the bracket
features.whatItDoes: The tournament pushes people already receive on their phones actually land on the right tournament screen instead of nowhere.
gotchas: The three kinds are `tournament_published`, `tournament_match_ready`, `tournament_champion`. All three are already in `profiles.notif_types`' default list AND already in the iOS APNs sender's pushable set (`media-server/apns-sender.js` lists `"tournament_published", "tournament_match_ready", "tournament_champion"`). Registered iOS devices are already receiving these pushes today; the app just has nowhere to land them.

⚠️ The deep link in the payload is a WEB path — and it is not always populated. `_notify_tournament_all` / `_notify_tournament_match` build `notifications.url` from `_tournament_deep_link`: `/family-fest/schedule/<schedule_item_id>` for a fest tournament, `/events?activity=<private_activity_id>` for a private one. But `_notify_match_matchup` (0148 — the `notify_match` RPC AND the cron reminders) was never updated for the polymorphic parent: it still hardcodes `'/family-fest/schedule/' || schedule_item_id`, so for a PRIVATE-ACTIVITY tournament that concatenation is NULL and the row lands with NO url at all.

ROUTE OFF `entity_type`/`entity_id`, NOT THE URL — every kind carries `entity_type = 'tournament'` and `entity_id = <tournament id>`, and that's the only stable contract (and the ids are what you actually need anyway).

`tournament_match_ready` is not always about one specific match: `generate_bracket_from_pools` reuses that same kind for a whole-tournament fan-out ("Knockout bracket is set: …") rather than `tournament_published`.

Account-less typed-in names can never receive a notification (`_notify_tournament_*` and `_notify_match_matchup` all filter `pp.user_id is not null`) — never promise a push to a typed-in name in copy.
features.nativeOpportunity: The three pushes already reach registered iOS devices via APNs today; only the landing screen is missing.

features.name: Only the activity's organizer can run the tournament
features.whatItDoes: The person running the activity gets the buttons to seed and score; everyone else just watches.
gotchas: There is NO new organizer role. `is_tournament_manager(p_tournament uuid)` (0144, granted to `authenticated`) was recreated in 0150 with a two-way branch: fest host → `_can_manage_item_signups(schedule_item_id)` (= `can_edit_fest()` — admin OR a `committee_roster` link to the `family-fest` committee — OR `fest_schedule_items.lead_user_id = auth.uid()` OR `auth.uid() = any(fest_schedule_items.crew_user_ids)`); private-activity host → `is_private_activity_host(private_activity_id)` (creator, app admin, or a roster row with `role = 'host'`).
Every mutating RPC re-checks this server-side, so the client flag is UI-only.

Three ways to compute it, best first: (1) `rpc("is_tournament_manager", ["p_tournament": id])` → `Bool` — can't drift from the server, needs the tournament to already exist (web never calls this, but it exists and is granted); (2) for "can I CREATE one here": `rpc("_can_manage_item_signups", ["p_item_id": scheduleItemId])` or `rpc("is_private_activity_host", ["p_activity": id])`; (3) what web actually does to avoid a round-trip per row: cache `rpc("can_edit_fest")` once per session and OR it with a local `event.leadUserId == uid || event.crewUserIds.contains(uid)` check.

⚠️ Most tournament helper functions are REVOKED from `authenticated` and will 404/403 if you call them: `_tournament_advance`, `_tournament_seed_order`, `_tournament_build_bracket`, `_tournament_deep_link`, `_seed_activity_tournament`, `_notify_tournament_all`, `_notify_tournament_match`, `_notify_match_matchup`, `run_tournament_match_reminders`, and `_notify` itself. Also revoked: the row-taking `_can_manage_schedule_signups(fest_schedule_items)`. The one underscore-prefixed function you'd ever want is `_can_manage_item_signups(uuid)` (the leading underscore is fine over PostgREST — this one IS granted).

features.name: Score a game with one tap
features.whatItDoes: The organizer taps the winner of a game and it's recorded; typing the actual scores is optional.
rpcs: record_match_result(p_match uuid, p_winner uuid = null, p_score1 int = null, p_score2 int = null) → void
gotchas: Rules in the order the live SQL (0145 replaced 0144's version) runs them: (1) both slots must be filled, else "Both sides must be set before recording a result"; (2) if `p_winner` is given it must be one of the two slot entrants — A WINNER ALONE IS A COMPLETE RESULT, that's the primary interaction; (3) if `p_winner` is null but both scores are given, the higher score wins; (4) equal scores raise unless `allow_ties`; (5) on save, scores + winner are written and `status='complete'`.

Propagation: if `next_match_id` is set and the winner actually changed, `_tournament_advance(next_match_id, next_slot, old_winner, new_winner)` runs; then if that next match is now `ready` and `ready_notified` is false, everybody in it gets a one-time `tournament_match_ready` notification.

If there's no `next_match_id` and the format is `single_elim`/`pools_bracket` and `stage='bracket'` → this is the FINAL: `tournaments.winner_entrant_id`/`status='complete'` are set and a `tournament_champion` notification fans out. For `round_robin` nothing propagates; once zero matches remain incomplete the standings leader is crowned.
The result sheet leads with "Tap the winner" (two big buttons), with scores behind an "Add scores (optional)" disclosure.

⚠️ Concurrency: every mutating RPC takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(tournament_id::text, 0))`, so two managers scoring at once are serialized server-side (one call blocks briefly, it does not fail). STILL keep a per-match in-flight guard in Swift so a double-tap can't fire two writes that settle out of order — web keeps a `[matchId: Task]` dictionary and returns the existing task on a second tap.

⚠️ Optimistic UI: web's `applyMatchResult` models ONLY the single forward step (decide the match, put the winner in `nextSlot` of `nextMatchId`, recompute that match's `ready`/`pending`, set the tournament complete if it was the final). It DELIBERATELY does not model the cascade-clear, and refetches from the server the moment the RPC returns. Copy that split exactly — a local cascade implementation is a second source of truth that will disagree.
`target_score` and `win_by` on `tournaments` are DISPLAY HINTS ONLY (e.g. cornhole to 21) — nothing enforces them.

features.name: Undo a game's result
features.whatItDoes: The organizer can wipe a game's result so it can be replayed.
gotchas: `clear_match_result(p_match)` runs the same recursive cascade as a changed result, from a standing start — every downstream result derived from the old winner is wiped and those slots emptied.

⚠️ `clear_match_result` RE-OPENS THE TOURNAMENT FOR ANY MATCH WITH NO `next_match_id`, not just "the final". The SQL is `update tournaments set status='live', winner_entrant_id=null where id = m.tournament_id and m.next_match_id is null` — and every round-robin game and every `stage='pool'` game also has a null pointer. So clearing one round-robin result flips the whole tournament back to `live` and drops the champion. That's usually what you want there, but don't model it as "only the final".
Clearing the FINAL directly is the one path that correctly resets `tournaments.status`/`winner_entrant_id` — a cascade through `_tournament_advance` never does (see the stale-champion gotcha).

features.name: Warning before a change wipes later games
features.whatItDoes: If the organizer changes an already-decided game, the app spells out exactly which later games will be reset before they tap.
rpcs: record_match_result(p_match uuid, p_winner uuid = null, p_score1 int = null, p_score2 int = null) → void
gotchas: THE CASCADE: `_tournament_advance` puts the new winner into the next match's slot; if that match was already decided its result is now invalid — winner and both scores are cleared, `ready_notified` reset, status recomputed (`ready` if both slots filled, else `pending`) — AND IT RECURSES FORWARD WITH `p_new = null`, so every downstream result derived from the old winner is wiped and the slots emptied.

Before saving a CHANGE to an already-decided match, walk the `nextMatchId` chain forward collecting matches that currently hold a `winnerEntrantId` and spell it out: "⚠️ Changing this will reset N later matches (Semifinal, Final) so they can be replayed", and swap the button to "Change & reset".
The doc calls this "the single most valuable piece of UX in this feature — the cascade is destructive and invisible otherwise."
Do not implement the cascade locally as an optimistic update; warn, then let the server do it and refetch.

features.name: Start a tournament on an activity
features.whatItDoes: The organizer creates a tournament for an activity — names it and picks the format, singles or teams.
rpcs: create_tournament(p_item uuid, p_title text, p_format text = 'single_elim', p_entrant_type text = 'individual', p_team_size int = null, p_bye_strategy text = 'byes') → uuid
create_activity_tournament(p_activity uuid, p_title text, p_format text = 'single_elim', p_entrant_type text = 'individual', p_team_size int = null, p_bye_strategy text = 'byes') → uuid
gotchas: Supabase RPC calls are keyed by parameter NAME, so a typo fails at runtime with a "function does not exist" style error. All these RPCs are `revoke ... from public, anon` + `grant execute ... to authenticated`.

`create_activity_tournament` is IDEMPOTENT (it returns the existing tournament's id instead of inserting), auto-seeds the roster, and flips `private_activities.tournament_enabled` true. `create_tournament` (fest) is NOT idempotent and does NOT auto-seed — repeated taps stack duplicate tournaments on the same fest activity, and the manager must pull sign-ups in.
`tournaments` has a `tournaments_one_host check (num_nonnulls(schedule_item_id, private_activity_id) = 1)` — exactly one parent is set, always.
`team_size` null/1 = individual; 2 = doubles. `bye_strategy` is `byes` | `play_in`. `tiebreakers` defaults to `{win_pct,head_to_head,point_diff,points_for}`. `status` starts at `setup`.
Web's setup sheet is 458 lines — this is the biggest chunk of UI and the least urgent: a manager can set the bracket up on the web and score it on the phone (the doc's v2 bucket).

features.name: Rename, switch format, reset, or delete a tournament
features.whatItDoes: The organizer can rename a tournament, change its format before it starts, start the bracket over, or delete it.
rpcs: update_tournament(p_tournament uuid, p_title text = null, p_bye_strategy text = null, p_allow_ties boolean = null, p_target_score int = null, p_win_by int = null) → void
gotchas: `set_tournament_format` is SETUP STATUS ONLY (migration 0154) — it raises "Reset the bracket before changing the format" otherwise. Same entrants work for all three formats, so no data reshaping is needed.

Each generator hard-refuses a mismatched format: `generate_bracket` → "Only single-elimination is supported yet" if `format <> 'single_elim'`; `generate_round_robin` → "This tournament isn't a round-robin"; `generate_pools`/`generate_bracket_from_pools` → "This tournament isn't a pools → bracket". Call `set_tournament_format` first.
`reset_bracket` deletes all matches, nulls every `seed`, returns to `status='setup'`, and clears `winner_entrant_id`. Entrants and participants are KEPT.

⚠️ `reset_bracket` does NOT clear `tournament_entrants.pool` or `tournaments.pool_count`/`advance_per_pool`, so a pools tournament in setup still carries its 'A'/'B' labels — a UI that derives pool tabs from `entrant.pool` will show pools with zero pool games until you regenerate.
The only field any web screen ever sends to `update_tournament` is `p_bye_strategy`; `p_allow_ties`, `p_target_score` and `p_win_by` are exposed but unused by any surface.

features.name: Pull the sign-up list into the tournament
features.whatItDoes: The organizer pulls everyone who signed up for the activity into the tournament in one tap.
gotchas: DESTRUCTIVE: it refuses unless `status='setup'`, and it DELETEs every existing participant AND entrant first.

For a TEAM tournament (`entrant_type='team'` and `team_size > 1`), each `fest_schedule_signups.team_id` group becomes one entrant (label = the group's `team_name`, else the members joined with `" & "`, else `"Team"`) with its people attached, and un-teamed sign-ups drop into the pool. For an INDIVIDUAL tournament every sign-up lands in the pool. Returns the count (teams created, or people pooled).

⚠️ It does NOT check that the tournament is a fest tournament: called on a private-activity tournament it still deletes every participant and entrant, then imports nothing (its reads are `where s.schedule_item_id = v_t.schedule_item_id`, which is NULL there) and returns `0` WITH NO ERROR. Only ever call it for `.schedule(...)` hosts.
`create_tournament` (fest) does not auto-seed, so this is the required first step for a fest tournament — unlike the private-activity path where it's only a re-sync.

features.name: Re-sync players from a private activity's roster
features.whatItDoes: For a private get-together, the organizer can re-pull the invited people into the tournament.
gotchas: DESTRUCTIVE: refuses unless `status='setup'`, and DELETEs every existing participant AND entrant first.
Guarded, unlike the signups import: `raise exception 'Not a private-activity tournament'` when `private_activity_id is null`.
Individuals are seeded as REAL ENTRANTS IMMEDIATELY (one solo entrant each, so the seed-order list is orderable right away); teams land in the pool. Returns the roster count.

`create_activity_tournament` already seeds the players from the activity roster (0152/0153, via `_seed_activity_tournament`) — for a private activity the roster IS the player list, so this button is only a "↻ Re-sync players from activity" affordance, not a required first step.
Depends on the whole private-activities feature (0150) being ported — explicitly omitted from v1.

features.name: Add or remove a person by hand
features.whatItDoes: The organizer can add someone who didn't sign up — an app member or just a typed-in name — or take someone out.
rpcs: add_participant(p_tournament uuid, p_for_user uuid = null, p_name text = null) → uuid
gotchas: `add_participant` puts one person into the POOL. Pass `p_for_user` for a linked member (the name is snapshotted from `profiles.display_name`), or `p_name` for an account-less typed name.

⚠️ There's a partial unique index `tournament_participants_uniq_user (tournament_id, user_id) where user_id is not null`, so adding the same member twice fails with Postgres `23505` — catch it and say "already in". Typed names are deliberately NOT deduped (two "John"s are fine).

⚠️ Account-less typed names are FIRST-CLASS everywhere — they seed, they play, they win, they appear in standings. The single thing they can't do is receive a notification (`_notify_tournament_*` and `_notify_match_matchup` all filter `pp.user_id is not null`). Never promise a push to a typed-in name in copy.

⚠️ "How many will actually compete" is NOT `entrants.count`. For `entrant_type='individual'` the generators promote every pool participant to a solo entrant at generation time, so the real number is `entrants.count + pool.count` (web calls this `readyCount` and gates its Generate button on `readyCount >= 2`). For teams, only formed entrants count. Getting this wrong disables Generate on a perfectly valid tournament — or lets a manager generate with one entrant, raising "Need at least two entrants to generate a bracket".
There is no "withdraw" path: `withdrawn_at` has no writer and the tables take no client UPDATE (§15 gap #3).

features.name: Teams — make them, group them, ungroup them
features.whatItDoes: For a doubles tournament, the organizer can enter an existing team, randomly pair everyone into teams, or dump everyone back into one pile.
rpcs: add_entrant(p_tournament uuid, p_team_name text = null, p_members jsonb = null) → uuid
gotchas: `add_entrant` is the "they're already a team" path. `p_members` is a JSON array of `{"for_user": uuid|null, "name": string|null}`; it must be non-empty ("Add at least one person"). For a team tournament the count must equal `team_size` EXACTLY ("A team needs exactly N people"). Display name = `p_team_name`, else the members joined with `" & "`.
`remove_entrant` is SETUP ONLY; its members drop back to the pool (`entrant_id → null`) rather than being deleted.

`generate_teams` random-pairs the pool into teams of `team_size` and returns `{"teams_created": n, "leftover": m}` — ⚠️ LEFTOVER PEOPLE STAY IN THE POOL AND WILL NOT COMPETE. Setup only, team format only.
`ungroup_teams` puts everyone back in the pool and deletes all entrants. Setup only.
For teams, only FORMED entrants count toward "how many will compete" — the pool-promotion rule only applies to `entrant_type='individual'`.
`tournament_entrants.signup_team_id` back-links to `fest_schedule_signups.team_id` when a team came in from sign-ups.
Explicitly omitted from v1 ("Teams (`entrant_type='team'`, `generate_teams`, `add_entrant`, the pool concept in the UI)").

features.name: Seed the players and build the bracket
features.whatItDoes: The organizer puts the players in order (or lets it be random), sees a preview of who plays who in round one, and builds the bracket.
rpcs: generate_bracket(p_tournament uuid, p_seed_order uuid[] = null) → void
gotchas: Bracket size B = next power of two ≥ N; rounds R = log₂B. Round 1 is seated by standard fold-seed order (`_tournament_seed_order`), so seed 1 meets the weakest and 1 v 2 can only happen in the final. Phantom seeds > N leave a null slot = a BYE, which the generator immediately completes (winner set, `status='complete'`) and advances.

`bye_strategy`: `byes` (top seeds rest — falls out of fold seeding) or `play_in` (identical graph; round-1 real games get `is_play_in = true` so you can label them). Passing `p_seed_order = nil` gives random seeding, which naturally scatters the byes.

⚠️ `p_seed_order` is ENTRANT IDS, index 0 = seed 1. It is applied ONLY when `array_length(p_seed_order,1)` equals the live entrant count EXACTLY — otherwise it is SILENTLY IGNORED and seeding is randomized. Two ways that bites: (a) if you let the manager reorder while someone else is adding a player, the reorder is quietly discarded; (b) for `entrant_type='individual'` the count is taken AFTER the RPC promotes every pool participant to a solo entrant, so ANY NON-EMPTY POOL GUARANTEES a length mismatch and random seeding. Web reflects this — `doGenerate` sends `null` unless the order array length equals the EXISTING entrant count. Send `nil` for random.

Port the pure math EXACTLY from `lib/tournaments.ts` or the manager sees one bracket and gets another: `bracketSize(n)` (n < 2 ? n : next power of two), `byeCount(n) = max(0, bracketSize(n) - n)`, `lowerPow2(n)`, and `seedOrder(size)` — start `[1,2]`, then for each `s` append `s` and `2*sz + 1 - s`, doubling `sz`; element p (0-based) is the 1-based seed occupying slot p. Must match SQL `_tournament_seed_order`.

`firstRoundPreview(names, strategy)` walks `i in 0..<(B/2)` taking `order[2i]` and `order[2i+1]`; a seed > N is a bye (nil name); `isPlayIn = strategy == .playIn && B > N && !isBye`. `bracketSummary` is the one-liner ("12 entrants · 16-team bracket · 4 byes (top seeds rest)" / "12 entrants · 4 play-in games → clean 8-team draw").
Gate the Generate button on `readyCount >= 2` where `readyCount = entrants.count + pool.count` for individuals — the server raises "Need at least two entrants to generate a bracket".
`generate_bracket` refuses a non-`single_elim` tournament ("Only single-elimination is supported yet") — call `set_tournament_format` first (setup only).
Generation fans out a `tournament_published` notification to every participant with an account.
features.v1Cut: Ship random seeding only: send `p_seed_order: nil`, skip the drag-to-reorder list, and skip the fold-seed preview + `bracketSummary`. The doc puts all of setup in v2 anyway — a manager can build the bracket on the web and score it on the phone.

features.name: Round-robin: everyone plays everyone, with a standings table
features.whatItDoes: A format where every player or team plays each other once, with a W-L table that ranks everyone.
rpcs: generate_round_robin(p_tournament uuid, p_seed_order uuid[] = null) → void
record_match_result(p_match uuid, p_winner uuid = null, p_score1 int = null, p_score2 int = null) → void
gotchas: Rows look like: `stage='bracket'`, `next_match_id` IS NULL ON EVERY ROW, and `round`/`position` are DISPLAY-ONLY groupings from the circle method. Circle method, every pair once; an odd count gets a phantom that simply produces no row that round.
Because nothing has a `nextMatchId`, "Final / SF / QF" labels are WRONG — always render `"Round n · Game m"` (web decides with `matches.allSatisfy { $0.nextMatchId == nil }`).

Standings are computed CLIENT-SIDE from the tournament's ordered `tiebreakers`; the server only stamps a best-effort leader as champion once every game is complete (wins → point diff → points-for → seed), for the notification and the banner.

`computeStandings(tournament, pool:)` counts only `status == .complete` matches where both slots are present AND both entrants are in scope; a match with `winnerEntrantId == nil` counts as a TIE for both. `winPct = (wins + 0.5*ties) / played` (0 when unplayed). Sort by the tournament's ordered `tiebreakers` array — `win_pct`, `point_diff` (`pointsFor - pointsAgainst`), `points_for`, `head_to_head` (find the one match between the two; the winner sorts first; no match or a tied match contributes 0 and falls through) — with `seed ?? position ?? .max` as the final tiebreak.
POINT COLUMNS ARE HIDDEN until any score exists anywhere (`hasAnyScores`), because scores are optional and a winner-only round-robin should read as a clean W-L table.
Recording a round-robin result propagates nothing; once zero matches remain incomplete the standings leader is crowned (`tournament_champion`).
⚠️ Every round-robin game has a null `next_match_id`, so `clear_match_result` on ANY of them flips the whole tournament back to `status='live'` and drops the champion.
Explicitly omitted from v1 — with pools it's "a third of the whole feature".
features.v1Cut: Omit entirely from v1 (the doc's explicit cut). If shipped later, render the W-L table on `win_pct` alone with point columns hidden, and skip `head_to_head` ordering plus the tiebreaker legend.

features.name: Pools then a knockout bracket
features.whatItDoes: Players are split into pools that each play a mini round-robin, then the top finishers move into a knockout bracket.
rpcs: generate_pools(p_tournament uuid, p_pool_count int = 2, p_advance int = 1, p_seed_order uuid[] = null) → void
gotchas: Pool games are `stage='pool'` + `pool='A'…`; the knockout is `stage='bracket'` with `next_match_id`/`next_slot` pointers. Filter by `stage` per tab — a card list mixing pool games and knockout games is meaningless.

Entrants are dealt across `pool_count` pools by seed: `pool = chr(65 + ((seed-1) % pool_count))`, i.e. seed 1→A, 2→B, 3→A, 4→B… ⚠️ The SQL comment calls this "snaked", but the formula is a plain round-robin DEAL, not a serpentine snake (which would be 1→A, 2→B, 3→B, 4→A) — IMPLEMENT THE FORMULA, NOT THE WORD, or your preview will disagree with the server.

`generate_bracket_from_pools` REFUSES until every `stage='pool'` game is complete ("Finish every pool game first (N left)"), then takes the top `advance_per_pool` per pool and cross-seeds: global seed = `(pool_rank-1) * pool_count + pool_index + 1` (pool_index from `ascii(pool) - 65`), so pool winners land on opposite ends of the draw.

⚠️ `generate_bracket_from_pools` sets `status='live'` WITHOUT nulling `winner_entrant_id` (unlike `generate_bracket`/`generate_round_robin`/`generate_pools`, which all null it), so regenerating a pools knockout leaves the PREVIOUS CHAMPION in place.

⚠️ It also fans out a whole-tournament `tournament_match_ready` notification ("Knockout bracket is set: …") rather than `tournament_published` — so don't assume a `tournament_match_ready` row is always about one specific match.
Each pool's standings use the same client-side `computeStandings(tournament, pool:)` as round-robin, scoped to that pool's entrants.

Pool games record without propagating; the knockout crowns the champion like `single_elim`. Every pool game has a null `next_match_id`, so clearing one re-opens the whole tournament (`status='live'`, champion dropped).
⚠️ `reset_bracket` does not clear `tournament_entrants.pool` or `pool_count`/`advance_per_pool`, so pool tabs derived from `entrant.pool` will show pools with zero games until you regenerate.
UI is a Pools / Games / Bracket tab set with a manager "Generate knockout bracket" button once pools finish. Explicitly omitted from v1.
features.v1Cut: Omit entirely from v1 (the doc's explicit cut). If shipped later: pool games + per-pool standings first, `generate_bracket_from_pools` after, and skip the tiebreaker legend.

features.name: Move a player to a different spot in the bracket
features.whatItDoes: The organizer can drag a player or team into a different slot, or swap two of them.
rpcs: set_match_entrant(p_match uuid, p_slot int, p_entrant_id uuid) → void
swap_match_entrants(p_match_a uuid, p_slot_a int, p_match_b uuid, p_slot_b int) → void
gotchas: ⚠️ `set_match_entrant` and `swap_match_entrants` ALSO WIPE RESULTS. `set_match_entrant(p_match, p_slot, p_entrant_id)` unconditionally nulls that match's `winner_entrant_id`, `slot1_score`, `slot2_score` (and `ready_notified`) — EVEN WHEN YOU'RE ONLY FILLING AN EMPTY SLOT — and, if the match had been decided, cascades forward.
⚠️ `swap_match_entrants` is literally two `set_match_entrant` calls, so a swap DESTROYS THE RESULTS OF BOTH MATCHES. Both matches must be in the same tournament.
`p_slot` must be 1 or 2; `p_entrant_id` may be null to clear (NO DEFAULT — pass it explicitly).
Web's "⇄ Rearrange" mode is deliberately only offered on a bracket view. If you ship rearrange in v1, WARN BEFORE THE TAP.
Explicitly omitted from v1 — "destructive and fiddly".
Match cards must not be tappable-to-score while rearranging.

features.name: Give a game a time (with reminders)
features.whatItDoes: The organizer can set when a game happens and have the players reminded beforehand.
rpcs: schedule_match(p_match uuid, p_at timestamptz = null, p_reminders int[] = '{}') → void
gotchas: `schedule_match` sets/clears a match's time and its reminder lead-times in minutes. Re-scheduling DELETES THE FIRED-REMINDER LEDGER ROWS for that match so the new time re-arms them. Web only ever sends `[15]`.
`reminder_minutes` is NOT NULL with a `{}` default — decode as `[Int]` but still coerce `nil → []`.

Server-side only, no client involvement: `run_tournament_match_reminders()` ticks every minute, fires `_notify_match_matchup` for each `(match, lead-time)` whose moment has arrived, and dedupes through the `tournament_match_reminders_sent (match_id, minutes)` ledger. It only considers matches that are NOT `complete` and have BOTH slots filled, and it SKIPS any whose `scheduled_at` is more than 2 hours in the past. (`run_tournament_match_reminders` is revoked from `authenticated` — don't call it.)

⚠️ The cron's matchup reminder deep-link is broken for private activities: `_notify_match_matchup` predates 0150 and hardcodes `'/family-fest/schedule/' || schedule_item_id`, yielding a NULL `url` there. Route off `entity_type`/`entity_id` instead (§15 gap #4).

Verify with one `select` before building against it: the migration-0148 columns `tournament_matches.scheduled_at` / `.reminder_minutes`, the `tournament_match_reminders_sent` ledger table, and the `schedule_match` / `notify_match` RPCs. Web reads/calls them and web is live, so they should be present — but 0183 only proves the four base tables exist.
Explicitly omitted from v1.
features.nativeOpportunity: Use a native `DatePicker` and send `ISO8601DateFormatter` output WITH the offset — `p_at` is a real `timestamptz`, so the offset matters and there is no date-string trap here (unlike sign-up slots, which store bare `YYYY-MM-DD`). This replaces web's hand-rolled `datetime-local` local-offset shim (`toLocalInput`).

features.name: Tell both sides their game is up
features.whatItDoes: The organizer taps a button and both sides of a game get a push telling them who they're playing.
rpcs: notify_match(p_match uuid, p_when text = 'is up next!') → void
gotchas: Immediate per-side push: each side is told THE OTHER entrant's name ("Your matchup against {other} {p_when}").

⚠️ `p_when` is appended VERBATIM to the notification body. This app already learned the hard way (migration 0165, in the sign-up reminders) that a sender-chosen phrase like "is in 30 minutes" can flatly contradict the stored time with no way for the recipient to tell. Either reuse web's two fixed phrases (`"is up next!"`, `"is in about 15 minutes"`) or state the real `scheduled_at` — DO NOT build a free-text lead-time picker.
Account-less typed-in names get nothing (`_notify_match_matchup` filters `pp.user_id is not null`).
⚠️ For a private-activity tournament this notification lands with NO url at all (`_notify_match_matchup` predates the polymorphic parent) — route off `entity_type`/`entity_id`.
Explicitly omitted from v1.

features.name: Allow a game to end in a tie
features.whatItDoes: For a round-robin, let a game be recorded as a draw instead of forcing a winner.
rpcs: update_tournament(p_tournament uuid, p_title text = null, p_bye_strategy text = null, p_allow_ties boolean = null, p_target_score int = null, p_win_by int = null) → void
record_match_result(p_match uuid, p_winner uuid = null, p_score1 int = null, p_score2 int = null) → void
gotchas: ⚠️ You CANNOT record a tie through the current client API as web uses it: the web wrapper always requires a non-nil winner, and NOTHING anywhere in the web UI ever sets `allow_ties` (`update_tournament` exposes `p_allow_ties`, but no surface calls it — the only field any web screen sends is `p_bye_strategy`).
To make ties work: (a) call `update_tournament` with `p_allow_ties: true`, and (b) call `record_match_result` with `p_winner: nil` and BOTH scores — ROUND-ROBIN ONLY.

If both scores are equal, the RPC raises unless `allow_ties`; with it, the winner is recorded as NULL (a real tie) — but a bracket match with a `next_match_id`, or any `single_elim`/`pools_bracket` tournament, raises "a bracket game can't end tied".
In `computeStandings`, a complete match with `winnerEntrantId == nil` counts as a tie for both, and `winPct = (wins + 0.5*ties) / played`.
No migration needed (the RPC parameter exists) — just a client surface. Treat as OUT OF V1 SCOPE (§15 gap #2).

features.name: Tournaments on a private get-together
features.whatItDoes: A member-created private activity can run its own tournament, visible only to the people invited.
rpcs: create_activity_tournament(p_activity uuid, p_title text, p_format text = 'single_elim', p_entrant_type text = 'individual', p_team_size int = null, p_bye_strategy text = 'byes') → uuid
gotchas: Originally (0144) `tournaments.schedule_item_id` was NOT NULL. Migration 0150 dropped that, added `private_activity_id`, and added `constraint tournaments_one_host check (num_nonnulls(schedule_item_id, private_activity_id) = 1)` — so exactly one is set, always.

Model it as an enum, not two optionals: `enum TournamentHost { case schedule(UUID) /* a fest_schedule_items row */; case activity(UUID) /* a private_activities row */ }`, threaded through fetch/create/import. (Web's equivalent is the TS discriminated union `TournamentHost = {kind:'schedule'|'activity', id}`.) Fetch is `.eq("schedule_item_id", id)` or `.eq("private_activity_id", id)`, ordered by `created_at` ascending.

Private activities ARE capped at one tournament: migration 0151's partial unique index `tournaments_one_per_activity on tournaments (private_activity_id) where private_activity_id is not null`, plus an idempotent `create_activity_tournament`. Fest activities are NOT capped.

RLS: a `tournaments` row with `private_activity_id` set is readable only when you are also that activity's creator, on its roster, or an admin (`is_private_activity_member()`); the three child tables inherit the same predicate via an `exists` subquery on the parent.
⚠️ Never call `import_entrants_from_signups` on a private-activity tournament — it deletes every participant and entrant, imports nothing, and returns `0` with no error.
⚠️ Matchup-reminder / `notify_match` notifications for a private-activity tournament land with NO url (`_notify_match_matchup` predates 0150). Route off `entity_id`.

This depends on the whole private-activities feature (0150) also being ported. If private activities aren't in scope, HARD-CODE `TournamentHost = .schedule(...)` and the polymorphism costs you nothing. Explicitly omitted from v1.
features.nativeOpportunity: Swift's enums let the XOR parent be unrepresentable-if-wrong, instead of web's two nullable columns you have to keep straight.

features.name: Honest message when you can't see the bracket yet
features.whatItDoes: A brand-new member waiting to be approved, or someone not signed in, gets told why the bracket is empty instead of seeing a blank screen.
gotchas: Migration 0183 dropped and recreated all four SELECT policies, REPLACING the old `auth.uid() is not null` clause with `is_approved_member()` (= `profiles.approved` true OR `profiles.is_admin` true — the admin-verification gate from 0181/0182). The function resolves `where id = auth.uid()`, so it already implies a real session; there is no separate signed-in clause any more.

AN EMPTY RESULT ALMOST ALWAYS MEANS "NOT PERMITTED", NOT "NO DATA." Specifically: a brand-new unverified signup gets ZERO ROWS ON ALL FOUR TABLES and will see an apparently empty/broken tournament screen. Handle that with the same "waiting for a grown-up to verify you" state the rest of the app uses — DO NOT show "no bracket yet".
Guests (no session) get nothing; web renders a "Sign in to see the bracket and scores" card in place of the section.
The other cause of a mysteriously empty tournament is the PostgREST embed ambiguity (HTTP 300 / `PGRST201`) — check the HTTP status before showing any empty state.
Because reads are stale-while-revalidate cached, keep the uid in the cache key so a revoked/unverified viewer can't paint another member's cached bracket.

features.name: Your activities list on the Events screen
features.whatItDoes: Shows the invite-only get-togethers you've been included in, right on the Events screen, each with a one-line summary of who's in and whether it has a tournament.
gotchas: One fetch gets both tables; the web selects `"*, private_activity_members(*)"` (single FK between these two, so no PostgREST embed-ambiguity trap here — that trap applies to the tournament fetch).

RLS `private_activities: member read` = `for select using (public.is_private_activity_member(id))`: you can read an activity only if you created it, you're an app admin, or you're on its roster. `private_activity_members: member read` = `using (public.is_private_activity_member(activity_id))`.

An empty list means "you weren't invited to anything", and an empty roster on an activity you can see should never happen (the creator is always inserted as a member, and `remove_private_activity_member` refuses to delete their row). A zero-row read is never "no data yet" in the sense of a missing feature.

⚠️ Roster display order is not plain `created_at`. The web fetch sorts hosts first, `created_at` only within a role (`lib/privateActivities.ts`), and then `PrivateActivitySheet` renders `[...going, ...other]` — everyone whose `rsvp == "going"` first. Copy both steps; `created_at` alone will order it differently.

⚠️ Decode `role`/`rsvp` defensively — model them as enums with a fallback case rather than a bare `enum: String, Decodable`; a strict enum turns a future value (or a hand-edited row) into a whole-list decode failure, which reads as "private activities are broken", not "one row is odd".

⚠️ Timestamps are `timestamptz` and Postgres returns 6-digit fractional seconds (`2026-08-09T14:03:22.481293+00:00`). Swift's stock `.iso8601` date strategy rejects fractional seconds outright. Use whatever custom decoding mlr-app-ios already uses for `posts.created_at` / `house_stays` — do not introduce a second, stricter one here.
`starts_at` null = "sometime" / TBD — this is the normal case, not an error. `ends_at`: nothing in the web UI ever sets it; expect null.
`tournament_enabled` defaults `false` in the DB, but the web composer's "🏆 Make it a tournament" toggle defaults ON, so most existing rows are `true`.
`emoji` is a plain `text` column, can be null/empty, and nothing enforces it's actually an emoji — the list row falls back to `🎉`.
Treat `""` as "no value" everywhere on read (`location?.isEmpty == false` before rendering) — because of the update-RPC workaround, `''` and `NULL` both mean absent.

Don't let a decode or network error throw into the view — an empty list plus a retry beats a crash. (The web's `fetchPrivateActivities` returns `[]` on ANY error; the `isMissingTable`/42P01 degradation is belt-and-braces on iOS since all five migrations are live in production.)

The web's SWR/`sessionStorage` cache (`privateActivities.<uid>`) exists only because Next remounts screens on tab navigation — iOS has no such problem, use your existing observable store; there's nothing to port. If you DO cache, keep the uid in the key: a shared device that switches accounts must not paint the previous member's private activities (a shared cache key once leaked one member's private chat to the next user).
`updated_at` is maintained by trigger `private_activities_set_updated_at`, which calls the shared `set_updated_at()` defined in `0001_profiles.sql`, not 0035 (0150's own comment misattributes it).

features.name: Create an activity
features.whatItDoes: Any signed-in member can start a private get-together — a name, an emoji, where, an optional time (or "no set time") — and pick the handful of people it's shared with.
rpcs: create_private_activity(p_title text, p_emoji text default null, p_description text default null, p_location text default null, p_starts_at timestamptz default null, p_ends_at timestamptz default null, p_tournament_enabled boolean default false, p_members jsonb default null, p_notify boolean default false) returns uuid
gotchas: Gates on nothing but `auth.uid() is not null` — the polls / work-items / cabin-request doctrine, NOT the admin-only `events` model. On the web the entry point is a "🎉 Create an activity" button on `/events` shown to everyone, which calls `promptSignIn()` for a guest instead of opening the composer. Mirror that: the button is always visible, sign-in is the gate.

⚠️⚠️ There are NO insert / update / delete policies on either table. RLS denies by default, so every direct table write from the app is refused — never write `.from("private_activities").insert(...)`. Every write goes through the SECURITY DEFINER RPCs.
Raises `Sign in required` / `A title is required` (title is `btrim`-ed and must be non-empty). `p_title` has no default and must be sent; params with a default may be omitted.
Supabase RPC calls are keyed by name, so a wrong key is a runtime 404 from the schema cache (`Could not find the function public.x(...)`), not a compile error.
Inserts the creator as the first roster row automatically: `role='host'`, `rsvp='going'`, `name = display_name` (or `'Me'`). Don't include yourself in `p_members` — the loop skips your own id anyway.

`p_members` must be a JSON array; the web sends one object per invitee, always with both keys present: `{"user_id": "<uuid>"|null, "name": "<string>"|null}`. For an entry with a `user_id` the supplied `name` is IGNORED and re-resolved from `profiles.display_name`; an entry with neither a `user_id` nor a non-blank name is skipped. An empty array is fine.

⚠️ A `user_id` here that matches no profile is NOT an error (unlike `add_private_activity_member`): the name lookup comes back null and the row is inserted, linked to that id, named `'Guest'`. Validate ids client-side if you ever build them from anything but a live directory fetch.
The create path `btrim`s + `nullif`s emoji / description / location, so a blank string lands as NULL on create (the empty-string trick applies only to *update*).

Duplicate linked invitees collapse via `on conflict … do nothing`. There is no uniqueness at all on typed names (two "Uncle Rick"s are legal) — the web composer de-dupes case-insensitively as each chip is added, not at submit time.

jsonb from Swift: build `p_members` as an `Encodable` array of a two-field struct (`user_id: UUID?`, `name: String?`) inside your params struct — supabase-swift will encode it as jsonb. The SQL checks `jsonb_typeof(p_members) = 'array'`, so a dictionary or a stringified array is silently ignored, not an error.

`<input type="datetime-local">` → `DatePicker`: the composer defaults to a "No set time — we'll just play" checkbox (checked), and only when unchecked reads the local datetime and converts with `new Date(value).toISOString()`. Send `p_starts_at` as an ISO-8601 UTC string — the column is `timestamptz`, so a local-time string without an offset is interpreted in the server's timezone.
Emoji field: the web clamps input to the last two characters, pre-fills `🏓`, and offers a quick-pick row (`🏓 🎯 🎲 🏆 🃏 ⛳️ 🏀 🎱 🥏 🎳`).
The "🏆 Make it a tournament" toggle sets `p_tournament_enabled` and defaults ON in the web composer.
Returns the new activity's uuid → decode as `UUID`.

features.name: "Let them know" invite notification
features.whatItDoes: An optional ping to just the people who were added — off by default, so nobody gets bothered unless the organizer asks for it.
rpcs: _notify_private_activity_invite(p_activity, p_only_user) — NOT callable from the client (execute revoked from authenticated too)
gotchas: There is exactly ONE notification kind for this feature: `private_activity_invite`.

It fires only from `create_private_activity` when `p_notify = true` (to every roster member with an account, except the actor) or from `add_private_activity_member` when `p_notify = true` (to that one person). There is NO notification on RSVP, edit, archive, delete, or role change. Do not add one client-side.

The web surfaces it as a "🔔 Let them know" toggle on the composer that defaults OFF, with the copy "Send a notification to the people you added (only them). Off = no one is pinged." Keep the default off — that's the product promise.

Fan-out runs through the shared `_notify(...)` (defined in 0030, last recreated by 0047 — which only adds a `help_urgent` bypass, so this kind still respects prefs), which drops the row if the recipient is the actor, or if the recipient doesn't have `'private_activity_invite'` in `profiles.notif_types`.

In-app is ON by default (0150 changed the `profiles.notif_types` column default and appended the value to every existing row; no later migration touches that default). Phone push is OPT-IN — `private_activity_invite` is deliberately absent from `DEFAULT_PUSH_TYPES`, and both mini senders (`media-server/apns-sender.js`, `push-sender.js`) include it in their pushable set but require it in the member's `push_types`. A member who has push on but never opted into this category correctly gets nothing.
Typed-name roster entries are never notified (no `user_id`). If the organizer expects "everyone got told", they didn't.

`p_notify = true` on `add_private_activity_member` pings only that one person, and only when `p_user_id` is non-null. On a duplicate add the RPC returns NULL and nothing is notified either (the notify branch requires a real inserted id).

The tournament pings a private activity can produce (`tournament_published`, `tournament_match_ready`, `tournament_champion`) were already participant-scoped before this feature, so they stay private too; 0150 only changed where they point.

features.name: Open an activity
features.whatItDoes: Tapping an activity shows the whole plan — what, when, where, the note, and everyone who's in with their yes/maybe/no — plus the organizer's controls.
gotchas: ⚠️ Roster display order is two steps: hosts first with `created_at` only within a role, then `[...going, ...other]` (everyone whose `rsvp == "going"` first). `created_at` alone will order it differently.
Render typed-name people distinctly — the web appends a quiet `(not on app)` after the name.
The web hides per-member controls for `m.userId == activity.createdBy` (the organizer's ✕ should just not be rendered).
Show RSVP controls only when the viewer actually has their own roster row (the web computes `myRow` and renders the control only if it exists).
`starts_at` null = "sometime" / TBD is the normal case; `ends_at` is never set by the web UI.
Treat `""` as "no value" everywhere on read (`location?.isEmpty == false`) — `''` and `NULL` both mean absent.
`canManage` does not exist in the database — it's computed client-side (see the organizer-powers entry) for affordance gating only.
The web's edit sheet only exposes title + location even though `update_private_activity` takes everything; a richer iOS detail/edit surface needs no backend work.

features.name: Organizer powers (who can change things)
features.whatItDoes: The creator, anyone made an organizer, and app admins see the edit / add-people / archive / delete controls; everyone else just sees the plan.
gotchas: ⚠️ `canManage` does not exist in the database. `lib/privateActivities.ts` computes it client-side as `isAdmin || row.created_by == myUserId || (my roster row has role == "host")`. Mirror that for affordance gating, and let the server's own host check be the real gate — every mutating RPC re-checks `is_private_activity_host` and raises `Not authorized`.

`is_private_activity_member(p_activity)` = activity's `created_by = auth.uid()`, OR caller has `profiles.is_admin`, OR caller has a roster row on it. `is_private_activity_host(p_activity)` = `created_by = auth.uid()`, OR caller is an app admin, OR caller has a roster row with `role = 'host'`.

Both predicates are `security definer stable set search_path = ''` with `grant execute … to authenticated` and ARE callable as RPCs if you want a server-truth check — the web never calls them, it derives `canManage` locally.
Both grant admins full read + host powers, for moderation — an admin sees every private activity in the app.
⚠️ Privacy is deliberately absolute: there is no "all members" or public visibility mode. Don't add a "share with everyone" affordance; that's what `events` is for.

A typed-name person shouldn't be made an organizer — `set_private_activity_member_role` will happily set `role='host'` on a `user_id`-null row, but `is_private_activity_host` matches on `m.user_id = auth.uid()`, so the standing is inert.

features.name: Edit the plan
features.whatItDoes: An organizer can change the name, place, note, emoji, or time of an activity — or switch it back to "no set time".
rpcs: update_private_activity(p_activity uuid, p_title text default null, p_emoji text default null, p_description text default null, p_location text default null, p_starts_at timestamptz default null, p_ends_at timestamptz default null, p_tournament_enabled boolean default null, p_clear_start boolean default false) returns void
gotchas: Host gate. Semantics are `coalesce(p_x, x)` per field: null means "leave unchanged", which is how partial updates work here.

⚠️ You therefore CANNOT null out `emoji` / `description` / `location` through this RPC. The web has this exact bug live: `PrivateActivitySheet`'s `saveEdit` sends `location: location.trim() || null`, so clearing the Where field and tapping Save silently keeps the old value. Don't copy it. With no backend change, send an empty string `""` instead of null — that's non-null so `coalesce` takes it, and the column ends up `''`. Which means: treat `""` as "no value" everywhere on read, because `''` and `NULL` both now mean absent.

⚠️ The empty-string workaround is verified from the SQL (`coalesce(p_location, location)`) and the web's call site, but has NOT been exercised against production — try it once in a scratch activity before shipping the edit form.
`p_title` can't be blanked (`coalesce(nullif(btrim(...),''), title)`) — an empty title is a no-op, not an error. Validate client-side.

The ONLY clearable fields are the times: `p_clear_start = true` sets BOTH `starts_at` and `ends_at` to null (it's the "make it TBD" switch), and when true it ignores whatever you passed for `p_starts_at`/`p_ends_at`.
The web's edit sheet only exposes title + location even though the RPC takes everything. A richer iOS edit form (emoji, description, time, TBD toggle) needs no backend work.
⚠️⚠️ There are no update policies on the table — a direct `.update(...)` fails as *zero rows affected with no error*, the worst possible failure shape. Go through the RPC.
No notification fires on edit. Don't add one client-side.

features.name: Add people to an activity
features.whatItDoes: An organizer can invite more family later — either an app member or just a typed-in name.
rpcs: add_private_activity_member(p_activity uuid, p_user_id uuid default null, p_name text default null, p_role text default 'player', p_notify boolean default false) returns uuid
gotchas: Host gate. Pass EITHER `p_user_id` (a linked member; name is resolved from `profiles`, raises `Member not found` if that profile doesn't exist) OR `p_name` (a typed name; raises `A name is required` if blank). If both are sent, `p_user_id` wins and `p_name` is ignored.
`p_role` is coerced: anything other than the literal `'host'` becomes `'player'`.

⚠️⚠️ Returns NULL, not an error, when that member is already on the roster (`on conflict (activity_id, user_id) … do nothing` leaves the `returning` empty). Decode this as `UUID?` — a non-optional `UUID` decode will throw on a duplicate add and surface as a spurious error to the user. Nothing is notified in that case either.
`p_notify = true` pings only that one person, and only when `p_user_id` is non-null.

Unique index `private_activity_members_uniq` on `(activity_id, user_id) where user_id is not null` — one row per app member per activity, and NO uniqueness at all on typed names (two "Uncle Rick"s are legal; dedupe in your UI if you care — the web composer de-dupes case-insensitively as each chip is added, and the detail sheet's typed-name add doesn't dedupe at all).
`private_activity_members.name` is a snapshot; for a linked member it's their `display_name` at add time.
⚠️⚠️ No insert policy exists — a direct table insert is refused. Only this RPC works.

features.name: People who aren't on the app
features.whatItDoes: Lets an organizer include family who don't have accounts by just typing their name — they show on the roster and can play, they just can't be pinged or answer.
rpcs: add_private_activity_member(p_activity uuid, p_user_id uuid default null, p_name text default null, p_role text default 'player', p_notify boolean default false) returns uuid
set_private_activity_rsvp(p_activity uuid, p_rsvp text) returns void
set_private_activity_member_role(p_member uuid, p_role text) returns void
gotchas: The typed-name roster idiom (inherited from migration 0143's linked-or-typed pattern): a roster entry is either a linked app member (`user_id` set, `name` snapshotted from `profiles.display_name`) or an account-less typed name (`user_id` null, `name` whatever was typed). `user_id` references `profiles(id) on delete set null` — null = a typed-in name.
A typed-name person CAN play in a tournament but can NEVER receive a notification (no `user_id` for `_notify` to target).
A typed-name person can't RSVP — `set_private_activity_rsvp` keys on `auth.uid()`, so there's no row to write.

A typed-name person shouldn't be made an organizer. `set_private_activity_member_role` will happily set `role='host'` on a `user_id`-null row, but `is_private_activity_host` matches on `m.user_id = auth.uid()`, so the standing is inert. The web hides the "Make organizer" button unless `m.userId != nil` — copy that rule; the server won't stop you.
Render them distinctly. The web appends a quiet `(not on app)` after the name.

No uniqueness at all on typed names — two identical names are legal; the web composer de-dupes case-insensitively as each chip is added (not at submit), and the detail sheet's typed-name add doesn't dedupe at all.

features.name: Remove someone / leave an activity
features.whatItDoes: An organizer can take someone off the list, and anyone on the list can bow out themselves.
gotchas: Takes the roster ROW id (`private_activity_members.id`), not a user id.
Allowed for a host OR for the member removing their own row (i.e. "leave"). Raises `Not found` for an unknown row id, `Not authorized` otherwise.

⚠️ Refuses the creator's own row with `The organizer can't leave — delete the activity instead` — and that check runs BEFORE the authorization check, so it's the message you get for the creator's row even without host rights. Surface it as a real message; the organizer's ✕ should just not be rendered (the web hides controls for `m.userId == activity.createdBy`).
Because the creator's row can never be deleted, an activity you can see should never have an empty roster.
No notification fires on removal.

features.name: Make someone an organizer
features.whatItDoes: An organizer can hand co-organizer powers to another app member on the list (or take them back).
rpcs: set_private_activity_member_role(p_member uuid, p_role text) returns void
gotchas: Host gate; `p_role` must be `'host'` or `'player'` (else `Unknown role`). Roster ROW id again — an unknown id raises `Not found`.
Column is `role text not null default 'player'` with `check (role in ('host','player'))`.

⚠️ Hide the "Make organizer" button unless `m.userId != nil` — the RPC will set `role='host'` on a typed-name (`user_id` null) row, but `is_private_activity_host` matches on `m.user_id = auth.uid()`, so the standing is inert. The server won't stop you.
No notification fires on a role change. Don't add one client-side.
Roster display sorts hosts first, so a promotion reorders the list.

features.name: Say if you're coming
features.whatItDoes: Anyone on the list taps Going / Maybe / Can't — and tapping their current answer again clears it.
rpcs: set_private_activity_rsvp(p_activity uuid, p_rsvp text) returns void
gotchas: MEMBER gate (not host) — anyone who can see the activity may call it.
`p_rsvp` ∈ `going|maybe|out`, or null to clear (the web toggles: tapping your current choice again sends null). Anything else raises `Unknown RSVP` (validated BEFORE the membership gate).
Column is `rsvp text null` with `check (rsvp in ('going','maybe','out'))` — null = no answer yet.

⚠️ The UPDATE is `where activity_id = p_activity and user_id = auth.uid()`. An admin who isn't on the roster passes the permission gate but updates ZERO rows — a silent no-op with no error. Only show RSVP controls when the viewer actually has their own roster row (the web computes `myRow` and renders the control only if it exists).
A typed-name person can't RSVP — there's no row keyed to an `auth.uid()`.
RSVP affects display order: the sheet renders `[...going, ...other]`, so answering reorders the roster.
No notification fires on RSVP. Don't add one client-side.

features.name: Archive a finished game
features.whatItDoes: An organizer tucks a finished get-together away under a "Finished & archived" section instead of deleting it.
rpcs: set_private_activity_archived(p_activity uuid, p_archived boolean) returns void
gotchas: Host-gated. Stamps `archived_at = now()` (or clears it back to null when `p_archived = false`).

Nothing is destroyed and the row STILL comes back in the normal fetch — the client partitions on `archived_at`. The web shows live ones under "Your activities" and archived ones behind a collapsed "Finished & archived (n)" disclosure, dimmed, still openable and still deletable.
Label it as the web does — "🗄️ Archive (game's over)" / "♻︎ Unarchive".
Archive and delete are two genuinely different host-only actions; don't collapse them into one.
No notification fires on archive.

features.name: Delete an activity
features.whatItDoes: An organizer can remove the whole get-together for everyone, permanently.
gotchas: Host-gated HARD delete. The FK cascade takes out `private_activity_members`, the `tournaments` row, and (via that row's own cascades from migration 0144) `tournament_entrants` / `tournament_participants` / `tournament_matches`. Irreversible.
The web puts it behind an inline confirm ("Delete this activity for everyone? This can't be undone.").
An archived activity is still deletable.
A deleted activity is exactly why a deep-link uuid may not resolve — handle that calmly on the receiving side.
No notification fires on delete.

features.name: Tapping an invite opens the activity
features.whatItDoes: Tapping the invite notification (or a shared link) lands you straight on that activity's page.
rpcs: _notify_private_activity_invite(p_activity, p_only_user) — NOT callable from the client
gotchas: The activity deep-link is a QUERY PARAMETER, not a route segment: `/events?activity=<activity-uuid>`. It's produced in two places server-side — `_notify_private_activity_invite` builds `'/events?activity=' || p_activity::text`, and `_tournament_deep_link` returns the same for any tournament whose `private_activity_id` is set.

The APNs payload your app already receives (from `apns-sender.js`'s `handleFeed`): `title` = notification title ("🏓 Ping-pong tournament"), `body` = "<organizer> invited you to join", `url` = "<APP_URL>/events?activity=<activity-uuid>", `type` = "private_activity_invite", `target_type` = "private_activity", `target_id` = "<activity-uuid>".

⚠️ Route off `target_type` + `target_id`, NOT by parsing `url`. The url is a *web* path that only exists because the notification row is shared with the PWA; `target_id` is the activity uuid directly. Same for the tournament kinds.

Register a deep-link case that carries the activity uuid, reached from (a) an APNs tap where `target_type == "private_activity"` (use `target_id`), (b) an in-app Activity-feed row whose `notifications.url` matches `/events?activity=…`, and (c) any universal link on the web path. It should push/present the activity detail on top of your Events screen, same as the web.

⚠️ The uuid may not resolve. The activity can have been deleted, or you may have been removed from its roster, since the notification was written — RLS then returns nothing. Handle "not found or no longer shared with you" as a real, calm state rather than a spinner or a crash on a force-unwrap.
On web, `app/events/page.tsx` reads `params.get("activity")` on mount and sets `openActivityId`, which opens the detail sheet over the calendar.

features.name: Changes show up without a refresh
features.whatItDoes: When someone RSVPs, is added, or edits the plan, everyone's screen updates on its own — including the moment you're added to a brand-new activity.
gotchas: Realtime is enabled on BOTH tables (`replica identity full`, both added to the `supabase_realtime` publication).
The web hook subscribes to `event: "*"` on `private_activities` AND `private_activity_members` with NO filter, and on any event just debounce-reloads (250 ms) the RLS-scoped fetch.

⚠️ Do the same: treat a realtime event as "something changed, refetch", and NEVER render from the payload. An unfiltered subscription is the only practical shape (you don't know your activity ids up front, and roster changes are what add you to one), and a `private_activity_members` insert is precisely the event that GRANTS you read access — so only a refetch can materialize the activity you just gained.

features.name: "This one has a tournament" (v1 placeholder)
features.whatItDoes: Shows that an activity is set up as a tournament and points people to the web app to run the bracket, until the native bracket ships.
gotchas: Suggested v1: ship the activity, skip the bracket. Store and display `tournament_enabled` (the list row reads "Private · 🏆 Tournament · 4 people") but render a "manage the bracket in the web app" line instead of the bracket UI.
Expect `tournament_enabled` to be TRUE on most existing rows — the DB default is false, but the web composer's toggle defaults on.
Make the tournament area distinguish "no tournament yet" from "couldn't read it" (see the approval-gate entry).

features.name: Set up the tournament
features.whatItDoes: An organizer turns the activity into a real tournament, and everyone on the list is entered automatically.
rpcs: create_activity_tournament(p_activity uuid, p_title text, p_format text default 'single_elim', p_entrant_type text default 'individual', p_team_size int default null, p_bye_strategy text default 'byes') returns uuid
_seed_activity_tournament(p_tournament, p_activity, p_entrant_type) — NOT callable from the client
gotchas: Migration 0150 made `tournaments` polymorphic rather than forking the bracket engine: `tournaments.schedule_item_id` was made nullable and `tournaments.private_activity_id uuid references private_activities(id) on delete cascade` was added, with `check (num_nonnulls(schedule_item_id, private_activity_id) = 1)` (constraint `tournaments_one_host`) — exactly one host.

`is_tournament_manager(p_tournament)` branches: a fest tournament defers to `_can_manage_item_signups(item)`, a private-activity tournament to `is_private_activity_host(activity)`. No new organizer role.

0151 added partial unique index `tournaments_one_per_activity on tournaments(private_activity_id) where private_activity_id is not null`, and made `create_activity_tournament` IDEMPOTENT — if the activity already has a tournament it returns that id and ignores the other params (the early return happens before the title/format validation and before `tournament_enabled` is re-set, so a re-tap with garbage params is a silent no-op).

⚠️ That guard exists because of a real incident: a client display hiccup meant nothing rendered after creation, so the "Set up a tournament" button kept reappearing and each tap inserted another tournament row. The DB now refuses duplicates, but still disable your button while the call is in flight and render off the refetched state.

0152 → 0153: creating a tournament AUTO-SEEDS the players from the activity roster, so there is no separate "import" step for a v1.
