For `p_entrant_type = 'individual'` each roster member becomes a real `tournament_entrants` row (`position` 0..n-1, `seed` still null until generate) plus a linked `tournament_participants` row — they land already listed and reorderable. For `'team'` they all land in the pre-team pool (`tournament_participants.entrant_id = null`) and the host taps "auto-make teams" first.
The tournament seeder's order key is `private_activity_members.created_at` (`_seed_activity_tournament … order by created_at`) — not the hosts-first display order.
⚠️ The `tournaments` fetch MUST name the entrants FK — see the bracket entry; a plain `tournament_entrants(*)` embed returns HTTP 300 / PGRST201 and an empty result.

features.name: Watch and score the bracket
features.whatItDoes: Everyone on the list can follow the bracket, and the organizer taps the winner of each game to move it along.
gotchas: ⚠️ The `tournaments` fetch MUST name the entrants FK. `tournaments` has two relationships to `tournament_entrants` (the child's `tournament_id` FK plus `tournaments.winner_entrant_id`), so a plain `tournament_entrants(*)` embed returns HTTP 300 / PGRST201 and an EMPTY result. The web's select is `"*, tournament_entrants!tournament_entrants_tournament_id_fkey(*), tournament_matches(*), tournament_participants(*)"` — copy it verbatim. (`matches`/`participants` have one relationship each and are fine.)

Read rules (as re-stated by migration 0183): `tournaments` is `using (is_approved_member() and (private_activity_id is null or is_private_activity_member(private_activity_id)))`. The three child tables have no host column of their own, so each resolves through its parent: `using (is_approved_member() and exists (select 1 from tournaments t where t.id = <table>.tournament_id and (t.private_activity_id is null or is_private_activity_member(t.private_activity_id))))`. A private bracket and its scores are not readable by the rest of the family.

Honest sizing: the private-activity feature itself is small, but the tournament half is LARGE and independent — `lib/tournaments.ts` is ~31 KB, plus `TournamentView` / `TournamentBracket` / `TournamentStandings` / `MatchResultSheet` / `TournamentSetupSheet`, covering three formats, byes/play-ins, rearrange mode, pools→knockout promotion, and an optimistic `record_match_result` with a per-match in-flight lock.

If you want a tournament v1, the cheapest real one is `single_elim` only: `create_activity_tournament` already seeds the entrants, so you need only `generate_bracket` + `record_match_result` + a round pager — you can skip entrant management entirely.
Make the iOS tournament view distinguish "no tournament yet" from "couldn't read it" (an unapproved member gets zero rows here while still reading the activity — see the approval-gate entry).

Tournament pings (`tournament_published`, `tournament_match_ready`, `tournament_champion`) were already participant-scoped, so they stay private; route them off `target_type` + `target_id` like the invite, and their deep link is `/events?activity=<id>` for a private-activity tournament.
`_notify_tournament_all(...)` and `_notify_tournament_match(...)` are NOT callable from the client (execute revoked from `authenticated` too).
features.v1Cut: single_elim only — ship generate_bracket + record_match_result + a round pager. Skip entrant management, rearrange mode, standings, byes/play-in configuration, team entrants, and pools→knockout promotion; creation already auto-seeds the roster.

features.name: Re-sync players from the activity
features.whatItDoes: If people were added or dropped after the tournament was set up, the organizer can rebuild the player list from the current roster.
rpcs: _seed_activity_tournament(p_tournament, p_activity, p_entrant_type) — NOT callable from the client
gotchas: This is the "↻ Re-sync players from activity" action: manager gate, requires `private_activity_id is not null` (else `Not a private-activity tournament`) and `status = 'setup'` (else `Reset the bracket before re-importing`), wipes participants + entrants, re-seeds via the same `_seed_activity_tournament`, and returns the roster COUNT as an `int`.
Not needed for a v1 — creating a tournament already auto-seeds the players from the roster, so there is no separate "import" step.
Order key when re-seeding is `private_activity_members.created_at`, not the hosts-first display order.

features.name: Change the tournament format
features.whatItDoes: Before any games are played, the organizer can switch between a knockout bracket, everyone-plays-everyone, or pools.
rpcs: set_tournament_format(p_tournament uuid, p_format text) returns void
gotchas: 0154's `set_tournament_format(p_tournament, p_format)` lets a MANAGER switch `single_elim` / `round_robin` / `pools_bracket` while still in `setup` (else `Reset the bracket before changing the format`).
Pointless in a single_elim-only v1 — ship it with the other formats, not before.
`create_activity_tournament` is idempotent and ignores `p_format` once a tournament exists, so this RPC is the only way to change format afterwards.

features.name: Round-robin and pools tournaments
features.whatItDoes: Runs the other two tournament styles — everyone plays everyone with a standings table, or pool play that feeds into a knockout.
rpcs: set_tournament_format(p_tournament uuid, p_format text) returns void
gotchas: This is the bulk of the "large and independent" tournament half: `lib/tournaments.ts` is ~31 KB, plus `TournamentView` / `TournamentBracket` / `TournamentStandings` / `MatchResultSheet` / `TournamentSetupSheet`, covering three formats, byes/play-ins, rearrange mode, pools→knockout promotion, and an optimistic `record_match_result` with a per-match in-flight lock.
Formats are `single_elim` / `round_robin` / `pools_bracket`, switchable only while `status = 'setup'`.
Same read-policy and FK-naming traps as the bracket view apply.
features.v1Cut: Skip entirely for v1 — ship single_elim only and don't surface the format switcher.

features.name: Unverified members see the activity but not its bracket
features.whatItDoes: A brand-new member who hasn't been verified yet can open an activity they were added to, but its tournament comes back empty — so the screen has to say so instead of looking broken.
gotchas: ⚠️ Asymmetric approval gate. Migration 0183 re-gated the four tournament read policies onto `is_approved_member()` (verified member per 0181/0182) but LEFT `private_activities` / `private_activity_members` on the original `is_private_activity_member(...)` predicate, which does not check `approved`. So an unverified/unapproved signup who is added to a roster CAN read the activity and its roster but gets ZERO rows for its tournament — the tournament section would render silently empty for them.
This is what the SQL says today; confirm with Brian whether that's intended before designing around it.
Either way, make the iOS tournament view distinguish "no tournament yet" from "couldn't read it".
Remember RLS filters rather than raising — a zero-row tournament read looks identical to "nothing created yet" unless you model the two states separately.

features.name: Seeing a room's meetings and their proposed times
features.whatItDoes: Loads the meetings for the committee channel, house, or the whole family, together with the time options that were proposed, so anything about a meeting can appear in the app.
endpoints: CORRECTED select string: id, scope_type, committee_slug, area, house_id, title, description, created_by, created_at, respond_by, status, chosen_slot_id, meet_url, created_event_id, meeting_slots!meeting_slots_meeting_id_fkey(id, starts_at, ends_at, duration_min, position)

Filters: committee → .eq("scope_type","committee").eq("committee_slug", slug) then .is("area", value: nil) for the General channel or .eq("area", area); house → .eq("scope_type","house").eq("house_id", houseId); family → .eq("scope_type","family"). Order created_at descending.
Second query: plain meeting_availability select with .in("meeting_id", values: ids) — no embed, no ambiguity
webFiles: MeetingSection.tsx (owns the fetch + realtime + ?meeting= deep link)
fetchMeetingsForRoom (web's version ships the BROKEN unqualified embed)
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ The embed MUST name the foreign key. There are TWO relationships between meetings and meeting_slots: meeting_slots.meeting_id → meetings.id (`meeting_slots_meeting_id_fkey`, one-to-many) AND meetings.chosen_slot_id → meeting_slots.id (`meetings_chosen_slot_fk`, many-to-one, added at the bottom of 0116). An unqualified meeting_slots(...) embed returns HTTP 300 PGRST201 "Could not embed because more than one relationship was found for 'meetings' and 'meeting_slots'" — probed live 2026-08-10.

Do NOT copy web's select string: fetchMeetingsForRoom ships the unqualified form and swallows the error into `return []`, so the ENTIRE meetings read path on web is dead right now and nobody can see it, because there are no meetings to miss.

The JSON key stays `meeting_slots` (the hint after `!` is not part of the key), so the decoder is unchanged. If you'd rather be explicit, alias it: slots:meeting_slots!meeting_slots_meeting_id_fkey(...) and rename the property to slots.

Never swallow a read error into []. Log PGRST201 / PGRST203 / 42501 distinctly and surface them in debug builds — RLS emptiness and a malformed query are different states. That single habit is what hid this bug on web for months.

⚠️ An empty result means "not permitted", not "no meetings". RLS filters; it never raises. An unapproved brand-new signup or a non-member who IS signed in gets [] with HTTP 200 for every one of these tables. Don't render "No meetings yet" without knowing which case you're in — that ambiguity is exactly what hid the committee_areas outage.

⚠️ Signed OUT is different and loud: anon has no EXECUTE on is_house_member (0064 grants it to authenticated only), so an unauthenticated read of any of these four tables returns HTTP 401 {"code":"42501","message":"permission denied for function is_house_member"} — verified live. Treat that specific 42501 as "no session", not a broken policy, and never fire these reads before the session is restored.

Live-data reality check: `select count(*) from meetings` is 0 — nobody has ever created a meeting in production. You will be the first person to ever see a real meeting row render, so "looks empty" is not evidence it works.

Scope is enforced by a CHECK: committee ⇒ committee_id set / house_id null; house ⇒ the reverse; family ⇒ BOTH null. In Swift keep committeeId and houseId both String? and branch on scopeType, never on nil-ness of one field.
respond_by is a bare `date` ("2026-07-31") — decode as String and treat it as a calendar day, never an instant. It is INFORMATIONAL ONLY; nothing enforces it.

timestamptz arrives as 2026-07-31T09:00:00.123456+00:00 (up to 6 fractional digits) and sometimes with none at all; a single ISO8601DateFormatter config will throw on one of those. Use JSONDecoder.dateDecodingStrategy = .custom that tries with and without fractional seconds.

Read rules: meetings readable iff committee scope → can_access_committee_area(committee_id, area); house scope → is_house_member(house_id); family scope → is_approved_member() (profiles.approved is true OR is_admin is true). meeting_slots and meeting_availability are readable iff their parent meeting is — so everyone in the room sees everyone's answers; that's the whole point.
Decode meeting_slots as optional and default to []. respond_by, chosen_slot_id, meet_url, created_event_id, created_by, area, house_id, committee_slug, description are all optional.

Key any on-device cache by the REAL uid and clear it on sign-out — a shared cache key once leaked one member's private chat to the next user (CLAUDE.md, PR #244). Web's localStorage SWR snapshot (meetings.<uid>.<roomKey>) does not transfer; use your own store.

Resolve "is this mine" from the EFFECTIVE user id, and make every write a no-op while previewing as another member — the web app's hard rule after admin Edit/Delete affordances leaked onto a previewed member's screen.

features.name: Meeting answers and tallies updating live
features.whatItDoes: Keeps a meeting's vote counts and time options current on screen while other people are answering, without pulling to refresh.
gotchas: Web opens one channel per room, meetings-<roomKey> where roomKey is c:<slug>|<area> / h:<houseId> / family, subscribing to postgres_changes event: "*" on ALL THREE tables with NO filter, then debounces ~250ms and refetches everything. Copy that: the useful values (buckets, score, best slot, respondent count) are all derived, so applying row deltas by hand is not worth it.
All three tables are in the supabase_realtime publication with replica identity full (verified).
Tear the channel down when the room closes.
Realtime honours RLS, so you only receive rows you could read anyway.
A refetch triggered by realtime must use the FK-named embed too, or it silently returns PGRST201 forever (see the read-layer entry).

features.name: Vote counts and the "best time so far"
features.whatItDoes: Works out, for each proposed time, who said yes, who said if-need-be and who said no, and which option is winning.
gotchas: Derived values are computed CLIENT-SIDE — there are no columns for any of these. Per slot: bucket user_ids into yes / ifNeedBe / no; score = yes.count + ifNeedBe.count * 0.5; bestSlotId = highest score with ties going to the FIRST slot in (position, starts_at) order; respondentCount = distinct user_ids across the whole meeting; myAnswers[slotId] = your own rows.
Resolve user_id → name against the room roster you already have, falling back to "A member", and print "You" for yourself.
Resolve "is this mine" from the EFFECTIVE user id (never a raw session lookup), so an admin previewing as another member doesn't see their own answers highlighted.
Status strings are exactly 'yes' | 'if_need_be' | 'no' — meeting_availability.status has no other legal value, and the PK is (slot_id, user_id).

features.name: Only the right people see "Schedule a meeting"
features.whatItDoes: Hides the option to start a meeting from anyone who isn't allowed to run one in that room.
gotchas: Ask the server, don't infer. Web calls the RPC (fetchCanOrganize) purely so the button can't drift from the gate. Do the same — one cheap round-trip, false on any error.

The rule: app admin (any scope, unconditionally) OR — committee scope ONLY — you have a committee_roster row linked to your uid on that committee where p_area IS NULL → any role matching like '%· Lead', or p_area given → the exact string p_area || ' · Lead' is in roles[].
Consequence: houses and family scope are ADMIN-ONLY (no branch matches — there is no house-lead concept).
Because the check is literal string concatenation, organizing in the pseudo-area 'Leads' would require a role literally named "Leads · Lead" — so the Leads channel is admin-only in practice.
The `·` is U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT surrounded by spaces (verified: bytes c2 b7 20 4c 65 61 64). Get that character wrong anywhere and lead detection silently fails.

⚠️ Do not reuse this gate for cancel/delete/finalize — those are CREATOR-or-admin, not lead-or-admin. A committee lead who did not create the meeting can propose new ones but cannot finalize or cancel that one (web: canManage = isAdmin || meeting.createdByMe).
All nine meeting RPCs are `grant execute ... to authenticated` and revoked from anon (confirmed via has_function_privilege).

features.name: Proposing times and opening a meeting for votes
features.whatItDoes: Lets an organizer suggest up to ten possible times for a get-together and ask everyone in the room to mark when they're free.
rpcs: create_meeting(p_scope, p_committee_id, p_area, p_house_id, p_title, p_description, p_slots, p_respond_by, p_email) -> uuid
webFiles: FeedView.tsx → MeetingComposer.tsx (Room ⋯ menu, "📅 Schedule a meeting", organizer-gated — creation only, kept out of the composer bar)
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ SEE THE OVERLOAD FIX ENTRY BEFORE CALLING THIS. create_meeting has TWO live overloads. A body carrying p_email (9 keys) can only bind the 0117 overload: 'family' scope is REJECTED with raise exception 'Invalid scope', and every date-range slot's ends_at is SILENTLY DROPPED (its slot INSERT has no ends_at column).

Omitting p_email does NOT silently mis-bind — it fails loudly: an 8-key body returns HTTP 300 PGRST203 "Could not choose the best candidate function between: …(p_respond_by => date), …(p_respond_by => date, p_email => boolean)" (probed live). Don't build on it either way.
Until the §A.6 SQL runs, ship v1 as committee/house + point-in-time slots only and ALWAYS send p_email. After it runs, always send all 9 keys explicitly.

p_slots is a jsonb ARRAY of objects: { "starts_at": ISO8601, "duration_min": Int, "ends_at": ISO8601|null }. 1..10 elements or it raises ("Add at least one time option" / "A meeting can have at most 10 time options").
A misspelled key inside p_slots (e.g. starts_at) becomes NULL and hits a not-null violation — that one at least fails loudly.

Server-side validation to mirror in the UI: title required ("A title is required"), max 200 chars ("Keep the title under 200 characters"); committee scope resolves the slug and raises 'Committee not found' if the committee_id is bogus; sign-in required.

Swift's synthesized Encodable uses encodeIfPresent, so a nil optional OMITS the key entirely — which changes which overload you bind to (i.e. a PGRST203, not a wrong answer). Encode nulls explicitly: a custom encode(to:) using container.encode(...), or build params as [String: AnyJSON] with AnyJSON.null.
p_email true ⇒ stamps meetings.notify_email (the mac mini mails the room); it is NOT a send from the app.
committee_slug is denormalised at insert and never changes (0112); area NULL means the committee-wide "General" channel, never a real role.
Creating a meeting fans out meeting_proposed via _notify_meeting_room — you don't post anything yourself.
features.v1Cut: Committee + house scope, point-in-time slots only, single "Find a time" mode; omit the Times/Dates toggle, family scope, the respond_by picker, and the "Also email everyone a link to vote" checkbox (but still always send p_email explicitly).

features.name: Setting one known time with no voting
features.whatItDoes: Lets an organizer just announce a meeting at a time they already know, skipping the whole voting step.
rpcs: create_scheduled_meeting(p_scope, p_committee_id, p_area, p_house_id, p_title, p_description, p_starts_at, p_duration_min, p_meet_url, p_ends_at) -> uuid
webFiles: MeetingComposer.tsx ("Set a time now" mode of the two-mode toggle)
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ Same overload trap, one function over: create_scheduled_meeting exists as BOTH the 9-arg (0119) and the 10-arg (0122, with p_ends_at). ALWAYS send p_ends_at, even as an explicit null — a 9-key body returns HTTP 300 PGRST203 (probed live).

It inserts the meeting + one slot and immediately calls finalize_meeting internally — which posts the room chat message, fans out meeting_scheduled, and triggers the confirmation email. Do NOT post your own message or send your own notification.
No meeting_proposed and no voting happens on this path.
Swift nil-omission: encode nulls explicitly or you change which overload you bind to.
Deferred in the recommended v1 cut.

features.name: Proposing whole date ranges instead of times
features.whatItDoes: Lets an organizer offer spans of days ("Fri Jul 25 – Sun Jul 27") as the options people vote on, instead of an hour-long call.
rpcs: create_meeting(p_scope, p_committee_id, p_area, p_house_id, p_title, p_description, p_slots, p_respond_by, p_email) -> uuid
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ BLOCKED until the §A.6 SQL runs: a body carrying p_email binds the 0117 overload whose slot INSERT has no ends_at column, so every date-range slot SILENTLY loses its ends_at and renders as a point-in-time call. Web has shipped this bug since 0122; zero meetings in prod is why nobody noticed.
meeting_slots.ends_at non-null means the slot is a SPAN, not an hour — and duration_min is meaningless for that slot.
Web stores local midnight for both ends (new Date("2026-07-25T00:00").toISOString()) and formats a range as two weekday/month/day labels with no clock.
The composer's Times vs Dates toggle defaults to Dates for family scope and Times otherwise.

⚠️ Never derive the display day by parsing a bare YYYY-MM-DD (or a UTC-midnight instant) and formatting it in the device's zone — that's the off-by-one-day bug that mislabeled the whole fest sign-up UI (migration 0168), and it also silently corrupted the data the picker wrote. starts_at/ends_at are full timestamptz so they're safe as long as you format them in a fixed calendar; respond_by is a bare date and must stay a calendar-day string.

features.name: Marking when you're free (Yes / If-need-be / No)
features.whatItDoes: Lets every member of the room say, for each proposed time, whether they can make it, might be able to, or can't.
gotchas: p_answers is a jsonb OBJECT, not an array: { "<slot uuid>": "yes" | "if_need_be" | "no" }.

⚠️ Enum raw values must be EXACT. The RPC filters with where (value #>> '{}') in ('yes','if_need_be','no') and only upserts slot ids that belong to the meeting — anything else is SILENTLY SKIPPED and the call returns success. So "if-need-be" (hyphens) writes nothing, reports nothing, and looks like a UI bug.
⚠️ Upsert-only. Omitted slots keep their previous answer, and there is NO delete path — a member can change an answer but can never un-answer. Don't build a "clear" affordance.
It raises 'This meeting is closed' for any status <> 'open'.
Web sends the FULL draft map (seeded from myAnswers) every time; do the same.
Everyone in the room can see everyone's answers (meeting_availability is readable iff its parent meeting is) — that's intended, not a leak.
Writes must be a no-op while an admin is previewing as another member.

features.name: The meeting scheduler screen
features.whatItDoes: One screen where you mark your availability, see how everyone answered, see which time is winning, and (if you're the organizer) lock the meeting in.
rpcs: finalize_meeting_as_event(p_meeting, p_slot, p_kind, p_title, p_description, p_location) -> uuid
webFiles: MeetingSchedulerSheet.tsx (availability grid, tallies, who's-free expander, guided finalize)
gotchas: The organizer gate for finalize/cancel/delete is CREATOR-or-admin, not lead-or-admin: canManage = isAdmin || meeting.createdByMe.

Hide the finalize affordance once created_event_id is set (web: canManage && !meeting.createdEventId) — finalize_meeting_as_event has no uniqueness protection and a second call creates a SECOND events row.
Tallies, best-slot and respondent count have no columns — compute them client-side (see the derived-tallies entry).
window.confirm does not transfer for the cancel/delete confirmations — use a native alert.
The ?meeting=<id> URL-param deep link does not transfer — use your own route.
Name resolution needs the room roster's ids; fall back to "A member", print "You" for yourself.
Both finalize RPCs have NO status guard — calling finalize_meeting again on a scheduled meeting is the supported "Change time or link" path.
features.v1Cut: Ship the availability grid with per-slot tri-state controls, live tallies, best-so-far, and the finalize_meeting (Meet link) outcome. Omit the expandable who's-free list, the "Create an event" outcome, and the prefilled Google Calendar hand-off (accept a pasted link only).

features.name: The meeting bar at the top of a chat
features.whatItDoes: When a meeting is live in a room, a strip at the top of that chat invites everyone to mark when they're free — and shows nothing at all the rest of the time.
webFiles: MeetingSection.tsx (owns the fetch + realtime + ?meeting= deep link)
gotchas: It renders NOTHING unless a meeting is live — do not show an empty bar or a "No meetings yet" line.
⚠️ Don't render "No meetings yet" without knowing which case you're in: [] can mean "not permitted" (unapproved signup, non-member) just as easily as "no meetings".
This surface owns the room's meetings fetch + realtime subscription; a meeting created from the room ⋯ menu appears here on the next realtime tick.
The ?meeting=<id> deep link does not transfer — use your own route; prefer the APNs target_type/target_id ('meeting' / the meeting id) over parsing the notification URL.
The scheduler sheet mounts from here because it needs the room roster's ids for name resolution.

features.name: The meeting bar on Events and on a committee page
features.whatItDoes: Shows the same meeting response strip as a rounded card on the Events screen and on a committee's page, so people find it outside the chat too.
gotchas: Same component, card surface — the three-way split of mount points is deliberate, so mirror it rather than inventing a fourth surface.
The /events mount is also where family-scope meetings live, and family scope is blocked on the §A.6 SQL.
Deferred in the recommended v1 cut.

features.name: Locking in a time with a Google Meet link
features.whatItDoes: The organizer picks the winning time, optionally pastes a Google Meet link, and the whole room gets told in the chat plus an email with a Join button.
gotchas: Sets status='scheduled', chosen_slot_id, meet_url (null if blank), finalized_at/by.

It POSTS A MESSAGE INTO THE ROOM'S CHAT ITSELF, as the finalizer, straight into committee_messages (with area = m.area) or house_messages. Body: `📅 Meeting set — {title} · {Dy Mon DD, HH12:MI AM}` rendered at time zone 'America/Chicago' plus \nJoin: {url}. iOS does nothing here — the message arrives through your existing chat realtime. DON'T double-post. Because the RPC is SECURITY DEFINER, that insert bypasses RLS.
Fans out meeting_scheduled to the room with the _meeting_url web path — you don't send anything.

The confirmation email is NOT sent by this function: the mac-mini alert-mailer.js watches for a meetings UPDATE to status='scheduled' and is gated on meet_url being non-null (if (!row || row.status !== "scheduled" || !row.meet_url || row.confirm_email_sent_at) return;), so a linkless finalize waits and fires later when the link is added.
There is NO status guard — calling it again on a scheduled meeting is the supported "Change time or link" path.

Google Meet is GUIDED, not OAuth: build a prefilled https://calendar.google.com/calendar/render?action=TEMPLATE&text=…&dates=<start>/<end>&details=… link (compact UTC stamps, e.g. 20260720T143000Z), the organizer taps it, adds Meet, saves, and pastes the link back into a field in your sheet.
Link validation is loose on purpose: ^https?:// AND host contains meet.google.com / calendar.google.com / goo.gl. A BLANK link is explicitly allowed (lock the time now, add the link later).
Auth is creator-or-admin (canManage = isAdmin || createdByMe), NOT lead-or-admin.

features.name: Turning the winning date into a real calendar event
features.whatItDoes: Instead of a video call, the organizer can turn the winning date into an actual event on the resort calendar, with everyone who voted yes already pencilled in as coming.
rpcs: finalize_meeting_as_event(p_meeting, p_slot, p_kind, p_title, p_description, p_location) -> uuid
webFiles: MeetingSchedulerSheet.tsx ("Schedule a call" vs "Create an event" outcome toggle)
gotchas: p_kind defaults 'work_weekend'; the others default null (title falls back to the meeting's).

Inserts into events with source='meeting', source_meeting_id = p_meeting, start_date = the slot's start IN America/Chicago, end_date = the slot's ends_at date or null. Sets meetings.created_event_id for the reverse link and marks the meeting scheduled.

Carries RSVPs over as UNCONFIRMED: every meeting_availability row on the winning slot with yes → going, if_need_be → maybe, inserted into event_attendance with confirmed = false. 'no' voters get NO row at all.
event_attendance.event_id is TEXT (v_event_id::text), not a uuid FK — that table also holds seed slugs like family-fest-2026.

⚠️⚠️ No status guard and NO uniqueness protection: calling it twice creates TWO events rows and leaves created_event_id pointing at the second. Disable the button once createdEventId != nil (web hides the affordance: canManage && !meeting.createdEventId).

Its own meeting_scheduled fan-out does NOT use _meeting_url: title `Event created: {title}`, body `Dy Mon DD` (with ` – Dy Mon DD` for a range), url /events?open=<event id> — while the notification's entity stays ('meeting', p_meeting), so target_id is the MEETING id and the url points at the EVENT. Handle that mismatch deliberately.

It auto-queues one scheduled_broadcasts reminder 14 days before the event at 09:00 Central (skipped if already past) with payload.onlyUnconfirmed = true; run_scheduled_broadcasts() (pg_cron) narrows that send. Nothing for iOS to build, but know its shape: that reminder is written DIRECTLY into notifications by run_scheduled_broadcasts, not through _notify, as type='broadcast', entity_type='broadcast', NO entity_id, url /events?open=<event id> — so its push is gated on the `alerts` push category, not meeting_scheduled, and it carries no target_id to route on.
Available in EVERY scope, not just family — a committee meeting can become an Event too. Web defaults the outcome toggle to "event" for family scope and "call" otherwise.
Partly blocked: the reconfirm half depends on the §A.6 set_event_attendance fix. Deferred in the recommended v1 cut.

features.name: "Hasn't confirmed yet" on a meeting-created event
features.whatItDoes: For an event made from a meeting vote, shows which people were pencilled in from their vote but haven't actually confirmed they're coming — and lets tapping your Going/Maybe/Can't control count as that confirmation.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ BROKEN TODAY — DON'T BUILD THE RECONFIRM LOOP ON TOP OF THIS. pg_proc holds BOTH set_event_attendance(text, text, jsonb) (created by 0122; its upsert ends … confirmed = true, updated_at = now()) and set_event_attendance(text, text, jsonb, text) (0036; its upsert never mentions confirmed, and it is the one that fans out event_rsvp).
Every client sends p_title, so the 4-arg runs and `confirmed` stays FALSE forever; a 3-key call returns HTTP 300 PGRST203 (probed live), so the confirming body is unreachable over REST.

Web papers over it optimistically (confirmed: true in local state, comment: "mirrors set_event_attendance's upsert") and the next refetch reverts it. Net effect until the §A.6 SQL runs: the "(hasn't confirmed)" tag never clears and the onlyUnconfirmed reminder re-nudges people who already re-answered.

Once fixed, the verb stays the same — tapping your existing Going/Maybe/Can't control IS the confirmation. No new button to learn. Show a quiet "(hasn't confirmed)" tag next to unconfirmed names, like web's EventSheet.
event_attendance.event_id is TEXT, not a uuid FK.
Deferred in the recommended v1 cut (blocked on the §A.6 SQL).

features.name: Cancelling or deleting a meeting
features.whatItDoes: Lets the person who created a meeting (or an admin) call it off, keeping a cancelled record, or remove it entirely.
gotchas: cancel_meeting keeps the record with status='cancelled'; delete_meeting cascades slots + availability.

⚠️ Creator-or-admin, NOT lead-or-admin. A committee lead who did not create the meeting can propose new ones but cannot cancel or delete that one. Web's gate is literally canManage = isAdmin || meeting.createdByMe.
set_my_availability raises 'This meeting is closed' for any status <> 'open', so a cancelled meeting must stop accepting answers in the UI too.
window.confirm does not transfer — use a native alert.
Writes must be a no-op while previewing as another member.
features.nativeOpportunity: Replace web's window.confirm with a real native confirmation alert.

features.name: Family-wide date polls ("which weekend works?")
features.whatItDoes: An admin can ask the whole family — not just one committee or house — which dates work, with the poll living on the Events screen.
rpcs: create_meeting(p_scope, p_committee_id, p_area, p_house_id, p_title, p_description, p_slots, p_respond_by, p_email) -> uuid
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ BLOCKED until the §A.6 SQL runs: the 0117 overload (the one a p_email-carrying body binds) REJECTS family scope with raise exception 'Invalid scope'. Web's own family-wide "📅 Propose dates" on /events raises that today.
Family scope means committee_id AND house_id are BOTH null — branch on scope_type, never on nil-ness of one field.
Reads are gated on is_approved_member() → profiles.approved is true OR is_admin is true (migration 0183), so an unapproved brand-new signup gets [] with HTTP 200.
Organizing a family meeting is ADMIN-ONLY, which falls straight out of can_organize_meeting's unconditional admin branch.

⚠️ For family scope the notification fan-out is `from public.profiles p` with NO FILTER AT ALL — every profile row, including brand-new unapproved signups who cannot read the meeting they were just told about. Not yours to fix, but don't be surprised.
The family deep link is /events?meeting=<id> (not /posts?...).
Deferred in the recommended v1 cut.

features.name: "Also email everyone a link to vote"
features.whatItDoes: An optional tick when proposing times that emails the room a heads-up with a button that opens the voting screen.
rpcs: create_meeting(p_scope, p_committee_id, p_area, p_house_id, p_title, p_description, p_slots, p_respond_by, p_email) -> uuid
gotchas: iOS only surfaces the checkbox — "Also email everyone a link to vote" → p_email, default OFF. Emails are entirely mac-mini side effects; the recipient RPCs are service_role-only, so there is NOTHING for the app to call.
p_email true just stamps meetings.notify_email; the mini does the sending (and needs to be running/restarted).

Principle from 0132/0133: profiles.email_alerts gates ONLY broadcast alerts — transactional meeting emails OVERRIDE it and reach verified members, invited-but-unverified accounts, and account-less roster people with an email (committee_roster for committee meetings, family_roster for house meetings).

Sending p_email is what binds the 0117 overload — see the overload entry; until the §A.6 SQL runs you must send it anyway, so treat the checkbox as controlling the boolean's VALUE, never whether the key is present.
Deferred in the recommended v1 cut.

features.name: Getting told about a meeting (in-app and on your phone)
features.whatItDoes: Sends everyone in the room a notification when a meeting is proposed and again when it's set, and taps land on the right meeting.
gotchas: Two kinds, both fanned out by _notify_meeting_room: meeting_proposed ("{name} wants to schedule: {title}" / "Tap to mark when you're free") and meeting_scheduled. _notify skips the actor and honours the recipient's profiles.notif_types (only help_urgent is exempt from that gate).

The fan-out predicate is CLOSE TO but not identical to the read gate: committee → committee_roster rows for that slug with linked_user_id is not null and (area is null OR the area / '<area> · Lead' in roles[]); house → profiles in that house. Both read gates additionally return true for an app admin, so an admin who isn't roster-linked (or isn't in the house) CAN READ a meeting and is NEVER TOLD about it.
⚠️ For family scope the fan-out is `from public.profiles p` with no filter at all — every profile row, including unapproved signups who can't read the meeting.

In-app is ON by default (both kinds are in the live notif_types column default). PHONE PUSH IS OFF BY DEFAULT — neither is in DEFAULT_PUSH_TYPES, though both are in apns-sender.js's PUSHABLE set, gated on push_types.includes(n.type). A member must opt in per category (push_types defaults to '{}': no push at all until the first-run prompt is accepted).

Deep links live in the notification's url and are WEB paths, built by _meeting_url: /posts?c=<slug>[&area=<area>]&meeting=<id>, /posts?house=<slug>&meeting=<id>, or /events?meeting=<id> for family. The one exception is finalize_meeting_as_event, which sends /events?open=<event id>.

APNs payload is { title, body, url: APP_URL + n.url, type, target_type: n.entity_type, target_id: n.entity_id } — 'meeting' / the meeting id here, 'chat_poll' / the poll id for polls — so PREFER target_type/target_id over parsing the URL.
For a finalize-as-event notification, target_id is the MEETING id while the url points at the EVENT — route deliberately.
features.nativeOpportunity: APNs carries target_type/target_id, so route natively off those instead of parsing web URL paths — which also sidesteps the finalize-as-event url/entity mismatch.

features.name: Fixing the three duplicated database functions (hand the SQL to Brian)
features.whatItDoes: A one-time database cleanup, without which family-wide date polls, whole-date-range options, and "yes I'm still coming" confirmations cannot work at all.
rpcs: create_meeting(p_scope, p_committee_id, p_area, p_house_id, p_title, p_description, p_slots, p_respond_by, p_email) -> uuid
create_scheduled_meeting(p_scope, p_committee_id, p_area, p_house_id, p_title, p_description, p_starts_at, p_duration_min, p_meet_url, p_ends_at) -> uuid
drop function if exists public.create_meeting(text, uuid, text, uuid, text, text, jsonb, date)
drop function if exists public.create_scheduled_meeting(text, uuid, text, uuid, text, text, timestamptz, int, text)
drop function if exists public.set_event_attendance(text, text, jsonb)
migrations: 0092/0108 (the earlier cabins dual-overload trap this repeats)
gotchas: Repo convention: DB changes are HANDED OVER AS SQL for Brian to run, never applied by an agent. The full, ready-to-run script is in §A.6 of the doc and is a no-op for existing rows.

create_meeting: 9-arg (0117, ends p_respond_by date, p_email boolean) rejects 'family' with raise exception 'Invalid scope' and silently drops ends_at; 8-arg (0122, ends p_respond_by date) allows family and honours ends_at but has no notify_email. A p_email-carrying body can only bind the broken one; an 8-key body returns HTTP 300 PGRST203. The fix keeps ONE create_meeting — the 9-arg signature with 0122's family + ends_at body merged in.
create_scheduled_meeting: same duplication (9-arg 0119 vs 10-arg 0122 with p_ends_at). The fix drops the stale 9-arg. Until then, always send p_ends_at explicitly.

set_event_attendance: the trap a THIRD time. 0036 dropped the 3-arg and created a 4-arg (…, p_title) that fans out event_rsvp; 0122 then `create or replace`d the 3-ARG to add confirmed = true — a new overload, not a fix. Every client sends p_title, so the 4-arg (no `confirmed`) runs and nothing can ever clear confirmed = false; a 3-key call is PGRST203. The fix keeps the 4-arg and adds `confirmed = true` to its upsert.

History worth knowing: 0117 deliberately dropped 0116's 8-arg version "so there is only ONE overload — avoids the dual-overload trap from cabins 0092/0108". Then 0122 `create or replace`d an 8-arg signature, which CREATED A SECOND OVERLOAD instead of replacing anything, re-opening the exact trap 0117 called out.

UNTIL IT RUNS: ship iOS v1 as committee/house + point-in-time slots only (always sending p_email), and skip family scope, date ranges, finalize-as-event's reconfirm loop, and the unconfirmed-RSVP surface.
AFTER IT RUNS: always send all 9 / all 10 keys explicitly — Swift's Encodable omits nil keys, and an omitted key changes (or breaks) overload resolution.

features.name: Loading a room's quick polls and your own answers
features.whatItDoes: Fetches every poll in a committee or house chat with its vote counts and which options you personally picked.
endpoints: POST /rest/v1/rpc/fetch_chat_polls_for_room — returns jsonb; decode [ChatPollRow].self straight off .execute(), don't wrap it
DO NOT USE: chat_polls?select=id,chat_poll_options(...) — returns HTTP 300 PGRST201 (probed live)
migrations: 0183 (verified-member read tightening — deliberately left these tables alone)
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ NEVER read chat_poll_votes. It has RLS enabled and ZERO policies — but the table grants still exist (anon AND authenticated both hold SELECT; the migration header claims it gets "NO select grant at all", which never happened, and Supabase's default privileges granted it anyway). So a from("chat_poll_votes").select() does NOT 403 and does NOT error: probed live it returns [], HTTP 200, NO ERROR — always, for everyone, including for your own votes. Build a tally off that query and you ship a poll UI that permanently reads "0 votes" and looks like a data problem. Same failure mode as the committee_areas incident; when a list reads empty but writes clearly work, check pg_policies FIRST.

Tallies come from denormalised columns only: chat_poll_options.vote_count and chat_polls.respondent_count (distinct voters), both maintained by the AFTER INSERT OR DELETE row trigger chat_poll_votes_recount (function _chat_poll_votes_recount). These are the only numbers you should ever display.

⚠️ Don't skip the RPC to read the two readable tables directly: chat_polls?select=id,chat_poll_options(...) ALSO returns HTTP 300 PGRST201 (probed live), because chat_poll_votes forms a second, many-to-many relationship between them. You'd have to write chat_poll_options!chat_poll_options_poll_id_fkey(...) — and you'd still be missing my_option_ids, and every count would need the unreadable votes table.

fetch_chat_polls_for_room RE-CHECKS MEMBERSHIP ITSELF (a SECURITY DEFINER function bypasses your RLS), so passing someone else's committee/house id returns [] rather than leaking — which means empty is still AMBIGUOUS between "not a member" and "no polls".

It matches on p.committee_id = p_committee_id (the committee UUID, NOT the slug) and p.area is not distinct from p_area, so null really does mean the General channel. Results come back newest-first (order by t.created_at desc).
Both this and chat_poll_voters return jsonb, not a table — PostgREST puts the array in the response body directly.

Field shapes: options always present and sorted by position server-side; my_option_ids coalesced to [], never null; created_by_me is server-computed (created_by = auth.uid()); closes_on is a bare "YYYY-MM-DD" — decode as String.
scope_type is 'committee' | 'house' ONLY — there is no 'family' poll, and the Main Feed isn't a room.

RLS reads: chat_polls readable iff you can access its room (can_access_committee_area(committee_id, area) for committee, is_house_member(house_id) for house); chat_poll_options iff its parent poll is; chat_poll_votes by nobody, ever.
Signed OUT gives HTTP 401 42501 "permission denied for function is_house_member" — treat as "no session", never fire before the session is restored.
Cache keyed by the REAL uid (web caches under chatPolls.<uid>.<roomKey>) and cleared on sign-out.
Never swallow a read error into [] — log PGRST201 / PGRST203 / 42501 distinctly.

features.name: Polls appearing in the conversation where they happened
features.whatItDoes: Mixes polls into the chat's message list in time order, so a poll shows up right where it was asked instead of in a bar you scroll past.
gotchas: enum TimelineItem { case message(Msg), poll(ChatPoll) } — sorted ASCENDING by ts (message) / createdAt (poll), then run through the same day-grouping you already use for date separators.
The first cut pinned open polls in a top bar mirroring MeetingSection and it was TOO EASY TO MISS, because that isn't where anyone is looking. Don't rebuild that.
A poll renders as a full-width, ROOM-WIDE card — not attached to any sender's bubble, no avatar gutter.

features.name: The poll card itself
features.whatItDoes: Shows the question, each option with a filled bar and its share of the vote, a check on your own picks, and who voted for what when the poll isn't anonymous.
gotchas: Per-option bar fill is vote_count / respondent_count — RESPONDENTS, not total votes, so a multi-select poll can legitimately sum past 100%.
A ✓ on your own picks; vote_count · pct on the right.

A row of ≤8 small avatars under each option when the poll isn't anonymous (+N beyond that); the write-in renders as `name: text` lines instead of avatars; for an anonymous poll with write-ins, a bare "N write-in answers (anonymous)".
Close/Delete sit on the card for isAdmin || created_by_me.
Interactive in place: tapping an option votes immediately, no sheet.
Display only the trigger-maintained counts — never a count derived from chat_poll_votes (which always reads []).
Derive `closed` yourself (is_closed OR past closes_on) before disabling anything — web gets this wrong.

features.name: Voting in a chat poll
features.whatItDoes: Tapping an option records your answer right away, and you can change it while the poll is open.
gotchas: ⚠️ set_chat_poll_votes is a FULL REPLACE of your own rows — it deletes any of your votes not in p_option_ids. For a single-select poll always send exactly one id; for multi-select send the COMPLETE new set, never a delta.
p_option_ids is uuid[] → send [String] of uuid strings; an EMPTY array is the valid "clear my vote" payload.

It raises on: a closed poll, an option id not in the poll, more than one id when allow_multiple is false, and "Other" selected with blank text ("Say what \"Other\" means") — so validate the write-in before sending.
Multi-select means several chat_poll_votes rows per voter (PK is (poll_id, option_id, user_id)).
⚠️ If you paint optimistically, remember respondent_count is DISTINCT VOTERS: adding your second pick in a multi-select must NOT increment it.
Never verify a vote landed by reading chat_poll_votes — it returns [] with no error, forever.
Writes must be a no-op while previewing as another member.
features.nativeOpportunity: Web's vote path is not optimistic — it awaits the RPC then refetches the whole room (if (!error) await reloadPolls()), so a tap visibly lags. Worth doing better natively.

features.name: Starting a poll in a chat
features.whatItDoes: Any member of a committee or house chat can ask the room a question with 2–10 answers, choosing single- or multi-select and whether results are anonymous.
rpcs: create_chat_poll(p_scope, p_committee_id, p_area, p_house_id, p_question, p_options, p_allow_multiple, p_anonymous, p_allow_other, p_closes_on) -> uuid
gotchas: NO organizer gate — the doctrine difference from meetings: anyone who can read the room can start a poll. Any room member creates.
It refuses in an ARCHIVED committee area.
p_options is text[] → [String]. Blank entries are dropped server-side; what's left must be 2–10 or it raises.
An "Other" slot is APPENDED AUTOMATICALLY when p_allow_other is true (label 'Other', is_other = true) and does NOT count against the 10.
question is ≤300 chars, enforced.
closes_on null ⇒ open until closed by hand; it's a bare date, not an instant.
Swift's Encodable omits nil keys — encode nulls explicitly (custom encode(to:) or [String: AnyJSON] with AnyJSON.null).

Entry point placement is deliberate: Poll lives in the room's ⋯ menu (with "📅 Schedule a meeting" and "✉️ Email members") precisely BECAUSE it is not a file picker. The rule from the picker incident: if an action needs to live behind a menu, it must not be a file picker — move the other actions there instead. (The standalone, non-embedded chat route has no ⋯ menu, so it keeps a poll button in the composer next to +.)
scope is committee | house only; a MeetingScope is a superset — just drop the "family" case.

features.name: Closing or deleting a poll
features.whatItDoes: The person who started a poll (or an admin) can stop it taking votes, or remove it from the chat entirely.
gotchas: Creator or admin only; delete cascades options + votes.
Close/Delete sit right on the card for isAdmin || created_by_me — no sheet.
There is NO notification on vote or close (mirrors family polls).
Use a native alert for the confirmation; web's window.confirm doesn't transfer.

features.name: Seeing who voted for what
features.whatItDoes: On a poll that isn't anonymous, shows little avatars of the people behind each option (and their write-in text).
gotchas: Identity is revealed in EXACTLY ONE PLACE: chat_poll_voters(p_poll). It returns '[]'::jsonb when chat_polls.anonymous is true, and raises 'Not authorized' for a non-member. The server refuses — your client never has to be trusted with the check. (Web's ChatPollCard still short-circuits on poll.anonymous as an optimisation, but the guarantee is server-side.)
Returns jsonb, not a table. VoterRow: { option_id, user_id, name, avatar_url, other_text }.
One extra call per card — call it once per card mount.
≤8 avatars per option, +N beyond that; write-ins render as `name: text` lines instead of avatars.
Deferred in the recommended v1 cut ("defer cheaply").

features.name: The "Other" write-in answer
features.whatItDoes: Lets a poll accept a typed-in answer of your own instead of only the listed options.
rpcs: create_chat_poll(p_scope, p_committee_id, p_area, p_house_id, p_question, p_options, p_allow_multiple, p_anonymous, p_allow_other, p_closes_on) -> uuid
gotchas: The Other option is appended SERVER-SIDE when p_allow_other is true (label 'Other', is_other = true) and does not count against the 2–10 limit — don't add your own row for it.
set_chat_poll_votes raises when Other is selected with blank text ("Say what \"Other\" means") — validate the write-in before sending.
other_text lives on the unreadable chat_poll_votes, but your own value comes back as my_other_text from fetch_chat_polls_for_room.
Write-ins render as `name: text` lines instead of avatars; for an anonymous poll with write-ins, show a bare "N write-in answers (anonymous)".
Deferred in the recommended v1 cut (an extra option kind plus an inline text field and its error state).

features.name: A poll that closes on its own date
features.whatItDoes: A poll can be set to stop taking votes after a given day, and the card should show it as closed once that day has passed.
gotchas: The server rejects a vote when is_closed OR (closes_on is not null AND closes_on < current_date).

⚠️ A small web bug NOT to copy: ChatPollCard only checks poll.isClosed (every disabled= on the card is poll.isClosed), so a poll past its closes_on still renders as votable and the tap fails server-side with "This poll is closed".
Derive it properly on iOS: closed = is_closed || (closes_on != nil && closes_on! < todayYMD), comparing the STRINGS as calendar days.
The database session timezone is UTC (verified), so current_date flips in the early evening Central — the boundary is fuzzy by a few hours either way. Don't try to be cleverer than a day comparison.
closes_on is a bare YYYY-MM-DD — never parse it as a UTC instant and format locally (the 0168 day-shift bug).
Deferred in the recommended v1 cut.

features.name: Poll counts moving live
features.whatItDoes: Vote counts on a poll card update as other people vote, without a refresh.
gotchas: One channel chat-polls-<roomKey> on chat_polls and chat_poll_options — NEVER votes — debounced ~250ms → refetch via fetch_chat_polls_for_room.
Realtime publishes chat_polls + chat_poll_options only; chat_poll_votes is deliberately NOT in the publication ("there is nothing safe to broadcast from it"), confirmed against pg_publication_tables.
This still works: someone else voting fires the recount trigger, which UPDATEs chat_poll_options, which arrives on your channel — so tallies move live without any vote row ever crossing the wire.
Call the hook unconditionally per the rules of hooks even before the room/committee id resolves — scope stays null until then and the subscription no-ops.
Tear the channel down when the room closes; realtime honours RLS.

features.name: Getting told a poll was started
features.whatItDoes: Everyone in the room gets a notification when someone starts a poll, and tapping it opens that room.
gotchas: One kind: chat_poll_created (entity_type = 'chat_poll'), in-app ON by default, phone push OPT-IN, relayed by apns-sender.js. No notification on vote or close.

⚠️ The deep link is /posts?c=<slug>[&area=]&poll=<id> (or ?house=<slug>&poll=<id>), but NO WEB CLIENT CODE READS ?poll= AT ALL (grep-confirmed) — the link opens the room and drops you wherever the room happens to scroll. The id in the URL is currently decorative.
APNs payload carries target_type / target_id ('chat_poll' / the poll id) — prefer those over parsing the URL.
features.nativeOpportunity: Wire target_id to scroll-and-flash the poll inside the room — nicer than web, where nothing reads ?poll= at all.

features.name: Attaching a photo, video, or file in a room chat
features.whatItDoes: Lets someone add a photo, take one, or pick a file while chatting in a committee or house room.
webFiles: CommitteeChat.tsx:1040–1046 (plain always-mounted trigger + input, deliberately no accept filter)
PostsView.tsx (the Main Feed composer that was never broken)
gotchas: Background: attaching a photo in a committee/house chat was SILENTLY, COMPLETELY DEAD in the installed iOS PWA for as long as the `+` popup menu existed — the native picker opened, you could select a photo and tap the checkmark, and NOTHING arrived in the composer, with no error of any kind. Non-standalone Safari was fine.

THREE fixes were attempted and ALL FAILED on-device — recorded so nobody retries them: (1) mounting the inputs unconditionally at the composer root, outside the menu; (2) not closing the menu on tap so it only dismissed after the picker resolved; (3) sr-only instead of hidden.

What actually fixed it was DELETING THE POPUP, not the `+`. The glyph was never the problem. Today the trigger and input are plain always-mounted siblings, no overlay, nothing conditionally rendered anywhere in the path.

The rule that came out of it: if an action needs to live behind a menu, it must NOT be a file picker — move the other actions there instead (which is exactly where Poll, "Schedule a meeting" and "Email members" went).
⚠️ Do NOT port web's "one unfiltered button" compromise. That existed only because iOS's own action sheet had to stand in for three destinations.

The transferable lesson is PRESENTER LIFETIME: attach .photosPicker(isPresented:) / .sheet / .fullScreenCover to a STABLE PARENT (the composer root), and never let the action that opens the picker also dismiss the thing that owns it. A Menu item, popover, or context menu that tears itself down while presenting is the same class of mistake, and in SwiftUI it presents as the same symptom — the picker appears, the user picks, and your onChange/completion never fires. Keep the selection binding on the composer's own state, not on the menu's.

⚠️ Verify on a REAL DEVICE in the REAL INSTALLED APP. Every server-side check on the web bug came back healthy — HTTP 200, clean console, valid manifest — so curl and a headless browser both said "fine" while the feature was 100% broken for the family. Natively, the simulator's photo library and a canned asset will happily pass a flow that fails against a real camera roll, a HEIC original, or an iCloud-optimised photo that has to download first.
Capture metadata: <canvas>/re-encode strips EXIF, so read capture metadata off the ORIGINAL asset before any resize.
The accepted web regression was losing the one-tap capture="environment" camera shortcut — native gets it back for free.
features.nativeOpportunity: PhotosPicker and UIImagePickerController are not affected by the WebKit/PWA bug at all, and you get real camera + Files + library APIs instead of one unfiltered <input>. Offer Photo Library / Take Photo / Choose File as three explicit destinations — what the web menu was trying to be. Also take PHAsset.creationDate, which is strictly better than what web can read.

features.name: See the house's shared lists
features.whatItDoes: Open a screen showing every list your house has going — the grocery run, the cabin close-up checklist, what to pack — with each list's items and how many are done.
gotchas: Backend is LIVE — no migration, RPC or policy needs to be written for any of this; you are writing Swift against schema that already exists (verified against the live DB 2026-08-10).
Two migrations share the number 0172 in this repo (0172_committee_leads_chat_and_lead_roster.sql and 0172_callout_drop_box_and_fest_album.sql) — search by full filename, not by number.

RLS read on house_lists is `is_house_member(house_id)` (your profiles.house_id equals that house, OR you are an app admin). house_list_items is the identical rule on the item's own house_id column. Those are the ONLY policies on either table: one SELECT policy each and ZERO INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies at all.
⚠️ Therefore an empty result is "not permitted," not "no data."
Live counts as of 2026-08-10: house_lists = 0 rows, house_list_items = 0 rows. You must create the first list from the web app or an empty iOS screen proves nothing.

⚠️⚠️ house_list_items has TWO foreign keys to profiles (created_by and checked_by), so a bare profiles(display_name) embed is ambiguous — PostgREST answers HTTP 300 / PGRST201, which the client sees as an EMPTY ARRAY, not an error. Name the FK exactly: `author:created_by(display_name)` and `checker:checked_by(display_name)`. This class of bug already bit a tournaments ↔ tournament_entrants embed. If the list screen renders empty while the RPCs clearly work, check the embed spelling before anything else.

Web's one-round-trip select is: `id, house_id, title, emoji, note, position, created_by, created_at, updated_at, author:created_by(display_name), house_list_items(id, list_id, text, checked_at, checked_by, created_by, created_at, position, checker:checked_by(display_name))`.

Zero-embed-risk alternative: two flat queries (house_lists filtered by house, house_list_items filtered by house — the denormalised house_id is exactly what makes that possible without a join) plus one profiles fetch for the checked_by ids, stitched client-side. Perfectly acceptable.

A joined profile embed decodes as an object OR a 1-element array depending on the FK shape (web's `embeddedName` handles both) — prefer the flat-queries route, or write a small @propertyWrapper / custom init(from:) that tolerates both.

⚠️ Timestamps: these are timestamptz and PostgREST serialises them with MICROSECOND fractional seconds (2026-08-09T18:22:41.123456+00:00). JSONDecoder.DateDecodingStrategy.iso8601 rejects fractional seconds and you get a decode failure that looks like a schema mismatch. Reuse the decoder the existing HouseStay model already uses (it decodes house_stays.created_at, same timestamptz) rather than introducing a second one.
Good news: no bare `date` column anywhere in house lists — everything is timestamptz, so the web YYYY-MM-DD-parsed-as-UTC-midnight day-shift bug cannot occur here.

Sorting: query `.order("position", ascending: true).order("created_at", ascending: false)` for lists (newest first, because create assigns min - 1). Items are sorted CLIENT-SIDE, not by the server: open items first in insertion order (web sorts by checked_at presence, then created_at ascending), checked ones settling to the bottom. Client-side is deliberate — it keeps the fetch to one round-trip and lets an optimistic check re-sort instantly without a refetch.
Progress string: "{done} of {total} done", or "All N done", or "Empty — add the first item" for a list with no items. Used both on the list card and as the House Hub row subtitle.
There is NO media on lists — no *_media child table, nothing to upload, no moderation path. A real simplification versus work items.
⚠️ `position` exists on items but there is no reorder RPC and no UPDATE policy — do NOT build drag-to-reorder. There is no server-side write path for it; the column only records insertion order.

No notifications, by design: no trigger, no _notify call, no notif_types entry, no PushType — nothing outside 0169_house_lists.sql references these tables at all ("a grocery run would spam the whole house"). Do NOT add a local notification, a badge, or an APNs category for lists. Contrast work_item_created, which DOES notify + push (0070) — easy to copy the wrong neighbour.

No localStorage idiom to port. Web caches under a `houseLists.<houseId>` stale-while-revalidate key (useCachedResource, persist: "local"). If you mirror it, key it on the HOUSE id as web does — a list cache keyed on house id is fine because the house is the audience — but wipe it on sign-out (a shared cache key once leaked one member's cached private chat to the next user on the device).
Neither table was touched by migration 0183 — is_house_member is the whole gate, and it already implies an approved account in practice (an unapproved signup has no house assigned).
Don't merge this with work items: house lists are the shared scratchpad; the house's tracked, author-owned work stays in work_items (migration 0066, which iOS already has).

features.name: Start a new list
features.whatItDoes: Anyone in the house can start a list with a name, an emoji handle, and an optional note.
rpcs: create_house_list(p_house uuid, p_title text, p_emoji text DEFAULT '📝', p_note text DEFAULT NULL) -> uuid (new list id)
gotchas: Deliberately ONE flexible shape — a list is a title + items and every item can be checked off, so a shopping list and a checklist are the same thing and there is NO "kind" to pick at creation time.
Sorts a new list to the TOP: position = coalesce(min(position), 0) - 1 over that house. So position ascending = newest first.
Every mutation must go through an RPC. A direct INSERT raises 42501 (new row violates row-level security policy) — there are zero INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies on either table.

All nine list RPCs are SECURITY DEFINER, set search_path = '', revoked from public/anon and granted to authenticated. Supabase RPC calls are keyed by parameter NAME, so a typo fails at runtime with PGRST202 function ... does not exist.
Returns a BARE JSON string — decode as UUID or String, not an object or an array.
Server-side truncation, silently: title is `left(…, 120)`. Cap your text field at 120 so the user isn't surprised.
Empty input raises, and the message is user-facing copy you can show directly: 'A list needs a name', 'Not a member of this house', 'Sign in required'.
emoji is NOT NULL with a server-side default of '📝' — never nil in the Swift model.
Never send updated_at: it is maintained server-side on both tables by before-update triggers house_lists_set_updated_at / house_list_items_set_updated_at, both executing public.set_updated_at().
Writes are gated on MEMBERSHIP, not authorship — every RPC checks is_house_member(...) and nothing about who created the row.

features.name: Rename a list, change its emoji, or edit its note
features.whatItDoes: Any member of the house can retitle a list, swap its emoji, or change the note under it.
rpcs: update_house_list(p_id uuid, p_title text, p_emoji text DEFAULT NULL, p_note text DEFAULT NULL) -> void
gotchas: ⚠️ ASYMMETRIC ABOUT NIL. p_emoji = nil KEEPS the existing emoji (coalesce(nullif(btrim(coalesce(p_emoji,'')),''), emoji)), but p_note = nil CLEARS the note to NULL (note = nullif(btrim(coalesce(p_note,'')),''), applied unconditionally). A Swift "partial update" struct that omits note will silently wipe it — always send the current note.
p_title must be non-empty on EVERY call — you cannot update just the note. Empty raises 'A list needs a name'.
Raises 'List not found' if the row is gone (unlike the deletes, which are idempotent).
title is silently truncated with left(…, 120).
void RPCs return an empty body — don't try to decode a response, or you'll get a "data is empty" error on a call that actually succeeded.

Membership, not authorship: any member may rename or re-emoji ANY list, including one someone else made. Do NOT add an author check in the iOS UI or the two apps will disagree on screen for the same house. (Contrast house_stays / update_house_stay, which really is author-or-admin and raises 'Not authorized' — the two house features deliberately differ.)
The doc's v1 can defer this entirely (rename / re-emoji / the note field).

features.name: Delete a list
features.whatItDoes: Any member of the house can throw away a whole list once it's done with.
gotchas: Idempotent — returns quietly if the row is already gone.
Items cascade (house_list_items.list_id -> house_lists(id) on delete cascade), so expect a burst of DELETE realtime payloads.

⚠️⚠️ A direct table DELETE from iOS fails in the WORST possible way: silently. With RLS on and no DELETE policy, Postgres FILTERS the rows instead of erroring, so the statement matches 0 rows and PostgREST returns success (204 / empty array). Only INSERTs raise 42501. Never trust "no error" as "it wrote."
Membership, not authorship — any member can delete any list.

features.name: Add something to a list
features.whatItDoes: Type a line — milk, close the shutters, bug spray — and it lands at the bottom of the list for everyone in the house.
rpcs: add_house_list_item(p_list uuid, p_text text) -> uuid (new item id)
gotchas: Appends: position = coalesce(max(position), 0) + 1 within the list.
Returns a BARE JSON string — decode as UUID or String.
Server-side truncation, silently: item text is `left(…, 300)`. Cap the field at 300.
Empty input raises 'An item needs some text'; a missing parent raises 'List not found'.

⚠️ NEVER send house_id yourself. It is denormalised onto the item row on purpose (flat RLS with no join, and a Realtime filter with no join — Supabase postgres_changes filters are single-column predicates on the changed row). Every RPC copies it from the parent list AND a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF list_id trigger `trg_house_list_item_sync_house` re-derives it from house_lists (function house_list_item_sync_house()), raising 'List not found' if the parent is missing.

⚠️ Never try to call house_list_item_sync_house() as an RPC — it is a trigger function and EXECUTE is revoked from public, anon and authenticated specifically so it isn't reachable. The trigger still fires (it runs as the table owner).
Membership, not authorship — anyone in the house can add to any list.
Don't waste an hour on a direct .from("house_list_items").insert(...) — it raises 42501; the RPC is the only write path.

features.name: Check something off (and un-check it)
features.whatItDoes: Tap the box next to an item to mark it done, or tap again to put it back on the list.
gotchas: "Checked" is a STAMP, not a boolean: checked_at timestamptz NULL + checked_by uuid NULL. `checked_at IS NULL` means OPEN. In Swift: `var isChecked: Bool { checkedAt != nil }` — checkedAt IS the boolean.
Passing p_checked: false CLEARS BOTH columns (checked_at = null, checked_by = null) deliberately, "so the stamp never lies." Don't preserve checked_by on uncheck.
Raises 'Item not found'.

⚠️⚠️ A direct .from("house_list_items").update(...) can NEVER work and will NEVER complain: with RLS on and no UPDATE policy, Postgres filters the rows, the statement matches 0 rows, and PostgREST returns success (204 / empty array). Your checkbox will appear to save and change nothing in the database, forever.

Optimistic checkbox is required, not optional: web keeps a local [itemID: Bool] override so the box flips instantly and drops the entry once the write settles. Without it the checkbox waits on an RPC round-trip and feels broken.
void RPC — empty response body; don't decode it.

Membership, not authorship: any member can check or uncheck any item, including one someone else added. That is the design — "the person who got the milk is rarely the person who wrote it down." Do NOT hide the affordance behind item.createdBy == effectiveUserId.
No notification/badge/push for a check, by design.

features.name: "Got by {name}" under a checked item
features.whatItDoes: A checked-off item shows who got the milk or closed the windows, and when.
gotchas: The stamp exists precisely so the list also answers "who got the milk / who closed the windows, and when." Web renders `Got by {name}` under a checked row.
To render the name you need the profile behind checked_by — that means either the FK-named embed `checker:checked_by(display_name)` or a separate profiles fetch for the checked_by ids.
⚠️ A bare profiles(display_name) embed here is ambiguous (two FKs to profiles: created_by and checked_by) → HTTP 300 / PGRST201 → the client sees an EMPTY ARRAY with no error.
checked_by is `on delete set null` on profiles(id), so a removed member leaves a checked item with a null name — render the checked state without a name rather than dropping the row.

features.name: Fix the wording of an item
features.whatItDoes: Edit an item's text — "milk" becomes "2% milk, 2 gallons".
gotchas: Raises 'Item not found'; empty text raises 'An item needs some text'.
Silently truncated with left(…, 300).
Membership, not authorship — anyone in the house may edit anyone's item.
The doc's v1 explicitly defers item text editing.

features.name: Remove an item from a list
features.whatItDoes: Delete a line off the list outright, instead of checking it off.
gotchas: Idempotent — returns quietly if the row is already gone.
A direct table DELETE matches 0 rows and returns SUCCESS (RLS filters, it does not raise) — must go through the RPC.
Membership, not authorship.

features.name: "We're home from the store" — clear the checked items
features.whatItDoes: One tap deletes everything already checked off, so a shopping list doesn't have to be rebuilt by hand next time.
rpcs: clear_checked_house_list_items(p_list uuid) -> integer (how many were deleted)
gotchas: One of the two sweeps that are the whole recurring-list story — worth shipping in v1 ("one RPC each, and they're the reason a recurring list works at all").
Returns a BARE number → decode as Int, not an object or array.
Raises 'List not found'.
Can fire a dozen DELETEs in one statement — this is exactly why the Realtime strategy is debounce-then-refetch rather than patching rows.
Membership, not authorship.

features.name: Reuse a checklist next trip
features.whatItDoes: One tap un-checks every item so the cabin close-up checklist is ready to run again.
rpcs: uncheck_house_list_items(p_list uuid) -> integer (how many were reset)
gotchas: The second recurring-list sweep — keep it in v1.
Returns a BARE number → Int.
Raises 'List not found'.
It clears BOTH checked_at and checked_by on every reset row (the stamp never lies) — don't try to preserve who checked it.
Membership, not authorship.

features.name: Lists update live while you're looking at them
features.whatItDoes: When someone else in the house adds or checks something, it appears on your screen without a refresh.
gotchas: Both tables are in the supabase_realtime publication and both are REPLICA IDENTITY FULL (verified relreplident = 'f'). Full replica identity is what makes the DELETE payload carry the whole old row — which is what lets the house_id filter apply to deletes at all.

Web subscribes ONE channel with TWO postgres_changes listeners, both filtered house_id=eq.<houseId>: `schema: public, table: house_lists, filter: house_id=eq.<uuid>` and `schema: public, table: house_list_items, filter: house_id=eq.<uuid>`.

Debounce a FULL REFETCH by 250 ms rather than patching rows — clear_checked_house_list_items can fire a dozen DELETEs in one statement and the payloads are small enough that a refetch is cheaper than reconciling.

The denormalised house_id on items is what makes this possible at all: Realtime filters are single-column predicates on the changed row, so without it you'd have to subscribe to every item change in the database and filter client-side.
Lists are a quiet pull-only surface kept live by Realtime while the screen is open — no notifications, no badge.

features.name: Lists row on the House Hub
features.whatItDoes: The house's home screen shows the top list and how far along it is, and taps through to all the lists.
gotchas: On web this is a Lists section on the House Hub whose subtitle is the top list plus its progress: "{emoji} {title} · {progress} · +N more", linking to /house/lists?house=<slug>.
iOS already has HouseHubView (per the web repo's iOS-parity note), so a row there → a new lists screen is the natural placement.
Reuse the same progress string as the list card ("{done} of {total} done" / "All N done" / "Empty — add the first item").
With 0 lists in the database today the row must render a sensible empty state rather than a misleading blank.

features.name: A private Leads room appears for people who lead a committee
features.whatItDoes: If you lead a committee (or one of its subcommittees), a private room for just the leads shows up in your chat list — and nobody else, not even an admin, sees it.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ READ FIRST: 0177 CHANGED the lead predicate — do NOT implement 0172's version. can_access_committee_area's 'leads' branch now calls is_committee_lead(cid), NOT is_committee_area_lead(cid). (0177 is the newest of three definitions: 0063 → 0172 → 0177.)

The 0172 functions is_committee_area_lead(cid) / is_committee_area_lead_slug(p_slug) still exist but are wired into nothing (grep confirms zero live callers outside 0172). If you call is_committee_area_lead for a client-side check, a committee-level lead of a role-less committee will be told they aren't a lead — while the database happily lets them into the room.

The predicate, exactly: there is a committee_roster row for this committee whose linked_user_id = auth.uid(), AND that row either has is_lead = true OR holds at least one roles[] entry matching LIKE '% · Lead'. Both functions are SECURITY DEFINER, STABLE, granted to authenticated.

⚠️⚠️ is_committee_lead is an OLD name that 0177 REDEFINED — do not read "0177" as "new function". Since 0015_roles_and_alerts.sql it meant committee_members.role = 'Lead' OR profiles.is_admin. 0177 issued create or replace on the same name/signature, so the roster-based body is live — but that also silently repointed every other caller: review_join_request, set_committee_areas, set_committee_lead, reject_committee_admin, the committee_join_requests read/delete policies, and the email-recipient helper. ALL of those now EXCLUDE plain app admins (the 0177 body has no is_admin clause). Don't assume "admin" gets through any RPC gated on is_committee_lead, and don't reuse the name for a Swift helper meaning the 0015 thing.

⚠️ There is NO admin override, deliberately: both functions exclude profiles.is_admin entirely ("the Leads chat is for actual leads only — an admin who isn't a lead of the committee is not in its Leads room"). Compute the Leads channel from the viewer's OWN roster rows, never from isAdmin. An admin who isn't a lead sees no Leads room and gets zero rows if they force the query — that is the feature working. This is the OPPOSITE of every other branch of can_access_committee_area, which does grant admins; it's the one asymmetry in the whole chat gate.

⚠️ linked_user_id is the key, not name or email. An account-less roster lead (one of the 5 current lead rows — Lauren Zerfas, seeded in 0056 with a null email) is a lead on paper and can never enter the room, because there is no auth.uid() to match. Correct behaviour, not a bug to work around.
is_lead boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false on committee_roster (added by 0177) is committee-WIDE and needs no subcommittee. Currently 0 rows have it set.

⚠️ Mirror the real-'Leads'-area guard, and mirror the SQL version, NOT the web version. SQL-faithful check: does committee_areas contain a row for this committee with lower(area) = 'leads'? If yes, do NOT synthesise a Leads channel at all. Web checks `iAmLead && !committeeArchived && !myAreas.includes("Leads")` — i.e. do I personally hold an area named Leads — which is NARROWER and has a latent bug: a lead of some other role on a committee that has a real "Leads" role would get a room that reads empty and refuses their messages. Do keep web's other two conditions: you must lead something there, and skip archived committees.
You're already fetching committee_areas to build the area channels, so the guard costs nothing. Currently 0 committees have a real "Leads" area, so the sentinel branch is live everywhere.

The guard is why the sentinel is safe and why the word did NOT have to be reserved in add_committee_area / rename_committee_area — if an admin names a real role "Leads", the branch backs off and 'Leads' behaves as an ordinary area for that committee.

valid_committee_areas(cid, areas) (0073) rejects 'general' and any area not in committee_areas, so nobody can be ASSIGNED the role "Leads" through the RPCs that call it (request_to_join, review_join_request, set_committee_areas, set_my_committee_areas). ⚠️ It is NOT a table constraint — Part C's roster writes are direct table writes gated only by RLS, so an admin or lead can put any string including 'Leads' into committee_roster.roles. The sentinel survives (a plain 'Leads' never matches LIKE '% · Lead'), but don't lean on validation that isn't in your write path.

TESTING: family-fest is the ONLY committee with a reachable Leads room today. Live data 2026-08-10 — 5 roster rows carry a ' · Lead' role, all on committee_slug = 'family-fest' (4 of them linked to a real account); 0 rows have is_lead = true; 0 committee_messages with area = 'Leads'; 0 committees have a real role named "Leads". Sign in as one of those 4 accounts or nothing here is testable.

⚠️ committee_roster reads require an APPROVED member, not merely a signed-in one — 0183 swapped auth.uid() is not null for is_approved_member() (profiles.approved is true OR profiles.is_admin). A brand-new signup awaiting verification gets ZERO roster rows — no committees, no channels, no lead status, no Leads room — with NO error. If your channel list is mysteriously empty for a new test account, check profiles.approved first. (DB column is `approved`; the UI calls it "Verified" — don't unify the names.)

⚠️⚠️ Reading the roster hits the two-FKs-to-profiles embed trap: committee_roster references profiles(id) from BOTH linked_user_id and updated_by, so a bare profiles(display_name) embed answers HTTP 300 / PGRST201 and your client sees []. Name the FK: `profiles:linked_user_id(display_name, avatar_url)`.

features.name: Read and post in the Leads room
features.whatItDoes: The leads of a committee get a normal chat room of their own — messages, photos, reactions, replies — that only they can see.
gotchas: NO new tables. Messages live in committee_messages with area = 'Leads'. There is no leads table, no leads_messages, no flag column. area IS NULL = the committee-wide channel; 'Leads' = this room. iOS already has committee area chat, so this is one synthetic channel value, not a new chat implementation.

⚠️ Write the area string as EXACTLY "Leads" — capital L, no other casing. The RLS branch is case-insensitive (lower(p_area) = 'leads') so lowercase would still READ, but two other things compare it exactly: (1) committee_area_reads' primary key is (committee_id, user_id, area) on the RAW string, so "leads" and "Leads" become two separate unread/mute rows and your badge will never clear; (2) the mini's push senders (media-server/apns-sender.js, push-sender.js) both branch on msg.area === "Leads" to resolve recipients, and the mute lookup does .eq("area", msg.area || "") — a message stored with any other casing falls into the ordinary-area branch, matches nobody's roles[], and SILENTLY PUSHES TO NO ONE. Use one constant: `let leadsArea = "Leads"`, for the insert, the query, mark_area_read and set_area_mute.

⚠️ The read policy is NOT just can_access_committee_area. Its live definition (last rewritten by 0128_chat_moderation.sql) is: using ( can_access_committee_area(committee_id, area) and (status = 'visible' or author_id = auth.uid() or exists (select 1 from profiles p where p.id = auth.uid() and p.is_admin)) ).

committee_messages.status is text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'visible' CHECK (status IN ('visible','pending','hidden')).
