⚠️ Closing a room or a whole place only blocks NEW picks — cabin_room_availability / request_cabin_stay / set_booking_rooms all gate on `active`, but none touch existing cabin_booking_rooms rows. No cleanup step needed or wanted.
⚠️ set_booking_rooms deletes ALL existing links unconditionally before inserting, so passing nil or [] CLEARS the assignment — it is not a no-op.

cabin_room_availability returns 6 columns since 0094 (description was added, which required a DROP first); the picker shows 'Temporarily closed' (!active) vs 'Already booked' (!available) and disables a row only when !available && !selected.

features.name: "Not sure yet" + choose your room later
features.whatItDoes: Lets someone book without picking a room yet, then come back and choose it themselves once they know.
gotchas: ⚠️ An approved booking with NO room picked still consumes capacity: cabin_availability's room-based branch subtracts one slot (0108) and one bed (0111) per approved room-less overlapping booking. Before that fix a place read '4 of 4 rooms left' with a real guest already coming.
set_booking_rooms was admin-only until 0106 widened it to the booking's own requester (user_id = auth.uid()); the overlap check is identical either way, so a member cannot double-book.
Surface 'Choose your room' only when rooms.isEmpty AND the place has named rooms AND status is pending or approved — web fetches cabin_rooms per row to decide.

The approval-confirmation email nudges an unassigned requester because cabin_booking_notification returns room_names + cabin_has_rooms (0107) — nothing for iOS to send, but the copy the member already received refers to this screen.

features.name: Approve / deny a stay request
features.whatItDoes: Whoever reviews a place sees waiting requests and approves or denies them, optionally with a note that rides along in the email.
gotchas: 🚩⚠️⚠️ REGRESSION TO VERIFY: 0092 gave review_cabin_stay a per-room capacity branch; 0104 recreated the function from the 0032 body to add p_notify and DROPPED that branch, and 0114 carried the regressed body forward. The live function only runs the cabin-wide room_count check, so two pending requests for the SAME named room can both be approved and double-book it (Red & White House has room_count 4 but 5 named rooms). Verify with `select pg_get_functiondef(oid) from pg_proc where proname='review_cabin_stay'` and look for cabin_booking_rooms. Fix is server-side; do not compensate client-side.
⚠️ Canonical signature is the 4-arg (p_booking, p_approve, p_note, p_notify) — 0104 dropped the 3-arg form.

⚠️ p_notify defaults TRUE and works by PRE-STAMPING decision_email_sent_at when false, which 'claims' the row so the mac-mini mailer's `where ... is null` finds nothing. There is no 'send email' call to make.
The gate is is_cabin_approver(cabin_id) — app admin OR that place's named approver — not is_admin.

Surface the RPC's thrown message verbatim: the capacity refusals ('% is already booked for one or more of those nights', 'No rooms left in % for one or more of those nights') are the only place a conflict is reported.
A cancelled request cannot be reviewed ('That request was cancelled').
features.nativeOpportunity: Actionable Approve / Deny buttons on the cabin_request push (once the APNs handler exists) — the person who owns a bookable private house is exactly the user for whom opening an app is the friction.

features.name: A per-place approver who isn't an app admin
features.whatItDoes: Lets the owner of a private house review requests for their own place without giving them any other admin powers, and shows them their queue on the normal member-facing stay screen.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ The admin section stays admin-gated, so the queue MUST also be mounted on the member-facing stay screen for non-admins. Web renders `{!isAdmin && <AdminCabinBookings />}` and the component computes its own canManage = isAdmin || approvesAtLeastOnePlace, rendering nothing for everyone else. Without this split a non-admin approver has literally no way to learn a request arrived.

⚠️ is_cabin_approver is the gate on review / cancel / admin_update / set_booking_rooms AND the READ RLS on cabin_bookings, cabin_booking_rooms and cabin_messages — so an empty queue for a non-approver is 'not permitted', not 'nothing waiting'.

⚠️ A named approver CANNOT edit the place or its rooms: cabins and cabin_rooms writes are direct table writes gated on profiles.is_admin only. Don't offer them that editor — the writes would just be denied.
approver_user_id null means 'all app admins review this place' — the unchanged default.
Resolve 'do I approve anything?' with one query: cabins.select('id').eq('approver_user_id', userId) — works because cabins is public-read.
An app admin sees the full queue (all places) only in the admin section, not just places they're named on.

features.name: Add a new place to stay (admin)
features.whatItDoes: Lets an admin add another bookable place — a shared cabin or a family member's private house with spare bedrooms — and name who reviews it.
rpcs: create_cabin(p_name, p_kind, p_room_count, p_bed_count, p_notes, p_approver_user_id)
gotchas: create_cabin auto-slugs server-side (slugify + a -1/-2 uniqueness loop) so the client never guesses a slug — mirroring create_committee.
⚠️ It returns a `public.cabins` composite, i.e. a SINGLE JSON object, not an array. Decode accordingly.
⚠️ kind ('cabin' | 'house') is a DISPLAY BADGE ONLY — no booking, capacity or approval behavior differs by it. The member card shows a '🏠 Private house' chip when it's 'house'.
bed_count is reused for 'extra beds outside the bedrooms' once a place has named rooms (rather than adding a column) — the label changes, the column doesn't.
cabins.notes is a free-form heads-up shown to members ('water isn't hooked up yet'); active=false pulls a place out of the bookable list without losing its booking history.
Edits are a direct table update on cabins (admin RLS), not an RPC.
⚠️ cabins and cabin_rooms are NOT in the realtime publication — refetch manually after an edit.
features.v1Cut: Skip in v1 — an admin can add a place on web; iOS only needs to book into it.

features.name: Book a stay for someone else (admin)
features.whatItDoes: Lets an admin book a room for a family member who doesn't use the app, and approve it in the same step.
rpcs: request_cabin_stay(p_cabin, p_check_in, p_check_out, p_guests, p_notes, p_for_user, p_room_ids, p_notify)
gotchas: ⚠️ The web flow AUTO-APPROVES: it calls requestStay then immediately reviewStay(id, true, nil, notify) so the admin doesn't approve their own booking a second time. If the auto-approve fails (capacity), the booking is LEFT PENDING and the admin is told — do not roll back the request.
p_for_user is admin-only, enforced server-side; a non-admin may only omit it or pass their own id.
booked_by is stamped to the admin so the queue shows 'booked by {admin}' instead of implying the member did it themselves.
The sheet's 'Email {name} a confirmation' checkbox feeds p_notify on the REVIEW call, not the request call.
The 'Booking for / Yourself' picker row is admin-only and lives on the member stay screen.

features.name: Edit an existing request (dates, guests, notes, rooms)
features.whatItDoes: Lets whoever reviews a place fix a request after the fact — move the dates, trim '2 beds' to 1, swap which room it uses — all in one sheet.
rpcs: admin_update_cabin_booking(p_booking, p_check_in, p_check_out, p_guests, p_notes, p_notify)
gotchas: ⚠️ Two RPCs in sequence — admin_update_cabin_booking handles dates/guests/notes ONLY; rooms go through set_booking_rooms. Neither touches status.

⚠️ p_notify here defaults FALSE (most edits are small corrections, and this is an email members have never received before) while approve/deny and cancel default TRUE. Preserve those defaults; they're a product decision.

The edit email uses a two-column claim pair: p_notify=true stamps edit_notify_requested_at, and the mailer claims by advancing edit_email_sent_at to match — so EACH edit can independently send or skip.

⚠️ Works on a pending OR already-approved booking, and capacity is NOT re-checked here (only at review time) — so an admin can legitimately edit an approved booking into a conflict. Accepted behavior, not a client-side bug to fix.
Apply the available=true override for rooms this booking already holds (see cabin-named-rooms-picker) or saving is impossible without dropping its own room.

features.name: Cancel a stay
features.whatItDoes: Lets a member cancel their own request, or whoever reviews the place cancel someone's stay.
gotchas: ⚠️ Canonical signature is the 2-arg (p_booking, p_notify) — 0109 dropped the 1-arg form.

⚠️ p_notify only matters when someone ELSE cancels: the RPC pre-stamps cancel_email_sent_at (suppressing the mailer) whenever the requester cancels their OWN booking or p_notify is false. An admin cancelling another member's stay is the only case that leaves it for the mailer.
Gate is requester OR is_cabin_approver (0114) — widened from 'own or admin'.
cancelled_by is stamped for the same 'who did this' reason reviewed_by is.
There is no notify checkbox wired on web — both call sites use the default. Don't invent one without asking.
A cancelled booking cannot later be reviewed.

features.name: Message the guests staying at a place
features.whatItDoes: Lets whoever runs a place send one note to everyone currently or soon staying there — "water's off this weekend", "gate code changed".
gotchas: Recipients are resolved SERVER-side: distinct members with an APPROVED booking whose stay hasn't ended (check_out >= current_date), minus the sender. The client only picks the place and writes the note.
⚠️ The RPC returns an Int recipient count — 0 is a SUCCESS state ('Message saved — no one has an upcoming stay there right now'), not an error.
Body is required and capped at 2000 chars; subject is optional and the notification title becomes '{place} — {subject or "A note about your stay"}'.
The button must appear for BOTH admins and non-admin approvers, i.e. wherever the queue is mounted.
Auto-select the place when the viewer runs exactly one (fetchManageableCabins: all places for an admin, else where approver_user_id = me).
⚠️ Unlike the transactional approve/deny/edit/cancel emails (which override the preference), the optional guest email DOES respect profiles.email_alerts — say so in the UI, as web does.

cabin_message is a NotifType AND a PushType, in DEFAULT_PUSH_TYPES and both mini senders' pushable sets, and 0120 backfilled it onto every existing profile — so it works on iOS today with no mini change. Deep-links to /request-stay.
features.nativeOpportunity: Deliver it with the place name as the notification SUBTITLE and the full body as long-form content, so a 'water's off this weekend' note is readable without opening anything.

features.name: "X of Y rooms / beds left"
features.whatItDoes: Shows at a glance how much room is left in each place for the dates you're looking at, without exposing anyone else's booking.
gotchas: ⚠️ cabin_availability returns SEVEN columns since 0111 (beds_total, beds_available added; the return-type change required a DROP first). Verify the iOS decoder isn't still on the 5-column shape — extra keys are ignored by most decoders, so this fails silently as 'beds never show'.
⚠️ beds_total / beds_available are NULL for a place with no named rooms — that's the signal to fall back to cabins.bed_count for display, not an error.
This CANNOT be computed client-side: cabin_bookings is own-or-approver read, so a plain member cannot see other approved bookings. That's why it's a SECURITY DEFINER RPC.
room_count/available are derived from active cabin_rooms whenever any exist (falling back to the manual cabins.room_count), so the two can't drift once rooms are defined.
An approved room-LESS booking subtracts one room slot and one bed (0108/0111) — assumed to occupy exactly one, mirroring 'one room per bed needed'.
The card shows 'Currently full' at 0 but the request button stays enabled — 'Currently full — you can still request' is deliberate.

features.name: Phone alert for a new cabin request
features.whatItDoes: Buzzes whoever reviews a place when a new stay request comes in, instead of them having to open the app to find out.
gotchas: 🛠️⚠️⚠️ THIS IS THE ONE GENUINE BACKEND GAP IN THIS SECTION. The in-app rows come from a DB trigger, but the PUSH comes from a bespoke handleCabinRequest() in push-sender.js that subscribes to cabin_bookings INSERT directly (it predates the generic feed relay). apns-sender.js subscribes only to committee_messages, house_messages, announcements, notifications and profiles, and cabin_request is not in its PUSHABLE set — so an iOS-only admin or approver NEVER gets buzzed. Fix: mirror handleCabinRequest into apns-sender.js, then git pull + `launchctl kickstart -k` on the mini.
⚠️ cabin_request is a NotifType but NOT a PushType — the web handler gates on notif_types containing 'cabin_request', not push_types. Match that exactly; do not invent a new push category.
The handler must honor NEW.request_notify === false (skip entirely), skip the requester, and include the place's non-admin approver_user_id in addition to every is_admin profile.

⚠️ DEEP-LINK REGRESSION: 0091 deliberately changed the admin url to /admin/cabins?booking=<id> so the tap lands where you can act, but 0108 recreated the trigger from the 0033 body and reverted it to /profile; 0114 carried that forward. Live today: admins get /profile, the approver gets /request-stay. Verify with pg_get_functiondef before building the iOS route table, and fix it with one more recreate FROM PRODUCTION rather than pattern-matching /profile on the client.
The queue screen already reads ?booking=<id> to scroll to and flash-ring the request — keep that behavior once the url is fixed.
features.nativeOpportunity: Once the APNs path exists, make it an actionable notification with Approve / Deny — the strongest argument for the native app for the one person who reviews a private house.

features.name: Edit a place and its rooms (admin)
features.whatItDoes: Lets an admin rename a place, set its room and bed counts, add a note members see, open or close it, and add / rename / open / close / delete its named rooms.
gotchas: ⚠️ These are DIRECT TABLE writes (cabins update/insert, cabin_rooms FOR ALL), gated on profiles.is_admin — not RPCs. So a per-place approver cannot use this screen at all; web hard-returns null for non-admins.
⚠️ cabins and cabin_rooms are NOT in the realtime publication — refetch after every write, don't wait for a change event.
cabin_rooms is unique on (cabin_id, name), so a rename to an existing name fails; surface the error.
Deleting a room cascades cabin_booking_rooms, so past bookings keep their history but lose that link — closing (active=false) is almost always the right action instead.
Use fetchCabinsAdmin (no active filter) here — the member-facing list filters to active only.
bed_count relabels to 'extra beds outside the bedrooms' once the place has named rooms; room_count stops being the capacity source at that point (cabin_availability derives it from cabin_rooms).
features.v1Cut: Skip in v1 — admins can edit places on web.

features.name: Ask for Help (post a request + the shared log + "On my way")
features.whatItDoes: Someone at the resort posts a quick request for a hand, everyone willing and also up there gets pinged, and helpers tap "On my way" — with the open requests visible to everyone in one list.
rpcs: request_help(p_description, p_category, p_where_text, p_lat, p_lng, p_needed_at, p_needed_count, p_audience, p_eligible, p_strict, p_today, p_expires_at, p_items, p_work_item_id, p_followup_at)
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ request_help almost certainly has TWO live overloads: 0046's 13-arg version was never dropped, and its body still calls is_beta_tester(), which 0100 DELETED. Send all 14 keys the web sends (explicit null/[] rather than omitting) or you may resolve to the stale one and get 'function public.is_beta_tester() does not exist' or a PGRST203 ambiguity. Verify: select oid::regprocedure from pg_proc where proname='request_help'. Clean fix is a one-line drop — hand the SQL to Brian, don't run it via MCP.

⚠️⚠️ help_requests has TWO FKs to profiles (user_id and resolved_by), so an unqualified profiles(...) embed returns HTTP 300 / PGRST201 and reads as an empty list with NO error. Must use profiles!help_requests_user_id_fkey. Same trap that broke the tournaments embed.
⚠️ RETURNS TABLE means PostgREST gives you a JSON ARRAY of one object — decode [RequestHelpResult] and take .first, don't decode a bare object.
⚠️ There are NO client write policies on help_requests/help_responses/help_request_items. A direct .insert() always fails; every write is a SECURITY DEFINER RPC.

⚠️ Reads are gated on is_approved_member() (0183), so an unverified new signup gets ZERO rows with no error — that is 'not permitted', not 'no requests'. Show a 'waiting for verification' state, not an empty list.

⚠️ 'Is this mine?' must resolve through the effective viewer id, never a raw auth session lookup — the web specifically removed that from HelpRequestsView because it returns the real admin during a 'view as' preview and leaked their Resolve/Cancel buttons onto the previewed member's screen. Every write must also no-op while previewing.
⚠️ Anti-spam is a cap of 10 concurrent OPEN requests per member, not a cooldown. Surface the server message verbatim — it's actionable.
⚠️ respond_to_help and claim_help_item require status='open'; 'That request is no longer open' is a normal race outcome, treat it as a state refresh not an error toast.

⚠️ HELP_TYPES keys are a hard contract with SQL: hand | move | setup | ride | supplies | urgent (default hand). The trigger's case NEW.category maps those exact strings to push glyphs; an unknown key silently falls through to 🙌.
⚠️ The web's confirmation copy is deliberately honest when notified == 0 ('No one else is checked in as here right now…'). Don't replace it with a false 'Sent!'.
features.nativeOpportunity: The APNs sender already maps help_request/help_urgent to a HELP_REQUEST notification category that apns-sender.js says is registered in NotificationActions.swift — so lock-screen "On my way" / "Can't make it" action buttons calling respond_to_help/withdraw_help are the single highest-value native win here: a helper commits in two seconds without unlocking. Add a Live Activity / Dynamic Island for a request you're on the way to (n of N, ticking toward needed_at), success haptics on commit (lib/haptics.ts is a no-op on iOS today), and a Shortcuts/App Intent "Ask MLR for help".
features.v1Cut: Ship post + log + On my way/withdraw + Covered + resolve/cancel your own + correct notification handling. Defer bring-items, schedule-ahead, the work-item link, and the specific-time picker. Do NOT defer the p_today/p_eligible/p_strict snapshot or the notif_types gate — getting those wrong means the request reaches nobody, which is indistinguishable from the feature being broken.

features.name: "Am I at the resort?" presence gate (no geolocation)
features.whatItDoes: Decides whether you count as being up north today — from your RSVPs and cabin stays, not from your phone's location — which is what unlocks asking for help and what decides who gets asked.
rpcs: _help_recipients(p_eligible, p_strict, p_today, p_audience, p_exclude) — DEFINER-only, no client grant
gotchas: ⚠️ The rule: EVENT_PRESENCE_GRACE_DAYS = 2. eligibleEvents = events where addDays(start,-2) <= today <= addDays(end ?? start,+2). strict = the subset that is dayRsvp && isOngoing(event, today). effectiveStatus = 'going' if the overall status OR any day in the days map is going.

⚠️ The server TRUSTS the client's event-window snapshot — it only checks 'are you RSVP'd going to one of the ids you handed me'. That's what keeps help event-gated (you can never reach random members). Mirror helpTargeting; don't invent event ids.

⚠️ p_today is currently the DEVICE's local calendar date (toISODate uses getFullYear/getMonth/getDate), even though the migrations call it 'resort-local' and days/check_in/check_out are all resort-calendar values. Compute it in America/Chicago on iOS and flag the deliberate divergence to Brian.

⚠️⚠️ NEVER parse a bare 'YYYY-MM-DD' into a Date. This codebase already ate a full incident (0168): a bare new Date('2026-07-31') is UTC midnight and renders as the previous day in Central, which mislabeled every sign-up slot AND corrupted 10 stored rows because the bad label fed a picker. All the date math here is ISO STRING comparison — keep it that way in Swift.

⚠️ addDays() in lib/cabins.ts is subtly wrong and must not be ported literally: it builds local midnight then calls toISOString(), which returns the PREVIOUS day in any positive-UTC-offset zone, silently shifting the ±2-day grace window. Use Calendar.date(byAdding:) on a Chicago calendar.

⚠️ cabin_bookings RLS is 'own rows OR is_cabin_approver(cabin_id)' — a plain member sees only THEIR OWN booking. The server-side _help_recipients runs as DEFINER and sees everyone's, so the client's own presence check and the server's recipient set are computed from different visibility. That asymmetry is correct; don't try to reconcile it client-side.
⚠️ cabin_bookings.check_out is EXCLUSIVE (check_in <= today AND check_out > today); house_stays.end_date is INCLUSIVE. Two different conventions in the same feature.
⚠️ _help_recipients also requires 'help_request' in the recipient's notif_types, which is why notified_count equals the delivered count for non-urgent requests. Don't add a client-side count.
features.nativeOpportunity: This is the flagship opportunity, but be precise: the server-side gate (_help_recipients reading event_attendance/cabin_bookings) is what actually decides recipients, so a geofence alone changes nothing. NO-BACKEND-CHANGE win: a CLCircularRegion geofence on the resort (45.53492,-89.69830) or significant-location-change wakes the app on arrival and prompts "You're at MLR — RSVP going to {live event}?", writing the exact event_attendance row the server already reads. That also kills the feature's worst dead-end, where a member standing at the pavilion is told to "RSVP going to a current event first". WITH a backend change: a member_presence(user_id, present_on, source) table + set_my_presence RPC + one extra OR exists(...) clause in _help_recipients and request_help's requester gate — recreate both from their CURRENT 0100 bodies, per the standing rule that burned 0128 (it silently reverted 0044's whole-word blocklist fix by copy-pasting an older body). Don't ship that without Brian's sign-off: it turns a location permission into something that changes who gets notified.
features.v1Cut: Port the pure functions (eligibleEvents / helpTargeting / eventTargeting / amIPresent / effectiveStatus / isOngoing) exactly, with string date math and a Chicago 'today'. Skip geofencing entirely for v1.

features.name: "What to bring" checklist with race-safe claiming
features.whatItDoes: The person asking lists what's needed (2 long tables, 6 chairs, 3 coolers) and helpers tick off the ones they're bringing — one bringer per item.
gotchas: ⚠️ Items can ONLY be created inside request_help via p_items (blank labels dropped, position = 0-based array index). There is no add-an-item-later RPC — an item list is fixed at post time.

⚠️ Claiming is race-safe in SQL: update ... where claimed_by is null or claimed_by = auth.uid(), then raise 'Someone else is already bringing that' if not found. Don't add optimistic claiming that can't be rolled back — surface that message.

⚠️ Claiming an item ALSO inserts a help_responses row (on conflict do nothing), so bringing something counts toward the head-count. Releasing a claim deliberately LEAVES your 'on my way' in place — don't undo it.
⚠️ Keep the per-item busy lock independent of the per-request lock, or ticking one item disables the whole card (the web fixed this explicitly).
⚠️ Rows claimed by someone else must be disabled, labeled "{FirstName}'s bringing" vs "You're bringing", with an n/N covered tally.
features.nativeOpportunity: A per-item notification action ("I'll bring the tables") on the HELP_REQUEST category — claim straight from the lock screen. Also a natural Live Activity row set.
features.v1Cut: Render the list read-only in v1 if needed (it's still useful information); claiming can follow.

features.name: Urgent help — alerts everyone, can't be muted
features.whatItDoes: Marking a request Urgent makes it an emergency: it goes to every member in the family app-wide, regardless of who's up north or who opted in.
rpcs: _notify (0047 skips the notif_types check for 'help_urgent' only)
gotchas: ⚠️ category='urgent' bypasses the willing + present filter entirely: notif_on_help_request fans help_urgent out to EVERY profile except the requester. The '✅ Covered' fan-out branches the same way.

⚠️ 0047 makes _notify treat help_urgent as NON-SUPPRESSIBLE — it skips the notif_types membership check for that type. So urgent cannot be muted in-app; the web renders its NotifPrefs row with locked: true and copy saying only the OS permission can silence it. Do NOT offer a working mute toggle.

⚠️ help_urgent is a NotifType but NOT a PushType. Don't add it to a push-category picker — there's nothing to opt into and a row would imply it can be turned off. Both mini senders treat it as an override: buzz anyone whose push_types is non-empty regardless of per-category picks.

⚠️ help_request and help_response ARE real PushTypes, in DEFAULT_PUSH_TYPES (on by default), and each needs its own visible opt-OUT row — web shipped without them and members had only the blunt 'turn off push entirely' switch.

⚠️ notified_count UNDERCOUNTS for urgent: request_help counts only profiles with 'help_urgent' in notif_types, but 0047 later made delivery ignore notif_types. Faithful port; don't build UI that asserts the number is exact.
features.nativeOpportunity: Send urgent at APNs interruption-level: time-sensitive so it pierces Focus — that's a mini-side payload change, not an app change. Critical alerts would be the honest ideal (bypasses silent mode) but need an Apple-granted entitlement that is rarely given to non-safety apps: treat it as an ask, not a plan. A distinct urgent-only sound + haptic pattern is free.
features.v1Cut: None — this is small and it's the emergency path.

features.name: Schedule a help request for a future event you're going to
features.whatItDoes: Ask now for help at an upcoming weekend you're RSVP'd to, so everyone attending hears about it today and can plan.
rpcs: request_help — p_eligible=[event.id], p_strict=[] (no server change was needed)
gotchas: ⚠️ Targets come from goingFuture = events with startDate > today that the viewer is effectiveStatus === 'going' to, sorted ascending. You can only ever target an event you're going to, which is what stops random off-resort asks.
⚠️ eventTargeting sets strict = [] so it matches anyone going on ANY day (not just today), and needed_at = the event's morning ({startDate}T09:00:00 as an instant).

⚠️ For a scheduled request the audience is FORCED to 'present', the 'notify everyone willing' escape hatch is HIDDEN, and the specific-time picker is HIDDEN — it's scoped to the event's crew and anchored to the event date.

⚠️ No server change was needed because both the requester gate and _help_recipients key off event_attendance for whatever ids they're handed — and the server does no date check at all. Don't add one client-side either.
features.nativeOpportunity: Offer "Add to Calendar" for the event the request is attached to, via EKEventStore.
features.v1Cut: Defer entirely from v1 — the right-now path is the common case.

features.name: "Did it get done?" follow-up (iOS-only today)
features.whatItDoes: If a help request was linked to a resort to-do task, later that evening the app asks the person who requested it whether the job actually got finished.
gotchas: ⚠️ This push is APNs-ONLY — media-server/work-followup.js has no web-push equivalent. If iOS doesn't register a WORK_FOLLOWUP notification category with a 'Yes, done' action wired to mark_work_item_done, the push is a dead end. Verify in the iOS repo.
⚠️ Payload contract: title 'Did it get done?', category 'WORK_FOLLOWUP', userInfo { work_item_id, request_id }.

⚠️ followup_at is computed CLIENT-side as 9 PM America/Chicago today, or 8 AM tomorrow if it's already past 6 PM (AskForHelpSheet's followupAtISO()). Mirror the Chicago timezone math, not device-local.
⚠️ The mini stamps followup_sent = true on every processed row, including ones where the task was already done (which send nothing) — so it can never re-fire.
⚠️ work-followup.js goes dormant (stops its poll, logs once) if the columns aren't deployed rather than erroring every interval — so silence here can mean 'schema missing', not 'nothing due'.
features.nativeOpportunity: This IS the native-only feature — iOS is already ahead of web here. Finish it: a two-button notification action (Done / Not yet) that writes mark_work_item_done without opening the app.
features.v1Cut: Register the category and handle the tap-through even if the inline action comes later — an unhandled push is worse than no push.

features.name: "Willing to help" opt-in
features.whatItDoes: A switch in your settings saying you're happy to be asked for a hand while you're up north.
gotchas: ⚠️ No RPC — it's a plain update on profiles, allowed by a COLUMN-LEVEL grant: grant update (willing_to_help) on public.profiles to authenticated. That narrow grant is the guardrail that stops a client touching is_admin/house_id/approved in the same statement, so don't widen it and don't batch it with other columns you can't write.

⚠️ Without this flag ON, a member receives NO non-urgent help requests, no matter what their notification prefs say. It is the real opt-in; notif_types/push_types only mute or route. If iOS omits this switch the feature silently reaches nobody.

⚠️ Must be in the profile select alongside display_name/avatar_url/notif_types/push_types, and written optimistically with rollback on error (web re-pins the on-device identity snapshot to the last-good value so a failed write doesn't survive a cold open).
⚠️ Keep the web's copy — it promises 'you're only pinged while you're actually up there', which is the presence rule, not a nicety.

features.name: Home swipe-away call-out stack
features.whatItDoes: Temporary notices (a t-shirt order flyer, a work-weekend poster) stack as cards at the top of Home that you can swipe away, with the Family Fest card permanently underneath so the slot never grows or empties.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ 'Session' dismissal on iOS is PROCESS LIFETIME, not UserDefaults. The web contract is explicit: a swiped card comes back the next time the app is opened. Persisting swipes to UserDefaults silently converts it into the permanent dismissal and deletes the feature's point. sceneWillEnterForeground is NOT a new session — don't reset there.

⚠️⚠️ Session dismissal keys on dismiss_id (mutable, editor-versioned, so a re-issued callout resurfaces); permanent completion keys on id (immutable, so bumping dismiss_id can't resurrect a card you acted on). Swap them and you get either nagging or silent loss.
⚠️ link_href / link_label were DROPPED in 0093 — the live column is links jsonb, an ordered array of {href, label}, each rendered on its OWN line so two actions read as separate.

⚠️ home_callouts is PUBLIC read (using (true)) and was deliberately NOT swapped to is_approved_member() by 0183 — guests see callouts. Writes are can_edit_fest() (admin OR family-fest committee), direct table writes, no RPC.

⚠️ The 📝 Sign up button is gated on the linked fest item actually being signup_enabled, NOT merely on signup_item_id being set — the picker was widened so a callout can borrow an activity's content. HomeSpotlight resolves that from the fest schedule it already has; no extra round-trip.
⚠️ signup_item_id and event_id are DIFFERENT things: event_id is targeting only (hide from non-attendees), signup_item_id is a deep link. A callout can carry both at once.

⚠️ fetchFestContent falls back to FALLBACK_CALLOUTS on a table-missing ERROR only — NEVER on an empty result, because empty legitimately means 'no call-outs' and resurrecting a deleted seed card is a bug. This exact seed-fallback idiom is what hid the committee_areas RLS incident for weeks. Prefer shipping no fallback at all on iOS.

⚠️ Show window: is_active, plus starts_on <= today <= ends_on with ends_on INCLUSIVE, compared as ISO STRINGS. Never parse a bare YYYY-MM-DD into a Date (the 0168 incident); CalloutCard appends 'T00:00:00' before formatting for exactly this reason.

⚠️ Event targeting hides a card ONLY from someone whose rolled-up status for that event is not_going. A no-response member (or going/maybe) still sees it, deliberately — a silent no-response read as 'excluded' risks someone missing something. exclude_not_attending defaults to TRUE once an event is picked.

⚠️ In-card controls must not be eaten by the drag gesture. The web marks every button/link data-callout-no-drag and bails out of pointerdown on them, because trackpad drift between mousedown and mouseup marked the gesture 'dragged' and silently swallowed the button's click. Verify 'I did this', every link, and the ✕ all fire mid-tiny-drag on a real device.

⚠️ Numbers to match: SWIPE_THRESHOLD 140px (deliberately long so scroll jitter never dismisses), PEEK 8px, MAX_PEEK 2, FLY_MS 260, 6px axis-lock deadzone, one wiggle hint per session skipped under reduce-motion.
⚠️ Order by position ASCENDING — position 0 is the FRONT card. Items are passed front-to-back with the non-swipeable base LAST.
⚠️ saveCallout retries the write without drop_box_id if the error mentions that column (pre-0172 degradation) — an unknown column fails the whole statement.
features.nativeOpportunity: SwiftUI can mount every card cheaply and give the stack real depth/parallax and velocity-based fling with rubber-banding, instead of the web's hand-tuned 140px threshold, manual axis lock, and static decorative 'plates' faking the cards behind. Add .sensoryFeedback on dismiss and on 'I did this' (lib/haptics.ts is a no-op on iOS). ShareLink on a flyer image beats 'long-press in Safari' — forwarding a flyer is the thing family members actually do. EKEventStore 'add to Calendar/Reminders' from deadline_at. A WidgetKit widget showing the front callout puts the flyer on the home screen.
features.v1Cut: Ship fetch + render (image / title / body / links / signup / drop-box / due line) + the permanent base card + swipe/✕ with in-memory session dismissal + 'I did this' + client-side event targeting. Defer the admin authoring UI, reminder scheduling, and the peeking-plate depth polish.

features.name: "I did this — don't show again" (permanent callout completion)
features.whatItDoes: Once you've actually ordered the t-shirts, one tap stops that card nagging you forever, on every device — unlike swiping it away, which only lasts until the next time you open the app.
gotchas: ⚠️ Plain own-row RLS, no RPC: for all using (user_id = auth.uid()) with check (user_id = auth.uid()). You can only ever read/write your own completions.
⚠️ Keys on the callout's stable id, NOT the mutable dismiss_id. See the callout-stack gotcha.
⚠️ Upsert with onConflict callout_id,user_id and ignoreDuplicates so a double-tap before the card disappears can't throw a unique violation.

⚠️ Optimistic + persisted in one step, then RE-APPLIED after the write lands — otherwise an in-flight pre-write fetch overwrites the optimistic id. Cache locally (web: calloutsDone.<uid>) so the completed card is filtered out from the FIRST paint on the next cold open; web explicitly fixed a 'shows for half a second then vanishes' flash here.
⚠️ Key the cache on the REAL user id, never a preview identity — completions always belong to the real account.
⚠️ A guest tapping it gets the sign-in prompt (there's no row to attach), not a silent no-op.
⚠️ The button must NOT render in an admin preview of a callout (web omits onMarkDone there), or an editor marks it done for themselves while previewing.
⚠️ This table is NOT in the realtime publication — a completion on another device appears on the next fetch, not live.

⚠️ Server-side consequence: run_scheduled_broadcasts() reads payload.excludeCalloutDone (default true via coalesce) and skips anyone with a completion row, so 'I did this' also suppresses that callout's reminder pushes.

features.name: Create and edit Home call-outs (admin / fest committee)
features.whatItDoes: An admin or Family Fest committee member writes the notice card everyone sees on Home — image, text, action buttons, a show window, and optionally a notification or email at the same time.
rpcs: send_broadcast_notification(p_title, p_body, p_url, p_audience, p_expires_at, p_event_id, p_exclude_not_attending)
gotchas: ⚠️ Writes are direct table writes gated by RLS on can_edit_fest() — app admin OR a committee_members row joined to committees.slug = 'family-fest'. There is no create/update RPC, so a failed write surfaces as an RLS denial, not a friendly error.
⚠️ dismiss_id must be VERSIONED (web suggests slug+date) or a brand-new alert won't resurface for someone who swiped the previous same-purpose card in the same session.

⚠️ The two side-action toggles ('🔔 Also send a notification', '✉️ Also email everyone who opted in') default OFF every time the sheet opens — they are NOT properties of the saved row, so editing an old callout never silently resends. Firing happens after the save succeeds; a send failure must block the sheet from closing WITHOUT undoing the already-saved callout so the admin can retry.
⚠️ deadline_at is the reminder anchor and is distinct from starts_on/ends_on, which only gate the show window.
⚠️ Reminders can only be attached to a callout that already has an id — save first, then add reminders.

⚠️ Known-fixed-on-web: send_broadcast_notification writes type='broadcast', which was never a real PushType, so that channel silently never pushed to ANY phone. Both mini senders now include 'broadcast' and gate it on the recipient's 'alerts' category instead. If a broadcast lands in the feed but no phone buzzes, that's the shape of the bug.
features.nativeOpportunity: PhotosPicker + on-device image compression for flyer art, and a genuinely live preview card (the same view Home renders, not a lookalike).
features.v1Cut: Skip entirely for v1 — this is a rarely-used admin surface and web already has it.

features.name: "Up North today" card
features.whatItDoes: A strip on Home showing who's at the resort today, with a tap-through to the full list and each person's profile.
gotchas: ⚠️ This card is deliberately STRICTER than Ask for Help: graceBefore is ALWAYS 0 (an event that hasn't started never counts, however close) and graceAfter defaults to 0 (the card clears the moment the event ends). Don't reuse Ask for Help's ±2 grace here.

⚠️ On a lingering-after shoulder day it widens grace around the PERSON'S OWN last 'going' day, not the event's full run — otherwise someone who RSVP'd Sun–Tue shows as up north all week because the event's graced window ran that long.

⚠️ presentFromCabins is nearly useless for a non-admin: cabin_bookings RLS is own-rows-or-approver, so a regular member sees only themselves from that source. That's correct, not a bug — do NOT widen the RLS to 'fix' it.

⚠️ presentFromHouseStays is scoped to your own house (is_house_member) and only surfaces created_by; free-text guest_names have no profile to show. end_date is INCLUSIVE here, unlike cabins' exclusive check_out.
⚠️ Every source returns [] on failure and never throws; the card self-hides for guests and whenever the merged list is empty. Never render an empty shell or an error.
⚠️ Cache key is DATE-SCOPED (whosUpNorth.<uid>.<today>, 30-min TTL) — that's what makes it structurally impossible to paint yesterday's list from a stale cache. A date in the key beats any TTL.

⚠️ Wording is a product decision: 'Up North today', never 'right now', plus the sheet's 'Based on who's RSVP'd or booked for today — not their exact arrival time'. This is inferred from RSVPs; the copy must not promise more.

⚠️ It reads fetchEvents()/fetchAttendance() directly rather than the events hook, because the hook only exposes summaries rolled up over the whole run and loses the per-day days map this needs. event_attendance embeds profiles(...) unqualified safely — it has exactly one FK to profiles, unlike help_requests.
features.nativeOpportunity: A WidgetKit widget — "who's up north" is the single best small-widget candidate in the app, and it's already a cheap day-scoped read. If geofenced presence ever ships, this card becomes real-time rather than inferred and the copy can finally say 'right now'.
features.v1Cut: Ship the attendance source only (it's the resort-wide one); the cabin and house-stay sources add almost nothing for a non-admin viewer.

features.name: Lake weather card
features.whatItDoes: Current temperature and today's high/low for the lake, tapping to reveal a five-day forecast.
gotchas: ⚠️ The ONE public, no-sign-in card in the garnish run — everything else is members-only.

⚠️ Fixed coordinates 45.53492, -89.69830 (Tomahawk, WI), forecast_days=6 (index 0 is today's hi/lo, 1..5 the strip), temperature_unit=fahrenheit, timezone=America/Chicago. Those same coordinates are the natural geofence centre if presence ever goes native.

⚠️ The fetch THROWS on a non-ok response or a malformed payload, on purpose — so the cache keeps the last good snapshot instead of overwriting it with nothing. Don't swallow the error into a nil snapshot.

⚠️ Renders NOTHING before the first successful fetch — never a spinner, never an error state, never an empty shell. It sits at the very top of Home so an empty box there is the most visible failure in the app.
⚠️ WMO weather_code maps to exactly 7 emoji buckets; keep the same mapping so web and iOS agree.
⚠️ Cache 'weather' is unscoped (public data) with a 30-minute TTL.
features.nativeOpportunity: A WeatherKit swap is tempting and should be DECLINED for v1 — Open-Meteo needs no key, no entitlement and no attribution UI, and web/iOS showing the same number matters more than provider polish. A weather widget and a Lock Screen complication are the real wins.

features.name: Upcoming birthdays card
features.whatItDoes: Names of family members with a birthday in the next two weeks, tapping through to their contact card.
gotchas: ⚠️ Year-agnostic month/day compare in LOCAL time, 14-day window, today sorts first and reads 'today! 🎉'.

⚠️ A Feb-29 birthday falls back to Feb-28 in a non-leap target year so it is never silently skipped — this mirrors media-server/birthday-notifier.js exactly; keep the two consistent or the card and the push will disagree.
⚠️ Members-only (profiles read is is_approved_member() or id = auth.uid()); self-hides for guests and for an empty window.
⚠️ Cache key is date-scoped (birthdays.<uid>.<localDay>, 6h TTL) so 'in 3 days' can never show a day late.
⚠️ Names deep-link via ?member=<id>, the SAME convention the birthday push already uses — web needs a real page load for its sheet host to fire; iOS should route this to its member sheet.
features.nativeOpportunity: Offer "add to Contacts / Calendar" for a family birthday — a one-tap native affordance with no web equivalent. Plus a widget for the next birthday.

features.name: "On this day" photo memory
features.whatItDoes: A photo from the family feed taken around this date in a previous year.
gotchas: ⚠️ The pick is DETERMINISTIC — dayOfYear % candidates.count after sorting by id — NOT random. Everyone in the family sees the same memory on the same day, and it rotates naturally year to year. Randomising it breaks the shared-experience point.
⚠️ Uses a CIRCULAR day-of-year distance so Dec 30 and Jan 2 read as 3 days apart, not 363. Window is ±3 days, prior years only (d.getFullYear() < currentYear).
⚠️ Skips any post whose status is not 'visible' (moderation holds) and any post with no image — 'a photo memory', so the first non-video post_media row per post, or the legacy image_path.
⚠️ Members-only under the 0081/0183 lockdown; self-hides for guests, and returns nil rather than an error when nothing qualifies.

⚠️ Post media served from the mini needs the media-token query param (see the media section); Supabase Storage 'post-photos' URLs and site-assets do not. Implement the mediaSrc() equivalent as a no-op for non-mini URLs so a mini-hosted URL can never slip through unsigned.
⚠️ Cache key is date-scoped (onThisDay.<uid>.<localDay>, 24h TTL).
⚠️ Prefer thumbnail_url (migration 0173) over the full-res file for the 48px thumbnail — every *_media table has the column.
features.nativeOpportunity: A real Live Photo-aware viewer, ShareLink to forward the memory, and AsyncImage + a disk cache so the thumbnail is instant. A 'memories' widget is an obvious follow-on.
features.v1Cut: Defer — this is the lowest-value card and the most fetch-heavy (it reads all posts + all post_media).

features.name: Active poll card on Home
features.whatItDoes: Spotlights the newest open family poll with its running vote count, linking straight to voting.
gotchas: ⚠️ It self-hides for guests, no open poll, AND a missing 0084 table with no extra checks, because fetchPolls() already degrades to [] for all three. Preserve that: one 'no open poll' path, not three error states.
⚠️ 'Newest open' = fetchPolls() is already ordered created_at desc, so it's just the first row with isClosed false. A poll also closes implicitly once closes_on has passed (open THROUGH that day).
⚠️ polls/poll_options/poll_votes are all members-only (is_approved_member()) — a guest gets zero rows, not an error.
⚠️ Cache activePoll.<uid>, 6h TTL, with a preview-scoped MEMORY-ONLY key while an admin is viewing-as (persist: undefined) — a preview must never write to a persisted cache.
features.nativeOpportunity: Vote inline from the card with a haptic confirmation, rather than navigating to a separate polls screen.

features.name: Activity tab (the notifications feed)
features.whatItDoes: A personal list of everything that happened involving you — comments and reactions on your posts, mentions, new posts, committee decisions, cabin news, reminders and announcements — that keeps working even when the phone got no push.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ The actor join MUST name the FK: actor:profiles!actor_id(display_name, avatar_url). notifications has two FKs to profiles (recipient_id + actor_id), so an unhinted embed returns HTTP 300 / PGRST201 with ZERO rows and no thrown error — a permanently empty tab that looks like RLS.

⚠️⚠️ Decode `type` as String, never a closed Swift enum. `new_member` rows are in production and absent from web's own NotifType union. In Swift an unknown enum case fails the decode of the whole 100-row page, blanking the entire tab; map to a glyph with a fallback instead.
⚠️ RLS read rule: recipient_id = auth.uid() only. An empty feed means 'nothing happened involving you', never 'not permitted'. No admin override exists.
⚠️ There is NO insert and NO update policy on notifications — a direct client write always fails. Keep optimism in the view model only.

⚠️ title and body are already-composed prose built in SQL (emoji, '· 📍 location' suffixes, 'In this slot: Alice, Bob.'). Render verbatim; never re-derive copy from type + actor name or it will drift on the next migration.
⚠️ _notify skips recipient == actor, so you are never notified of your own action. Don't re-implement that filter and don't treat its absence as a bug.
⚠️ Web caps at limit(100) with no pagination — native keyset pagination on created_at is an easy improvement but not v1.
⚠️ notifications is NOT replica identity full, so a DELETE's old record carries only the PK and cannot match a recipient_id=eq. realtime filter. Remove dismissed rows locally.
⚠️ notifications was untouched by the 0181/0183 verified-member lockdown — do not add an `approved` check client-side.
features.nativeOpportunity: Persist the last few hundred rows locally (web is capped at a 200KB localStorage snapshot) so the tab renders instantly and works with no signal on the drive up. Day-grouped sections with native section headers, and swipe-to-dismiss against the already-existing DELETE policy.
features.v1Cut: Ship the flat list + day grouping + the three read RPCs. Defer keyset pagination past 100 rows, swipe-to-dismiss, and full offline persistence.

features.name: Unread badge and the seen/read/expired model
features.whatItDoes: The red count on the Activity tab, and the bold-versus-read look of each row.
gotchas: ⚠️ Three fields, three jobs: seen_at drives the BADGE ONLY (bulk-stamped on screen open), read_at drives per-row bold (stamped on tap), expires_at removes a row from the badge while KEEPING it in the list.
⚠️ The badge query must include .or("expires_at.is.null,expires_at.gt.<nowIso>"). Omit it and one old admin broadcast pins a permanent badge that nothing can clear.
⚠️ The count is TIME-DEPENDENT — a row silently leaves the count when expires_at passes, with no database event. Recompute on foreground and on a timer, not only on a realtime tick.
⚠️ mark_notification_read sets seen_at too (coalesce), so tapping a row from a push also clears it from the badge. Mirror that or the badge and the list disagree.
⚠️ Web renders '99+' above 99.
features.nativeOpportunity: Reconcile the real unseen count into UNUserNotificationCenter.setBadgeCount on every foreground and every received push, which also lets the app icon DECREMENT when the member reads something on another device. Web push on iOS cannot set an app badge at all.

features.name: An app icon badge that is actually correct
features.whatItDoes: The number on the home-screen icon matches how many new things are really waiting, without opening the app.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ apns-sender.js hard-codes `badge: 1` in the aps dictionary — EVERY push sets the icon badge to literally 1, regardless of the real unseen count. This is not a bug in iOS's handling; it is what the server sends.

Two routes: (a) have the mini compute the recipient's unseen-unexpired count next to the existing push_types read in handleFeed (four lines, a mini change); or (b) keep it fully native — reconcile setBadgeCount on foreground and on didReceiveRemoteNotification, optionally with mutable-content:1 + a service extension for the background case.
Prefer (b) first: no mini change, no deploy coupling, and it can decrement as well as increment.
features.nativeOpportunity: This is the single highest-value native win in the section — the badge is the most-seen surface in the app and Web Push on iOS has no badge capability whatsoever.
features.v1Cut: Foreground-only reconciliation is already a strict improvement over `badge: 1`. Add the service extension later.

features.name: Notification preferences (which activities show in Activity)
features.whatItDoes: Per-kind on/off switches controlling what lands in your Activity tab, grouped into labelled sections.
gotchas: ⚠️ 28 hand-authored rows in 10 sections (Your activity · Social · Committees · Cabin stays · Events · House calendar · Work items · Meetings & Polls · Family Fest · Help requests). The list is NOT derived from the type union in either codebase — web's own comment says the layout mirrors the iOS NotifPrefsView and asks that section order stay in sync. Verify every row exists in the iOS repo; the recently-added kinds are the likely gaps.

⚠️ Exactly two rows are admin-gated in the UI: committee_join_request and cabin_request. A section whose every row filters out renders NOTHING. This is honesty, not security — a non-admin toggling 'New cabin stay requests' and never receiving one reads as broken.

⚠️ help_urgent is a LOCKED row: a static '🔒 Always on' chip, no switch. That is backed in SQL — migration 0047 made help_urgent the one type _notify inserts regardless of notif_types. Say in the subtitle that the only way to silence it is the OS permission.
⚠️ admin_test is deliberately absent (29 member-selectable types, 28 rows) — there is nothing to opt into.
⚠️ notif_types has NO check constraint and NO allow-list. A typo'd string is accepted by Postgres and silently matches nothing forever.

⚠️ Write is a whole-ARRAY replace through the column grant `grant update (notif_types)`, not an RPC and not an element op. Two devices toggling different rows within one round-trip clobber each other (web accepts last-writer-wins).
⚠️ Fall back to DEFAULT_NOTIF_TYPES (28 entries) when the column reads null — defaulting to [] silently mutes a member whose profile hasn't loaded yet.
⚠️ Do not include is_admin / house_id / approved / notifications_confirmed in the same update statement — they are outside the grant and would fail the WHOLE update.
features.nativeOpportunity: Native Form + Toggle rows with section headers get this for free where web hand-rolls switches, and a search field over 28 rows is trivial in SwiftUI.

features.name: Push notification preferences (what buzzes the phone)
features.whatItDoes: A master push switch plus per-category picks for what actually buzzes the phone, separate from the in-app Activity list.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ There is NO push_enabled boolean anywhere. The master switch is the CONVENTION `push_types.count > 0`. Master-on writes the full DEFAULT_PUSH_TYPES (14 entries) and registers the device; master-off writes [] and unregisters; unticking the LAST category does the same. Do both halves in that order.

⚠️⚠️ The help_urgent and admin_test overrides gate on `push_types.length === 0`, so an empty array IS the off switch for emergencies too. A populated array with no registered device is a member who 'has push on' and receives nothing.

⚠️⚠️ push_types is per-ACCOUNT, not per-device. A member with the iPhone app AND the installed web PWA shares one array — turning push off natively silences their browser too. Do not paper over it with device-local state that drifts from the column.

⚠️ 25 rows, verified one-to-one against the PushType union. Off-by-default (11): committee_join_request, event_rsvp, work_item_created, house_stay_created, meeting_proposed, meeting_scheduled, chat_poll_created, the three tournament_*, private_activity_invite. Everything else is in DEFAULT_PUSH_TYPES.

⚠️ Keep the 'Not getting notifications? Re-register this device' recovery action. Its web comment records why: iOS rotates/drops a token after a re-install or OS update while Apple keeps 200-ing the dead token, so pushes vanish with no error anywhere.
⚠️ push_types has NO check constraint either. Same silent-typo failure as notif_types.

⚠️ push_self_notify does NOTHING for native push — apns-sender.js declares SELF_NOTIFY_IDS at line 163 and never reads it again. Don't ship that switch on iOS expecting it to work; use the admin send_test_notification tool for solo testing.
features.nativeOpportunity: Native can read the real UNAuthorizationStatus and show 'notifications are off in iOS Settings' with a deep link to Settings — web can only guess. And the whole 'add the app to your Home Screen first' copy path that PushToggle needs on iOS Safari can be deleted outright.

features.name: APNs device token registration
features.whatItDoes: Registers this iPhone so the resort's Mac mini can reach it, and cleans up when you sign out.
gotchas: ⚠️ RLS read rule: user_id = auth.uid() for all four commands. An empty read means 'this account has registered no devices', never a permission failure. The mini reads everyone's with the service-role key.

⚠️⚠️ `environment` is per-ROW and the mini routes on it: 'sandbox' → api.sandbox.push.apple.com, anything else → api.push.apple.com. A debug build registering 'production' gets 400 BadDeviceToken, and sendToUser DELETES the row on BadDeviceToken / Unregistered / 410 — so the device silently deregisters itself and the tester concludes push is broken. Gate it: #if DEBUG → "sandbox", else "production" (TestFlight and App Store are both production).

⚠️ Re-upsert on EVERY launch and every didRegisterForRemoteNotifications callback, not just on first permission grant. That is the only thing that heals the rotated-token case, and it's exactly why web keeps a manual re-register button.

⚠️ On sign-out, DELETE this account's row for this device. Nothing cleans up an account switch on a shared phone, and the stale row will push the previous member's private chat titles to the next member's lock screen. Web has the analogous cache-key leak on record (fixed PR #244) — same shape, different table.
⚠️ Upsert with onConflict: "user_id,device_token" — the PK is the pair, so the same phone under two accounts is two legitimate rows.

features.name: Handling a tapped push and landing on the right screen
features.whatItDoes: Tapping a notification opens the exact post, comment, chat message, request or slot it was about — never just the app's home screen.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ `url` in the payload is ABSOLUTE, prefixed with the mini's APP_URL (default https://mlr-app-omega.vercel.app) because the same relay feeds the web PWA. Strip the origin and route the path+query with your own navigator. Handing it to UIApplication.open bounces the member out to Safari.
⚠️ Extra userInfo keys are FLATTENED to the top level, not nested under a userInfo object. committee_join_request carries request_id + committee_id; WORK_FOLLOWUP carries work_item_id + request_id.

⚠️ target_type/target_id are entity_type/entity_id passed straight through and are often ABSENT or coarser than the url — for post_comment, entity_id is the POST id while the url carries &comment=. The url is authoritative; target_* is a hint.

⚠️ 15 real path shapes to handle: /posts?post=<uuid>&comment=<uuid> · /posts?post=<uuid> · /posts?c=<slug>&area=<urlencoded>&m=<uuid> · /posts?house=<slug>&m=<uuid> · /committees/<slug> · /committees · /request-stay · /help-requests · /?work=<uuid> · /people?member=<uuid> · /family-fest/schedule/<uuid> · /family-fest · /events?activity=<uuid> · /profile · /

⚠️⚠️ NEVER route a chat notification to /committees/<slug>/chat. Migration 0030 emitted that shape originally; 0063 superseded it with the /posts?c= feed form precisely because the standalone route dies outright in the installed PWA. Old rows may still carry the legacy url — normalize it to your native chat screen rather than dead-ending.

⚠️ Tapping a push should also call mark_notification_read(p_id:) so the Activity row isn't still bold after the member clearly saw it. The notification id is not in the payload, so match on the url/target or refetch.
⚠️ The mini's `once()` de-dupe is an in-memory Set cleared past 5000 entries and EMPTIED by a restart, so a replayed row can re-push. Be idempotent on arrival.
features.nativeOpportunity: A native router transitions in place with no reload, where the web PWA had a documented bug in which sw.js's client.navigate() silently failed in installed iOS PWAs and every deep link was dropped (fixed with a postMessage fallback in PushDeepLink.tsx). Native simply doesn't have that failure mode.
features.v1Cut: Handle the post/comment, both chat forms, and help/cabin/signup paths first; the rest can fall back to opening the app's home screen.

features.name: Guard against a notification kind that silently never pushes
features.whatItDoes: Nothing a member sees — it stops a whole category of notification from being invisible to everyone forever.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ A kind pushes only if it is in ALL THREE of: (1) the client PushType list AND a matching toggle row, (2) the mini's PUSHABLE set, (3) an actual notifications row inserted with that exact type string. Miss any one and you get ZERO pushes, forever, for everyone, with no error in any log on any device at any layer.

⚠️⚠️ INCIDENT: `broadcast` was invisible to every recipient. send_broadcast_notification inserts type='broadcast' but 'broadcast' was never a real PushType, so pushTypes.includes(n.type) could never be true. Admins checking '🔔 Activity tab' or a callout's '🔔 Also send a notification' saw the item land in everyone's feed and NOBODY was buzzed — including admins with every category on. Fixed by adding it to both senders' pushable sets and special-casing it onto the existing 'alerts' category rather than minting a PushType.

⚠️ INCIDENT: help_request and help_response had NO toggle row at all. Both were real PushTypes, both in DEFAULT_PUSH_TYPES, both correctly in the pushable sets — the hand-authored row list just omitted them, so every member got these pushes with no way to opt out short of the master switch. Found by diffing the PushType union against the toggle rows' values. Do that diff in a Swift unit test.

⚠️ Consequence for iOS: `broadcast` and `admin_test` will NEVER appear in any member's push_types. A 'which categories are on?' diagnostic built off the PushType union will report the two that always fire as off.
⚠️ And the fourth place: notif_types. A feed-backed kind's push depends on the feed row existing, so turning the in-app category off also kills its push.

features.name: Act on a notification without opening the app
features.whatItDoes: "On my way" on a help request, Going / Can't-make-it on an event, Approve / Decline on a committee join request, Done / Still-open on a work follow-up — straight from the notification.
gotchas: The server side already exists: categoryFor() stamps EVENT_REMINDER, HELP_REQUEST (for both help_request and help_urgent), CHAT_MENTION, COMMITTEE_JOIN_REQUEST; work-followup.js stamps WORK_FOLLOWUP. The migration header for 0052 and apns-sender's comment both reference an existing iOS NotificationActions.swift — verify what's actually wired.

⚠️ CHAT_MENTION is UNREACHABLE dead code today: chat_mention is not in PUSHABLE, and the chat firehose payload sends type:"chat" which maps to null. Whatever iOS registered for that category never fires.

⚠️ committee_join_request forwards request_id + committee_id as TOP-LEVEL keys because entity_id is the request id and the inline Approve button needs the committee too. Read them from userInfo, not from target_id.
⚠️ Also call mark_notification_read(p_id:) inside the action handler, or the Activity row stays bold after the member has visibly acted on it.
⚠️ Use a background-executing action (not foreground) so the member never sees the app open — that's the whole point.
features.nativeOpportunity: Web Push on iOS has no action buttons at all, ever. This is a capability gap, not polish — and the payload plumbing is already sending the category and the ids.
features.v1Cut: Start with HELP_REQUEST's 'On my way' (one RPC, one param) and EVENT_REMINDER's RSVP. Defer COMMITTEE_JOIN_REQUEST and WORK_FOLLOWUP.

features.name: Group a burst of notifications into one stack
features.whatItDoes: Ten comments on one post collapse into a single "9 more comments on your post" stack instead of ten separate banners.
gotchas: 31 kinds fanned out per-recipient means a live fest evening produces a wall of individual banners — new_post alone fires to every member with the category on.

⚠️ Needs `aps["thread-id"]` from the mini (derive it from entity_type + entity_id so every comment on one post threads together) — ~5 lines in sendToUser, plus a UNNotificationCategory with categorySummaryFormat on the client. Alternatively a service extension gated on mutable-content:1 can set threadIdentifier, but that's more moving parts.
⚠️ No apns-collapse-id is sent either, so there is no server-side coalescing today.
features.nativeOpportunity: iOS does the grouping and writes the summary text for free once thread-id is set. Web push gets one flat banner per row and always will.
features.v1Cut: Skip in v1 — it needs a mini change and a deploy.

features.name: A photo preview inside the notification
features.whatItDoes: A comment or new post about a photo shows that photo right on the lock screen.
gotchas: ⚠️ Needs `mutable-content: 1` in aps plus an image URL in the payload — a mini change — then a UNNotificationServiceExtension downloading it into a UNNotificationAttachment.
⚠️⚠️ /f reads are token-signed (?t=, MEDIA_AUTH). The extension is a SEPARATE PROCESS with its own container, so the token hand-off must be designed deliberately (shared App Group, most likely).

⚠️⚠️ MEDIA_AUTH is currently 'report' rather than 'on' SPECIFICALLY because the native app cannot sign yet. Do this after the media-token work lands, not before, or you'll be debugging 403s that are the expected behaviour.
Every *_media table has a nullable thumbnail_url since 0173, so there is a small file to attach rather than a full-res phone photo.
features.nativeOpportunity: A thumbnail on the lock screen is most of the value of a photo notification, and web push cannot attach media on iOS at all.
features.v1Cut: Defer entirely from v1 — blocked on the media token.

features.name: Live Activity during Family Fest week
features.whatItDoes: During the fest, the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island show what's next today and when your own sign-up slot starts, without unlocking the phone.
gotchas: The data is already time-resolved SERVER-side: run_signup_reminders() computes each slot's absolute instant as (day || ' ' || start_time)::timestamp at time zone 'America/Chicago', DST-safe. Read the same fields rather than re-deriving.

⚠️⚠️ NEVER hand a bare 'YYYY-MM-DD' to a date parser. Web's formatDate() did exactly that and labelled EVERY sign-up slot a day early across the whole fest UI — and because the broken label also fed the organiser's day picker, it CORRUPTED the stored rows (10 slots had to be corrected by hand with `day = day - 1`). The reminders were always right; only the labels lied, and they lied self-consistently so nothing on screen revealed it.
The signup_reminder push can carry the Live Activity update, so no new server channel is needed.
Gate on the fest season phase (live/wrap), or you ship a Live Activity that runs 50 weeks a year with nothing in it.
features.nativeOpportunity: The one genuinely native-only feature with an obvious home in this app. No browser can do it.
features.v1Cut: Scope as its own project after the feed port; do not attempt inside v1.

features.name: On-device reminders that work even if the resort's server is down
features.whatItDoes: Your own sign-up slot still reminds you on time even if the Mac mini at the resort is off, the router is down, or the internet isn't there.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ There is NO unsent-row ledger for push. Unlike email (which alert-mailer.js re-sweeps every 3 minutes), a push missed during a dropped Realtime channel is GONE with no recovery. Both senders resubscribe 5s after CHANNEL_ERROR/TIMED_OUT/CLOSED, and that reconnect is the whole fix on the server side.
Once the app knows a member's own slot times, schedule UNCalendarNotificationTriggers locally for them. This is the only reminder path that survives the mini being off.
⚠️ Cancel and reschedule local notifications when the member removes a sign-up or the organiser edits a slot, or you'll buzz someone about a slot they left.

⚠️ Don't duplicate: if the server push lands too, the member gets two. Either use the same identifier so iOS replaces it, or accept the duplicate as the cheaper failure than a missed reminder (server-side dedup is impossible here).
features.nativeOpportunity: Structurally impossible in a browser — a PWA cannot schedule a future local notification.
features.v1Cut: Defer, but note it in CLAUDE.md as the intended reliability answer to the mini being a single point of failure.

features.name: Swipe a notification away
features.whatItDoes: Clear an item out of your Activity list for good.
gotchas: The `notifications: own delete` RLS policy (recipient_id = auth.uid()) has existed since 0030 and NO web surface uses it — the feature is already permitted server-side, just never built.
⚠️ Remove the row locally; do not wait for a realtime echo. notifications is not replica identity full, so a DELETE's old record has only the PK and cannot match a recipient_id=eq. filter.
The feed is a real inbox capped at 100 rows on read, and today it cannot be cleaned out at all.
features.nativeOpportunity: A native swipe action is two lines against a policy that already exists — a straight win over web with no backend work.

features.name: Cabin stay request push for iPhone admins and approvers
features.whatItDoes: Whoever approves stays at a place gets buzzed when someone requests one — which currently only happens in a browser, not on an iPhone.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ THIS ONE NEEDS A BACKEND (MINI) CHANGE, not Swift. push-sender.js has a bespoke handleCabinRequest on cabin_bookings INSERT; apns-sender.js has NO such handler and does not subscribe to cabin_bookings at all, and `cabin_request` is absent from its PUSHABLE set. So an admin — or the private-house owner who is the designated approver and has no admin access — gets the Activity row and, on iPhone, no push.

⚠️ The web handler's gate is unusual: it checks `notif_types` containing 'cabin_request', NOT push_types (cabin_request is not a PushType). Port that gate exactly or admins who turned the in-app kind off will start getting pushes.
⚠️ Also honor `cabin_bookings.request_notify = false` (migration 0108) and include the non-admin `cabins.approver_user_id` (0114) in the recipient list — both are in the web handler.
~40 lines in apns-sender.js, calling apns.sendToUser instead of sendToUser. Needs a mini git pull + restart (Admin → Media server).

features.name: Push when you're @mentioned in a chat
features.whatItDoes: Being tagged by name in a committee or house chat buzzes your phone, even if you've turned off the every-message firehose.
gotchas: ⚠️ chat_mention produces a feed row but is in NEITHER the PushType union NOR either sender's pushable set. It reaches a phone only incidentally via the `chat` firehose — so a member who turns `chat` off to escape the firehose loses @mention pushes entirely, which is the exact opposite of what they wanted.

⚠️ Consequence: apns-sender's categoryFor("chat_mention") → "CHAT_MENTION" is unreachable dead code (the firehose payload sends type:"chat", which maps to null), so whatever iOS registered under that category never appears on a real notification.

⚠️ Fixing it properly is a THREE-PLACE change (PushType + toggle row + both senders' pushable sets) — exactly the invariant that produced the broadcast incident. Raise it with Brian as a product call before writing code; it is not a bug to fix unilaterally.
features.v1Cut: Raise the question in v1; ship the change only with Brian's sign-off.

features.name: Admin: test one member's notifications and record who's confirmed
features.whatItDoes: An admin pings one specific member to check their notifications actually work, and ticks them off a list once they've watched it land.
gotchas: ⚠️ send_test_notification bypasses notif_types AND is an OVERRIDE push in both senders — only a fully-empty push_types blocks it, which is itself useful diagnostic signal ('push is fully off for them').
⚠️ admin_test is deliberately absent from the prefs UI — there is nothing to opt into. Don't add a row for it.

⚠️ notifications_confirmed / _at / _by are deliberately outside every client update grant, so set_notification_test_confirmed is the ONLY write path. A direct profiles update on those columns fails the whole statement.

⚠️ Keep lib/notificationTest.ts's pre-migration fallback shape: on an error selecting the three columns, re-select just id/display_name/avatar_url and return everyone unconfirmed rather than throwing.
The checklist is deliberately NOT wired to the send tool (an admin can tick it after a phone call) and NOT scoped to whoever sent the ping — any admin can check or uncheck anyone.
features.nativeOpportunity: These tools exist FOR iOS support calls, so having them on the admin's own phone while standing next to the member whose notifications are broken is the actual use case.
features.v1Cut: Defer — two admins use it, usually on a laptop.

features.name: Admin: send an announcement to everyone's Activity tab
features.whatItDoes: An admin sends a one-off notice that lands in every member's Activity list and buzzes anyone with broadcast alerts on.
rpcs: send_broadcast_notification(p_title, p_body, p_url, p_audience, p_expires_at, p_event_id, p_exclude_not_attending)
gotchas: ⚠️ p_audience is 'everyone' or 'admins' ONLY — 'beta' was removed in 0100 and now raises 'Unknown audience'. Returns an integer recipient count.
⚠️ p_event_id is TEXT, not uuid — seed events carry string ids like 'family-fest-2026'.
⚠️ p_exclude_not_attending is deliberately NARROW: it hides the item only from someone who explicitly RSVP'd status='not_going'. A no-response member still gets it, on purpose.

⚠️⚠️ This channel's push is the broadcast incident (see three-place-invariant-test): type='broadcast' is not a PushType, so the mini special-cases it onto the recipient's 'alerts' category. Do not build a client-side 'will this push?' preview off the PushType union — it will say no.
⚠️ Broadcast rows can also appear with no user action at all, from run_scheduled_broadcasts() on pg_cron. Don't assume every feed row followed a foreground event.
Keep lib/broadcast.ts's pre-migration retry shape: on an error mentioning p_event_id/p_exclude_not_attending, retry the 5-arg call.
features.v1Cut: Ship the send-now path only; defer scheduling, event targeting and the banner/email channels (those belong to the announcements table, a different section).

features.name: Don't break when the server invents a new notification kind
features.whatItDoes: Nothing visible — it stops one unrecognised item from blanking the whole Activity tab.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ `new_member` rows are in production (migration 0062) and are ABSENT from web's own NotifType union — which is why web's TYPE_EMOJI lookup returns undefined and the corner badge on an admin's '👋 Someone joined the resort' row renders BLANK.
⚠️⚠️ In Swift the same mismatch is far worse than a blank glyph: a closed enum + Decodable THROWS, and one unknown type fails the decode of the entire 100-row page, blanking the whole tab.
Decode `type` as String, map to a glyph via a dictionary with a fallback (🔔), and render title/body verbatim — they're already user-facing prose, so an unknown kind still displays correctly.
This is structural, not a one-off: 13 migrations have added kinds so far, and every future one ships to the database before it ships to the App Store.

features.name: First-run "turn on notifications?" step
features.whatItDoes: A new member is asked once, during sign-up, whether to turn on phone notifications — with everything sensible pre-ticked.
gotchas: ⚠️ profiles.push_prompted (boolean, default false, grant update (push_prompted)) is the once-only flag. 0034 backfilled it true for anyone who already had a non-empty push_types, so existing members aren't re-asked.

⚠️ Web's flow: WelcomeIntro step 2 drops the member into the real PushToggle with the master ON by default (untick what you don't want), and reaching that step stamps push_prompted so the standalone PushPrompt never also fires. Two prompts asking the same question is the failure mode to avoid.
⚠️ Accepting writes the full DEFAULT_PUSH_TYPES (14 entries) — not every category. Don't write the whole 25-value list.

⚠️ On iOS the OS permission prompt is one-shot: if the member declines, you cannot re-ask, only deep-link to Settings. Ask at a moment where the value is obvious (right after their first sign-in, as web does), not on cold launch.
features.nativeOpportunity: Native asks once, in-flow, with no 'add the app to your Home Screen first' detour — web needs a whole InstallFirstNudge interstitial before it can even ask, because iOS Safari won't grant push to a non-standalone PWA.

features.name: Committees list & a committee's page
features.whatItDoes: Browse every committee, see how many people are on it and what subcommittees it has, then open one to read its description, roles and roster.
gotchas: Everything about a committee is PUBLIC to browse — chat is the only thing membership buys. committees and committee_areas are both `using (true)`, guests included.
Member counts come from committee_roster (49 live), never committee_members (17). Using the latter is how the web card once showed '3 members' beside a 20-person roster.
Filter archived_at IS NULL for the live list; an archived committee must still be openable with an 'Archived — read-only' note.
Fetch all committees' subcommittees in ONE round-trip keyed by slug (web's fetchAreasByCommittee), not one query per row.
⚠️ Only 2 committees exist live (resort-maintenance, family-fest). Beautification was hard-deleted. Any hardcoded committee list you ship is already wrong.
⚠️ committee_areas is NOT in the realtime publication — refetch on appear and after any taxonomy RPC returns.
features.nativeOpportunity: Cache the whole list + rosters (49 rows total) in SwiftData and render fully offline with a staleness stamp — this is exactly what people look up at the lake where signal is worst.

features.name: The committee roster (who's on it, grouped by subcommittee)
features.whatItDoes: Shows everyone on a committee grouped by the subcommittee they help with, marks the leads, marks people who haven't joined the app yet, and gives each person a Text/Call/Email row.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ NEVER compare a role string raw. An entry is either 'Meals & Head Chefs' or 'Meals & Head Chefs · Lead' (U+00B7 middle dot, space either side). A raw compare already caused silent data loss on web: a lead's chip rendered unlit, so editing their other areas SAVED A LIST WITH THEIR LEAD STANDING STRIPPED. Port baseArea/isOnArea/isAreaLead/withArea/withoutArea.

⚠️⚠️ Do NOT ship a hardcoded area/roster seed as an empty-read fallback. That is exactly what hid the 0170 incident for months, and the web seed is already wrong ('Meals' vs the live 'Meals & Head Chefs').

⚠️ fetchCommitteeRoster returns the in-bundle COMMITTEES seed on a ZERO-ROW read — and 0183 makes the read return zero rows for an unapproved account, so web shows an unverified signup a hardcoded family roster. On iOS show a 'waiting to be verified' state instead.

⚠️ PostgREST embed ambiguity: committee_roster has TWO FKs to profiles (linked_user_id, updated_by). A bare `profiles(*)` embed answers HTTP 300 / PGRST201 and reads like 'no data'. Always write `profiles:linked_user_id(display_name, avatar_url)`.
Render an EMPTY subcommittee's card too ('Nobody on this one yet') — hiding it hid exactly the roles that need volunteers.
Layout areas = the DB allow-list UNION any area someone still holds that isn't in it (a role archived out from under them), so nobody silently drops off the roster.
Contact precedence: for a linked person the LINKED PROFILE's phone/contact_email wins over the roster row's own columns. Backwards, and you dial a stale number.
committee_roster SELECT is is_approved_member() — an empty read means 'not admin-approved', not 'no members'.
features.nativeOpportunity: Native Call/Message/Mail swipe actions with haptics, plus a 'Add to Contacts' CNContact write-back so the family's roster becomes the family's phone book. No browser equivalent.
features.v1Cut: Ship read + grouping + the three link states first; the add/edit sheet can come with roster-management.

features.name: A placeholder upgrades to a real account by email
features.whatItDoes: Someone can be listed on a committee before they have an account; the moment they sign up with that email their spot becomes their spot — real name, photo, contact and chat access — with no duplicate entry.
gotchas: All four triggers are SECURITY DEFINER and server-side — iOS writes an email and RENDERS the result; it never computes a link.
