⚠️ EMAIL is the only key that stamps linked_user_id. nameMatches() (the fuzzy prefix-token matcher in lib/committees.ts) is DISPLAY-ONLY forever — a fuzzy match would grant the wrong relative access to a private committee chat.
Matching is case-insensitive AND trim-insensitive on both sides; 0056 lacked the trims and silently missed a stray leading space.

⚠️ link_family_roster_from_row() sets new.linked_user_id := null FIRST and re-derives from the email, so any linked_user_id you send is DISCARDED. There is no manual-link path for family_roster — do not build a 'pick a member' control there.
⚠️ (committee_slug, name) is UNIQUE. Two same-named people can't both be on one committee and a colliding rename fails 23505 — surface that error, don't swallow it.

⚠️ review_join_request sets committee_roster.name = profiles.display_name, so approving can rename the roster row. It links an existing UNLINKED slot (email, then a forgiving name compare) before inserting — before 0090 a case difference produced a visible duplicate ('Rob' twice).
Model it as a three-case enum — linked / pending (no account, has email) / placeholder (no account, no email). Only .pending will ever auto-link.
features.nativeOpportunity: CNContactPicker when adding someone means the email — the ONE field the whole linking design depends on — is filled from the address book instead of hand-typed. Typo'd emails are the entire failure mode here.

features.name: Your own spot on a committee (self-service)
features.whatItDoes: At the top of a committee page you see your own roles, and can change which areas you help with, step down as a lead of one area while staying on it, or leave the committee — all without asking anyone.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ SUSPECTED LIVE DEFECT: leave_committee nulls linked_user_id, but that UPDATE fires link_committee_roster_from_slot_trg (BEFORE UPDATE OF email, linked_user_id) which re-stamps it from the matching email — so leaving may revoke nothing. All 6 unlinked roster rows live have emails matching NO account, i.e. there is no counter-example in the table. TEST a real leave before shipping the button.

⚠️ MyCommitteeCard paints 'You've left {committee}' optimistically on RPC success, which would hide that defect. After leave_committee, RE-READ your roster row and only show 'you left' if linked_user_id really came back nil.

⚠️ A LEAD must edit their areas via a direct committee_roster write (saveRosterEntry), NOT set_my_committee_areas — the RPC strips every ' · Lead' and would erase their standing. A plain member uses the RPC.
set_my_committee_areas requires is_committee_member(cid) first and can never self-appoint lead — that's deliberate, don't add a lead toggle here.
Step-down means replacing 'X · Lead' with 'X' in roles[] — they stay on the role as a volunteer, they don't leave it.
Self-hide for guests, non-members, and any committee without a real DB uuid (the writes key on the uuid).

features.name: Request to join a committee
features.whatItDoes: A member asks to be added to a committee, picking at least one thing they'd like to help with, and a lead approves.
gotchas: Exactly ONE overload live: request_to_join(cid uuid, msg text, requested_areas text[]). Earlier 2- and 3-arg (text) versions were dropped, so there is no ambiguity to worry about — but the arg name is `cid`, not `p_cid`.

It no-ops (and backfills a committee_members row) if you already have a linked roster slot — that 0090 fix is why a pre-registered member isn't asked to request access they already have. Mirror fetchJoinState's order: committee_members, then a linked roster slot, then a pending request.
UPSERTs on (committee_id, user_id), so re-asking after a rejection flips the same row back to pending rather than creating a new one.
The ≥1-area requirement for a role-based committee is UI-ONLY — the RPC still accepts [] deliberately, so other callers (the chat's own lock card) keep working. Build the blocking picker anyway.

Server-side validation rejects 'general'/'General' outright (reserved for the area IS NULL committee-wide channel) and, via 0076, 'admin'/'committee admin' with an 'update your app' message — a check that exists BECAUSE a stale client kept sending a role the UI no longer offered.
Read requested_areas[] and fall back to the legacy scalar requested_area.
features.v1Cut: Ship request-to-join; the approve side can wait (see join-request-queue and its blocking gate bug).

features.name: Approve or reject join requests
features.whatItDoes: Whoever runs a committee sees who has asked to join, with the areas they picked, and approves or rejects them.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ VERIFIED LIVE DEFECT: 0177 redefined is_committee_lead(cid) to the roster-based check with NO admin override, but the RLS read/delete policies on committee_join_requests and review_join_request/set_committee_member/set_committee_lead/set_committee_areas all gate on it. So an app admin who is NOT a roster lead of that committee reads ZERO pending requests (HTTP 200, empty) and gets 'Not authorized' from Approve. Verified by pg_get_functiondef + pg_policies on 2026-08-10.

⚠️ Do NOT show approve/reject based on profiles.is_admin alone or the buttons will throw. Gate on is_committee_lead-equivalent state resolved from the roster, and treat an empty request list as possibly-DENIED rather than definitely-empty.

⚠️ The right fix is backend, not Swift: restore the admin branch in is_committee_lead, or add `OR profiles.is_admin` at the five call sites and leave the Leads-chat predicate strict. Hand Brian the SQL.

⚠️ An empty requested_areas on approve means 'didn't ask for anything', NEVER 'clear their roles' (0075 — a member's two curated areas were wiped because the chat's join prompt sends '{}'). The RPC guards it now; just pass through.

⚠️ committee_join_requests is NOT in the realtime publication, yet the web app subscribes to postgres_changes on it in TWO places. Those subscriptions can never fire. Refresh on appear / on the push arriving, not via realtime.
0 pending requests live, which is why nobody has noticed the gate bug.
features.nativeOpportunity: Actionable APNs: 0061 already retargeted the committee_join_request notification entity to the REQUEST id specifically so a sender could carry an inline Approve. Ship a UNNotificationCategory with Approve/Reject calling review_join_request from the lock screen — surface the error if the gate rejects it.
features.v1Cut: Skip entirely in v1 while the gate bug is open; web can handle the (currently zero) queue.

features.name: Add, edit and remove people on a committee; assign subcommittees; make leads
features.whatItDoes: An admin or a committee's lead adds someone (with or without an app account), edits their name/email/phone, ticks which subcommittees they're on, marks leads, and removes people.
gotchas: These are DIRECT PostgREST table writes on committee_roster, not RPCs. Two permissive policies OR together: admin FOR ALL, plus lead insert/update/delete gated on is_committee_lead_slug(committee_slug) — so a lead can manage only their OWN committee, never cross-committee.

⚠️ Do NOT use set_committee_areas for assignment: it keys on user_id and so SILENTLY SKIPS account-less roster people, which made them invisible in the roles UI. Writing committee_roster directly is what lets a Pending person be put on a subcommittee.
⚠️ Do NOT use set_committee_lead: it writes the DEAD committee_members.role column. Make a lead by setting committee_roster.is_lead or adding a ' · Lead' role.
⚠️ Preserve the roster row's OWN name on write — never overwrite it with the linked account's display name (web's RolesManager keeps `rosterName` separately for exactly this).
A role can have MORE THAN ONE lead. Don't build a single-lead picker.
(committee_slug, name) is UNIQUE — a duplicate name fails 23505. Surface it.
Adding an email'd account-less person auto-creates a family_roster row (0125 trigger), so the admin can manage their house/phone/invite in one place. Say so in the UI.
Offer the pending-people picker from family_roster (fetchPendingRosterPeople) — it's the superset, and includes family who aren't on any committee yet.
Removing a person = deleting the roster row, which revokes their chat access. Confirm destructively.
features.nativeOpportunity: CNContactPicker for the add flow — name, email and phone in one tap, with the email correct. Also a native multi-select for area assignment instead of a wrap of tap-toggle chips.
features.v1Cut: v1: read-only roster. Defer add/edit/remove and lead toggles to v2 — an admin can use the web app.

features.name: Committee-level leads (a lead with no subcommittee)
features.whatItDoes: A committee can name as many overall leads as it likes without needing any subcommittees at all — they get the private Leads chat and can run the roster.
gotchas: is_lead is boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false. 0 rows use it live, so you have no real data to look at — set one in a test.

⚠️ Unify the two notions in ONE client helper: isCommitteeLead = r.isLead || r.roles.contains { $0.hasSuffix(' · Lead') }. Anything that checks only one of the two will be wrong for one of the two committees.

⚠️ is_committee_lead deliberately EXCLUDES app admins (an admin who isn't a lead is not in the Leads room). Don't 'helpfully' add an admin bypass client-side — but see join-request-queue for where that same omission is a bug.

⚠️ An account-less lead grants NOTHING: Keith Thibodeau holds 'Entertainment & Games · Lead' with linked_user_id NULL, so he shows a Lead badge and is a mailto target but can never satisfy is_committee_lead (which needs linked_user_id = auth.uid()). Of 5 lead entries live, only 4 confer anything. Gate affordances on the LINKED entry.
Don't call the older is_committee_area_lead / is_committee_area_lead_slug — nothing live references them and they miss committee-level leads.

features.name: The private "Leads" chat entry point
features.whatItDoes: Every committee has a side room only its leads can see, for discussing and deciding without the whole committee watching.
gotchas: No new tables: it's the reserved string area = 'Leads' on committee_messages, so unread/mute/mark-read all work unchanged through the existing RPCs.

⚠️ Mirror the SQL's not-exists guard client-side: skip the Leads channel row if a REAL committee_areas row named 'leads' exists (0 do today), because the DB branch backs off to ordinary-area behaviour in that case and the sentinel would otherwise hijack a real role.
⚠️ No admin override, on purpose. An app admin who isn't a lead of that committee must NOT see the room.
⚠️ 'Leads' is not a valid area for assignment — valid_committee_areas would reject it — so nobody is ever assigned it and it will never appear in an area picker.

Web opens every committee room through the Feed (/posts?c=&area=) because the standalone /committees/<slug>/chat route dies in the installed PWA before React runs. That's a WebKit-container bug with NO iOS equivalent — don't copy the URL shape as if it were meaningful.

features.name: Create, rename and delete committees
features.whatItDoes: An app admin makes a new committee, edits its name/emoji/description, archives it (reversibly), restores it, or deletes it forever.
gotchas: ⚠️ The SLUG IS IMMUTABLE. update_committee edits display fields only, because committee_roster and committee_areas key off the slug with NO foreign key — changing it orphans both tables. Never expose a slug editor.
create_committee RETURNS the new committees row (auto-slugged via slugify with -1/-2 de-duping); the others return void.
Arg names are exact and Supabase keys by name: it's `cid`, not `p_cid`, on every RPC except create_committee.
update_committee coalesces each param to the existing value when blank/null — so you can send only what changed.
'Delete' in the UI must mean ARCHIVE with restore-is-easy copy; 0178's delete_committee is a separate 'Delete forever' offered only on already-archived items, and it cascades away all chat history.
committee_roster/committee_areas have no FK to committees, so delete_committee removes them explicitly before the cascade. Don't try to clean up client-side.
features.v1Cut: Omit entirely in v1 — 2 committees change a few times a year and an admin can use the web app.

features.name: Create, describe, rename and delete subcommittees (roles)
features.whatItDoes: An admin adds a subcommittee to a committee, gives it a description, renames it, archives it, or deletes it forever — and each one is its own chat channel.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ rename_committee_area IS NOT A TABLE EDIT — it is a SEVEN-WAY cascade in one transaction: committee_areas, committee_roster.roles[] (both 'X' and 'X · Lead'), committee_members.areas[] (both forms), committee_messages.area (the CHAT HISTORY), committee_area_reads.area, committee_join_requests.requested_areas[]/requested_area, and meetings.area (added by 0121 because 0112 predated meetings and a rename orphaned the scheduled meeting). Renaming by writing the table strips history and memberships off the old name.

⚠️⚠️ THE 0170 INCIDENT: committee_areas had RLS ENABLED WITH ZERO POLICIES (switched on out-of-band from the Supabase dashboard, almost certainly to silence the Security Advisor). Writes kept working because the RPCs are SECURITY DEFINER; READS returned zero rows WITH NO ERROR because RLS filters, it doesn't raise. Adding a subcommittee looked like it did nothing, every time. And the seed fallback made Family Fest look healthy, so it went unnoticed for months.

⚠️ Knock-on from that: the role picker only renders when areaOptions.length > 0, so the ASSIGNMENT UI didn't exist on screen either — one unreadable table silently deleted the whole feature in both directions. When a list reads empty but writes succeed, check pg_policies FIRST.
⚠️ In Swift, never merge empty/denied/failed: `enum Load<T> { case loaded(T), empty, denied, failed(Error) }`. PostgREST returns 200 + [] for an RLS-denied read.
⚠️ Ship NO hardcoded area seed. Web's FAMILY_FEST_AREAS says 'Meals' where the DB says 'Meals & Head Chefs', and its fallback fires on ANY read error, not just a missing table.
Validation rejects empty names, 'general'/'General' (reserved for area IS NULL), and anything already ending ' · Lead'. Surface the thrown message inline.
Re-adding an archived name UN-ARCHIVES it (history returns live) instead of erroring on the PK — say so in the UI.
Archiving deliberately does NOT strip the role from anyone's roles[]; that's what preserves 'they were in it' and makes restore a flag flip.
delete_committee_area is destructive: it array_removes both forms from every roster/members list AND deletes that channel's committee_messages and committee_area_reads.
features.v1Cut: v1: read committee_areas from the DB (non-negotiable) but omit the whole editor. Adding a description is the cheapest single piece to add later.

features.name: Archived committees & subcommittees (read-only history)
features.whatItDoes: A committee or subcommittee that's been retired drops out of the live lists but its chat history stays readable, tucked away, and it can be brought back exactly as it was.
gotchas: Read-only is enforced in RLS, not just UI: the committee_messages insert policy carries AND NOT is_committee_area_archived(committee_id, area). Render with NO composer rather than relying on the insert failing.
A channel is archived if its COMMITTEE is archived OR its ROLE's committee_areas row is archived — build the set from both archived_at columns.
Reads still work for the people who were in it plus admins; that's deliberate and is what makes the history readable.
Keep archived chats reachable even for a member who has ONLY archived chats.
Confirm-dialog copy must say archive / restorable, not permanently delete — the destroy path is a separate action on already-archived items.
features.v1Cut: Omit the archived disclosure in v1; there are 0 archived committees and 0 archived areas live.

features.name: Family roster — relatives who aren't on the app yet
features.whatItDoes: Keeps the whole family's names, emails and phone numbers on file with a house assignment, so they still get every house and resort email, and everything pre-set for them switches on the moment they sign up.
gotchas: 14 rows live, 12 unlinked. Read = is_approved_member(); write = app admins only. An unverified account reads ZERO rows — show the verification state, not an empty list.
⚠️ UNIQUE index on lower(email) WHERE email IS NOT NULL — a second row with the same address fails 23505. Surface it.
⚠️ You cannot set linked_user_id yourself: link_family_roster_from_row() nulls it and re-derives from the email. Email is the only key.

One signup fires three things at once: the link stamp, the pre-assigned house applied to profiles.house_id (ONLY when it's null, so it never overrides a later explicit assignment), and the temp name seeding display_name (only when the member's own is blank or the raw email prefix, e.g. 'motu42').
Applying the house is NOT an escalation: house_id is out of the client update allowlist entirely, so this is just the admin's earlier decision taking effect.

⚠️ Two cascade triggers (0125) keep the rosters from drifting: adding an email'd account-less person to ANY committee auto-creates a family_roster row; editing name/email/phone here cascades to their account-less committee slots, matched by the OLD email, keeping the slot's old name on a (committee_slug, name) collision. Both are INSERT/UPDATE-only — deleting a family_roster row never touches committee slots or real accounts.

⚠️⚠️ 0184's lesson: 0183 tightened 29 RLS POLICIES but contained no function statements, and a SECURITY DEFINER function bypasses RLS by design — so directory_recipients() and admin_recipients() kept their old 'any signed-in user' check and leaked the whole 68-person family email directory (12 of whom never made an account) plus all 7 admins to any throwaway signup over the public RPC endpoint. If you add an RPC here, put the predicate INSIDE the body, and re-run 0184's pg_proc audit query.
⚠️ PostgREST embed ambiguity again: family_roster has TWO FKs to profiles (linked_user_id, updated_by) — name the FK, `profiles:linked_user_id(...)`.
family_roster is NOT in the realtime publication.
features.nativeOpportunity: CNContactPicker makes bulk-entering 12 relatives (name + email + phone) a few taps instead of 36 typed fields — and the email, the only field that makes linking work at all, comes out correct.
features.v1Cut: v1: read-only list of who's on the roster and whether they're on the app yet. Defer add/edit/remove, house chips and Invite/Invite-all.

features.name: Email a whole committee, its leads, or one subcommittee
features.whatItDoes: One tap drafts an email to everyone on a committee, to just the people running it, or to just one subcommittee — including relatives who don't have an account.
gotchas: Nothing is sent from the app — it's a hand-off. Web builds `mailto:?bcc=…`; on iOS use MFMailComposeViewController.

⚠️ committee_member_recipients(cid) returns a trailing roles text[] (0124) but reads the LEGACY committee_members.areas, so roles is empty for anyone seeded straight into the roster (most people). Resolve recipients from committee_roster yourself for a committee/role blast; keep the RPC for the shared composer.

Resolve each person's address the same way the roster does: the linked profile's contact_email wins, then their login email, then the roster row's own email — so account-less people are included and nobody's stale address is used.
'Email the leads' means everyone with is_lead OR any ' · Lead' role — including account-less ones, who are legitimate mailto targets even though they can't satisfy is_committee_lead.
Web warns past MAILTO_WARN_COUNT = 50 recipients because mail apps truncate or refuse a long mailto: URL — a native compose sheet has no such cliff, so drop the warning.
All these RPCs are SECURITY DEFINER; after 0184 the two directory ones require an APPROVED member, so an unverified account gets nothing.
features.nativeOpportunity: MFMailComposeViewController removes the mailto URL-length cliff entirely, and the roster row can carry real Call/Message/Mail swipe actions instead of a row of tiny link glyphs.
features.v1Cut: Ship 'Email everyone' and 'Email the leads' only; defer per-role and the shared composer pools.

features.name: The Family Fest season (off-season → planning → live → wrap)
features.whatItDoes: The whole app quietly changes shape across the year: a quiet banner most months, a 'planning underway' phase from 60 days out, a full 'Day 3 of 7' takeover during the week, and a 'post your photos' tail for two weeks after.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ MUST be computed from a live 'now'. A build-time evaluation freezes the phase at ship; a launch-once evaluation freezes it for as long as the app stays resident — which during fest week is days, so a backgrounded app shows 'Day 1 of 7' on Friday.
Recompute on willEnterForeground, NSCalendarDayChanged, significantTimeChange, a next-midnight timer, and any fest_config date change.
Use Calendar.startOfDay + dateComponents(.day), never TimeInterval/86400 — DST breaks the raw division and can flip a rounding boundary.

⚠️ fest_config (2026-07-27→2026-07-31) and the lib/data.ts FAMILY_FEST constant (2026-07-26→2026-08-01) ALREADY DISAGREE on web. Read fest_config and only fest_config; bundle a constant strictly as the offline seed.
Exact constants: PLANNING_LEAD_DAYS = 60, WRAP_TAIL_DAYS = 14. isSoon = isPlanning && daysUntilStart <= 7.
Publish it as an ObservableObject seeded synchronously, so no view flashes an off-season banner during the live week.
features.nativeOpportunity: A phase transition can drive real system integration a browser cannot: start a Live Activity when phase flips to live, end it at wrap; swap to a fest app-icon alternate; schedule the widget timeline.

features.name: Family Fest hub screen
features.whatItDoes: The one screen that answers 'what is Family Fest and what's happening' — cover photo, name, theme and dates, then today, RSVP, dues, committee contact, and the whole week.
gotchas: Order is deliberate: cover → title/theme/dates → Edit pill → FestStatus → FestRsvp → dues callout → committee link → FestWeek.
Sub-nav is Overview · Dinners · Pay only. There is deliberately NO Schedule pill — the Overview already renders the full week, so a Schedule tab showed the same accordion twice.
⚠️ The theme string 'Ye Olde Family Feste' lives ONLY in lib/data.ts — there is no theme column in fest_config. Bundle it or ask for a column.
⚠️ can_edit_fest() must be cached/seeded (web persists it under canEditFest.{uid}) or the Edit pill pops in a frame or two late on every visit.
Hide the sub-nav on the editor surfaces (planner/master) — they carry their own chrome.
features.nativeOpportunity: Render entirely from an on-disk cache with a quiet 'as of 8:12 AM' line instead of a spinner — this screen is opened dozens of times a day on weak lake wifi.

features.name: "Happening today" (Day n of N)
features.whatItDoes: During the week, the top of the fest screen shows every event today plus tonight's dinner in full — time, place, what it is, what to bring, and who to call — so nobody has to dig on the day.
gotchas: Events and the dinner merge into ONE time-ordered timeline via dayTimeline() — a 5:30 dinner sorts before a 6:30 event, not pinned to the bottom of the day.
Unset/unparseable times sort last (+Infinity), stably, so ties keep events before the dinner.
⚠️ Filter out anytime events from 'today' (eventsForDay(...).filter(e => !e.anytime)) or the scavenger hunt appears on all seven days.
Cards are fully expanded — no tap-to-expand here, unlike FestWeek's rows.
⚠️ Countdown: at diff == 0 swap to '🎉 Family Fest is on'; before the first tick show '——' placeholders, never a fake '00'.
⚠️ Wrap CTA points at the Drop Box album (FEST_ALBUM_BOX_ID = 0000fe57-2026-4000-8000-000000000001), which iOS does not have yet — don't ship a dead link.
Empty state is 'Nothing scheduled today — enjoy the lake! 🛶', shown only when there are no events AND no dinner.
features.nativeOpportunity: This is the screen that deserves a Live Activity and a widget: 'Day 3 of 7 · next: Dinner 6:00 PM · Main Lodge', updated off the same timeline. Plus MapKit on the location line and a contact sheet instead of a bare tel: hop.

features.name: The whole week (day-by-day schedule)
features.whatItDoes: Every day of the fest as a card, each event and that night's dinner expanding in place to its full detail — no drilling into separate pages.
gotchas: Day cards come from days-that-have-content (a Set over event days + dinner days, sorted) — NOT the full config window. The full window (eventDays) is a separate list used only for the editors' day pickers. Keep them distinct.
⚠️ Today STAYS in the list during the live week. It used to be omitted 'because FestStatus covers it', which removed today's row AND its edit button.
⚠️ Mount a tournament/realtime-bearing subview only while the row is expanded — otherwise you open one channel per event row across seven days.
Dinner rows show a 2-up Served / Crew-preps tile grid; prep location falls back to the served location when null.
⚠️ 'links' is the 0142 jsonb array. link_url/link_label were DROPPED — naming them in a select fails the whole request.
features.nativeOpportunity: A native List with sticky day headers and swipe actions (call the lead, add to calendar, share) beats an accordion; and the whole week can be persisted for offline reading.

features.name: "Anytime all week" things to do
features.whatItDoes: Things with no set time — the scavenger hunt, merch pickup — listed in their own group instead of pinned to a day.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ iOS STILL READS fest_activities. That table only still exists because of iOS, and a web edit to a converted event does not reflect on the untouched activity row — the two are drifting in live data right now. Switch iOS to fest_schedule_items where anytime = true; that is what finally lets the table be dropped.
⚠️ An anytime item still has a NOT NULL day, parked on current_date by 0141. Never display or group on it.
0141 folded the old blurb + details into the event's single description with concat_ws(E'\n\n', …) — a two-field iOS layout becomes one body field.
Use source_activity_id / source_activity_slot_id / source_activity_signup_id to reconcile any iOS-local state; the conversion is idempotent.

formatEventTime has THREE distinct strings: 'TBD' (day-locked, time still pending), 'No specific time' (anytime, no slots), 'Specific time slots' (anytime with non-headcount sign-ups). Port all three — they mean different things.

features.name: Single event detail screen
features.whatItDoes: One event on its own screen — what it is, where, what to bring, who's in charge, its sign-ups and tournament. The target of notification and call-out deep links.
gotchas: This is the deep-link target: /family-fest/schedule/{id} is what a Home call-out's 'Sign up' button and every change-notify notification point at. iOS needs a matching route in its deep-link handler or those taps land nowhere.
Header reads 'Anytime all week' instead of a date when anytime is true.
A missing event must say 'This event isn't on the schedule anymore' — not 404 hard, since a DB-only event may not have resolved yet.
canManage here is the same predicate as everywhere: can_edit_fest() OR leadUserId == uid OR crewUserIds contains uid.
⚠️ This screen has NO edit affordance on web (a known pre-existing gap — the dinner equivalent does). Don't assume symmetry.
features.nativeOpportunity: Universal Links so a notification tap opens the native event screen rather than Safari, and a share sheet that exports the event as a calendar invite.

features.name: Dinners — the weekly menu
features.whatItDoes: Reads like a menu posted on the fridge: each night's day, serving time, what's being made, the head chef, and which families are on crew — all visible at once, no tapping.
gotchas: No tap-to-expand and no click-through by design — everything a reader needs is on the card.
⚠️ Deliberately OMITS crew prep time/location. Only the crew needs that logistics; it stays editable but is not shown to every reader. Don't 'complete' the card by adding it back.
Edit is an always-visible button (not hidden behind a tap), opening the chef/crew narrow sheet or the full DinnerSheet depending on permission.
'houses' is family names as free text (comma-split on save), NOT member ids. crew_user_ids is the separate who-can-edit list.
Render chef_name (the trigger-synced snapshot), not a name resolved from profiles — an account-less chef's name exists only in that column.
The standalone dinners/[id] detail route still exists for direct links but nothing in the app points at it; keep or drop deliberately.
features.nativeOpportunity: A chef can attach a photo of the dish straight from the camera; the menu text supports Dynamic Type properly for older eyes, which the web only approximates with a text-size control.

features.name: Chef/lead/crew self-edit of operational details
features.whatItDoes: Whoever is actually cooking that night or running that event can fix the menu, the time, or the location themselves — without being on the Family Fest committee.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ The narrowness is CLIENT-SIDE ONLY. Postgres RLS is row-level, not column-level — the 0099/0110 FOR UPDATE policies authorize the whole ROW, so a lead or crew member with a REST client can change day/title/lead_user_id/crew_user_ids. NEVER show the full editor to someone whose can_edit_fest() is false. Actually enforcing it needs a SECURITY DEFINER RPC per surface (a real migration — raise it, don't ship it unilaterally).

⚠️ Writes MUST be partial (a small dictionary PATCH), not a full-model encode. The web comment: updateDinnerDetails deliberately avoids saveDinner 'which always writes every DinnerInput field and would clobber fields this surface never touches, e.g. position'. A full-model save from a screen that never loaded position writes 0 and reorders the schedule.
Dinner scope is exactly {menu, served_time, served_location, prep_time, prep_location}. Event scope is exactly {location, description, bring, links}.
The policies are FOR UPDATE, not FOR ALL — a chef cannot insert or delete a dinner.
⚠️ Don't copy the web's nil→'TBD' coercion into the model layer: the edit sheet then has to undo it (menu === 'TBD' ? '' : menu), which silently blanks a chef who literally types 'TBD'.
The edit permission check uses *_user_id, never a name match.
features.nativeOpportunity: A chef standing in the kitchen with no signal can edit and have it queue: an offline write queue that retries on reconnect is exactly the case a browser form cannot handle.

features.name: Full committee editing, right where the item shows
features.whatItDoes: An admin or committee member can change an event's or dinner's day, title, time, chef, crew and houses from the schedule itself — no trip to the Planner.
gotchas: Web reuses the Planner's OWN ScheduleSheet/DinnerSheet (exported for exactly this) rather than a duplicate narrower form. Do the same on iOS — one editor, two entry points.

⚠️ Only fetch the draft rows + member directory once can_edit_fest() resolves TRUE. Three extra round-trips on the busiest screen of the year otherwise; a chef/crew self-editor or ordinary member must never pay for them.
The full editor needs the DRAFT row (position, is_private, lead links), which the display model deliberately drops — you need a second, wider fetch/model.
fullEdit = canEditAll && draft != nil. If the draft hasn't landed, fall back to the narrow sheet rather than showing a broken full form.
After a save, both the content bundle and the drafts must reload (web threads an onContentSaved callback up to the screen that owns the fetch).
features.v1Cut: Ship the narrow self-edit sheets first and keep sending full editors to the web master editor via the existing session hand-off. Full in-place editing is the largest read-path-adjacent chunk in this section.

features.name: Lead/chef names that follow a rename
features.whatItDoes: When someone changes their display name, every event they lead and dinner they cook updates to the new name automatically.
gotchas: Fully server-side — a profiles AFTER UPDATE OF display_name trigger plus a one-time backfill. It fixed web and iOS at once precisely because both read the same columns. NO client change is needed.
⚠️ Therefore: RENDER lead_name / chef_name, not a name you join from profiles. An account-less lead's name exists ONLY in the snapshot column, so a join diverges from web and shows nothing.
Use *_user_id ONLY for the 'is this me?' edit check — never a name match. The trigger itself matches on *_user_id for the same reason (an account-less lead is left untouched).
An empty/blank lead_name means 'no lead' (render no In-charge block), not 'unknown lead'. Dinners differ: a missing chef coerces to 'TBD' so the card always has a chef line.
The bug this fixed: a member assigned while their name was still the email prefix 'motu42' kept showing motu42 forever, even though the edit sheet resolved the live profile.

features.name: Dues calculator
features.whatItDoes: Plus/minus steppers per dues tier — '2 adults, 1 kid' — that work out the total and fill in the payment amount and note for you.
gotchas: Two groups: flat tiers (count × amount) and per_day tiers (count × amount × days), where ALL per-day tiers share ONE day-count stepper — a single payment assumes everyone in it is here the same span. Mixed households run it twice; Reset clears it.
maxDays = max(1, getFestSeason(config.startDate, config.endDate).totalDays) — another reason the season function has to be right.
⚠️ amount is a nullable INT of whole dollars. nil means TBD — never render '$0', and render NO stepper at all for an unpriced tier.
The per-day block only appears when at least one per_day tier has a non-nil amount.
Counts clamp to 0…99.

features.name: Family Fest card on Home

gotchas: This card may belong to the Home section's spec — coordinate so it isn't built twice.

The committee-membership check is cached under the SAME festMember.{uid} key FestStatus uses, so the two share one deduped fetch — otherwise the 'Join the Family Fest committee' CTA flashes in and vanishes for an actual member on every home visit.

It is the permanent, non-swipeable BASE of the Home call-out stack — temporary call-outs stack on top of it and it never goes away.

features.name: Verified-member check on your own account
features.whatItDoes: The app quietly checks whether an admin has okayed your account, and always assumes you are okay whenever it cannot tell.
tables: profiles (approved boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, approved_at timestamptz nullable, approved_by uuid -> profiles(id) ON DELETE SET NULL)
rpcs: is_approved_member() -> boolean (SECURITY DEFINER, STABLE, EXECUTE granted to authenticated AND anon)
gotchas: The database column is `profiles.approved`. The user-facing word is "Verified." That mismatch is deliberate and documented — Supabase already owns "verified" for email confirmation. Do not "clean this up" in either direction: keep `approved` in your Codable structs and "Verified" in the copy.

`approved` missing, null, or the read failed => TREAT AS VERIFIED. An unknown or unreadable approval flag must default to verified; the failure mode to avoid is locking real members out of their own app over an optional column, a dropped request, or a schema-cache miss.

The web defaults to verified in THREE independent places and you must mirror all three: the initial state value (`useState(true)`, so a returning member never flashes the waiting screen while the profile query is in flight), the read-error branch, and the column-absent branch (`e.approved === undefined ? true : e.approved !== false`). `false` is the only value that gates.
Auth still settling => neutral skeleton — never flash either wall.

Do NOT decode `approved` as non-optional `Bool`. A non-optional field makes the whole JSONDecoder throw if the key is missing, and your catch-all error path is exactly where you must not conclude "unverified". Use `let approved: Bool?` plus `verified = (flags.approved != false)`.

An admin is IMPLICITLY approved — `is_approved_member()` body is `exists(select 1 from profiles where id = auth.uid() and (approved is true or is_admin is true))`. There is no such thing as an unverified admin.

`approved` is NOT in any `grant update(...) on profiles to authenticated` list, so a client literally cannot write it (0001 revoked update from anon/authenticated then re-granted specific columns, so new columns are locked out by default). The RPC is the only write path.

Read `approved_at` in one direction only: `approved_at is null` means "never decided", but a non-NULL `approved_at` does NOT mean a human decided — 0181's backfill stamped it on all 56 rows and 0182's trigger stamps it too. `approved_at` set with `approved_by` NULL = the backfill or a roster auto-approval. You never need either column for a UI decision.

`approved_at` is `timestamptz`; PostgREST emits `2026-08-10T14:22:03.123456+00:00`. Swift's ISO8601DateFormatter with `.withFractionalSeconds` is fussy about 6-digit fractions — configure supabase-swift's decoder with a lenient date strategy, or decode as `String` and parse lazily.

The own-row escape hatch on `profiles` (`is_approved_member() or id = auth.uid()`) is load-bearing: without it an unverified member cannot read their own profile row, so you cannot load their identity, cannot read `approved`, and cannot even show them the waiting screen. It is recursion-safe because `is_approved_member()` is SECURITY DEFINER and bypasses RLS on `profiles`.
`is_preregistered_email(p_email text)` has `revoke all ... from public` and NO grant to authenticated — iOS CANNOT call it. It exists only for the auto-approve trigger.

0183 swapped exactly 29 SELECT policies inside a single BEGIN/COMMIT: iOS needs ZERO query changes, every table/column/filter stays identical — what changes is that an unapproved session gets empty arrays back.

features.name: "You're signed in — almost there" waiting screen
features.whatItDoes: A newcomer who has signed in but hasn't been okayed by an admin yet sees a friendly explanation instead of an app that looks empty and broken.
gotchas: THE TRAP: an unverified newcomer handed the normal member layout sees a Posts tab with no posts, a People tab with one person (themself), an album with no photos — an app that looks broken. You must add an explicit UI state.
In every case empty means "NOT PERMITTED", not "no data".

UI states: Signed out => existing guest view unchanged. Signed in with `approved == false` => treat as GUEST and on any members-only screen show an explicit "You're signed in — almost there" panel: an admin needs to okay the account, it's a quick check that everyone here is family, and there is nothing more to do on their end. Signed in with `approved == true` => full member view.

Read rules: `profiles` — readable by any approved member plus your own row always. `albums`, `committee_roster`, `family_roster`, `houses`, `event_attendance`, `help_requests`, `help_responses`, `help_request_items`, `polls`, `poll_options`, `poll_votes`, `post_media`, `post_comment_media`, `post_comment_mentions`, `post_reactions`, `post_tags`, `drop_boxes` — approved members only. `posts`/`post_comments` — approved member AND (status='visible' OR author OR admin). `drop_box_media` — approved member AND (status='visible' OR uploaded_by = auth.uid() OR admin). `work_items` — approved member AND (house_id is null OR in that house). `tournaments`/`tournament_entrants`/`tournament_matches`/`tournament_participants` — approved member AND private_activity_id is null or you're in that private activity. `meetings`/`meeting_slots`/`meeting_availability` — CASE on scope_type ('committee' -> can_access_committee_area, 'house' -> is_house_member, 'family' -> is_approved_member(), else false); only the 'family' branch changed.
Unchanged and already stricter: `committee_messages`/`house_messages` and their media (gated on can_access_committee_area / is_house_member) — chat was already closed to a stranger.

Unchanged, public by design: `events`, `cabins`, `announcements`, `committees`, `committee_areas` (using(true) since 0170), `resort_config`, `app_images`, and all the fest_* content tables (`fest_config`, `fest_dues`, `fest_schedule_items`, `fest_dinners`, `fest_payees`, `fest_activities` — using(true) since 0053).

`notifications` — your own rows only (`recipient_id = auth.uid()`), unchanged. An unapproved user can still RECEIVE and read a notification; tapping it lands on empty content, which is another reason the waiting state must exist.

`public_profiles` (view, 0081) — SELECT granted to anon AND authenticated; returns `id`, FIRST NAME ONLY, `avatar_url`. The masked name is `split_part(trim(coalesce(nullif(display_name, ''), full_name, '')), ' ', 1)` aliased back to `display_name`, so it falls back to `full_name` when `display_name` is blank. An unverified member now falls back to this tier for other people's names — same as a signed-out visitor.
With 56 members approved and 12 roster emails auto-approving, the waiting-for-approval state is RARE BUT REAL. Build it anyway; it is the whole point of the migration.
Do this BEFORE the Drop Box work — it costs almost nothing and it's what stops a newcomer seeing an app that looks broken.

features.name: "🔒 Waiting to be approved" inline chip
features.whatItDoes: Where a not-signed-in visitor sees a "sign in to see this" chip, someone waiting on approval sees a plain note that they're waiting — with no button to tap.
gotchas: Where the web shows an inline "🔒 Sign in to see" chip for a guest, an UNVERIFIED member gets a NON-INTERACTIVE "🔒 Waiting to be approved" chip instead — a sign-in button is actively wrong for someone who already signed in successfully and will just make them retry a thing that worked.

features.name: Instant paint of who you are on app open
features.whatItDoes: The app remembers your name and status on the device so a returning member sees their own view immediately instead of a blank or guest screen.
gotchas: The web caches an identity snapshot in `localStorage` keyed `identity.<userId>` so a returning member paints instantly. Use UserDefaults/Keychain on iOS.

KEY ANY CACHED PRIVATE DATA ON THE REAL PER-USER IDENTIFIER, NEVER A SHARED CONSTANT — the web app leaked one member's cached private chat to the next user of the same device because a cache key was a literal "self", and sign-out doesn't reload a native app either.
The initial verified state must start optimistic (true) specifically so a returning member never flashes the waiting screen while the profile query is in flight.

features.name: Photos and downloads respect the same approval gate
features.whatItDoes: Someone still waiting on approval can't load or upload photos, and gets the same friendly "almost there" screen rather than an error alert.
rpcs: isApprovedMemberByToken() (media-server helper, returns true / false / null)
endpoints: GET /media-token (requireUser + an inline approval gate) -> 403 { error: "…", pendingApproval: true }
gotchas: The Mac-mini media server (https://mlr-media.duckdns.org) enforces approval INDEPENDENTLY, because it serves the photo bytes.
`pendingApproval: true` is NOT an error state — it's the waiting state. Route a 403-with-pendingApproval to the same "almost there" screen, not to an alert.
`GET /media-token` answers `no-store` with NO ETag, written via `res.end()` so it can never 304.
`GET`/`POST /dropbox-zip` reads the JWT from the QUERY STRING / FORM BODY, which is why it needed a separate `isApprovedMemberByToken()` variant and was briefly ungated.

The server applies the identical FAIL-OPEN rule: `isApprovedMemberByToken()` returns true / false / null, and null (column missing, transient failure, service key unset) is treated as ALLOW. Callers only block on an explicit `false`.

VERIFY BEFORE RELYING: `MEDIA_AUTH` mode is reported as `report`, not `on`, specifically because the native app cannot sign media URLs yet — but this is not verifiable from the repo (`media-auth.js` defaults to `off` via `process.env.MEDIA_AUTH || "off"` and the live value lives only in the mini's gitignored .env), so check it on the box. Once iOS ships the media token it will be promoted to `on`, at which point an unsigned URL is a 403. Assume enforcement.

features.name: Admin can verify or un-verify a member
features.whatItDoes: An admin sees who is waiting to be okayed and taps a button to let them in — or to take access back.
rpcs: set_member_approved(p_user uuid, p_value boolean) -> void (SECURITY DEFINER; raises 'Only app admins can approve members' unless the caller has profiles.is_admin; stamps approved_at = now() and approved_by = auth.uid() on BOTH approve and revoke)
admin_members() (0100 definition returns id, display_name, avatar_url, household, email, is_admin, house_id, house_name, created_at — NO approved)
gotchas: THE WEB'S ADMIN VERIFY BUTTON DOES NOT CURRENTLY WORK, and reading the web code as a reference will mislead you. `AdminMembers.tsx` defines `mergeApproval(sb, rows)` — which does `sb.from("profiles").select("id, approved")` and merges it onto the directory — and NEVER calls it (exactly one occurrence, the definition at line 35).

Rows come from `admin_members()`, whose current definition (0100) returns no `approved`; the pre-0008 fallback path selects `id, display_name, avatar_url, household, is_admin` and doesn't include it either. So `m.approved` is always `undefined`, which means the "Not verified" chip, the ✓ Verify / Un-verify button (`m.approved !== undefined && m.approved !== null`), the VerifiedBadge (`if (verified !== true) return null`) and the "N people need verifying" banner ALL render nothing. Today an admin can only approve someone by calling `set_member_approved` from the SQL editor.

FOR iOS: fetch the flag yourself — `admin_members()` for the directory, then a SEPARATE `profiles.select("id, approved")` merged client-side by id. (`PeopleDirectory.tsx` does exactly that and its badge works.)

0181 deliberately did NOT widen `admin_members()`: per the 0160 lesson, that function has been recreated by 0008 -> 0029 -> 0064 -> 0100, and rebuilding it from an older copy silently drops whatever the newest version added. A plain additive select is the safe move.

Supabase RPC arguments are matched BY NAME, so a wrong key fails at runtime, not at compile time. Use a Codable struct whose property names are character-for-character the SQL parameter names: `struct SetMemberApproved: Encodable { let p_user: UUID; let p_value: Bool }`.

If you use a JSONEncoder with `.convertToSnakeCase` anywhere near these structs, `p_user` stays `p_user` but any camelCase key you invent will be silently renamed. Keep RPC param structs plain and snake_case-by-hand.
The Verify / Un-verify button is hidden for yourself and for admins, since an admin is implicitly approved.
Surface includes a "N people need verifying" banner and an explicit "Not verified" chip on the row.

VERIFY BEFORE RELYING: `mergeApproval` being dead code was confirmed by grep at commit `4a2ea79` and was still true as of this pass; it may be fixed on web by the time you read this. Either way, fetch `approved` yourself.
features.nativeOpportunity: The web's Verify button renders nothing today, so iOS would be the first actually-working admin verify surface.

features.name: ✓ Verified badge with a tap-to-learn-more explainer
features.whatItDoes: A small checkmark next to a relative's name shows an admin confirmed they're family, and tapping it explains what the checkmark means.
gotchas: The ✓ badge renders NOTHING for an unverified person on family-facing surfaces. An "unverified" label next to a relative's name in the directory is a quiet accusation and isn't actionable for a member. Admins get the explicit chip instead.

The badge is TAPPABLE and opens an explainer ("An admin confirmed that … is part of the family"). On web this had to be portaled out of the row (it was clipped to invisibility inside a `truncate` container) and could not be a `<button>` inside the row's `<button>`. Neither constraint exists in SwiftUI — but do keep the affordance; people ask what the checkmark means.
Fetch `approved` yourself in the directory's own query (`PeopleDirectory.tsx` does this and its badge works, unlike AdminMembers').
features.nativeOpportunity: SwiftUI has neither of web's constraints (no portal-out-of-row needed, no nested-button restriction), so the tappable badge is simpler natively.

features.name: Verified counts and a "show only unverified" filter in Admin → Members
features.whatItDoes: An admin can see at a glance how many people are verified versus waiting, and narrow the list to just the ones needing a decision.
gotchas: Two surfaces the section-writer expected and the web does NOT actually have — build them on iOS, but don't go looking for a working reference.

There is NO "N verified · N not verified" counter. The panel header renders `{members.length} members · {adminCount} admins` (AdminMembers.tsx:270). `verifiedCount` is computed at :255 and never referenced.
There is NO unverified-only filter control. `showOnly` exists (:80) and is applied at :261, but `setShowOnly` has zero call sites, so nothing can flip it.

features.name: Admin "view as" preview never shows the admin as unverified
features.whatItDoes: When an admin previews the app as a guest or another member, their own account never appears to be waiting for approval.
gotchas: The web forces `verified = true` while an admin is using "view as" preview, so an admin checking the guest view never appears unverified to themself. Only relevant if you port preview mode.

features.name: Close the self-approval loophole (backend SQL, not iOS)
features.whatItDoes: Stops someone who is waiting for approval from letting themselves in by typing a family member's email address into their own contact details.
rpcs: auto_approve_preregistered() (trigger fn, not callable; BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF contact_email ON profiles; trigger name trg_auto_approve_preregistered)
gotchas: BACKEND CHANGE NEEDED — a likely self-approval hole in 0182. VERIFY THIS, THEN FIX IT IN SQL, NOT IN iOS.

`contact_email` IS in a member's own update grant (0006: `grant update (phone, contact_email, venmo, …) on profiles to authenticated`), and the trigger fires BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF contact_email. Read literally, an unapproved signup can PATCH their own row's `contact_email` to any address that appears on `committee_roster.email` or `family_roster.email` — real family addresses, guessable, and visible to any approved member — and the trigger sets `approved := true` because `approved_at` is still NULL.
`link_family_roster()` (0123) would additionally stamp `linked_user_id` and carry the roster's pre-assigned `house_id` onto the account.

The INSERT branch is sound (`handle_new_user()` seeds contact_email from the OTP-verified auth.users.email); the UPDATE branch trusts a self-settable column. Sensible fix directions: match against `auth.users.email` instead of `profiles.contact_email`, or drop the `UPDATE OF contact_email` branch entirely.
DO NOT paper over this by hiding the contact-email field in the iOS UI — the REST API is the boundary, not your app.

The auto-approve trigger is guarded on `approved_at is null` ("no human has decided yet"). Without that, an admin who deliberately REVOKED someone would see them silently re-approved the next time their email was touched, making revoke useless. Because it stamps `approved_at` itself, it can also only ever fire ONCE per person. Preserve this guard in any fix.

The trigger matches roster email trim + case-insensitively, same matching as the 0056/0060 roster auto-link, and sets TWO columns (`approved := true` and `approved_at := now()`) while deliberately leaving `approved_by` NULL because nobody tapped a button.

GENERALISE THE 0184 LESSON: policies and SECURITY DEFINER functions are two separate surfaces — sweep both. 0183 swapped 29 policies and contained no function statements, so `directory_recipients()` (name + best email for 68 people, 12 with no account) and `admin_recipients()` (name + email of all 7 admins — a target list) kept their old "any signed-in user" check and a brand-new throwaway account could still call them over the public REST RPC endpoint. If you add a gate, enumerate `pg_proc` for `prosecdef` functions executable by `authenticated` as well as `pg_policies`.

Also from 0184: both function bodies were copied VERBATIM from the live `pg_get_functiondef()` output, not from the migrations that created them, with the predicate as the only edit. Because they use `set search_path to ''`, every reference must be schema-qualified — `public.is_approved_member()`, not `is_approved_member()`, or it fails at runtime with "function does not exist."
VERIFY BEFORE RELYING: this was read from the SQL, not observed live. Confirm with a throwaway account against a NON-PRODUCTION project before deciding how urgent the fix is.

features.name: "Email a group" recipient lists are approval-gated
features.whatItDoes: The lists of family and admin email addresses used by the email-a-group tool are only handed out to members an admin has verified.
rpcs: directory_recipients() -> table(id uuid, name text, email text) (no parameters, SECURITY DEFINER, gated on public.is_approved_member())
admin_recipients() -> table(id uuid, name text, email text) (no parameters, SECURITY DEFINER, gated on public.is_approved_member())
gotchas: Only relevant if you build the "Email a group" tool.

VERIFY BEFORE RELYING: whether 0184 has been run on production. 0181–0183 were applied 2026-08-10. If 0184 hasn't landed, `directory_recipients()` / `admin_recipients()` are still open to ANY signed-in account. `is_approved_member()` being present is not evidence that 0184 is.
Both functions use `set search_path to ''`, so every reference must be schema-qualified — `public.is_approved_member()`, not `is_approved_member()`.

features.name: Attach photos and videos to a comment
features.whatItDoes: You can add photos or videos to a comment on the Main Feed, including a comment that is nothing but a photo.
tables: post_comment_media (id uuid PK, comment_id uuid NOT NULL -> post_comments(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, storage_path text NOT NULL, media_type text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'image' check in ('image','video'), position int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), thumbnail_url text nullable added by 0173)
endpoints: POST /upload (default category=posts) -> { url, thumbnailUrl, hlsUrl, capturedAt, capturedAtSource, name, originalName, type, path }
gotchas: No RPC — plain inserts. 1) Insert the comment: `post_comments` <- { post_id, author_id, text }, returning `id`. Text may be empty IF there is at least one attachment (a photo-only comment is valid, same rule as the post composer). 2) Optional mentions: `post_comment_mentions` <- { comment_id, mentioned_user_id }. 3) For each file: upload to POST /upload (default category=posts), then insert `post_comment_media` <- { comment_id, storage_path: res.url, media_type, position: i, thumbnail_url: res.thumbnailUrl }.
`storage_path` is the FULL MINI URL, not a relative path.
`post_comment_media` mirrors `post_media` (0004) exactly. Index: (comment_id, position). Added to the `supabase_realtime` publication.

RLS — Read: approved members only (0183). Insert: only if you are the author of that comment (`exists (select 1 from post_comments c where c.id = comment_id and c.author_id = auth.uid())`). Delete: the comment's author, or an admin.

features.name: Comment photos shown as a small row of thumbnails
features.whatItDoes: Photos on a comment appear as small tappable thumbnails inside the thread, and tapping one opens it full screen.
gotchas: Render comment media as a SMALL WRAPPING ROW OF THUMBNAILS, not the full-bleed grid a post uses — the post treatment is visually far too heavy inline in a thread. Tap opens the full-screen viewer.
Grids must render `thumbnail_url`, not `storage_path`; fall back to `storage_path` when `thumbnail_url` is nil.

features.name: A comment held for review disappears until an admin approves it
features.whatItDoes: If a comment's photo trips the automatic content check, the comment quietly becomes visible only to its author and admins — sometimes a few seconds after it was posted.
endpoints: POST /upload (category=posts — graded inline by the mini)
gotchas: Moderation needs ZERO client code, but the status can change under you. Uploads under `category=posts` are graded INLINE by the mini, so a flagged verdict usually already exists in `media_moderation` by the time you insert.

The DB trigger `hold_comment_on_flagged_media()` flips the parent `post_comments.status` from 'visible' to 'pending', and RLS hides it from everyone but the author and admins. There is also a reverse-race branch in `hold_content_on_media_verdict()` for a verdict that lands AFTER the row.
HONOUR `post_comments.status` WHEN RENDERING, and expect a comment you just posted to become `pending` a few seconds later. Don't cache the row's status forever.
The web does NOT select `status` on comments — it leans entirely on RLS — so there's no reference implementation to copy here; select it yourself.

features.name: Tapping a comment notification jumps to that exact comment
features.whatItDoes: Tapping a notification about a comment, reply, or mention opens the post and scrolls straight to the comment being talked about, flashing it briefly.
gotchas: URL shape: `/posts?post=<post uuid>&comment=<comment uuid>` for notification types `post_comment`, `post_reply` and `post_mention`. The APNs payload's `url` field is `${APP_URL}${n.url}`, so the query string arrives on device intact.
iOS work: parse BOTH `post` and `comment`, open the post, then scroll to and briefly flash that specific comment.

Comments render UNPAGINATED on web (every comment of a loaded post is in the tree), so there's no "expand thread first" step; if you paginate on iOS, you need to force-load the page containing that comment id.

Notification rows created BEFORE 0164 keep their post-only url. That's a deliberate, harmless degrade — it still opens the right post. Treat a missing `comment` param as NORMAL, never as a malformed link.

The `notifications` select needs an FK HINT, because the table has TWO FKs to `profiles` (`recipient_id` and `actor_id`): "id, type, actor_id, title, body, url, created_at, seen_at, read_at, expires_at, actor:profiles!actor_id(display_name, avatar_url)". An unhinted embed across two candidate FKs returns HTTP 300 / PGRST201 and decodes as an EMPTY ARRAY — a bug that looks exactly like "no data." Name the FK.

features.name: Mute a chat for 1 / 3 / 7 days or until you turn it back on
features.whatItDoes: You can silence a committee-area chat or your house chat for a set stretch of time, or indefinitely, and one tap un-mutes it.
tables: committee_area_reads (muted boolean existing, muted_until timestamptz added)
house_reads (muted boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false added, muted_until timestamptz added)
rpcs: set_area_mute(cid uuid, p_area text, p_muted boolean, p_muted_until timestamptz DEFAULT null) -> void (SECURITY DEFINER, EXECUTE to authenticated, upserts on (committee_id, user_id, area))
set_house_mute(hid uuid, p_muted boolean, p_muted_until timestamptz DEFAULT null) -> void (SECURITY DEFINER, EXECUTE to authenticated, upserts on (house_id, user_id))
gotchas: House chat had NO mute at all before 0155.

A row is effectively muted when `muted` is true OR `muted_until` is set and still in the future. A timer clears itself by going stale — there is NO cron and nothing writes `muted` back to false. Compute it at read time: `let mutedNow = (row.muted ?? false) || (row.muted_until.map { $0 > Date() } ?? false)`.
NOTE THE FIRST PARAMETER IS NOT `p_`-PREFIXED on either RPC (`cid`, `hid`). RPC args match by name, so a wrong key fails at runtime.
`p_muted = false` always clears `muted_until` too, so "unmute" fully resets the row.

`p_area` is `coalesce(p_area, '')` server-side — the committee's MAIN chat uses the EMPTY STRING, not null, as its area key. The Leads room uses the literal string 'Leads' as a sentinel area. Send "" for the main room or you'll upsert a second, orphaned read row.
RLS on both read tables: your own rows only (`user_id = auth.uid()`), so a query that returns nothing means "no row yet" (not muted), which is the correct default.

Push suppression is ALREADY SERVER-SIDE — `push-sender.js` and `apns-sender.js` both filter recipients with `.or("muted.eq.true,muted_until.gt.<now ISO>")` before sending. iOS gets correct mute behaviour on APNs for free; all you owe is the UI.
Web pattern: tapping the bell on an already-muted row is a one-tap UNMUTE; tapping an unmuted row opens the duration sheet.

features.name: Activity feed survives notification kinds it doesn't recognise
features.whatItDoes: A new kind of notification (like an admin's test ping) shows up harmlessly instead of breaking the whole Activity list.
gotchas: `admin_test` is a REAL NotifType your Activity feed and your APNs handler will receive. If your notification-type enum is a Swift `enum: String, Decodable`, an unknown raw value THROWS AND KILLS THE WHOLE DECODE OF THE FEED PAGE.
Give it an `unknown` fallback (`init(from:)` with `?? .unknown`) or keep `type` as a `String` with a lookup table for the icon. Web maps `admin_test` to 🧪.

`admin_test` is deliberately absent from the notification-preferences screen (there's nothing to opt into) — same as `broadcast`, which is also pushed via the `alerts` category rather than a type of its own.

features.name: Admin sends a test notification to one member
features.whatItDoes: An admin can fire a single test alert at one person's phone to check whether notifications reach them, without bothering anyone else.
rpcs: send_test_notification(p_user uuid, p_title text DEFAULT null, p_body text DEFAULT null) -> uuid (admin-gated SECURITY DEFINER; raises 'Not authorized' / 'Member not found')
gotchas: Inserts one `notifications` row of type `admin_test`, defaulting to title "🔔 Test notification".
It BYPASSES `profiles.notif_types` entirely (the admin explicitly targeted one person, so there's no preference to consult).

The phone push is an OVERRIDE. Both mini senders list `admin_test` alongside `help_urgent`: anyone with `push_types` non-empty gets buzzed regardless of their per-category picks. If push is fully off they correctly get nothing — that's useful diagnostic signal, not a bug.

features.name: "Notifications confirmed" checklist for admins
features.whatItDoes: Admins keep a simple checked-off list of family members whose notifications have actually been seen working on their phone.
tables: profiles (notifications_confirmed boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, notifications_confirmed_at timestamptz, notifications_confirmed_by uuid -> profiles(id) ON DELETE SET NULL)
rpcs: set_notification_test_confirmed(p_user uuid, p_value boolean) -> void (admin-gated; stamps or clears the timestamp and the who together)
gotchas: Only writable via the RPC — the three columns are not in any client update grant.
Any admin can check or uncheck anyone.
It is deliberately NOT wired to the send tool (an admin can confirm after a phone call just as well).

features.name: Family roster: family who aren't on the app yet
features.whatItDoes: Admins keep a list of relatives who don't have an account yet — name, email, phone, which house — so they're linked up automatically the day they sign in.
tables: family_roster (id uuid PK, name text NOT NULL, email text nullable — THE JOIN KEY with a unique index on lower(email) where not null, phone text nullable, house_id uuid -> houses(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, position int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, linked_user_id uuid -> profiles(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, updated_at, updated_by)
rpcs: link_family_roster() (trigger, SECURITY DEFINER, AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF contact_email ON profiles)
link_family_roster_from_row() (trigger, SECURITY DEFINER, BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF email ON family_roster)
family_from_committee_roster() (AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF email, linked_user_id ON committee_roster)
sync_committee_roster_from_family() (AFTER UPDATE OF name, email, phone)
house_member_recipients(hid uuid) -> table(id uuid, name text, email text) (gated on is_house_member(hid))
all_member_recipients() (gated on admin-or-any-committee-member — that check reads the legacy committee_members table, NOT committee_roster)
meeting_proposal_email(p_meeting uuid) -> table(title text, url text, emails text[]) (service-role only)
meeting_confirmed_email(p_meeting uuid) -> table(title text, description text, meet_url text, when_label text, url text, emails text[]) (service-role only)
committee_member_recipients(cid uuid) -> table(id uuid, name text, email text, roles text[]) (gated on is_committee_member(cid), not on approval)
gotchas: V1 RECOMMENDATION: SKIP THIS. It's an admin data-entry surface with no member-facing screen. The one thing worth knowing is that a member's house and display name can arrive from a roster row they never saw.

RLS — Read: approved members only (0183 — it carries emails, i.e. PII). Write (for all): app admins only. A non-admin's insert/update SILENTLY FAILS; don't build an optimistic write path for non-admins.

`link_family_roster()` stamps `linked_user_id`; carries the roster's `house_id` onto `profiles.house_id` ONLY IF the account has none yet; and seeds `display_name` from the roster name only if the member hasn't set their own (blank, or still the raw email prefix), preferring `family_roster` then `committee_roster`.
`link_family_roster_from_row()` sets `new.linked_user_id := null` first and re-resolves, so NEVER WRITE `linked_user_id` FROM A CLIENT — it will be overwritten.

0125 keeps one person as one record: adding an email'd, account-less person to ANY committee roster also creates their `family_roster` row, and editing name/email/phone on `family_roster` cascades to their account-less committee slots. So if you build a roster editor, expect a single write to change rows in TWO tables — refetch both, don't patch locally.

`meeting_proposal_email` / `meeting_confirmed_email` have been recreated several times — the CURRENT definitions are 0133's (0132 had accidentally dropped 0123's account-less roster UNIONs; 0133 restored them). The return shapes are unchanged.

0124 widened `committee_member_recipients(cid uuid)` to return `roles text[]` — THE RETURN TYPE CHANGED, so the old signature was `drop function`'d. `roles` is `null` when empty, not `[]`; decode as `[String]?`.

Swift shapes: `roles text[]` -> `[String]?`. `crew_user_ids uuid[]` -> `[UUID]`. The embed for the linked account is "…, profiles:linked_user_id(display_name, avatar_url)" — the alias names the FK column, which is what keeps it unambiguous.

Pre-migration degrade convention worth copying: the web probes with `family_roster.select("id").limit(1)` and treats 42P01 (undefined table) or PGRST205 (schema-cache miss) as "not ready", showing a hint instead of a silent empty list.
features.v1Cut: Skip the whole admin data-entry surface for v1; only honour that a member's house and display name may arrive from a roster row they never saw.

features.name: Photo grids load small previews instead of full-size files
features.whatItDoes: Scrolling an album or a photo grid is fast because each tile loads a small preview, and the full photo only loads when you tap it.
endpoints: POST /upload -> { url, thumbnailUrl, hlsUrl, capturedAt, capturedAtSource, name, originalName, type, path }
gotchas: 0173 added a nullable `thumbnail_url text` to ALL SIX media tables. The mini generates a ~400px JPEG preview at upload time (sharp for photos, one ffmpeg frame grab for videos) and returns it as `thumbnailUrl` in the /upload JSON response.

GRIDS MUST RENDER `thumbnail_url`, NOT `storage_path`. Every grid on web used to render the exact stored file, so scrolling an album re-downloaded full-resolution photos and post-transcode videos for every tile. Load the full asset ONLY when someone taps through to the full-screen viewer.

Fall back to `storage_path` when `thumbnail_url` is nil (pre-migration rows, or a generation that failed — it is best-effort and never fatal): `let tileURL = media.thumbnail_url ?? media.storage_path` — never the reverse.
A VIDEO TILE NEEDS A VISIBLE ▶ BADGE. With a generated poster frame it is indistinguishable from a photo; without one it's a black box.

A video's poster frame is seeked ~10% in (capped at 3s), not frame 0. Real phone video routinely opens on a black or half-exposed frame while the camera settles; grabbing frame 0 produced a whole album of black tiles. If you ever generate a poster client-side, do the same — and size-check the output, because a seek past the last keyframe can produce an empty file WITHOUT erroring.

The hard-won lesson: an enrichment that only runs at upload time covers none of the content already there. When thumbnail.js shipped, EVERY row in every media table still had `thumbnail_url = null` (0/48 album items, 0/45 post media) — grids were universally falling back to full-res and nobody noticed, because the fallback works. A separate sweep (`thumbnail-backfill.js`) fills the NULLs from files on disk. If you add an iOS-side enrichment, ask "what about the rows that already exist?"

features.name: New uploads save their preview image (and survive an older database)
features.whatItDoes: Every photo or video you upload records its small preview so grids stay fast, and a photo still attaches even if the server is missing the newer fields.
rpcs: add_work_item_media(p_work_item_id uuid, p_url text, p_media_type text DEFAULT 'image', p_position int DEFAULT 0, p_thumbnail_url text DEFAULT null) -> uuid
create_post(p_caption text, p_occurred_at timestamptz, p_media jsonb, p_tags uuid[], p_held boolean) -> uuid (every parameter has a DEFAULT, and PostgREST matches by name, so send only what you need)
gotchas: Four direct inserts, two RPCs: `post_media`, `post_comment_media`, `committee_message_media`, `house_message_media` are plain RLS-gated inserts — just include `thumbnail_url`. (`post_media` also gets written by `create_post`; the direct insert is the "add media to an existing post" path.)

`create_post`'s media array has per-item keys in camelCase: `path`, `type`, `thumbnail`, `capturedAt`, `capturedAtSource`. NOTE `thumbnail`, NOT `thumbnail_url`, and camelCase — a snake_case-converting encoder will silently drop `capturedAt`/`capturedAtSource` and you'll lose the date with NO ERROR.

SIGNATURE-CHANGE DISCIPLINE (the 0115 incident): every widening of `add_drop_box_media` / `add_work_item_media` explicitly `drop function`s the narrower overload first. Postgres would otherwise keep both, and PostgREST would resolve to whichever matched your argument count — so an old client silently kept writing rows without the new field. If you ever need a new param, drop the old overload.

AN UNKNOWN COLUMN FAILS THE WHOLE INSERT (42703) AND TAKES THE PHOTO DOWN WITH IT, not just the extra field. The web insert therefore retries in a COLUMN-GROUP LADDER, newest migration first: drop ["captured_at","captured_at_source"] (0176), retry; then drop ["thumbnail_url"] (0173), retry. Worth mirroring in Swift if you want the same "the photo still attaches, it just loses the enrichment" behaviour.

features.name: Chat photos also use small previews
features.whatItDoes: Photos sent in committee or house chat load as light previews rather than the full-size file.
gotchas: Chat bubbles are NOT wired yet: `committee_message_media` / `house_message_media` have the `thumbnail_url` column, but neither chat view passes a thumbnail through or renders one (CommitteeChat.tsx / HouseChat.tsx never mention it).
There is no web reference implementation to copy for this one.
features.nativeOpportunity: If iOS wires chat-bubble thumbnails, that's a genuine improvement over web, not parity drift.

features.name: Sort an album by when photos were taken
features.whatItDoes: An album can be ordered by the day the photos were actually taken instead of when they were uploaded, with upload order staying the default.
tables: drop_box_media (captured_at timestamptz — 0174; captured_at_source text check (… in ('exif','video','file','post')) — 0175)
rpcs: add_drop_box_media (normalises anything outside the four-value vocabulary to 'exif' and forces the source to null when the date is null)
gotchas: Sort rule: most-recent-first on `captured_at`, FALLING BACK TO `created_at` (upload time) when it's null — never hide an item for lacking metadata. The web's comparator is literally `(b.capturedAt ?? b.createdAt).localeCompare(a.capturedAt ?? a.createdAt)`.
On web, capture order is a PER-VIEWER VIEWING PREFERENCE, applied client-side over already-fetched rows and never written to the DB, so changing it can't reorder the album for anyone else.

THE DEFAULT IS UPLOAD ORDER, deliberately: capture order made a fresh upload scatter into the middle of the album by its shot date, which reads as the app glitching or losing the photos. Keep upload order as the default and put capture order behind a toggle (device-local — the web persists it in localStorage under `mlr.dropbox.sort`; use UserDefaults).

`captured_at_source` is a provenance RANKING and a sweep may only ever move a row UP the list, never down: 'exif' == 'video' > 'file' > 'post' (real file metadata > the picked file's mtime > the source post's own timestamp). The mini's periodic sweep (`captured-at-backfill.js`) upgrades a 'post' proxy to real 'exif'/'video' metadata if it can find any, and NEVER the reverse.
DECODE `captured_at_source` AS `String?`, NOT A STRICT ENUM — a fifth source would break a RawRepresentable decode of every row in the album.

The 0175 story, because it's the lesson: 0174 alone did almost nothing. The Family Fest album was 48 items — 41 referenced in from existing Feed posts, 7 direct uploads that predated the feature — so every single row had `captured_at = null` and the album collapsed to upload order. A bulk "add to album" writes every row inside the SAME SECOND, so those 41 had no meaningful order at all. Structural cause: a photo referenced from an existing post has NO File on the client, only a URL. 0175 added the server-side sweep plus the 'post' proxy — `min(coalesce(posts.occurred_at, posts.created_at))`, and only where exactly one post owns the file, so a shared file can't pick an arbitrary date. TAKEAWAY: a metadata read that only runs at upload time silently covers none of the content that's already there — and with a null-tolerant sort the failure is invisible, because it looks exactly like "these photos have no metadata."

features.name: Photos keep their real date and full quality when uploaded from iOS
features.whatItDoes: A photo you upload from your phone carries the real date it was taken, and the original file is sent so nothing is lost.
rpcs: create_post (media array keys capturedAt, capturedAtSource — camelCase)
endpoints: POST /upload (re-reads the stored bytes whenever the client's claim is only 'file' or absent)
webFiles: prepareImageForUpload() (now a deliberate no-op that returns the file untouched)
gotchas: iOS SHOULD USE `PHAsset.creationDate`, AND IT IS GENUINELY BETTER THAN WHAT WEB DOES. The web reads EXIF DateTimeOriginal client-side with a hand-rolled JPEG/TIFF IFD parser, and that parser CANNOT OPEN HEIC AT ALL — iPhone's default format.
Read `PHAsset.creationDate` from the ORIGINAL asset, BEFORE any resizing or re-encoding, and send it as `capturedAt` with `capturedAtSource = "exif"`.

UPLOAD THE ORIGINAL BYTES. HEIC is fine — the mini converts it with a real image library (sharp/libvips) and keeps the upload as `<uuid>_orig.<ext>`. Do NOT re-encode "to save bandwidth"; that is the exact mistake that caused this whole saga (the web composer used to run every photo through a `<canvas>` re-encode, which stripped every byte of EXIF; migrations 0174–0176 exist almost entirely to recover a date that re-encode destroyed).
Trade-off, accepted: a few MB per photo instead of ~1MB, so a large batch over cellular is slower. Report per-file failures with a retry.
If iOS ever writes a date, send the HONEST source: claim 'exif' only for a real capture date, 'file' for a filesystem mtime.

If you ever fall back to a file date on iOS, apply the web's freshness guard: rejected if missing, pre-1995, in the future, or WITHIN 60 SECONDS OF NOW (FRESH_COPY_MS = 60_000), because a picker that hands over a freshly-made temp copy stamps it with the current time, i.e. "upload time wearing a disguise."
features.nativeOpportunity: PHAsset.creationDate on the original asset beats web's EXIF parser outright — web cannot read HEIC at all, and its canvas re-encode used to destroy the date entirely.

features.name: Adding a post's photo to an album credits the person who took it
features.whatItDoes: When an admin adds someone's old post photo into a shared album, the album still shows the original poster as the person who contributed it.
rpcs: add_drop_box_media(p_box uuid, p_url text, p_type text, p_thumbnail_url text DEFAULT null, p_captured_at timestamptz DEFAULT null, p_captured_at_source text DEFAULT null, p_credit_user_id uuid DEFAULT null) -> uuid — current signature after 0180, 7 args in this order
gotchas: `p_credit_user_id` is honoured ONLY when the caller is an admin AND it names a real profile (and is not the caller themself); a non-admin's value is SILENTLY IGNORED (they can't attribute an upload to anyone but themselves).
It exists so an admin editing a member's post and ticking "also add to an album" credits the POST'S AUTHOR, not themself.

Argument ORDER matters for the 7-arg signature; and per the 0115 incident, any future widening must `drop function` the narrower overload first or PostgREST will resolve by argument count and an old client silently writes rows without the new field.

features.name: "Anytime all week" things to do come from the real schedule
features.whatItDoes: The Anytime-all-week section (scavenger hunt, merch, kids' activities) shows the same up-to-date items the rest of the family sees, instead of a stale copy nobody can edit.
tables: fest_schedule_items (anytime boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false — 0139; source_activity_id — 0141)
webFiles: lib/festContent.ts:392 (fetchFestContent still fetches and returns the activities array; nothing renders it)
lib/festContent.ts (saveActivity / deleteActivity / updateActivityDetails / fetchActivityDrafts — orphaned; fetchActivityDrafts still imported by FestPlanner at :40 and never called)
gotchas: iOS STILL READS `fest_activities`, AND THAT IS THE ONLY REASON THE TABLE STILL EXISTS. No reachable web path reads or writes it any more; the rows were deliberately not dropped so the native app kept working. Migrating iOS off `fest_activities` is what finally lets the table be dropped.

THE DRIFT RISK IS LIVE AND ONE-DIRECTIONAL: an admin editing a converted anytime event on web writes ONLY to `fest_schedule_items`. The untouched `fest_activities` row keeps its old title, description, location, lead and sign-up config FOREVER — so today an iOS "Anytime all week" section can show stale content nobody can fix from the web app (only raw SQL could). New anytime items created since 0141 exist ONLY as `fest_schedule_items` and are INVISIBLE TO iOS ENTIRELY.
The Planner's activity editor was NOT deleted, only orphaned — do not read its presence as "the web still manages activities." It's dead code, but it compiles and it will show up in your grep.
