Exact replacement query — `fest_schedule_items` select: id, day, start_time, end_time, title, emoji, location, description, bring, is_private, anytime, lead_user_id, lead_name, lead_phone, crew_user_ids, image_url, links, signup_enabled, signup_capacity, signup_slot_minutes, signup_start_time, signup_end_time, signup_mode, signup_instructions, signup_fields, signup_reminder_minutes, signup_reminder_email, signup_team_size, tournament_enabled, signup_hide_names; filter `.eq("fest_year", 2026)` (FEST_YEAR is a client constant = 2026); order by day then position; then partition on `anytime` — true -> "Anytime all week", false -> day cards. (`position` is ordered on but not selected — PostgREST allows that.)

An anytime item still carries a MEANINGLESS `day` value the client must ignore (0141 parked it on `current_date` at conversion). Day lists and "what's on today" must EXCLUDE anytime items; the detail header reads "Anytime all week."
It's modelled as a FLAG, not a nullable `day`, so the NOT NULL `day` column and every date formatter that reads it stay safe.

Two shape changes when reading the merged row instead of the activity: the activity's `blurb` and `details` are folded into the event's single `description`, joined by a blank line (`concat_ws(E'\n\n', blurb, details)`); and `day` is meaningless — ignore it.

RLS: `using (true)` on all fest_* content tables (0053) — public, unchanged by 0183, so this section renders for guests and unapproved members too. Writes require `can_edit_fest()` OR the item's own `lead_user_id` / a member in `crew_user_ids` (0110, and 0135/0138 for slots).

Swift decoding: `crew_user_ids` is `uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'` -> `[UUID]` (decode with `?? []`). `links` and `signup_fields` are `jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` — decode as your own nested Decodable types, defaulting to []. `signup_reminder_minutes` is `int[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`. `signup_mode` is `text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'interval'` (0136) with the check widened by 0143 to 'interval' | 'slots' | 'headcount' — never actually null; decoding as `String?` with a default rather than a strict enum is still the safer call.

`day` is a bare `date` (YYYY-MM-DD) and `start_time`/`end_time` are `time` strings — NEVER HAND A BARE YYYY-MM-DD TO A LENIENT DATE PARSER. On web `new Date("2026-07-31")` parsed as UTC midnight and rendered as the PREVIOUS day in Central, mislabelling every slot by one day — and because the label also fed the organiser's own picker, it CORRUPTED 10 STORED ROWS. Swift avoids that specific trap if you set an explicit `timeZone` on your DateFormatter, but the general lesson stands: a display bug inside a picker silently corrupts whatever that picker writes.

`is_private` is stored and editable in the web planner and mapped through lib/festContent.ts, but is NOT consumed by any web render path today — verify what you want it to mean before honouring it on iOS.
features.v1Cut: Render anytime items as read-only cards from fest_schedule_items and skip sign-ups entirely — sign-up slots, teams and tournaments hanging off those items are a much larger separate feature. The section swap itself is a couple of hours (same section, new source, one extra `anytime` filter on the day lists).

features.name: Search all your conversations
features.whatItDoes: Type a few words and find any message from the family feed, your committee/area chats, or your house chat, then tap the result to jump to it.
endpoints: POST https://mlr-media.duckdns.org/search  (Authorization: Bearer <the member's own Supabase access_token>, Content-Type: application/json, body { "q": "golf hat", "limit": 15 })
rpcs: public.search_conversations(query_embedding extensions.vector(512), query_text text default '', match_count integer default 20) returns table (source_type text, source_id uuid, content text, created_at timestamptz, similarity double precision, committee_id uuid, area text, house_id uuid, post_id uuid, author_id uuid)
gotchas: ⚠️ You CANNOT call `search_conversations` directly from iOS. Its first parameter is a non-defaulted `extensions.vector(512)`; you'd have to produce an Apple embedding client-side and serialize it as a pgvector literal. Go through `POST /search`.

The mini does two things: embeds `q` on-device (Apple `NLContextualEmbedding`, 512-d, via a separate Swift/Vapor `embed-service` on loopback :8786), then creates a second Supabase client using the caller's forwarded token and calls the RPC as them. RLS is the only scoping — the service-role key is deliberately never used for search (`media-server/server.js`, the `/search` handler).

⚠️ There is NO `min_similarity` parameter any more — `0130` dropped the `(vector, integer, double precision)` overload wholesale. Any older doc or snippet showing it is stale. The live signature is the only version that exists after `0130` dropped the original; `0131` replaced the body in place.

⚠️ Search is currently PURE KEYWORD, despite the name and the web's placeholder copy. Apple's mean-pooled `NLContextualEmbedding` vectors are anisotropic — cosine similarities bunch into a narrow ~0.85–0.92 band — so a threshold can't separate relevant from irrelevant. The embeddings now only break ties among keyword matches (`order by lex desc, similarity desc, created_at desc`). So: do NOT build a "% match" badge or sort control out of `similarity`, and don't ship copy promising "find it without the exact words" until someone mean-centres the embeddings (a noted future enhancement, not wired). `"pork"` matching nothing correctly returns zero rows.

⚠️⚠️ Filter with the full-text match operator `@@`, never a `ts_rank(...) > 0` test. That was the `0130` bug and it leaked the entire corpus: for a multi-word query `ts_rank` returns a tiny non-zero (~1e-20) for documents that don't match at all, so `lex > 0` was true for everything and "if any keyword matched, keep only matches" collapsed into "return everything, real hits on top and noise underneath". Single-word queries returned exactly 0.0, which is why "golf" looked perfect and "golf hat" looked broken. `0131` filters with `to_tsvector('english', content) @@ websearch_to_tsquery('english', query_text)` and uses `ts_rank` only for ordering. If you ever add a second search surface, a saved-search, or a "search this room" variant, do not reintroduce a score threshold — use the boolean operator.

⚠️ An empty/whitespace `query_text` returns ZERO rows, not "everything". `websearch_to_tsquery('english','')` is an empty tsquery and `@@` against it is false for every document. The mini has a legacy fallback that re-calls the RPC with only `{query_embedding, match_count}` if the 3-arg form isn't found (`PGRST202`) — post-`0130` that resolves to the same function with `query_text` defaulting to `''`, so that path returns an empty list. Always send a real `q`.

⚠️ A message is not searchable until the indexer has embedded it — typically up to ~2 minutes, longer after a restart. Every branch of the RPC is `from content_embeddings e join <table> …`, so content with no embedding row is INVISIBLE to search, not merely low-ranked. `media-server/search-indexer.js` reconciles on a timer (`SEARCH_INDEX_FIRST_MS` ≈ 20s after boot, then `SEARCH_INDEX_SWEEP_MS` ≈ 2 min), embedding new/edited rows (keyed by a sha256 `content_hash`, so an edit re-embeds) and pruning orphans. DO NOT write a test that sends a chat message and immediately searches for it — it will fail for a legitimate reason. If a member reports "my message isn't findable", check the mini's `[search-index]` log lines before anything else.

⚠️ Only `text` is indexed. Photos, videos, captions on media rows, poll questions, work items, events, drop-box items, and member names are all unsearchable. "Search everything" is a backend change (new `source_type` values in the `content_embeddings` check constraint + new branches in the RPC + new `SOURCES` entries in the indexer), not an iOS change.

⚠️ Search results reflect the CURRENT text, not the indexed text. Only a hash lives in `content_embeddings`; the RPC returns `content` from the live base table. An edited-then-not-yet-reindexed message is found by its OLD words but displayed with its NEW text. Intentional, but it will look like a bug in a demo.

`content_embeddings` is deny-all: RLS on with ZERO policies and `revoke all … from anon, authenticated`. Nothing but the RPC (and the service-role indexer) can read it. Don't try to query it from iOS; you'll get zero rows with no error.

RLS read rules, all re-implemented INSIDE the SECURITY DEFINER RPC — an empty result almost always means "not permitted or not indexed", never "the message doesn't exist": `posts` — visible if `status = 'visible'`, or you are `author_id`, or `profiles.is_admin`. `post_comments` — same rule AND the parent post must also pass it (both gates, joined). `committee_messages` — `deleted_at is null`, visible/own/admin, AND `public.can_access_committee_area(committee_id, area)`. `house_messages` — `deleted_at is null`, visible/own/admin, AND `public.is_house_member(house_id)` (`0064`, never redefined). Plus a hard `auth.uid() is not null` gate.

⚠️ `can_access_committee_area` was introduced in `0063` but the LIVE definition is `0177`'s — `0172` added a Leads branch and `0177` recreated the whole function verbatim and repointed that branch. Don't read `0063` and stop. `area is null` is the committee-wide General channel; the leads-only room matches case-insensitively (`lower(area) = 'leads'`, and only while no real area is literally named "Leads") and is gated on `public.is_committee_lead(committee_id)` (`0177`; it was `is_committee_area_lead` in `0172`) with NO admin override — an admin who isn't a lead of that committee gets no Leads results, even though the admin override covers every other area.
Consequence worth designing for: join a committee and its whole history becomes searchable on the next query; leave and it disappears. No index rebuild, no client cache to invalidate.
Server-side clamps: `q` trimmed and truncated to 500 chars; `limit` coerced into 1…50, default 20 (the RPC additionally caps at 100). The web sends `limit: 15`.
Web UI for reference: `components/ConversationSearch.tsx` is a full-screen search over the Feed channel list.
features.v1Cut: Ship without the "search this room only" filter (doesn't exist on web either).

features.name: Search results read correctly
features.whatItDoes: Each search hit shows the message text and when it was said, without crashing on missing details.
rpcs: public.search_conversations(query_embedding extensions.vector(512), query_text text default '', match_count integer default 20)
gotchas: `200` body is `{ "query": "...", "count": N, "results": [ ...rows... ] }`. Rows come straight from PostgREST, so keys are snake_case and five of them are nullable.

Swift model given in the doc: `SearchResult` with `id` = "\(sourceType.rawValue):\(sourceId)"; `SourceType` raw values `post`, `post_comment`, `committee_message`, `house_message`; CodingKeys map source_type/source_id/content/created_at/similarity/committee_id/area/house_id/post_id/author_id; plus `SearchResponse { query, count, results }`.
`content` is never null — the SQL filters empty/blank.

`committeeId` is set only for `committee_message`. `area` nil == the committee-wide "General" channel. `houseId` is set only for `house_message`. `postId`: for a post it's its own id, for a post_comment it's the PARENT post. `authorId` is nullable — don't force-unwrap.

`created_at` is an ISO-8601 timestamptz with fractional seconds and a `+00:00`/`Z` offset. Use a custom `DateFormatter`/`ISO8601DateFormatter` with `.withFractionalSeconds`, or the same decoding strategy the existing Posts feed already uses for `posts.created_at` — reuse it rather than inventing a second one.

features.name: Search tells you what went wrong
features.whatItDoes: When a search finds nothing, or the search service is still warming up, the screen says which one it is instead of showing a blank list.
gotchas: `200` with `count: 0` covers THREE different causes and all show "No matching messages you can see.": no keyword match; OR `q` shorter than 2 chars (the server short-circuits at `<2` and returns an empty result set, not an error); OR the query was un-embeddable — all punctuation/emoji, where `embedOne()` returns null and the handler answers `200` empty rather than `503`.
`401` = session expired mid-search (`requireUser` rejected the JWT). Treat as empty, refresh the session — web returns `[]` rather than an error here.

`503` = either the embed-service is unreachable/errored ("Search is warming up. Try again in a moment.") or `SUPABASE_URL`/`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` aren't set on the mini ("Search isn't configured."). This is a retryable "search is warming up" state — NOT "no results".
`502` = the RPC itself failed ("Couldn't run the search.") → generic error.
`429` = rate limit, 60 searches/min/IP (`searchLimiter`) → back off.
A member's brand-new message legitimately returns zero results for up to ~2 minutes (indexer delay) — check the mini's `[search-index]` log lines before treating "not findable" as a bug.
An empty result almost always means "not permitted or not indexed", never "the message doesn't exist".

features.name: Search keeps up while you type
features.whatItDoes: Typing in the search box doesn't hammer the server or show stale results from an earlier keystroke.
gotchas: The whole family can share one apparent IP behind the lake WiFi, so a 320ms debounce (what the web uses) is not just polish — it keeps a typing member from eating the shared 60/min bucket.
Carry over the web's monotonic sequence guard so a slow earlier response can't overwrite a newer one.
Server-side clamps: `q` trimmed and truncated to 500 chars; `limit` coerced into 1…50, default 20 (the RPC additionally caps at 100). The web sends `limit: 15`.

Rate limits: global (everything except `/health` and `/upload`) 600 / 15 min / IP; `/upload` NONE (skipped on purpose); `/search` 60 / min / IP; `/moderate/text` 60 / min / IP; `/geocode` 30 / min / IP.
`trust proxy` is 1, so limits key on the real client IP through Caddy — but the whole family often shares one WiFi and one apparent IP. Debounce anything typed.

features.name: Search results show who said it
features.whatItDoes: Each search hit shows the name of the person who wrote the message.
gotchas: `author_id` is only an id. The web resolves display names with a separate `profiles` read (`select id, display_name where id in (...)`) after results land, and just omits the name on a miss. Do the same, or reuse whatever profile cache the Posts feed already has.
`author_id` is nullable — don't force-unwrap.
features.v1Cut: A v1 can ship without author-name resolution at all (the doc explicitly allows this).

features.name: Tapping a search result jumps to the message
features.whatItDoes: Tapping a search hit opens the right feed post, committee/area chat, or house chat and scrolls to the exact message with a flash.
gotchas: Web sets URL params then switches the visible channel, and each room's existing `?m=` effect scrolls to + flashes the message (identical to an Activity-tab deep-link). Port the MAPPING, not the URL mechanics.

`post` / `post_comment` → Family Feed, carry `post_id`. For a comment this is the PARENT post; `source_id` is the comment. Landing on the exact comment is the `&comment=` behaviour from `0164`, which `openResult` itself does NOT use today.
`committee_message` → the committee/area chat matched by `committee_id` AND `(area ?? "") == (area ?? "")`; carry `source_id` as the message to scroll to.
`house_message` → house chat, only if `house_id` == the viewer's house; carry `source_id`.
⚠️ Note the area comparison: `nil` area and `""` must compare EQUAL or General-channel results silently fail to resolve (web coalesces both sides).
If no local channel matches (e.g. the member's channel list hasn't loaded), web bails silently — better to show a toast on iOS than to no-op.

features.name: Unapproved accounts can't search the family's posts
features.whatItDoes: Someone who signed up but hasn't been approved by an admin yet should not be able to read post and comment text through search.
rpcs: public.search_conversations(query_embedding extensions.vector(512), query_text text default '', match_count integer default 20)
gotchas: ⚠️ Backend gap — flag before shipping the UI: `search_conversations` does NOT check `is_approved_member()`. `0183` swapped the members-only read policies on `posts`/`post_comments` over to `is_approved_member()`, but the search RPC is SECURITY DEFINER and re-implements visibility itself with only `status`/author/admin + `auth.uid() is not null` — and `POST /search` on the mini is `requireUser` only, with no `requireApprovedMember`.

So a signed-up-but-unapproved account that can see NOTHING through a normal select can still read post and comment TEXT through `/search`. (`/upload`, `/media-token` and `/dropbox-zip` are approval-gated, so no photos leak; committee/house rooms are safe because an unapproved newcomer has no roster/house membership.)
Verified against the SQL: `0131`'s body contains no `is_approved_member()` call, and execute is granted to `authenticated`, which an unapproved signup is.

Fix: either (a) gate the search entry point behind the same `approved` flag your verified-member states already read, and/or (b) ask for a one-line migration adding `and public.is_approved_member()` to the RPC's outer `where`. Doing (a) alone is a UI fix over an open API.

features.name: Photos come from the right media server
features.whatItDoes: Every photo and video is loaded from the family's real media server, so pictures never silently stop appearing.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ The base URL is `https://mlr-media.duckdns.org`. NEVER the Tailscale funnel host. The retired host is `brians-mac-mini.tail49943c.ts.net` — it still resolves, which is exactly what makes it dangerous.

It silently un-signed every photo on the web app: `NEXT_PUBLIC_MEDIA_URL` was still set to the funnel host in Vercel and Next inlines `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` at build time, so the stale value won over the code default. `mediaSrc()` then did `if (!url.startsWith(MEDIA_URL)) return url` — a duckdns URL doesn't start with a ts.net prefix, so EVERY media URL was returned unsigned, with no error and no warning, indistinguishable from "we don't have a token yet". Confirmed by grepping the live bundle (2 chunks contained ts.net, zero contained duckdns) while the server logged 57 `tok=missing` requests from a phone that had fetched a valid token seconds earlier.

It also routes through Tailscale DERP and measured 12–21 Mbps against a 119 Mbps uplink. Reads already went direct (the mini stamps `PUBLIC_URL` into every stored row); it was WRITES — uploads and token fetches — quietly still taking the slow relay.

Rule 1: match by HOST against a known set, never by prefix against one configured string. iOS should keep a `Set<String>` of hosts whose URLs are ours to sign (`mlr-media.duckdns.org` always in it, whatever any config says) and decide "is this ours?" by `URLComponents(...)?.host`. A future host change then degrades to "add an entry", not an app-wide silent media outage.
Rule 2: any configured override that equals the retired host is IGNORED, not honoured. Genuine local-dev overrides still work; that one host is refused on purpose.
`PUBLIC_URL` is baked into ~1,700 stored rows, so changing it is a data migration, not a config change.
CORS is irrelevant to you: `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` gates browser origins only, and `URLSession` isn't subject to CORS. You do NOT need an entry added for the native app.

features.name: Photo links are signed so they work in the app
features.whatItDoes: The app quietly gets a pass from the media server and attaches it to every photo and video link, so pictures load for members and stop working if a link is forwarded outside the family.
endpoints: Authorization: Bearer <token> header is also accepted for programmatic callers
gotchas: The token comes from `GET /media-token` (`requireUser` + the approval gate; a `403 pendingApproval` here means no photos, matching what the DB already shows that member).

It is an HMAC over a rounded 24h window and is IDENTICAL for every member in that window — that sameness is load-bearing, because a per-request token would change every URL on every render and nothing would ever hit the cache. Verification accepts the current AND previous window, so a token is good for 24–48h.

The token rides in the query string (`?t=`) because image/video loaders can't attach an `Authorization` header and a cookie would have to be third-party (Safari/iOS blocks those outright). An `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header is also accepted for programmatic callers.

⚠️ Never append a token to a non-media URL. Supabase avatars, `data:`, local file URLs, and `/assets/*` must be returned untouched — signing them is noise at best and a cache-buster at worst. Make the signing helper IDEMPOTENT (`if url already has ?t=, return it`), which is what made a scripted sweep across ~18 web components safe.

⚠️ Signing key trivia that cost real debugging time: the issuing secret is `MEDIA_TOKEN_SECRET` OR, falling back, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` — so an unset `MEDIA_TOKEN_SECRET` never meant "unsigned". `MEDIA_TOKEN_SECRET` IS now set on the mini, and `media-auth.js` verifies against a SET of keys (`ACCEPTED_KEYS` = the issuing secret + the service-role key, permanently accepted but never issued + anything in the comma-separated `MEDIA_TOKEN_SECRETS_LEGACY`). So adopting a dedicated secret is no longer a rotation at all, and a genuine rotation staged through `MEDIA_TOKEN_SECRETS_LEGACY` is a non-event.

⚠️ If you ever need to mint a test token, call `require("./media-auth").issueToken()` on the mini — never hand-roll the HMAC. The message is `` `media:${window}` `` and the digest is base64url sliced to 43 chars; a reimplementation that signs the bare window index (or slices to 32) 403s and looks exactly like a real enforcement failure.

A cookie would be simpler and was explicitly DECLINED (2026-08-10). The app is on `vercel.app` and media on `duckdns.org` — different SITES, so the cookie would be third-party and Safari/iOS blocks it. Making it work needs a real domain (`app.<d>` + `media.<d>`). Brian chose to teach iOS to send the token instead. Don't re-pitch without a domain.
A v1 CANNOT skip the token, or every photo in the app 403s the moment `MEDIA_AUTH` goes to `on`.

features.name: Photos don't break after a day or on a new phone
features.whatItDoes: Pictures appear as soon as the app has its pass, and keep working across days, app restarts, and a fresh install — never a screen of broken photos.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ Signing is synchronous at render time, and an unsigned URL is returned silently. Web's `mediaSrc()` reads the cached token synchronously and returns the URL UNTOUCHED when there isn't one — so anything that obtains a token must ALSO force a re-render, or already-painted images stay unsigned and 403 forever. This was a latent screen-of-broken-photos on web: the cache is dropped a minute before its 24h expiry, so it would have hit everyone about daily, plus every first launch on a new device. In SwiftUI: hold the token in an `ObservableObject`/`@Published` (or the environment) so views re-render when it lands, and don't build URLs in a `let` computed once at init.

⚠️⚠️ Refetch the token on EVERY app open, cached or not — don't "optimize" that away. A cached token is only a GUESS about what the server will accept. It carries its own 24h expiry, so if the signing key changes the client keeps confidently signing with a dead key and every photo 403s until that expiry lapses — up to a full day, with NO self-healing. That is what turned a key rotation into an outage. (The server now also verifies against a legacy-key list, which makes a STAGED rotation harmless — but a key changed without staging the old value still lands exactly here.) One small authenticated request per launch buys automatic recovery.

⚠️ Track the token's expiry in memory, not just in storage. Web's in-memory copy used to be returned forever once set, so an app left open past 24h signed every URL with a dead token. Drop it ~60s early so a URL can't expire mid-flight.

⚠️ `GET /media-token` must be fetched with caching DISABLED. It used to answer `private, max-age=600` with an Express-generated ETag over a body that is byte-identical for the whole 24h window — so after 600s the client revalidated and got a 304, `res.ok` was false, the client concluded it had NO token, and every photo 403'd while `/media-token` looked perfectly healthy in the logs (alternating 200s and 304s). Observed live: 104 consecutive unsigned requests on one album. The server now sends `no-store` and no validator at all (written via `res.end`, because `res.json`/`res.send` always computes an ETag); on iOS use `.reloadIgnoringLocalCacheData` and treat a 304 as "keep what you have", NEVER as failure.
Because the token is stable per 24h window, signed URLs are cache-friendly — sign them the same way every render or you'll defeat it.

features.name: Photos and videos load and scrub natively
features.whatItDoes: Photos load and videos seek smoothly using the phone's built-in image loader and player.
gotchas: Every read requires a signed token sent as `?t=<token>` (`media-server/media-auth.js`) — ⚠️ but only once `MEDIA_AUTH=on`; the mini's `.env` says `report` TODAY, so an unsigned read still succeeds right now and is merely logged. BUILD AS IF IT WERE `on`.

⚠️ Range requests are supported and load-bearing — `/f` is `express.static` (and `res.sendFile` for `?dl=1`), both of which honour `Range` and answer `206`, which is what makes video seeking and the native player work. Do NOT fetch media through your own code into a `Data` blob to attach a header: that destroys HTTP caching and breaks Range. Hand `AVPlayer`/`AsyncImage` the signed URL directly.
Caching: `Cache-Control: max-age=365d, immutable` (filenames are unique). Let `URLSession`'s cache do its job.
`.m3u8` and `.ts` get explicit content types (`application/vnd.apple.mpegurl`, `video/mp2t`); the master playlist is served `no-store` because its contents depend on live load.
Always-public exceptions: `/health`, `/assets/*` (repo-shipped pay-method logos rendered on the sign-in screen), `/privacy` (App Store requirement), `/media-load`.

⚠️ Do NOT build a path-prefix exemption of your own inside `/f` — one existed and was an authentication bypass for the entire library: `GET /f/assets/%2e%2e/posts/2026-06/<uuid>.jpg` satisfied `startsWith("/assets/")`, skipped the token, and `express.static` then normalized the `..` and served the private photo. (`isAlwaysPublic()` still exists in `media-auth.js` but `requireMediaToken` deliberately no longer consults it.)
features.nativeOpportunity: Handing the signed URL straight to AsyncImage/AVPlayer gets native HTTP caching, Range/206 seeking and the system player for free — no custom loader, no in-memory blob.

features.name: Videos keep playing once photo security is enforced
features.whatItDoes: Videos don't break when the media server starts requiring signed links, even though the phone's player sometimes drops part of the link mid-playback.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ Known iOS-specific hazard, already written into the server's logs: the native player is known to DROP THE QUERY STRING on some Range retries. If video breaks under enforcement while photos are fine, that is the exact signature.
`media-auth.js`'s report-mode log line includes `range=yes|no` specifically so you can spot it.

If you hit it, an `AVAssetResourceLoaderDelegate` (or `AVURLAsset` with `AVURLAssetHTTPHeaderFieldsKey` where available) sending the token as a HEADER is the escape hatch — the server accepts both forms.
This is why step 2 of the MEDIA_AUTH promotion path requires separately PLAYING A VIDEO, not just scrolling an album — Range is a different code path.
features.v1Cut: Ship the plain signed URL first; only build the resource-loader delegate if report-mode WOULD-BLOCK lines with range=yes actually show up.

features.name: Uploaded photos land in the right folder
features.whatItDoes: A photo you add to a post, a chat, a work item, or a shared album gets filed in the right place on the family's media server.
gotchas: ⚠️ `category` and `room` MUST be QUERY PARAMETERS, not form fields. The upload destination (which volume, which folder) is chosen BEFORE ANY BYTES LAND, so the server can only read the query string at that point. A `category` sent as a multipart field is IGNORED and the file is filed under `posts/` — as is any unrecognized `category` value, since the server falls back to `posts`.
`file` is the ONLY accepted field name (multer `upload.single("file")`).
Optional form fields: `capturedAt` (ISO-8601 string) and `capturedAtSource` ("exif" | "file"; anything else is downgraded to "file"; ignored entirely unless `capturedAt` parses).
Folder layout the server derives (you never construct paths — you store the returned `url` verbatim): `posts/<YYYY-MM>/`, `chat/<room>/<YYYY-MM>/`, `work/<YYYY-MM>/`, `dropbox/<box-id>/<YYYY-MM>/`.

`room` and `category` are both LOWER-CASED and stripped to `[a-z0-9_-]`, max 40 chars (`safeSeg`) — a drop-box uuid passes through as-is, but anything with other characters silently becomes a DIFFERENT folder rather than an error.

features.name: The app saves the exact photo link the server returns
features.whatItDoes: After a photo uploads, the app remembers the link the server gave back so the picture still shows up later.
gotchas: `UploadResult` (200): `url` (full https URL — store this VERBATIM in `*_media.storage_path`), `thumbnailUrl` (null when generation failed — fall back to `url`, never fail the upload), `hlsUrl` (null today, `HLS_ENABLED=off` on the mini), `capturedAt` (ISO-8601 or null), `capturedAtSource` ("exif" | "video" | "file" | null), `name` (basename on disk), `originalName` (what you uploaded), `type` ("image" | "video" | "file"), `path` (path relative to the media root).

⚠️ The returned `url`'s extension can DIFFER from what you sent. A HEIC upload comes back as `…/<uuid>.jpg` because no browser (and no `AsyncImage`) can render HEIC over HTTP. ALWAYS store the returned `url`; never derive it from the local filename.

features.name: Upload failures say what actually happened
features.whatItDoes: If a photo won't upload, the app explains why — your account still needs approval, the server is out of space, or that file type isn't allowed — instead of a generic error.
gotchas: `401` — `requireUser`: no/invalid/expired Supabase JWT. Refresh the session and retry.

⚠️ `403` with `{"error": "...", "pendingApproval": true}` — NEW `requireApprovedMember`. A verified Supabase login is no longer enough; an admin must have set `profiles.approved` (an `is_admin` profile counts as approved). Show "an admin needs to approve your account first", not a generic failure. DETECT IT BY THE `pendingApproval` FLAG, NOT BY STRING-MATCHING THE MESSAGE. This gate exists because an unapproved signup could otherwise write files to the media volumes until the SSD hit its reserve and uploads started 507ing for the WHOLE FAMILY.

`415` — the magic-byte sniff said it isn't a real image/video, and `category != "chat"`. Chat allows any file (PDFs etc.) and a sniff miss there just means `type: "file"`. Posts/work/dropbox are images+videos only. The sniff reads the first 32 bytes — name and MIME are NOT trusted.
`507` — both volumes out of room / would breach the 15 GB boot-disk reserve. "The media server is out of space — tell an admin". Not the file's fault.
`400` — multer error, or no file in the request. Includes the file-size cap being blown.
`503` — the mini couldn't reach Supabase to validate the token.

features.name: Photos upload at full original quality
features.whatItDoes: Your photos are sent exactly as your phone took them, so nobody loses the full-resolution original or the date it was shot.
gotchas: ⚠️ Do NOT compress or re-encode photos before uploading. Web used to downscale to 1920px and re-encode at JPEG q0.82 through a `<canvas>`, which destroyed the full-resolution original PERMANENTLY and stripped every byte of EXIF — migrations `0174`–`0176` exist almost entirely to recover a date that destroyed. `prepareImageForUpload()` in `lib/media.ts` is now literally `return file`.
Send the ORIGINAL asset bytes. The mini builds the display copy itself (`media-server/display.js`: ~3200px long edge, JPEG q90, mozjpeg) and keeps your upload beside it as `<uuid>_orig.<ext>`.
HEIC is fine — it converts properly with a real image library. But the returned `url` will be `…/<uuid>.jpg`, so store what the server returns.
features.nativeOpportunity: iOS can hand over the untouched original asset bytes (HEIC included) straight from the photo library — there's no canvas re-encode step to remove in the first place.

features.name: Album photos sort by when they were taken
features.whatItDoes: Photos in a shared album appear in the order they were actually shot, not the order someone happened to upload them.
rpcs: add_drop_box_media(p_box, p_url, p_type, p_thumbnail_url, p_captured_at, p_captured_at_source, p_credit_user_id)
gotchas: For `capturedAt`, read `PHAsset.creationDate` from the ORIGINAL asset and send it with `capturedAtSource: "exif"`. That's strictly more reliable than the web's EXIF byte-scraping.
It's the value drop-box albums sort by (`drop_box_media.captured_at`, `0174`).
`captured_at_source` ranks providers `exif`/`video` > `file` > `post`, and a sweep may only ever move a row UP that list (`0175` adds the column to `drop_box_media`, `0176` to `post_media`).
If you send nothing, or send only `"file"`, the server re-reads the stored bytes itself (sharp for HEIC, ffprobe for video) and overwrites with real metadata.
`capturedAtSource` is ignored entirely unless `capturedAt` parses, and anything other than "exif"/"file" is downgraded to "file".
features.nativeOpportunity: PHAsset.creationDate is the real capture date straight from the photo library — strictly more reliable than the web's EXIF byte-scraping, and it works for formats (HEIC) the web parser can't read at all.

features.name: A whole album finishes uploading
features.whatItDoes: You can dump a big batch of photos or a long video and it keeps uploading with a progress bar, resuming rather than losing the whole transfer if the connection drops.
gotchas: Not rate-limited, deliberately: `/upload` is skipped by the global limiter (600 req/15min) precisely because a family dumping a fest album from one phone behind one shared IP was getting 429'd mid-dump. Safety comes from auth + the sniff + `MAX_MB`. So iOS may upload a whole album serially WITHOUT backing off — but see the timeout note.

⚠️ `MAX_MB` is 50 GB and the request timeout is 4h (`UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS`). NEITHER means a 50 GB upload works — bandwidth binds first, and raising the cap without the timeout just converts a clean `413` into a mid-transfer timeout, which wastes the entire transfer.

Use a BACKGROUND `URLSession` upload task with a FILE body (never load the asset into memory), report progress, and treat a dropped connection as retryable: the server reclaims the partial file on socket abort.
features.nativeOpportunity: A background URLSession keeps a whole-album upload running while the app is backgrounded or the screen is locked — something the web PWA simply cannot do.

features.name: Content held for review says so
features.whatItDoes: If a photo or message gets flagged for an admin to look at seconds after you post it, the app says "held for admin review" instead of claiming everyone can see it.
gotchas: Moderation used to block the upload response for posts/work/dropbox. It NO LONGER DOES for any category. `/upload` responds immediately and grades in the background via the mini's local `fm serve` (Apple PCC preferred, on-device fallback), downscaling a copy to ≤1024px first because `fm serve` caps request bodies at 1 MB.
You write NO moderation code. No pre-check, no wait, no verdict polling.

⚠️ But you MUST honour `status` when rendering, and you must expect it to CHANGE SECONDS AFTER a successful post. A post/comment/chat message can be `'visible'` when you insert it and `'pending'` on the next fetch. Don't cache "I posted this, so it's live" — re-read the row.

Web's post composer specifically re-reads the created row's `status` and says "held for admin review" instead of always claiming "Posted — everyone can see it now ✓", because the always-optimistic toast made a legitimate hold look like posting itself had broken.

A flagged verdict is written to `media_moderation` keyed by the PUBLIC URL (`storage_path`), and the DB trigger `trg_hold_on_media_verdict` → `hold_content_on_media_verdict()` then RETROACTIVELY flips the parent row's `status` from `'visible'` to `'pending'`, matching on `storage_path`. RLS then hides it from everyone but the author and admins.

The current live trigger has FOUR branches, in this order: `posts` (via `post_media`), `post_comments` (via `post_comment_media`, `0162`), `committee_messages` (via `committee_message_media`), `house_messages` (via `house_message_media`).

⚠️ A second race worth knowing about: the verdict is recorded against the URL that `/upload` returned, while the background transcode may repoint `*_media.storage_path` to a NEW URL. If the swap lands before the verdict, the trigger's `storage_path` match finds nothing and a flagged video stays visible. Low frequency, but don't be surprised by it, and don't "fix" it client-side.

features.name: Shared-album photos are not held after the fact (backend gap)
features.whatItDoes: A flagged photo in a shared download folder does not get hidden after it's already been added, unlike everywhere else in the app.
gotchas: ⚠️ `drop_box_media` has NO retroactive branch — VERIFY THIS BEFORE PROMISING DROP-BOX MODERATION ON iOS.

Its hold is `hold_drop_box_media_on_flagged()`, a BEFORE INSERT trigger (`drop_box_media_hold`) that reads an ALREADY-EXISTING verdict (`0171`, written when moderation was inline). With moderation now asynchronous, the verdict usually doesn't exist yet at insert time, and `hold_content_on_media_verdict()` (last recreated in `0162`, which predates drop boxes) never touches `drop_box_media`.
CLAUDE.md describes drop-box items as retroactively held; the SQL as written does NOT do that. If drop-box moderation matters for the iOS release, that's a BACKEND MIGRATION, not client work.

features.name: Videos keep working after the server re-encodes them
features.whatItDoes: A video you posted keeps playing even after the media server quietly makes a smaller, more compatible copy of it.
gotchas: Videos are transcoded to ≤1080p H.264 MP4 in the background (`media-server/transcode.js`, `maybeTranscode`), AFTER the response has already gone out carrying the ORIGINAL file's URL.
Same extension (you sent `.mp4`): the original is renamed to `<uuid>_orig.mp4` and the rendition is renamed into its place — atomic, same directory. THE URL NEVER CHANGES.

Different extension (`.mov` → `.mp4`): the original keeps serving at its own URL, fully playable, until the transcode finishes AND every `*_media` row has been repointed. `swapMediaStoragePath()` then PATCHes `storage_path` across all SIX tables — `post_media`, `post_comment_media`, `work_item_media`, `drop_box_media`, `committee_message_media`, `house_message_media` — and only then is the original renamed aside.

⚠️⚠️ So DO NOT cache a media URL forever, and NEVER persist it as your own source of truth. For a short window after upload the row points at the original (larger, possibly HEVC); afterwards it points at a DIFFERENT URL entirely. Re-read the `*_media` row (you already subscribe to realtime on most of these) rather than trusting a URL you captured at upload time. A hardcoded/derived URL will 404 after the swap.
This is the one genuinely NEW discipline in Part B — everything else is a one-time change.

features.name: Save the original photo or video to your phone
features.whatItDoes: Tapping Save gives you the untouched original file, not the smaller version the app shows on screen.
gotchas: The original ALWAYS survives as `<uuid>_orig.<ext>` and is what `?dl=1` hands back — so a "Save to Photos" action should hit `…/f/<rel>?dl=1&t=<token>`, which serves the untouched file with `Content-Disposition: attachment`, NOT the bitrate-capped rendition.
(This used to overwrite the upload with the re-encode, destroying every original the family ever shot. Don't reintroduce that.)
`?dl=1` is served via `res.sendFile`, which honours Range like `express.static`.
`/dropbox-zip` is approval-gated (like `/upload` and `/media-token`).
features.nativeOpportunity: Writing the downloaded original straight into the Photos library with PHPhotoLibrary is a real native win over the web's Content-Disposition download.
features.v1Cut: A v1 can skip ?dl=1 downloads entirely.

features.name: Uploads record their small preview image
features.whatItDoes: Every photo or video the app adds also stores the tiny preview the server made for it, so grids can load fast.
rpcs: add_work_item_media(p_work_item_id, p_url, p_media_type, p_position, p_thumbnail_url text default null)
add_drop_box_media(p_box, p_url, p_type, p_thumbnail_url, p_captured_at, p_captured_at_source, p_credit_user_id)
gotchas: Thread `thumbnailUrl` into EVERY `*_media` insert. All six tables have a nullable `thumbnail_url` (`0173`).

⚠️ It is a TRAILING param on `add_work_item_media(p_work_item_id, p_url, p_media_type, p_position, p_thumbnail_url text default null)` but NOT on `add_drop_box_media` any more — `0174`, `0175` and `0180` each appended a param after it, so the full current order is `p_box, p_url, p_type, p_thumbnail_url, p_captured_at, p_captured_at_source, p_credit_user_id` and `p_thumbnail_url` is the 4th. PASS RPC ARGS BY NAME, NEVER POSITIONALLY.
`thumbnailUrl` is null when generation failed — fall back to `url`, NEVER fail the upload.
`thumbnail_url` null is normal and never an error. Pre-`0173` rows are all null (at backfill time it was 0/48 album items and 0/45 post media), and a sweep fills them from files already on disk.

`media-server/thumbnail.js` runs INLINE during `/upload` (a single fast sharp resize, or one ffmpeg frame grab) and returns `thumbnailUrl`. ~400px long edge, JPEG q70, stored as a plain `<uuid>_thumb.jpg` sibling in the same `/f` tree — no new route.

features.name: Photo grids scroll fast and videos show a play badge
features.whatItDoes: Albums and photo grids show small previews and only load the big file when you tap one, and video tiles are marked with a play badge so you can tell them from photos.
gotchas: Render `thumbnail_url` in grids/albums and only load the full-res file on tap-through. This is the SINGLE BIGGEST scroll-performance win in the app.
`thumbnail_url` null is normal and never an error — fall back to the full-res URL.

⚠️ A video's poster frame is seeked ~10% in (capped at 3s), NOT frame 0 — real phone video routinely opens on a black or half-exposed frame while the camera settles, and frame 0 gave a whole album of black tiles. The output is size-checked because a seek past the last keyframe can produce an empty file WITHOUT erroring.

⚠️ A video tile still needs a ▶ badge. With a real poster frame it's otherwise indistinguishable from a photo. (Surfaces that render videos with native player controls don't need one — the controls are the affordance.)

features.name: Captions get a quick check before posting
features.whatItDoes: Before a caption goes up, the app can quietly ask the server whether the wording is a problem.
gotchas: Text moderation is a SEPARATE, OPTIONAL call: `POST /moderate/text` (`{text}` → `{flagged, category, reason}`), `requireUser`, 60/min, `express.json({limit:'64kb'})`, fail-open `{flagged:false}` on any error or when `MOD_ENABLED` is off.
Web calls it before publishing a caption.
There is also an ALWAYS-ON deterministic blocklist trigger in Postgres, so skipping this endpoint doesn't remove the floor.

features.name: Video quality adapts when the server is busy
features.whatItDoes: When lots of people are watching at once, the app can drop video quality so playback doesn't stall.
gotchas: `GET /media-load` is PUBLIC and returns an aggregate throughput + viewer count so a client can cap adaptive quality mid-playback. Nothing about who is watching what.
Optional for v1.
features.v1Cut: Skip /media-load entirely for v1.

features.name: Streaming video playlists (not on yet)
features.whatItDoes: Nothing to build yet — the streaming-playlist version of a video is switched off on the family's server.
gotchas: `hlsUrl` is advertised by convention BEFORE any ladder is built, but `HLS_ENABLED` is `off` on the mini today (it's not in the mini's `.env`, and the module default is `off`), so it comes back NULL.
Ignore it for v1; if it's ever turned on, the contract is "store one URL and fall back to the progressive mp4 until the playlist exists".
The master playlist is served `no-store` because its contents depend on live load.
features.v1Cut: Ignore hlsUrl completely for v1; it is always null today.

features.name: A missing or removed photo fails cleanly
features.whatItDoes: A photo that was deleted, or that lives on a drive that's unplugged, shows a tidy placeholder instead of a broken tile or a crash.
gotchas: 404s: a miss anywhere in the four-root fallback chain (SSD → SSD legacy → external drive → external legacy) ends in `404 {"error":"Not found."}`. A file that exists only on the external drive serves at the SAME URL — nothing in the database records which volume holds the bytes. If the external drive is unmounted, cold-only files 404 and everything else keeps working.

`400 {"error":"Bad request."}` for any path with a `..` segment, backslash or NUL (checked with repeated URL-decoding, so `%252e%252e` is caught too). This runs UNCONDITIONALLY, before the enforcement check.

Deleted media 404s — a quarantined file under `_trash/` is blocked for its 7-day hold. (That check sits just AFTER the token middleware, so under enforcement a token-less `_trash` request 403s before it 404s.)

features.name: Turning on photo-link security without breaking everyone
features.whatItDoes: The family's photos stay visible while the media server switches from "just watching" to actually requiring signed links.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ `MEDIA_AUTH` is currently `report`, and iOS is the reason. Enforcement was verified working on web (220/220 signed requests) and then DELIBERATELY backed off to `report` (confirmed: `MEDIA_AUTH=report` in the mini's `.env`), because `apns_subscriptions` shows registered iOS devices and the native app has no `/media-token` support — enforcement would 403 every photo in it.
`report` serves everything but logs `[media-auth] WOULD-BLOCK … tok=missing|invalid range=… ua=…`.

The promotion path — DO NOT SKIP STEP 3: (1) Ship the iOS token support. (2) Have a member open the iOS app and scroll an album, and separately PLAY A VIDEO (Range is a different code path). (3) `grep "WOULD-BLOCK"` on the mini — zero lines from real clients means every client is signing correctly. (4) Only then set `MEDIA_AUTH=on`.
Flipping straight to `on` broke the whole family's photos TWICE in one afternoon, and both times the evidence needed to predict it was only obtainable by breaking it.
Build as if `MEDIA_AUTH` were already `on` — an unsigned read succeeding today proves nothing.

features.name: Guest / waiting-to-be-approved / member gating
features.whatItDoes: Anyone can browse the app, but private things are hidden until you sign in — and a brand-new signup sees only public content, with a clear explanation, until a family admin okays their account.
gotchas: ⚠️ The DB column is profiles.approved but every human-facing string says "Verified" — Supabase already owns "verified" for email OTP. Do not unify them.

⚠️ approved == nil, a read error, or a missing column MUST resolve to APPROVED. The web defaults verified=true in three places (initial state, error branch, column-absent) because the other default locks real members out over a network blip.
⚠️ An unverified member must NOT be shown a "Sign in" button — they already signed in. Own copy, no button, non-interactive 🔒 chip inline.
⚠️ profiles keeps an own-row escape hatch (is_approved_member() or id = auth.uid()). Without it identity loading breaks for exactly the people who need the waiting screen.

⚠️ An empty array from any members-only table means NOT PERMITTED, not "no data". Never render an empty-state that implies emptiness on those surfaces — web degrades them to sign-in nudges (EventSheet "Sign in to see who's coming", WorkChecklist "Sign in to see the resort to-do list").
⚠️ Public-read regardless of session: events, cabins, announcements, committees, committee_areas, app_images, fest_content tables, resort_config. Empty there really is empty.
⚠️ The client is not the enforcement boundary — this is a Supabase-token app and anyone can hit the REST API with their own JWT. The wall exists to make the screen coherent.
⚠️ Guests see first names only (firstName(): name.trim().split(/\s+/)[0]), fed by the public_profiles view server-side. Don't render a full name a guest fetched from a fallback path.
⚠️ Admin "view as" forces verified: true and needsIntro: false — an admin checking the guest view must not appear unverified to themselves.
features.nativeOpportunity: The web needs a `resolving` skeleton state because prerendered HTML always ships the guest view, so a returning member can flash the sign-in wall on every cold open. iOS restores the session from the Keychain synchronously, so the very first frame can already be the member layout — keep the state for the network `approved` read, but it should be invisible in practice.

features.name: Stay signed in, and open already showing your stuff
features.whatItDoes: A returning member never sees the signed-out version of the app while it loads — their name, avatar and admin tools are there on the first frame.
gotchas: The web snapshots { user, isAdmin } to `identity.<uid>` with an INFINITE TTL (a live session implies the snapshot's owner) and restores it before the network profile fetch.
⚠️ The snapshot deliberately EXCLUDES the one-time intro flags (intro_seen / invitedViaLink) — restoring those could re-show the onboarding sheet.
⚠️ It is one-shot guarded (snapshotSeededRef) so a later auth-state-change re-entry can never clobber fresher state with the stale snapshot.
Accepted trade-off, written down: a since-demoted admin can paint admin UI for ~1s until the fresh profile lands. Fine, because is_admin is UI-only and RLS is the real gate.

⚠️ updateUser() is optimistic AND rolls back on a failed write, re-pinning the snapshot to the last-good value — otherwise a name that only ever lived on-device silently reverts to the email-prefix default on the next cold load.

Profile column mapping for writes: name→display_name, emailAlerts→email_alerts, pushTypes→push_types, pushSelfNotify→push_self_notify, notifyNewMembers→notify_new_members, notifTypes→notif_types, pushPrompted→push_prompted, willingToHelp→willing_to_help, avatarUrl→avatar_url.
Email change is in-app, two calls: auth.updateUser({ email }) then auth.verifyOtp({ email, token, type: "email_change" }). profiles stores no email, so nothing else needs syncing.

Sign-in: signInWithOtp({ email, options: { shouldCreateUser: true } }) then verifyOtp({ email, token, type: "email" }). ⚠️ The code field accepts 6–8 digits on purpose — never hard-code 6, since the project's OTP length can be reconfigured. 30s resend cooldown so tap-tap-tap can't trip Supabase's rate limit.
features.nativeOpportunity: Keychain-backed session restore is synchronous and survives app reinstall-adjacent cases better than localStorage; combined with a synchronous disk cache read, the first frame is the real member view with zero flash. Also: no Safari-vs-installed-PWA split login, so nobody ever signs in twice.

features.name: Tapping a notification lands on the exact thing
features.whatItDoes: Tapping "Cass commented on your post" opens that post at that comment — not the top of the feed.
gotchas: The full path inventory the triggers actually emit: /posts?post=<id>, /posts?post=<id>&comment=<id>, /posts?c=<slug>&m=<id>[&area=<area>], /posts?house=<slug>&m=<id>, /posts?c=<slug>[&area=]&poll=<id>, /posts?feed=main, /?work=<id>, /events?open=<id>, /events?activity=<id>, /events?meeting=<id>, /house/calendar?house=<slug>, /people?member=<id>, /family-fest/schedule/<id>, /drop?box=<id>, /request-stay, /admin/cabins?booking=<id>, /admin/committees?committee=<slug>.
⚠️ /chat?m=<id> is LEGACY (migration 0030, superseded by 0063). Older notification rows still carry it — handle it as an alias.

⚠️⚠️ Never route to /committees/<slug>/chat. In the installed PWA that navigation dies before React runs (WebKit's own "This page couldn't load"), while the same room via the Feed works. Every server-side check comes back healthy, so it's invisible outside a real installed PWA; three fixes failed before the cause was found. Even on native, the URL contract matters: the database's notification rows use the /posts?c=… form.
⚠️ Honour &from=<slug> — it's the Back target so a deep-linked room returns to the committee page instead of the chats list.

⚠️ A deep-linked launch must never paint the chats-list state first. Web captures bootChannelKey/bootHouseSlug at mount and holds a "Loading…" instead, because otherwise a member who IS in a house/committee sees the list for a beat and gets visibly "hopped".

⚠️ Queue a cold-launch link and replay it after the viewer state settles. The web's whole PushDeepLink component exists because the SW's client.navigate() rejects in an installed PWA, the error was swallowed, and taps just focused the app on whatever page it already showed.
⚠️ Resolve the link against your own origin and drop anything cross-origin — both sw.js and PushDeepLink filter same-origin before routing.
features.nativeOpportunity: One DeepLink enum with an `init?(path:)` serves cold launch, foreground tap, Universal Link, and in-app navigation. Then: actionable notifications (On my way / RSVP Going / Approve) straight from the lock screen against RPCs that already exist; NSUserActivity for Handoff + Spotlight; App Intents so the same enum powers Shortcuts; Universal Links so shared /drop?box= and /posts?post= links open the app instead of Safari.

features.name: Scroll to and highlight the item you were sent to
features.whatItDoes: After a deep link opens a screen, the specific post, comment or message briefly glows so you can see which one it meant.
gotchas: useDeepLinkFlash(idPrefix, target, ready) polls document.getElementById every 150ms up to 20 attempts (~3s), then scrollIntoView({ block: "center" }), then clears the flash after 2200ms.

⚠️ The polling exists because the target may not be in the DOM yet — a long list still rendering, or a TRIMMED cold-open snapshot that doesn't contain an older item the full fetch hasn't landed yet. Handle "the id isn't in the data" by landing on the screen, never nowhere.

The first landing in a mount snaps (behavior: "auto") because the viewer has nothing to scroll from; a LATER deep link in the same mount scrolls smoothly, because there the motion is the useful cue. Keep both behaviours.
`ready` must be the real data-loaded flag, not some unrelated local-state-settled flag.
PostsView runs TWO independent instances side by side ("post-" and "comment-"); the hook holds no shared state.
features.nativeOpportunity: ScrollViewReader.scrollTo(id, anchor: .center) after awaiting the fetch removes the 3-second DOM poll and the race entirely. The highlight becomes a real animated ring plus a UIImpactFeedbackGenerator tap — a "here it is" cue the web cannot produce.

features.name: Signing out leaves nothing behind
features.whatItDoes: When someone signs out on a shared iPad or a borrowed phone, none of their feed, chats, photos or name can paint for the next person.
gotchas: signOut() does FOUR things: auth.signOut(), clearAllCaches() (memory map + in-flight map + every mlr.cache.* key in BOTH storages), clearMediaToken(), and clears the preview key + all identity state.

⚠️ Uid-scoped keys are the SECOND line of defence for the token-expiry path where signOut never runs — leftover entries are inert without a session. Both layers are needed; neither alone is sufficient.
⚠️ Do NOT wipe the device-preference keys (text size, welcome-card seen, dismissed announcements, dropbox sort…). They belong to the device, not the account.

There is a real recorded incident behind this: a cache keyed on a shared "self" string instead of the real user identity leaked one member's cached private chat to the next user, because signOut doesn't reload the page. Key user-specific caches on the actual uid, always.
features.nativeOpportunity: Keychain deletion plus a directory removal is atomic and verifiable in a way clearing localStorage key-by-key is not; you can assert the cache directory is empty in a test.

features.name: Lead badges and area chips that don't quietly demote people
features.whatItDoes: The app understands that someone on "Meals · Lead" is also on "Meals", so editing their subcommittees never silently strips their lead standing.
rpcs: can_access_committee_area(committee_id, area) — accepts either form: p_area = any(r.roles) or (p_area || ' · Lead') = any(r.roles)
gotchas: Port these as a Swift extension BEFORE you write any roster UI, and never compare a role string with == again.
A person's role entry is EITHER the plain role name OR the name plus a trailing " · Lead". Both mean "on this role" — can_access_committee_area accepts either.

⚠️⚠️ THE REAL INCIDENT: the per-member area chip editor compared raw strings, so for someone holding "Meals · Lead" the Meals chip rendered UNLIT — it didn't match "Meals". An admin who then edited ANY of that person's areas saved a role list with the lead standing DELETED. No error, no warning; the person just quietly stopped being a lead, which under 0172/0177 also silently EVICTS them from the Leads chat and REVOKES their scoped roster control. It was found only by reading the code.

The sanctioned helpers (lib/committeeAdmin.ts) are the ONLY way to compare or edit a role entry: LEAD_SUFFIX (the literal " · Lead"); baseArea(entry) — the entry with any " · Lead" stripped; isOnArea(areas, area) — on it at all, as member or lead, = areas.some { baseArea($0) == area }; isAreaLead(areas, area) = areas.contains(area + LEAD_SUFFIX); withArea(areas, area, lead) — set the area, REPLACING any existing entry for it; withoutArea(areas, area) — remove it in either form; rolesIncludeAreaLead(roles) — holds any · Lead entry at all; isCommitteeLead(entry) = entry.isLead || rolesIncludeAreaLead(entry.roles).
The bug was literally `areas.contains(area)` where it needed `areas.contains { baseArea($0) == area }`.

⚠️ The separator is U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT (·, bytes C2 B7) with a plain ASCII SPACE on each side — verified by hexdump against migration 0177 (25 20 c2 b7 20 4c 65 61 64 for the pattern '% · Lead'). SQL matches LIKE '% · Lead'. A hyphen, a look-alike interpunct, a non-breaking space, or a smart-quote-mangled paste produces a role that NO lead check anywhere — SQL, web, or the two push senders — will ever recognise. Define it once as a constant and never type it again.

⚠️ Never build a role string from a localized or user-typed value. withArea composing area + " · Lead" is the only sanctioned construction — if a role name itself ever ended in " · Lead", baseArea would eat it.

withArea REPLACES rather than appends on purpose: appending gives a row holding BOTH "Meals" and "Meals · Lead" — is_committee_lead would still pass, but the roster UI double-renders and set_my_committee_areas would drop the · Lead copy while keeping the plain one, unpredictably.

features.name: A "Lead" badge on the committee roster
features.whatItDoes: The roster shows who leads the committee (or one of its subcommittees) at a glance.
gotchas: Compute it with the unified check: isCommitteeLead = is_lead == true || any roles[] entry ending in " · Lead" — never a raw string compare.
Web's roster read shape, verbatim: `id, name, email, phone, roles, position, linked_user_id, is_lead, profiles:linked_user_id(display_name, avatar_url)`.

⚠️⚠️ committee_roster references profiles(id) from BOTH linked_user_id and updated_by, so a bare profiles(display_name) embed answers HTTP 300 / PGRST201 and your client sees []. Always name the FK. Same failure signature as the house-lists embed: the roster renders empty while writes work fine.

⚠️ Reads require an APPROVED member — 0183 swapped auth.uid() is not null for is_approved_member() (= profiles.approved is true OR profiles.is_admin). A brand-new signup awaiting admin verification gets ZERO roster rows — no committees, no channels, no lead status — with NO error. Check profiles.approved before debugging anything else. (DB column is `approved`; the UI calls it "Verified" — don't unify the names, Supabase owns "verified" for email OTP.)
position int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 — new rows land at 0, so a fresh person sorts to the TOP of an .order("position") read. There is no reorder path for the roster.
Live data: 5 roster rows carry a ' · Lead' role, all on family-fest (4 linked to an account); 0 rows have is_lead = true.
This badge, plus the Leads room and self-service step-down/leave, IS the defensible v1 for Part C — it leaves every roster write path with the web admin UI, which already works.

features.name: A lead can run their own committee's roster from the phone
features.whatItDoes: Someone who leads a committee can add people, edit a person's name/email/phone, link them to an app account, put them on subcommittees, and make or unmake other leads — for their committee only, never anyone else's.
features.v1Cut: Omit the editor entirely. Ship the Lead badge, the private Leads room, and self-service step-down / leave — most of the value at a fraction of the work, leaving every write path in the hands of the web admin UI, which already works. Add the editor when someone asks to run their roster from a phone. If you do build it, cut the per-area ★ Lead toggles and the link-an-account picker first and keep name/email/phone/add/remove.
gotchas: ⚠️ Port the lead-suffix helpers FIRST (see lead-roster-lead-suffix-helpers) — comparing raw role strings has already silently deleted a person's lead standing on web, which also evicts them from the Leads chat.

Roster writes are PLAIN TABLE WRITES, not RPCs. Insert / update / delete committee_roster directly and let RLS decide. Live policies on public.committee_roster: `committee_roster write` (0056, ALL, EXISTS (select 1 from profiles p where p.id = auth.uid() and p.is_admin)); `committee_roster lead insert` (INSERT, WITH CHECK is_committee_lead_slug(committee_slug)); `committee_roster lead update` (UPDATE, USING and WITH CHECK is_committee_lead_slug(committee_slug)); `committee_roster lead delete` (DELETE, USING is_committee_lead_slug(committee_slug)); `committee_roster member read` (0183, SELECT, is_approved_member()).

Postgres ORs permissive policies per command — that's the whole trick: the three lead policies ADD a second writer alongside the admin FOR ALL policy without touching it. Admins keep full control everywhere; leads get the same power scoped to committees they lead.

⚠️ A cross-committee INSERT fails with 42501, but a cross-committee UPDATE/DELETE simply matches 0 ROWS and returns success (RLS filters rather than raising — the same silent-failure shape as house lists). CHECK THE AFFECTED-ROW COUNT, don't just check for an error.

Exact write shape (insert, or update by id) — the columns web's saveRosterEntry writes: committee_slug text (required; RLS keys on it); name text (part of UNIQUE (committee_slug, name)); email text? (ALSO the auto-link key — a DB trigger stamps linked_user_id when a profile's contact_email matches); phone text?; roles text[] (NOT NULL default '{}', e.g. ["Meals · Lead", "Logistics"]); linked_user_id uuid? (null == an account-less "Pending" person); is_lead boolean (committee-level, 0177 — web OMITS the key entirely when it has no opinion, and retries without it on 42703); updated_at timestamptz (ISO8601 now); updated_by uuid (your own uid).

Two columns the web writer deliberately never sends: position int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 (new rows land at 0 and sort to the top of an .order("position") read; there is no reorder path) — and note the table carries UNIQUE (committee_slug, name).

⚠️ Adding a second person with the same display name on one committee fails with 23505 unique-violation, NOT 42501. Surface that as "someone with this name is already on this committee", not as a permissions error.
deleteRosterEntry is DELETE … WHERE id = <id> — which IS "remove them from the committee", because committee_roster.linked_user_id has been the real chat-access gate since migration 0057.

Account-less roster people are FIRST-CLASS: linked_user_id = nil + a name (+ optional email) is a valid row, shown as "Pending", and can be put on subcommittees like anyone else. Two SECURITY DEFINER triggers auto-link them (one on profiles.contact_email from 0056, one on committee_roster.email from 0060, both trimmed + case-insensitive). The roster-side trigger only FILLS an empty link, so it never clobbers an explicit "pick a member" link.

Gate the UI on canManage = (isAdmin || iAmLead) && !previewAsId, where iAmLead = members.some { $0.linkedUserId == effectiveUserId && isCommitteeLead($0) } over YOUR OWN roster row for that committee.

⚠️ "Is this mine?" resolves through the EFFECTIVE user id, never a raw session lookup (web has an admin "view as" preview where the two differ). ⚠️ Every write must no-op while previewing — "view as" is strictly read-only. If iOS has no preview mode this collapses to the plain uid; don't invent one.

⚠️ Don't "simplify" the asymmetry: isAdmin DOES grant the roster editor (via the 0056 FOR ALL policy on direct table writes) but does NOT grant the Leads chat. Same screen, two different gates. And a third wrinkle from the is_committee_lead redefinition: the older RPCs gated on it (review_join_request, set_committee_areas, set_committee_lead) no longer grant an app admin who isn't a roster lead of that committee — "admin can do anything" holds for the roster table, not for those RPCs.
Reads need the FK-named embed (profiles:linked_user_id(...)) or the roster renders empty while writes work fine; and reads require an approved member (0183).
Scope of the web sheet, for sizing: name / email / phone / link-an-account / a "Lead of this committee" star / per-area checkboxes each with their own ★ Lead toggle, plus add and remove. ~300 lines.

features.name: Your own membership card on the committee page
features.whatItDoes: A card pinned at the top of a committee page shows what you're on, with the ways to change it in one place.
gotchas: Web pins a "my membership" card (MyCommitteeCard) offering: see your roles, step down from a lead role (you stay on the role as a volunteer), edit your areas, or leave.
Resolve "mine" through the effective user id, and make every write no-op while previewing ("view as" is read-only).
Render a lead entry with the suffix stripped via baseArea + a Lead marker — never show the raw "Meals · Lead" string as a role name comparison target.
It self-hides for guests and non-members.

features.name: Step down as lead but stay on the crew
features.whatItDoes: Drop the lead role for one subcommittee while staying on it as a volunteer.
gotchas: Step down from one area = rewrite roles, mapping "Meals · Lead" → "Meals", then write the row. There is NO dedicated RPC.
Use withArea(areas, area, lead: false) — it REPLACES the existing entry, so you can't end up holding both "Meals" and "Meals · Lead".

⚠️⚠️ Do NOT route this through set_my_committee_areas — that RPC does not strip the suffix, it DROPS the whole entry (the person leaves Meals entirely, loses the Meals area chat, and loses the Leads room).
A lead or admin edits by writing the committee_roster row directly (saveRosterEntry), reconstructing roles so any area they still hold AND still lead keeps its " · Lead" suffix.
Stepping down from your last · Lead entry (with is_lead false) removes you from the Leads room — that's correct, but it means the room can disappear from your chat list as a side effect.

features.name: Add or drop your own subcommittees
features.whatItDoes: A plain member can change which subcommittees they're on without asking an admin.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ It does NOT "strip the suffix" — it DROPS the whole entry. The filter is `where trim(a) <> '' and lower(trim(a)) <> 'general' and a not like '% · Lead'`, so "Meals · Lead" isn't rewritten to "Meals", it DISAPPEARS: the person is no longer on Meals at all, loses the Meals area chat, and loses the Leads room. Harmless for a plain member (they hold no · Lead entries); DOUBLY DESTRUCTIVE if you route a lead through it.

Which write path you use decides whether lead standing survives, and one of them costs more than the lead badge: a lead or admin writes the roster row directly; a PLAIN MEMBER uses this RPC. Never mix them up.
It requires existing committee_members membership (is_committee_member(cid)), else it raises "Join the committee first — ask an admin to approve your request".
It overwrites BOTH committee_members.areas AND committee_roster.roles.

valid_committee_areas(cid, areas) (0073) gates it — 'general' and any area not present in committee_areas for that committee are rejected, so nobody can be assigned the role "Leads" through this path.
It cannot self-appoint a " · Lead" entry.

features.name: Leave a committee
features.whatItDoes: Take yourself off a committee entirely — which also correctly removes your access to its chat rooms.
gotchas: leave_committee sets your committee_roster row's linked_user_id = null AND roles = '{}', and deletes your rows from committee_members and committee_join_requests.
Before migration 0073 it only cleared committee_members, so leaving silently didn't revoke chat access — that's fixed; don't hand-roll a replacement.
It leaves is_lead set, which is harmless: every lead check also requires linked_user_id = auth.uid().
Because the roster row survives (unlinked, with empty roles), the person stays on the roster as a "Pending"-style slot — don't render that as an error state.

features.name: Three viewer states: guest, signed-in-but-waiting, full member
features.whatItDoes: The app knows whether you're just browsing, signed in but still waiting for an admin to okay you, or a full member — and shows the right thing for each.
rpcs: is_approved_member() — SECURITY DEFINER, stable, granted to authenticated, anon; true when the caller's own profile has approved is true OR is_admin is true
set_member_approved(p_user uuid, p_value boolean) — admin-only, the ONLY write path
webFiles: components/Guard.tsx — useGuest() returns { guest, signedIn, resolving, awaitingVerification, promptSignIn }
gotchas: Columns: profiles.approved boolean not null default false, profiles.approved_at timestamptz, profiles.approved_by uuid references profiles(id) on delete set null.
Web derivation: awaitingVerification = isSupabaseConfigured && !!user && !verified; guest = isSupabaseConfigured && (!user || !verified); resolving = isSupabaseConfigured && !authReady && !user.

A signed-in but unapproved account is treated EXACTLY as a guest, plus an explicit 'You're signed in — almost there' explanation that an admin must okay them and there is nothing more to do on their end. Without this middle state the app looks broken (screens full of empty lists).

approved == nil AND any read error MUST resolve to APPROVED. The web client defaults verified to true in three separate places — initial state, read error, and column-absent — because defaulting the other way locks real members out of their own app over a transient network blip. Do the same and write the reason in the code comment or someone will 'fix' it later.
Decode approved as Bool? (nullable/possibly-absent column); nil == pre-migration == TREAT AS APPROVED.
The DB column is `approved`; every string a human sees says 'Verified.' Deliberate — Supabase already owns the word 'verified' for email confirmation. Do not unify them.

'Sign in' is the WRONG call to action for an unverified member — they already signed in successfully. Web shipped this wrong-ish first and it produced people retrying a thing that had worked. The unverified state gets its own copy and NO button at all.

The client is not the enforcement boundary. Anyone can hit the REST API directly with their own JWT; the UI wall exists so the screen is coherent, not to secure anything. Never 'optimise' a gated fetch by skipping RLS-covered filters client-side.
Admin 'view as' forces verified: true and needsIntro: false — an admin checking the guest view must not appear unverified to themselves.

profiles is readable by an approved member PLUS your own row unconditionally (is_approved_member() or id = auth.uid()). Without that escape hatch an unverified member couldn't read their own profile, so you couldn't even detect that they need the waiting screen. An empty result here means the session is gone, not that the person has no profile.

An empty array from ANY members-only table (posts, post_comments, post_media, committee_roster, event_attendance, work_items, houses, polls, drop_boxes, …) means 'not permitted', NOT 'no data' — never render it as a legitimate empty state.
Public-read regardless of session: events, cabins, announcements, committees, committee_areas, app_images, the fest_content tables, resort_config. An empty result THERE really does mean no rows.
0183 rewrote 29 SELECT policies onto is_approved_member().
Model it as ONE enum resolved in one place (resolving / guest / awaitingApproval / member(isAdmin:)) and never re-derive it from a raw session lookup. isGated == guest || awaitingApproval.
12 emails already on a roster are auto-approved at signup by the trigger, so some brand-new signups skip the waiting state entirely.
The document's own header warns that this section's verification pass did NOT run — confirm every table/column/RPC name against the database before building on it.
features.nativeOpportunity: The web's `resolving` state exists mostly because prerendered HTML always ships the guest view, so a returning member can flash the sign-in wall on a cold open. On iOS the session comes out of the Keychain synchronously at launch, so the very first frame can already be the member layout — resolving shrinks to 'first launch on this device only'. Keep the state (the approved flag still needs a network read) but expect it to be invisible.

features.name: Whole-screen 'sign in to see this' gate
features.whatItDoes: On members-only screens you get a clear sign-in card (or a 'you're almost there' note) instead of a blank page.
gotchas: Renders a SKELETON while resolving, the 'almost there' card while awaitingVerification, the sign-in card for a guest, and the children for a member — four states, not two.
Whole-screen walls exist on /posts, /polls, /people and /pay.

The awaitingVerification card must say an admin has to okay them and there is nothing more to do on their end, and must carry NO button (see the viewer-state gotcha about 'Sign in' being the wrong CTA).
The copy differences between SignInWall, Protected and PrivateName are the whole point — mirror all three one-for-one rather than collapsing them into one gate.

features.name: Locked phone numbers, emails and locations
features.whatItDoes: A single private detail (someone's phone, email or a location) shows as a small lock chip you can tap to sign in, instead of just being missing.
gotchas: A guest gets a TAPPABLE 🔒 {label} chip that opens sign-in.
An unverified (signed-in, not yet approved) member gets a NON-INTERACTIVE 🔒 'Waiting to be approved' chip — no tap target, because there is nothing for them to do.
Used inline for one phone number / email / location — not for whole screens.

features.name: Guests see first names only
features.whatItDoes: People's full names show to members; a guest only ever sees the first name.
gotchas: firstName() in lib/privacy.ts is exactly name.trim().split(/\s+/)[0] — mirror it rather than inventing a formatter.
Applies to the unverified state too, since an unverified member is treated exactly as a guest.

features.name: Opens already showing your stuff
features.whatItDoes: When a member reopens the app it comes straight up as their app — no flash of the signed-out version while it checks.
gotchas: Store the Supabase session in the Keychain (supabase-swift's keychain storage) instead of localStorage, and read it synchronously at launch so the first frame is the member layout.
Pair it with the identity snapshot on disk (cache key identity.<uid>) so name/isAdmin are present on the first frame too.
Sign-out must clear the Keychain AND the disk cache AND the media token — the web's signOut() does all three.
Keep the `resolving` state even though it becomes near-invisible: the approved flag still needs a network read before you can tell member from awaiting-approval.
Put the disk snapshot in Application Support, NOT Caches/ — iOS may purge Caches/ under pressure, silently reintroducing cold opens.
features.nativeOpportunity: Keychain gives the session synchronously at launch, which the web cannot do — this is the single biggest 'feels native' win in the privacy-wall area.

features.name: First-run welcome sheet for brand-new members
features.whatItDoes: The very first time someone new gets in, a short guided sheet walks them through turning on notifications and filling in their basics.
gotchas: The gate is computed in a SEPARATE, GUARDED query (a try/catch around a second select) precisely so a pre-migration column can never break sign-in.
Gate logic: sparse = !e.phone?.trim() && !e.birthday && !e.pay_preferred; needsIt = !e.intro_seen && sparse. So it only shows for someone whose profile holds nothing but the name they typed.
Existing members were backfilled intro_seen = true by 0045 and are never re-onboarded.
Steps are "confirm" | "push" | "basics" and the order is push FIRST, basics second — deliberately, so the first thing a newcomer sees after verifying is 'turn on notifications', not a form.
Dismissing (✕ / backdrop) COUNTS AS FINISHING the step you're on so it never re-nags.
The sheet hides via a local `dismissed` flag independent of the network write — otherwise a slow completeIntro() strands a dimmed overlay over the app.
completeIntro() sets profiles.intro_seen = true inside a try/catch (a no-op pre-migration) and clears the flag locally first.
Admin 'view as' forces needsIntro: false — an admin previewing must never trigger onboarding.
Section header warns the verification pass did not run — confirm profiles.intro_seen and the other column names before building.

features.name: Prove the invite link is yours
features.whatItDoes: If you got in through an admin invite link, the app asks you to type your own email address before letting you in, so a forwarded link can't drop you into someone else's account.
gotchas: Shown ONLY when invitedViaLink (profiles.invited_via = 'invite_link').
Why it exists: an admin invite-link email signs in WHOEVER CLICKS IT, with no code and no password, so a forwarded invite would silently drop the forwardee into the original invitee's account.
The step NEVER displays the target email — the member has to type it blind, because glancing at a displayed address and tapping Continue verifies nothing.
