After 3 wrong attempts it calls signOut() rather than ever revealing whose account it almost was.
The step has NO close button — Continue or sign out are the only exits.

features.name: Turn on notifications during onboarding
features.whatItDoes: Right after getting in, a new member is asked to turn on phone notifications and can untick the kinds they don't want.
gotchas: Mounts the REAL PushToggle settings (master on by default, untick what you don't want), not a fake preview.
Reaching this step stamps profiles.push_prompted = true so the standalone PushPrompt never asks twice.
Web only stamps it if (isPushSupported() && !(isIos() && !isStandalone())) — i.e. it skips the stamp where web push can't work. ON iOS NATIVE, ALWAYS STAMP IT.
Deliberately the FIRST step, before the basics form.
features.nativeOpportunity: Becomes a real UNUserNotificationCenter requestAuthorization at the one moment the person actually wants notifications — far better prompt conversion than a web push permission dialog, and there is no 'add to home screen first' caveat to explain at all.

features.name: Fill in your basics (name, phone, birthday, pay method)
features.whatItDoes: A short optional form so a new member never has to hunt through Settings to add their phone, birthday and how they like to be paid.
gotchas: All fields optional — an empty form is a valid skip.
Writes phone, birthday, and for pay TWO COLUMNS AT ONCE: row[payMethod] = handle plus row.pay_preferred = payMethod, where payMethod ∈ venmo | zelle | cashapp | paypal.
The name goes through updateUser({ name }) so the rest of the app picks it up.
AWAIT the name write before navigating. An unawaited write got cut off mid-flight and rolled the member back to the email-prefix default display name (motu42). Use `try await`, NOT a detached Task.
birthday is a "YYYY-MM-DD" string — do NOT parse it with a UTC formatter (this app has already been bitten by UTC/date-string skew).
Section header warns the verification pass did not run — confirm the pay/phone/birthday column names before building.
features.nativeOpportunity: Birthday uses a native DatePicker wheel instead of the hand-rolled BirthdayPicker; phone uses a .keyboardType(.phonePad) field with PhoneInput's formatting; the pay handle can offer paste-from-clipboard detection.

features.name: No 'add to home screen' nudges (nothing to build)
features.whatItDoes: Nothing — the web app's 'install me first so you only sign in once' prompts have no reason to exist in a real app.
gotchas: Do NOT port InstallFirstNudge. It exists solely because iOS Safari and an installed iOS PWA keep SEPARATE logins, so a guest who signs in in Safari has to sign in a second time in the icon app. That problem does not exist for a native app.
Same for InstallHint / InstallButton — nothing to port.
mlr.installNudge.seen is in the deliberately-not-cleared-on-signout list; it becomes dead storage on iOS.

features.name: Screens show their last known content instantly instead of loading spinners
features.whatItDoes: Every screen keeps a copy of what it last showed, paints that immediately, and quietly refreshes in the background.
webFiles: lib/swrCache.ts — useCachedResource<T>(key, empty, fetcher, opts?), readPersisted/writePersisted/removePersisted, clearAllCaches()
gotchas: Contract constants: key prefix "mlr.cache.v1." (bump to invalidate everything), MAX_PERSIST_BYTES = 200_000 (oversized snapshots stay memory-only, SILENTLY), DEFAULT_TTL_MS = 24h, envelope { ts: number, data: T }.

key = null ⇒ the hook is fully INERT (no seed, no fetch, data = empty). In Swift this is `key: String?` on the loader, NOT an `if let` around the call site — the call must still happen so the view's state machine stays consistent.
Two layers: a module-level memory Map (survives in-session screen remounts) and an optional persisted copy (paints the last known data on the NEXT app open).
`loading` is true ONLY when nothing could seed. A warm seed serves stale immediately with loading: false while the background revalidate runs.
In-flight dedup per key — two screens mounting the same key join one request ([String: Task] inside an actor).
A rejected fetch must NEVER stick on loading: setLoading(false) and keep the stale data.
commit() writes the memory/disk copy EVEN IF the component unmounted — 'don't lose the fetch'. In Swift, commit BEFORE the cancellation check when using Task cancellation.
reload() REPLACES any stale in-flight entry; mutate() writes state + memory + disk in one call and is the optimistic-update path.
markPending(key) fires only on a COLD load (feeds the launch readiness registry).
Disk location: Application Support/mlr.cache.v1/<sha256(key)>.json — NOT Caches/, which iOS may purge under pressure and would silently reintroduce cold opens.
Use Task cancellation via .task(id: key) instead of the web's `cancelled` boolean — it mirrors useCachedResource's [key] effect dependency exactly.
Never store a Date as an ISO8601-UTC string in the KEY; the payload is fine.

Two entries are TRIMMED snapshots, not full data, because of the 200 KB cap: postsFeed.<uid> keeps roughly the top ~15 posts with their comments/reactions/members, and chatRoom.* / houseChatRoom.* keep the last ~30 messages plus access/roster. Never persist full history. On iOS the cap is yours to choose — but KEEP A CAP, or a big album's snapshot turns a launch into a multi-megabyte JSON decode on the main thread.

Caching a chat room's messages on disk was an OWNER-APPROVED trade-off, on the grounds that the member can already read that room. It is uid-scoped and wiped on sign-out. Do NOT extend that reasoning to anything the viewer can't already read.
Everything is stale-while-revalidate: a seed ALWAYS gets a background refetch, so revoked access and deleted rows self-correct.
features.nativeOpportunity: No 200 KB quota and no synchronous localStorage — the snapshot can be the full feed, decoded off the main actor.
features.v1Cut: Memory + disk honouring rules 2–4 (uid-scoped keys, no preview persistence, wipe on sign-out) with NO TTL tuning. Persist only the handful of resources that actually cold-open (identity, feed, events, unread); leave everything else memory-only, and skip full-history snapshots entirely.

features.name: One member's cached data never shows up on another's screen
features.whatItDoes: Everything the app remembers on the device is filed under whose account it belongs to, so switching accounts can't leak the previous person's screens.
gotchas: Keep the SAME key shapes as web so the two apps are debuggable side by side: identity.<uid>, myHouse.<uid>, feed.<uid>, events.<uid|guest>, unread.<uid>, notifFeed.<uid>, postsFeed.<uid>, people.<uid>, polls.<uid>, activePoll.<uid>, calloutsDone.<uid>, workChecklist.<uid|guest>, helpRequests.<uid>, festMember.<uid>, dropBoxes.<uid>, dropBox.<uid>.<boxId>, privateActivities.<uid>, tournament.<uid>.<hostId>, chatRoom.<uid>.<slug>|<area>, houseChatRoom.<uid>.<slug>, chatPolls.<uid>.<roomKey>, meetings.<uid>.<roomKey> (roomKey = c:<slug>|<area> or h:<houseId>), resolvedHouse.<uid>.<slug|"mine">.<isAdmin>, chatEntry.<uid>.<slug>, managedCommittee.<uid>.<slug>.<isAdmin>, houseCalendar.<houseId>, houseLists.<houseId>, whosUpNorth.<uid>.<date>, birthdays.<uid>.<date>, onThisDay.<uid>.<date>.
Public, unscoped keys: festContent, appImages, weather.
Pass key = nil while the uid is unresolved so the hook stays inert — otherwise another account's rows can seed into the current viewer's screen.

Day-fresh data embeds the LOCAL date (birthdays.<uid>.<today>) so a stale day never paints. Compute that day key from local date parts — Calendar.current components — NEVER an ISO8601 UTC formatter / toISOString(). This app has already been bitten once by UTC/date-string skew.
Uid-scoped keys are the SECOND line of defence for the token-expiry path where signOut() never runs: leftover entries are inert without a session.

features.name: Admin 'view as' never leaves the other person's data behind
features.whatItDoes: While an admin is looking at the app as someone else, nothing from that view is saved to the device.
gotchas: Reference pattern: key = user && userId ? (previewAsId ? `myHouse.preview.${previewAsId}` : `myHouse.${userId}`) : null, with { persist: previewAsId ? undefined : "local" } — the preview id goes in the (memory-only) key AND persistence is switched off.
Same shape for activePoll.preview.<id>, chatEntry.preview.<id>.<slug>, resolvedHouse.preview.….
If a preview snapshot ever lands on disk, the admin's NEXT real cold open paints the previewed member's data as their own.

features.name: Signing out wipes the device clean (but keeps your text size)
features.whatItDoes: Signing out removes every trace of the account's content from the device, while leaving device preferences like text size alone.
gotchas: clearAllCaches() wipes the memory map, the in-flight map, AND every mlr.cache.* key in both storages, so nothing outlives an account switch on a shared device.
signOut() additionally calls clearMediaToken() and clears the preview key. On iOS it must ALSO clear the Keychain — sign-out has to clear Keychain AND the disk cache AND the media token.

Deliberately NOT cleared on sign-out (device preferences, not account data): mlr-text-scale, mlr-welcomed, mlr-dismissed-announcements, mlr.callouts.dismissed, mlr.callouts.wiggled, mlr.installNudge.seen, mlr.dropbox.sort, mlr.flaggedPosts, mlr-demo-date, mlr.chunkRecovery.lastReload. Port that split intentionally — text size and 'I've seen the welcome card' belong to the device; feed snapshots belong to the account.
Uid-scoped keys remain the backstop for the token-expiry path where signOut() never runs.

features.name: First frame after launch is already your content
features.whatItDoes: Opening the app from cold shows the last content it had straight away, rather than an empty shell that fills in a moment later.
gotchas: Rule 1 (memory seeds synchronously, storage seeds post-mount) is WEB-ONLY — do NOT port it. It exists purely for React hydration: the prerendered HTML is always the guest/empty view, so the first client render must match it byte-for-byte, which forces the persisted snapshot to be read inside an effect.
On iOS, read the disk snapshot SYNCHRONOUSLY before the first frame — that is strictly better and is the native version of the property Rule 1 was fighting to get.
useUrlParam being effect-only and FeedView's useIsoLayoutEffect are the same kind of hydration accommodation — also not worth porting.
Decode off the main actor if the snapshot is large; keep a size cap on what you persist.
features.nativeOpportunity: SwiftUI has no hydration, no server-rendered HTML and no mismatch to make, so the whole class of workaround disappears and the cached first frame is free.

features.name: Catches up after the app has been in the background
features.whatItDoes: When you come back to the app after a while it refreshes itself instead of showing yesterday's information.
webFiles: components/UpdateBanner.tsx (the web analogue: visibilitychange / focus / pageshow re-checks)
gotchas: Use @Environment(\.scenePhase) → revalidate on .active. This replaces the web's visibilitychange / focus / pageshow.persisted re-checks.
This is where the app catches up after a day in the background — and the right place to call ensureMediaToken(force:).
Keep the REASON the web's version poll exists: people sit on stale state without knowing. On iOS the analogue isn't a stale bundle, it's stale DATA.

features.name: Photos load fast and their access token stays out of the link
features.whatItDoes: Pictures and videos are cached properly by the phone, and the key that unlocks them never shows up in a link, a log or a screenshot.
endpoints: /f — the mini's requireMediaToken accepts EITHER ?t= or an Authorization: Bearer <mediaToken> header
gotchas: Send the media token as Authorization: Bearer <mediaToken> so URLCache keys on the CLEAN url and the token never appears in a URL, a log line, or a shared screenshot.
The web only gets HTTP caching at all because the media token is STABLE PER 24h WINDOW — a per-request token would bust every image cache.
URLCache handles media/HTTP caching for free with a shared URLSession config; pair it with ensureMediaToken(force:) on scenePhase .active.
features.nativeOpportunity: Bearer-header auth for media is impossible from an , so this is a native-only improvement over the web's ?t= query string.

features.name: Works with no signal at the lake
features.whatItDoes: With no cell service you can still read the feed, the schedule and photos you've already seen.
gotchas: The disk snapshot plus URLCache is the whole mechanism — no extra sync layer needed.
The web app cannot do this at all, because its service worker deliberately caches nothing.
This is the actual physical situation the app is used in (an iPhone with no signal at the lake), so it's a real product win rather than a nicety.
Needs the cache store's disk layer and the media-token/URLCache work in place first.
features.nativeOpportunity: Real offline reads via the disk snapshot + URLCache — something the web app is structurally incapable of.
features.v1Cut: Defer (explicit in the doc's v1 cut). v1 can simply let whatever the disk snapshot happens to hold paint, with no offline banner, no queued writes and no explicit offline empty-state copy.

features.name: Launch screen holds until the first screen is actually ready
features.whatItDoes: The app doesn't hand you a half-drawn screen — it stays on the opening screen for a moment until the first screen's content has landed.
gotchas: Constants: hold until authReady, then on a COLD open up to EXTRA_QUIET_MS = 700 more while cold data loads land; HOLD_MS = 1300 minimum hold; FLY_MS = 720; and MAX_WAIT_MS = 4500 WHICH ALWAYS WINS.
On a warm open every screen seeds instantly, nothing registers, and the hold adds ~0 ms.

onQuietOnce defers its first 'am I already quiet?' check by a MICROTASK so loads registered in the same commit are counted first. Without that it concludes 'quiet' before anything registered and the hold does nothing. In Swift the equivalent is a Task.yield() (or one run-loop hop) before the first check — this is the single easiest thing to get subtly wrong.

THE CAP IS NOT OPTIONAL. Every path out of the hold must be bounded; the web has TWO independent safety nets (the JS MAX_WAIT_MS timer and a pure-CSS splash-wash animation at 6000 ms that clears the overlay even if JS never runs). A launch gate with no ceiling is an app that won't start on a bad network.
markPending is called by the cache loader ONLY when nothing seeded, so the registry is inherently a cold-open concept.
features.nativeOpportunity: Hold the SYSTEM launch screen rather than painting a fake one over the app — 'hold the launch screen until the first screen is actually complete' is exactly what a premium native app does.
features.v1Cut: Defer entirely — a plain launch screen with no readiness registry is explicitly fine for v1.

features.name: The logo settles into place as the app opens
features.whatItDoes: The green MLR mark on the opening screen moves into its spot in the header instead of just disappearing.
gotchas: Do NOT port the splash animation itself. The web pops the green logo centre-screen and FLIP-translates/scales it into the header's #app-logo slot, holding the header copy at opacity: 0 so there's no second copy to blur against — that whole mechanism exists because the web has no launch screen.

iOS has one: use a LaunchScreen storyboard/asset with the same green mark, then matchedGeometryEffect (or a simple scale/position transition) into the Home header if you want the same 'placed there' feel.
Reduce-motion must skip STRAIGHT to the app (UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled / @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion)) — web checks prefers-reduced-motion in three places for this.
features.nativeOpportunity: A real system launch screen means the transition can be honest rather than a reconstructed FLIP.

features.name: Fest master editor opens straight in, with no splash or nag
features.whatItDoes: Opening the Family Fest master editor from the app drops you right into it, without the opening animation or any install prompt.
gotchas: A 'bare route' concept exists so the fest master editor, when opened FROM THE iOS APP, drops straight in with no splash/install nag.
If iOS still opens that editor in a web view, KEEP PASSING that route — verify in the iOS repo which way it currently opens.

features.name: Tapping a notification knows exactly where to go
features.whatItDoes: Every notification carries the address of the thing it's about, and the app understands all of those addresses.
endpoints: /events?activity=<privateActivityId> — private_activity_invite, tournament pings for a private activity
gotchas: Every notification row carries a ready-made in-app path in notifications.url, built server-side by the fan-out triggers, and THE SAME STRING ARRIVES IN THE APNs PAYLOAD — iOS must parse the identical set.

/chat?m=<id> is LEGACY (migration 0030), superseded by the /posts?c=…&m=… form in 0063. Older notification rows may still carry it. Handle it as an ALIAS, not a live shape, and accept it in ONE place (DeepLink(path:)).

NEVER route to /committees/<slug>/chat. In the installed PWA that navigation dies in the app container before React runs (WebKit's own 'This page couldn't load'), while opening the same room through the Feed works; every server-side check comes back healthy so it is invisible outside a real installed PWA, and three fixes failed before the cause was found. On iOS native this specific failure won't reproduce, but the URL CONTRACT STILL MATTERS: notification rows in the database use the Feed form, so parse /posts?c=…&area=…&m= and open your committee room from it.
Honour &from=<slug> — web uses it to make Back return to the committee page instead of the chats list.

Parse into a TYPE, never route on strings: enum DeepLink with post(id:comment:), mainFeed, committeeRoom(slug:area:message:poll:from:), houseRoom(slug:message:), workItem, event, privateActivity, meeting, houseCalendar, member, scheduleItem, dropBox, cabinBookings, admin(AdminDestination).
No backend change is needed — every deep-link string already exists in Supabase and is already produced by shipped triggers/RPCs.
Section header warns the verification pass did not run — confirm the notification kinds and url shapes against the migrations before building.

features.name: A tapped notification always lands, even from a cold start
features.whatItDoes: Whether the app was closed, already open, or you tapped a shared link, you end up on the exact thing you tapped.
gotchas: Drive one @Observable router (var pending: DeepLink?) consumed by the tab container, so a single code path serves: a cold launch from a notification (UNNotificationResponse in didFinishLaunching), a tap while running (userNotificationCenter(_:didReceive:)), a Universal Link, and an in-app tap.

A COLD LAUNCH FROM A NOTIFICATION MUST NOT LOSE THE LINK WHILE AUTH RESOLVES. Queue it and replay it after the viewer state settles — this is the native analogue of the bug PushDeepLink was written to fix (the service worker's client.navigate() rejecting in an installed PWA, swallowing the error, and just focusing the app on whatever page it already showed).

The web's useUrlParam one-time monkey-patches history.pushState/replaceState to dispatch a custom mlr:locationchange event (and listens to popstate) because Next doesn't remount on a router.push() to the SAME route — tapping a second notification while already on /posts would otherwise be a no-op. The native equivalent: the router must handle a second link arriving with no remount and re-arm the scroll/flash.
Parse once, in DeepLink(path:) — the router never inspects strings.

features.name: Jumps to the exact post, comment or message and highlights it
features.whatItDoes: After tapping a notification the app scrolls right to the item it was about and briefly highlights it so you can see which one.
gotchas: Web polls document.getElementById(idPrefix + target) every 150 ms up to 20 attempts (~3 s), then scrollIntoView({ block: "center" }), and clears the flash id after 2200 ms. On iOS use ScrollViewReader.scrollTo(id, anchor: .center) over a List/LazyVStack with STABLE ids after the fetch — no retries, no race.

The polling existed because the target node may not exist yet — a long list still rendering, or a TRIMMED COLD-OPEN SNAPSHOT that doesn't contain an older item the full fetch hasn't landed yet. Whatever you do on iOS, handle 'the target isn't in the data yet': await the real fetch, and if the id still isn't present, LAND ON THE SCREEN rather than nowhere.

The FIRST landing in a mount SNAPS (behavior: "auto") because the viewer hasn't been shown anything to scroll from and an animated scroll reads as an extra hop. A LATER deep-link (second notification, no remount) scrolls SMOOTHLY, because there the motion is the useful cue that the view moved. Both behaviours are deliberate and should survive the port.
It re-arms whenever target changes, and PostsView runs TWO INDEPENDENT INSTANCES side by side ("post-" and "comment-") — the hook has no shared state.
features.nativeOpportunity: ScrollViewReader.scrollTo replaces the 3-second DOM poll entirely; the flash becomes a real .overlay ring with withAnimation plus UIImpactFeedbackGenerator — a native 'here it is' cue the web can't produce.

features.name: A deep-linked room opens directly, without flashing the chat list
features.whatItDoes: Tapping a notification for a committee or house chat opens that room straight away instead of showing the list of chats and then jumping.
gotchas: FeedView holds a 'Loading…' instead of flashing the chats list while a ?c= / ?house= deep-link resolves; bootChannelKey / bootHouseSlug are CAPTURED AT MOUNT.
Without it a member who IS in a house/committee sees the plain chats list for a beat and then gets 'hopped' to the room — the deep link works but reads as broken.
Reproduce that on iOS: a deep-linked launch should never paint the list state AT ALL.

features.name: Reply from the lock screen without opening the app
features.whatItDoes: You can tap 'On my way', RSVP, or approve/remove content right on the notification, without opening the app.
gotchas: UNNotificationCategory actions cover 'On my way' (Ask for Help), RSVP Going/Can't-make, and Approve/Remove (moderation).
EVERY ONE OF THOSE ALREADY HAS AN RPC — no backend work, just wiring the action identifiers to the existing calls.
Actions fire with the app possibly not running; they must go through the same auth/session path and the same preview-mode no-op rules as in-app writes.
features.nativeOpportunity: Lock-screen actions are impossible on the web — the doc calls the deep-link/notification area the biggest native win in the section.

features.name: Unread count on the app icon
features.whatItDoes: The app icon shows how many new things are waiting, the same number as the Activity tab.
gotchas: Drive it from the SAME unread count the tab badge uses (cache key unread.<uid>) so the two can never disagree.
Keep it in sync when the Activity tab is opened (opening the tab clears the badge on web).
features.nativeOpportunity: App icon badging has no web equivalent at all.

features.name: Shared links open the app, not Safari
features.whatItDoes: When someone texts a link to a photo album or a post, it opens in the app instead of the website.
gotchas: Worth doing because the family shares those links in iMessage.
Reuse the same DeepLink(path:) parser — a Universal Link is just another producer of the same enum, routed through the same @Observable router.
Cold-launch links from a Universal Link need the same queue-and-replay-after-auth handling as notification taps.
features.nativeOpportunity: Universal Links make the existing shareable web URLs open the native app.

features.name: Siri, Spotlight and Handoff
features.whatItDoes: Screens show up in phone search and can be handed off between devices, and you can ask Siri things like who's up north.
gotchas: NSUserActivity on each screen gives Handoff and Spotlight for free.
The same DeepLink enum backs App Intents / Shortcuts ("Hey Siri, who's up north?") — build it on top of the parser rather than a second routing layer.
Explicitly on the doc's defer list for v1.
features.nativeOpportunity: NSUserActivity / App Intents have no web analogue whatsoever.

features.name: Text size follows the phone's own setting
features.whatItDoes: The app's text is as large as the size you already chose in your phone's settings — including the very large accessibility sizes.
gotchas: Do NOT port the three-button control. Web's TextSizeControl writes localStorage["mlr-text-scale"] ∈ normal | large | largest and sets document.documentElement.style.fontSize to 17 / 19 / 21 px, with a blocking inline script in app/layout.tsx re-applying it before first paint. It exists ONLY because the web has no access to the OS text-size setting.
iOS gets this for free and better: .font(.body) etc., @ScaledMetric for spacing, UIFontMetrics for anything custom — and it reaches the accessibility sizes the web's 21 px ceiling can't.
LAYOUT MUST SURVIVE THE LARGEST ACCESSIBILITY SIZES. Audit every card, chip and tab label at AX5, and prefer ViewThatFits / wrapping over truncation for member names and event titles.
globals.css warning, for context: 'don't re-pin a px font-size on body/html or you break it' — everything being rem-based is what makes one knob scale the whole app.

Doc drift to be aware of: CLAUDE.md says pinch-zoom is allowed (userScalable: true) but app/layout.tsx ships maximumScale: 1, userScalable: false with a comment that stray pinches were zooming the layout. THE CODE IS AUTHORITATIVE. On iOS this is moot, but it tells you the intent: text scaling is the supported path, not zoom.
features.nativeOpportunity: Dynamic Type honours the size the person already chose system-wide, which the web app fundamentally cannot read.

features.name: Secondary text stays readable for older eyes
features.whatItDoes: Timestamps, subtitles and helper text are a real readable grey-green rather than faded-out body text.
gotchas: THE READABILITY FLOOR IS A HARD PRODUCT RULE, NOT A STYLE PREFERENCE. --color-muted (#4b5b52) and --color-faint (#64716a) exist because text-foreground/40 reads too faint for older eyes, and ~40 components were swept onto them.
NEVER express secondary text as an OPACITY on the foreground colour. Define Color.mlrMuted / Color.mlrFaint as real semantic colours with their own DARK-MODE values.
These two stay sRGB (not Display P3) along with the other neutrals, so they keep matching the raster logo.

features.name: The app's colour set (pine green, birch, campfire orange)
features.whatItDoes: Every screen uses the same named resort colours, richer on screens that can show them.
gotchas: Palette verbatim: --color-background #f6f6f1 (warm birch near-white), --color-foreground #14241c (deep pine near-black), --color-card #ffffff, --color-border #e5e4da, --color-primary #15503a (pine green, the logo; white text passes), --color-logo #0c4029 (exact green baked into the raster logo), --color-accent #c2410c (campfire orange), --color-lake #0e7490, --color-campfire #c2410c, --color-sun #b45309, --color-dusk #6d28d9, --color-fest #8b2e2e (Family Fest heraldic wine, used OUTSIDE the fest section), --color-muted #4b5b52, --color-faint #64716a, --color-venmo #3d95ce, --color-paypal #003087.
Colours are TOKENS, never hex in a component.

NEVER use a dark translucent surface tint (bg-black/NN, bg-zinc-*/NN) as a card or panel background — it goes muddy grey on a light page, a recurring bug across the author's apps. A dark wash is acceptable ONLY as a full-screen modal scrim. (This rule INVERTS in dark mode — see the dark-mode entry.)
The web app is light-mode only by hard rule (globals.css says so three times, plus color-scheme: light) — there is therefore no dark palette to copy.

Display-P3 layer: only the ACCENTS are enriched (primary, accent, lake, campfire, sun, dusk, fest). Background, foreground, cards, borders, the readability floors and the logo band STAY sRGB so they keep matching the raster logo. Define the accents in Display P3 in the asset catalogue with an sRGB fallback and leave the neutrals in sRGB.
features.nativeOpportunity: Asset-catalogue Display P3 colours with sRGB fallbacks are a genuine 'premier experience' detail the web can only approximate.

features.name: Family Fest looks like parchment, the rest of the app looks like the resort
features.whatItDoes: The Family Fest section has its own warm parchment-and-wine look with a fancier serif, while everything else stays forest green.
gotchas: Fest palette: parchment #f4ecd8, sepia ink #3a2a18, vellum #fdfaf1, tan border #d8c7a3, heraldic wine primary #8b2e2e, azure accent #1e3a8a, plus a Cinzel display serif.
It is a scoped PALETTE SWAP, not a separate app — .ff-section re-declares the same --color-* variables so every utility inside that subtree renders parchment.
On iOS this is an @Environment(\.mlrTheme) value (a Theme struct of semantic colours + fonts) injected at the Family Fest tab's root — sheets inherit it naturally through the environment.

The web's extra machinery does NOT transfer: FestThemeSync toggles html[data-ff] so the viewport-level canvas behind rubber-band bounce matches, and ModalPortal/Sheet must RE-APPLY the class by route because portaling to <body> escapes the subtree.
--color-fest (#8b2e2e) is also used OUTSIDE the fest section (the tab tint + live dot), so it belongs in the main palette too.
The parchment theme needs its OWN dark counterpart — a candle-lit vellum, not an inverted one.
features.nativeOpportunity: Environment-injected theming means no class re-application problem and sheets inherit the sub-theme for free.
features.v1Cut: Ship the fest tab with the resort palette plus the wine accent/live dot and defer the full parchment + Cinzel treatment (fest sub-theme polish is on the doc's explicit defer list).

features.name: Dark mode
features.whatItDoes: The app looks right for people whose phone is set to dark — every screen, including the Family Fest section.
gotchas: iOS SUPPORTS DARK MODE AND THERE IS NO WEB REFERENCE TO COPY — the web app is light-mode only by hard rule. Budget for it explicitly rather than discovering it.
Every colour in the palette needs a dark counterpart, INCLUDING the parchment fest theme (a candle-lit vellum, not an inverted one) and including --color-muted / --color-faint.
The 'no dark translucent tint' rule INVERTS: in dark mode .ultraThinMaterial over a dark ground is CORRECT, which is the opposite of the web rule.

Decide per-surface and audit BOTH appearances on every screen. The July parity doc's build check already says 'verify light AND dark on every new surface' and that is the single most commonly skipped step.
features.v1Cut: If a per-surface dark palette can't be designed for v1, commit the app to a single explicit LIGHT appearance — every background and foreground painted from tokens, nothing relying on system semantic colours that auto-invert — and add dark surface-by-surface afterwards. What you must not ship is screens that half-invert.

features.name: The five bottom tabs
features.whatItDoes: Home, Feed, Family Fest, Activity and Profile along the bottom, with the current one highlighted.
gotchas: TABS is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for routes + labels + icons — mirror it as one table, not five hardcoded tabs.
Active detection: tab.href === "/" ? pathname === "/" : pathname.startsWith(tab.href).
People is NOT a tab (it moved to a Home tile) and Profile IS the last tab (it moved back from a header avatar). THIS HAS BEEN REVERSED BEFORE — don't 'improve' it without asking.

features.name: Unread count on the Activity tab
features.whatItDoes: A little number on the Activity tab shows how many new things there are, counting up as they arrive.
gotchas: Rendered as a count pill; anything > 99 shows '99+'; animated via AnimatedNumber on web.
Cache key is unread.<uid> — uid-scoped and wiped on sign-out like everything else.
Feed the app icon badge from this same count so they can't disagree.

features.name: Family Fest tab lights up during the fest
features.whatItDoes: While Family Fest is happening (and just after), its tab gets a pulsing dot and turns the fest's wine colour so you can spot it from anywhere.
gotchas: A pinging dot whenever getFestSeason(...) is isLive || isWrap.
The tab wears --color-fest (heraldic wine #8b2e2e) rather than forest green, so the fest reads as its own theme from anywhere in the app.
The season phase must be computed at RUN time, not baked at build time.

features.name: Nothing hides under the tab bar and sheets always sit on top
features.whatItDoes: Content always clears the bottom tab bar, full-screen panels are never trapped behind it, and the keyboard doesn't shove things around.
gotchas: THREE shell mechanisms are pure WebKit workarounds — DO NOT PORT ANY OF THEM: (1) the single #app-scroll scroll container (html, body { height: 100%; overflow: hidden } + overscroll-behavior-y: contain, with the TabBar as a SIBLING not a descendant, plus ScrollReset resetting scroll on every navigation); (2) ModalPortal; (3) KeyboardInset + the TabBar's keyboard hide.

The one real lesson that DOES survive: the bottom clearance for the tab bar is padding on an INNER CONTENT WRAPPER, not padding-bottom on the scroller, because iOS Safari drops the latter. The native analogue is safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) — use it rather than hardcoded padding.

Context for ModalPortal (so nobody reinvents it): .page-enter's slide-in transform makes the route wrapper a PERMANENT containing block and stacking context for position: fixed descendants on iOS Safari, even after the animation ends (the `backwards` fill removes the transform at rest, which is exactly why it looks fine on desktop and in dev), so an inline fixed inset-0 overlay gets clipped to the page box and confined below the TabBar's z-40. On iOS use .sheet / .fullScreenCover and this class of bug cannot occur.

Context for KeyboardInset: the iOS software keyboard OVERLAYS the layout viewport instead of shrinking it, so web measures visualViewport into a --keyboard-inset custom property and slides the fixed TabBar off-screen. There's a real bug recorded in TabBar.tsx: iOS fires a visualViewport resize with WRONG dimensions during the background→foreground transition, which locked the bar off-screen — so it resets on visibilitychange and re-checks after 300 ms. SwiftUI handles the keyboard safe area natively; none of this transfers.
NavigationStack gives per-navigation scroll reset for free.
features.nativeOpportunity: SwiftUI's TabView + ScrollView, .sheet/.fullScreenCover, NavigationStack and the keyboard safe area delete three whole subsystems of web workaround.

features.name: One '+' button that opens the phone's own photo picker
features.whatItDoes: Adding a photo or video is a single button that opens the normal iPhone picker — photo library, camera or files — with no extra menu first.
gotchas: The WEB rule (from the chat-attachment incident): a file input and its trigger must both be plain, always-mounted siblings, never inside a popup/menu, or an installed iOS PWA silently delivers nothing. On iOS this becomes PhotosPicker / UIImagePickerController and the constraint evaporates.
KEEP THE PRODUCT CONSEQUENCE though: ONE plain '+' button that opens the system picker covering photo library / camera / files — NOT a custom pre-menu.
features.nativeOpportunity: PHAsset-backed pickers with Live Photo and burst handling; AVPlayer with real background audio and PiP for videos, where the web falls back to a plain <video>.

features.name: Taps that actually feel like something
features.whatItDoes: Small taps and confirmations give a little haptic buzz.
gotchas: lib/haptics.ts is explicitly ANDROID-ONLY and a no-op on iOS — the tab-tap haptic the web wanted HAS NEVER FIRED for a single iPhone user.
Use CoreHaptics / UIFeedbackGenerator; pair UIImpactFeedbackGenerator with the deep-link flash as the 'here it is' cue.
features.nativeOpportunity: Haptics are simply unavailable to the web app on iOS, so every one of them is new.

features.name: Home-screen widgets
features.whatItDoes: Small home-screen tiles for who's up north today, the next event, and the countdown to Family Fest.
gotchas: All three read data the app already caches — no new backend.
Widget code cannot reach the Keychain session or the app's cache store without a shared app group; plan the cache location for that if you attempt it.
Explicitly on the doc's defer list for v1.
features.nativeOpportunity: Widgets have no web equivalent at all.
features.v1Cut: Defer entirely. If attempted, ship exactly one widget (fest countdown or next event) reading the existing disk snapshot, with no new backend, no interactivity and no timeline-refresh tuning.

features.name: No 'a new version is available' bar (the App Store handles it)
features.whatItDoes: Nothing — the web app's refresh-to-update bar and its chunk-error recovery have no native equivalent.
gotchas: For context: UpdateBanner bakes NEXT_PUBLIC_BUILD_ID into the bundle and publishes the same value at /version.json, polling it on mount, on visibilitychange, on focus, on pageshow.persisted, and every 5 minutes with cache: "no-store" plus a ?ts= cache-buster. On a mismatch it offers a one-tap Refresh that purges ALL of Cache Storage, calls registration.update() on any service worker (deliberately NOT unregister(), which would drop the push subscription), races that against a 1500 ms timeout, and reloads.
NONE OF THIS PORTS — it exists because an iOS home-screen PWA keeps running the build it launched with until it's fully closed and reopened. The App Store solves that.

Same for ChunkErrorRecovery (catches ChunkLoadError / 'Loading chunk … failed' and does one guarded hard reload, mlr.chunkRecovery.lastReload, one attempt per 30 s) — a bundler problem with no native equivalent.
DO keep the REASON the poll exists: people sit on stale state without knowing. On iOS the analogue isn't a stale bundle, it's stale DATA — handled by scenePhase revalidation and background refresh.

features.name: 'Please update the app' gate (deliberately not built yet)
features.whatItDoes: Nothing yet — there is no way for the server to tell old copies of the app that they must update, and for now that's fine.
gotchas: There is currently NO server-side minimum-version signal in the database. A native 'please update' gate would need one.
Option 1 — SKIP IT FOR V1. Recommended. Nothing in the app breaks on an old client today, because every client seam degrades gracefully on a missing table/column (42P01, column-not-found retries).

Option 2 — if a gate is later wanted, REUSE resort_config: it's already a singleton row, already PUBLIC-READ BY DESIGN (it holds the help contact, which can't be gated behind the sign-in it exists to unblock), and already admin-writable. Adding min_ios_build int there is one column, not a new table. ⚠️ THAT IS A BACKEND CHANGE — don't do it silently.

Everything else in this whole section needs NO backend change: every gate, flag and deep-link string already exists in Supabase and is already produced by shipped triggers/RPCs. The minimum-version signal is the single genuine server-side gap.

features.name: Fresh data at launch, and a quiet 'what's new'
features.whatItDoes: The app quietly refreshes in the background so it's up to date when you open it, and after an update it can show a short 'what's new' note.
gotchas: These are the real native equivalents of the web's version poll and need NO backend at all: background refresh so data is fresh at launch, plus a passive 'What's new' screen keyed on the LOCAL build number.
Keep it passive — no blocking gate, no forced refresh (there's no minimum-version signal to enforce one with anyway).
Pairs with scenePhase .active revalidation; background refresh is the 'app has been closed for a day' case that scenePhase alone can't cover.
features.nativeOpportunity: Background refresh means the app is already current when opened — the web app can only poll while it's on screen.

features.name: Uploads that keep going when you put the phone away
features.whatItDoes: Pick 30 photos, lock the phone or switch apps, and the upload finishes anyway instead of dying.
rpcs: add_drop_box_media(p_box, p_url, p_type, p_thumbnail_url, p_captured_at, p_captured_at_source, p_credit_user_id)
gotchas: ⚠️ A background URLSession CANNOT use an in-memory body — write the multipart body to a file and use uploadTask(with:fromFile:). Foreground works, background silently never fires.
⚠️ category and room MUST ride the query string, not multipart body fields — the server picks the destination folder before the bytes arrive (uploadSubdir(req) in server.js).
⚠️ Insert the *_media row only AFTER /upload returns, like web. The orphan sweep grants a fresh file a 48h grace period precisely because of this ordering.

⚠️ A background task can outlive the Supabase access token: refresh before enqueueing, treat 401/403 as re-auth-and-retry — EXCEPT a 403 'pendingApproval', which means the member isn't admin-verified (0181/0183) and no retry helps.

⚠️ /upload is deliberately EXEMPT from the rate limiter and has no count cap ('a fest is easily hundreds of photos from one phone'). Don't add client-side throttling; do cap concurrency at 3-4 so the mini's ffmpeg/moderation isn't starved.
⚠️ MAX_MB is 50GB and UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS is 4h, and neither means a 50GB upload succeeds — bandwidth binds first. Raising a cap without the timeout converts a clean 413 into a mid-transfer timeout.

⚠️ Moderation is ASYNCHRONOUS: a flagged verdict retroactively flips a row's status to 'pending' seconds after a successful post via a DB trigger. Honor status when rendering; write no moderation code.

⚠️ prepareImageForUpload() is now a deliberate no-op — do NOT reintroduce client-side compression. Its own comment: it destroyed the full-res original and stripped every byte of EXIF, which is why migrations 0174-0176 exist.
features.nativeOpportunity: URLSession background configuration + a persisted queue: the OS completes transfers while the app is suspended or terminated and wakes you at urlSessionDidFinishEvents to insert the rows. The web app physically cannot do this — its XHRs live on a page.
features.v1Cut: Serial-ish queue (3 concurrent) with retry and a persisted manifest. Skip resumable/chunked uploads, skip progress-per-byte fidelity, skip a general write outbox.

features.name: Real photo picking, real capture dates, real originals
features.whatItDoes: Pick unlimited photos in order, and every one lands with the exact date it was taken and at full resolution.
rpcs: add_drop_box_media(p_box, p_url, p_type, p_thumbnail_url, p_captured_at, p_captured_at_source, p_credit_user_id)
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ Read the date from the PHAsset (creationDate), NOT from the exported file. PHPickerResult hands you a temp copy stamped with NOW — literally the 'upload time wearing a disguise' the web code rejects when lastModified is within 60s of now.

⚠️ Set PHImageRequestOptions.version = .original AND isNetworkAccessAllowed = true. On a phone with iCloud Optimize Storage on, the naive path silently uploads a low-res proxy and nobody notices for months.

⚠️ post_media.storage_path is text holding EITHER a full mini URL (mini uploads, the common case) OR a legacy bucket-relative Supabase-Storage path. Web disambiguates with startsWith("http"). Do NOT type it as URL in Swift.
⚠️ drop_box_media.storage_path is ALWAYS the full mini URL — the two tables differ.
⚠️ create_post's p_media jsonb uses camelCase keys {path, type, thumbnail, capturedAt, capturedAtSource}, and despite the name 'path' web passes the FULL URL there.
⚠️ captured_at_source is free text ranked exif > video > file > post; a sweep may only ever move a row UP. Decode as String? mapped to an enum with an unknown case, never a strict Codable enum.
⚠️ thumbnail_url, captured_at and captured_at_source are all NULLABLE. Grids must fall back to the full-res url; a null date must never hide the item.
⚠️ Live Photos need a schema decision — nothing in post_media/drop_box_media links two files as a pair. Cut from v1; upload the still.

⚠️ Never trigger a picker from inside a popup/menu/overlay. On the installed iOS PWA the picker opened, you chose a photo, and nothing arrived with no error; three fixes that kept the popup all failed on device.
features.nativeOpportunity: PHAsset.creationDate replaces a hand-rolled JPEG/TIFF IFD walker, a brute byte-scan for the string 'Exif' in the first 256KB of a HEIC, and a guarded file.lastModified fallback — three migrations (0174-0176) plus a periodic server sweep exist only because a browser cannot get this. selectionLimit = 0 with .ordered selection gives unlimited ordered batch picking. HEIC uploads untouched and can be DISPLAYED natively from ?dl=1's preserved _orig.
features.v1Cut: PHPicker + creationDate + original-version fetch + HEIC pass-through. Skip Live Photos, skip location/EXIF beyond the date (no column exists), skip in-app editing.

features.name: The app works on the lake's weak wifi
features.whatItDoes: The fest schedule, recent photos and the last messages are on the phone, so opening the app in a dead zone shows the app instead of nothing.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ NEVER key a media cache on the signed URL. The token rides ?t= and rotates every 24h window (MEDIA_TOKEN_TTL_HOURS default 24), so the same file's URL changes daily and your cache hit rate silently becomes 0% every morning. Key on the row id or the token-stripped URL.

⚠️⚠️ Every user-scoped cache key must embed the auth uid. A cache keyed on a shared "self" string leaked one member's private chat to the next user on a shared device (web PR #244) — signing out does not reload a native app any more than it reloads a PWA.
⚠️ Sign-out must wipe the entire on-disk cache AND the media token (web: clearAllCaches() + clearMediaToken()).

⚠️ /f reads are NOT exempt from the mini's 600-request/15-minute PER-IP global limiter (only /health and /upload are skipped) — and the whole family shares one IP at the lake house. Every cached thumbnail is a request saved off that counter.
⚠️ A video's storage_path can change shortly after upload (a .mov -> .mp4 transcode repoints it). Re-read the row; don't cache the URL forever.

⚠️ The web app has NO offline capability to copy from — public/sw.js has no fetch handler by design, and lib/swrCache.ts is localStorage-only, 200KB per entry, 24h TTL, text only. There is no PWA cache to beat.

⚠️ Don't port the swallow-everything catch: the web's 'degrade to empty on 42P01' idiom disguises a broken read as 'empty but working', and a table with RLS on and zero policies returns zero rows with NO error — which once deleted a whole feature from every client for weeks. Log it.
features.nativeOpportunity: A URLCache plus a size-budgeted LRU thumbnail store on disk, and persisted model objects with no 200KB-per-key ceiling. This is the difference between 'the app is broken at the lake' and 'the app works at the lake', and it simultaneously takes read load off the mini's ~105-119 Mbps residential uplink and its per-IP rate limiter.
features.v1Cut: Read-cache only: thumbnails, display photos, fest schedule/dinners, current-week events, last ~50 messages per room, member directory. Plus an outbox for chat sends and uploads ONLY. Skip general offline writes and conflict resolution entirely.

features.name: Notifications with the photo in them, a correct badge, and buttons that work
features.whatItDoes: A push shows the actual photo, groups by chat room, badges the real unread count, and lets you RSVP or mark a task done from the Lock Screen.
gotchas: 🔧 BACKEND CHANGE REQUIRED (3 lines, media-server/apns-sender.js ~line 126): the aps dict is literally { alert, sound: 'default', badge: 1 }. Add "mutable-content": 1 (for attachments), add "thread-id" (for per-room grouping), and replace the HARDCODED badge: 1 with the recipient's real unread count.

⚠️⚠️ badge: 1 is hardcoded, so the app icon says '1' forever. The correct count is notifications where recipient_id = uid AND seen_at is null AND (expires_at is null OR expires_at > now()) — own-rows-only RLS, no RPC needed. Also call setBadgeCount(0) right after mark_notifications_seen() so it clears on tab-open, not on the next push.

⚠️⚠️ A Notification Service Extension is a SEPARATE PROCESS with no session — it needs the media token to fetch the attachment from /f. Put the Supabase session AND the media token in an App Group + shared Keychain BEFORE building any extension; retrofitting this is a weekend.
⚠️ An NSE has a hard ~30s budget: download the small thumbnail_url, never the full-res file, and always call the content handler with unmodified content on failure.
⚠️ The attachment URL must carry ?t= — an NSE cannot set an Authorization header on an image load any more than an can.

⚠️⚠️ set_event_attendance has TWO LIVE OVERLOADS. 0036's 4-arg (p_event, p_status, p_days, p_title) fans out the 'X is going to …' notification; 0122 later created a 3-arg (text,text,jsonb) that does NOT. PostgREST resolves by argument NAME, so always pass p_title (even nil) or your RSVP silently stops telling anyone.
⚠️ Verify against prod whether event_attendance.confirmed is actually set on the UPDATE branch — 0122 intended it, but the 4-arg version everyone calls does not do it.
⚠️ help_urgent deserves interruption-level .timeSensitive so it breaks Focus; the push type already carries the distinction and the transport throws it away.

⚠️ Categories EVENT_REMINDER / HELP_REQUEST / CHAT_MENTION / COMMITTEE_JOIN_REQUEST / WORK_FOLLOWUP already exist server-side and the sender's comment says they mirror NotificationActions.swift — audit in the iOS repo what is registered and what each handler actually does.
⚠️ Prune dead tokens: the sender already deletes an apns_subscriptions row on 410 / BadDeviceToken / Unregistered. Don't duplicate that logic client-side.
features.nativeOpportunity: Photo attachments in the notification itself (mutable-content + NSE), per-room grouping via thread-id, a correct app badge, .timeSensitive for urgent help requests, and one-tap RSVP / mark-done / claim from the Lock Screen against RPCs that already exist. Web push on iOS can do essentially none of this.
features.v1Cut: The 3-line server payload fix + NSE for photo attachments + real badge. Actions for EVENT_REMINDER and WORK_FOLLOWUP only. Defer inline chat reply and Live Activities.

features.name: Share photos from the Photos app straight into an album
features.whatItDoes: Select photos anywhere on the phone, tap Share, pick MLR, pick a folder — done.
rpcs: add_drop_box_media(p_box, p_url, p_type, p_thumbnail_url, p_captured_at, p_captured_at_source, p_credit_user_id)
gotchas: ⚠️ Structurally impossible on web, permanently: public/manifest.webmanifest has no share_target, and iOS Safari does not implement Web Share Target at all. This is a capability gap, not a polish gap.
⚠️ The extension must NOT upload inline — it is killed the moment its UI dismisses. Write items into the App Group container and enqueue on the shared background session.
⚠️ A background URLSession created inside an extension REQUIRES sharedContainerIdentifier or it will not run.

⚠️ A share sheet gives you an exported item, not a PHAsset, so creationDate is unavailable. Read DateTimeOriginal via CGImageSourceCopyProperties (kCGImagePropertyExifDictionary) and send capturedAtSource: 'exif'. If you get nothing, send NOTHING — the mini's own reader and the periodic backfill sweep will fill it, and the sweep only ever upgrades, never downgrades.
⚠️ The extension needs the Supabase session to mint an access token for /upload — App Group + shared Keychain. Handle 'signed out in the extension' with a real message, not a silent failure.
⚠️ The official Family Fest album has the fixed id 0000fe57-2026-4000-8000-000000000001 — deep-link it as the default destination.

⚠️ Drop-box moderation is deliberately MORE LENIENT than posts: if the model can't run, the upload is allowed and FINAL and is not re-queued, so a family album never strands photos behind an unreachable checker. Don't 'fix' that.
features.nativeOpportunity: Given Drop Boxes are described as the most-used surface on the web app, a Share Extension whose entire UI is 'which folder?' plus Post is arguably the highest-leverage screen in the iOS app — and the web app can never have it.
features.v1Cut: Images and videos, folder picker, enqueue-and-dismiss. No captions, no tagging, no in-extension progress UI.

features.name: Video that plays instantly, adapts to a weak connection, and casts to the TV
features.whatItDoes: Videos start fast, drop quality instead of stalling on bad signal, keep playing in a corner while you scroll, and AirPlay to the lake-house TV.
gotchas: 🔧 BACKEND CHANGE REQUIRED (env only): HLS_ENABLED is 'off' on the mini. Its own comment: 'Ladders are useless until the client can play them … then flip HLS_ENABLED=on'. hls.js is NOT in package.json, so iOS is what unlocks a feature that is already written and tested.

🔧 OPTIONAL BACKEND CHANGE: /upload computes and returns hlsUrl and NOTHING STORES IT — no column exists. Either add post_media.hls_url / drop_box_media.hls_url, or derive it: for a file at <dir>/<uuid>.<ext> the master is <dir>/<uuid>_hls/master.m3u8 (hlsDirFor/masterPathFor, MASTER_NAME) and HEAD-probe with a progressive fallback.

⚠️⚠️ VIDEO IS HOW THE MEDIA TOKEN BREAKS. AVPlayer issues Range requests and retries; a player that drops the query string on a range retry breaks video while photos look perfect. The log signature is 'range=yes tok=missing'. One ambiguous unsigned .mp4 is why token enforcement was not switched on sooner — exercise scrubbing, then grep WOULD-BLOCK in media-server/logs/server.log.
⚠️ Every HLS segment request carries the token. Verify the emitted playlist's URLs are relative (so ?t= is inherited) before assuming; otherwise use an AVAssetResourceLoaderDelegate.

⚠️ An HLS ladder is a DIRECTORY OF HUNDREDS OF FILES with no database row. Four subsystems already special-case _hls/ (orphan-sweep.js which QUARANTINES unreferenced files, media-usage.js, mirror-sweep.js, /dropbox-zip). Never invent a new derived directory from iOS.

⚠️ Turning HLS on roughly DOUBLES each video's storage. Check Admin -> Media server first: 25GB SSD allowance, 15GB boot-disk reserve, files over 250MB route to the external drive (and files over the per-file limit have NO second copy).

⚠️ Honor GET /media-load: the mini caps quality when MULTIPLE viewers saturate the ~105-119 Mbps house uplink. AVPlayer's preferredPeakBitRate / preferredMaximumResolution is the native equivalent of hls.js autoLevelCapping.
⚠️ A video's storage_path can change after upload (.mov -> .mp4). Re-read the row rather than caching the URL.
⚠️ A video tile needs a visible play badge or it is indistinguishable from a photo; poster frames are seeked ~10% in, not frame 0, because phone video often opens black.
features.nativeOpportunity: AVPlayer plays HLS with zero third-party code, so iOS unlocks the dormant three-rung ladder the mini already builds. Then PiP, AirPlay to the lake-house TV, AVAssetImageGenerator poster frames when thumbnail_url is null, and AVAssetDownloadTask to pre-download fest videos over house wifi for a dead zone.
features.v1Cut: AVPlayer + HLS HEAD-probe with progressive fallback + PiP + AirPlay. Defer AVAssetDownloadTask pre-download and the /media-load bitrate cap.

features.name: The app taps back
features.whatItDoes: Buttons, sends, RSVPs and votes give a real physical tick instead of nothing.
gotchas: ⚠️ lib/haptics.ts is a documented SILENT NO-OP on iOS — navigator.vibrate does not exist in Safari or the installed PWA, so every haptic() call site in the entire web app does nothing on an iPhone today.

Map the four existing kinds 1:1 — light -> UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(.light), medium -> .medium, success -> UINotificationFeedbackGenerator().notificationOccurred(.success), warning -> .warning. Add .selectionChanged() for segmented controls and the FamilyFestNav pill.
⚠️ Mirror the web behavior: haptics.ts skips the buzz under Reduce Motion ('treat Reduce Motion as keep it minimal'). Check UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled.
⚠️ Prepare the generator before the interaction — a cold generator adds latency that reads as a mistimed tap.
Ship this in the FIRST PR: it is hours of work and it changes how everything built after it feels.
features.nativeOpportunity: Pure native-only capability. Highest ratio of felt quality to effort in the whole document.

features.name: Fest countdown, today's schedule and tonight's dinner on the Home and Lock Screen
features.whatItDoes: Glance at your phone during fest week and see how many days out it is, what's on today, and what's for dinner and who's cooking.
gotchas: ✅ Unusually easy: fest_config, fest_dues, fest_schedule_items, fest_dinners, fest_payees and fest_activities are all SELECT using (true) from 0053, and 0183 DELIBERATELY left them public ('fest_content — public by design, no PII'). A widget extension needs only the anon key — no session, no keychain, no media token.

⚠️⚠️ NEVER hand a bare YYYY-MM-DD to a date parser. On web, new Date('2026-07-31') parsed as UTC midnight and rendered as the PREVIOUS day in Central — it mislabelled every sign-up slot, and because the label also fed the organiser's own picker it CORRUPTED 10 stored rows. Always parse fest_schedule_items.day / fest_dinners.day with an explicit America/Chicago timeZone. The lesson generalizes: a display bug in a picker silently corrupts whatever it writes.
⚠️ fest_schedule_items.start_time / end_time are FREEFORM NULLABLE TEXT — 'TBD' is a real value. String?, never a DateFormatter input.
⚠️ fest_dinners.houses is text[] (the houses on crew). Deliberately omit prep_time / prep_location from a public-facing widget — the web dinners index hides crew-only logistics from every reader.

⚠️ 'Who's up north' is the ONLY widget needing a session: event_attendance and houses are is_approved_member() (0183), so an unverified member gets an empty list. Render 'nothing scheduled', never an error, and never treat empty as broken.
⚠️ Keep the web app's deliberately soft wording: 'Up North today', NOT 'right now'. Presence is derived from RSVPs and bookings, not location, and cannot promise anyone has actually arrived.

⚠️ Presence is a UNION of three sources (lib/presence.ts): presentFromAttendance (RSVP'd going to an event happening today, day-aware via the days jsonb map), presentFromCabins (approved booking covering today), presentFromHouseStays. Port all three or the card lies.

⚠️ Widget timeline budget is stingy — refresh every 15-30 min, cache the last good payload in the App Group, and never let a widget be what trips the 600 req/15min /f limiter (read tables, not media).

⚠️ iOS still reads the retired fest_activities table; on web those were merged into anytime fest_schedule_items (0141). A widget should read fest_schedule_items so the old table can finally be dropped.
features.nativeOpportunity: Home Screen and Lock Screen presence during the one week of the year the whole family cares about — and the data source is public-read, so it is the cheapest widget backend imaginable. The web equivalent (Countdown.tsx) only counts while somebody is staring at the app.
features.v1Cut: Two widgets only: fest countdown (fest_config.start_date) and tonight's dinner. Defer 'who's up north' until the shared session works, defer Live Activities entirely.

features.name: Albums that scroll smoothly at any size
features.whatItDoes: A folder with hundreds of photos scrolls like Photos.app instead of hitching.
gotchas: ⚠️ The web album GRID is an unvirtualized items.map over every row (components/DropBoxes.tsx ~line 698) — a 2,000-item album is 2,000 DOM nodes. The CAROUSEL is windowed to <=3 elements and its comment explains why; the grid never got the same treatment. LazyVGrid gives you this for free.

⚠️ The fetch is unbounded: lib/dropBoxes.ts selects drop_box_media(...) as an embedded child with NO limit, NO range, NO pagination — every item, every open. Page at ~120 rows ordered captured_at desc nulls last, created_at desc.

⚠️⚠️ PostgREST embed ambiguity has bitten this project: a .select("*, child(*)") embed silently returns [] with HTTP 300 / PGRST201 when TWO foreign keys link the tables (it hit tournaments <-> tournament_entrants on the winner FK). If a second FK from drop_box_media to drop_boxes is ever added, this album query goes empty with no error. Name the FK, or run two queries.
⚠️ Render thumbnail_url in the grid and load the full-res only on tap-through — the parity doc calls this 'the single biggest scroll-performance win in the app'.
⚠️ Honest sizing: the live Family Fest album was 48 items, so this is not on fire today. Don't over-engineer — LazyVGrid plus a page size is the whole job.
⚠️ drop_box_media reads are status-aware: 'pending' rows are visible only to their uploader and admins, so a held photo missing from someone else's grid is correct behavior.
features.nativeOpportunity: LazyVGrid plus an image cache keyed on row id is a day of work and beats what the browser can do with loading="lazy" over thousands of nodes.
features.v1Cut: LazyVGrid + fixed page size + thumbnail-first rendering. Skip prefetch heuristics and skip a custom decode pipeline.

features.name: Warn before an inappropriate photo is uploaded
features.whatItDoes: Flags a likely-inappropriate photo on the phone before it uses the lake's uplink, instead of after the mini grades it.
gotchas: ⚠️ SCSensitivityAnalyzer requires the USER'S OWN Screen Time -> Sensitive Content Warning setting to be on; analysisPolicy returns .disabled otherwise and there is NO API to force it. Coverage across a 56-person family is unpredictable.

⚠️ The mini remains the authority. iOS's check is a courtesy warning, NEVER a gate, and must not change what gets inserted — the DB triggers (hold_drop_box_media_on_flagged, hold_comment_on_flagged_media, hold_content_on_media_verdict) are the real mechanism and iOS needs no moderation code at all.
⚠️ Moderation is asynchronous: a flagged verdict retroactively holds already-posted content seconds later. Expect status to flip to 'pending' AFTER a successful post and honor status when rendering.

⚠️ Drop-box uploads are deliberately more lenient — model unreachable means allowed and FINAL, not re-queued, so a family album never strands photos behind a broken checker. Don't change that from the client.
⚠️ Don't represent any of this as CSAM-safe: no third-party CSAM API exists and Apple exposes nothing for it. The human review queue is the backstop, not the model.

⚠️ The mini's fm serve caps request bodies at 1MB, which is why the server downscales a copy to <=1024px via sharp before base64. If iOS ever posts an image to a moderation endpoint, respect that ceiling.
features.nativeOpportunity: SCSensitivityAnalyzer runs on-device for free and instantly, so the phone can warn before a 40MB video crosses a residential uplink that is also serving everyone else's photos.
features.v1Cut: Cut entirely from v1.
